The isotopic compositions trace three stages of sulfate formation following the evolving temperature and pH of the lava tube system: 1) high-temperature combustion with atmospheric O2, 2) acidic aqueous oxidation by transition metals and H2O2, and 3) mildly acidic to alkaline oxidation by O3. On average, high temperature combustion accounts for ~40% of total sulfate. This finding demonstrates a direct isotopic link between volcanic sulfate and atmospheric O2 and identifies a pathway for preservation of this signal in volcanic sulfates. Applying this framework to dry acid fog deposits reveals a similarly significant combustion-sourced sulfate component. Accordingly, 16O-17O-18O compositions of volcanic sulfates can serve as robust proxies to constrain past environmental conditions, including local pH, planetary-scale CO2/O2, and global primary productivity when applied to samples from the geological record or returned from Mars.

title: Clumped isotope constraints on methane origin, formation depth, and migration of methane-bound gas hydrate in the Amazon deep-sea fan
description: Publication date: Available online 21 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Luiz Frederico Rodrigues, Alexis Gilbert, Malavika Sivan, Adolpho Herbert Augustin, Mayuko Nakagawa, Satoko Owari, Thomas Röckmann, João Marcelo Ketzer, Daniel Praeg, Jeffrey Poort, Aurelien Gay, José A. Cupertino, Dennis Miller, Cleverson Guizan Silva, Sébastien Migeon, Farid Chemale Junior
abstract: Deep-sea gas venting and gas hydrate systems are linked to major methane reservoirs in marine sediments and play a critical role in regulating methane transfer to the ocean and atmosphere, with implications for the global carbon cycle and Earth's climate system. Understanding methane provenance and thermal history in these systems is essential, and methane-clumped isotopes provide valuable constraints. Here, we present conventional stable isotope (δ13C-CH₄ and δD-CH₄) and clumped isotopologue (Δ13CH₃D and Δ12CH₂D₂) measurements of hydrate-bound methane from shallow sediments of the Amazon deep-sea fan, offshore Brazil. Gas hydrates were recovered in cores targeting water-column gas flares rising from seafloor mud volcanoes. Molecular and conventional isotope compositions indicate predominantly microbial methane with signatures consistent with CO₂ reduction. Methane recovered below the sulfate-methane transition zone (SMTZ) exhibits comparatively concordant apparent clumped isotope temperatures, whereas samples within the SMTZ show discrepancies between isotopologue-derived temperatures, consistent with possible shallow biogeochemical modification. Below the SMTZ, apparent formation/equilibration temperatures of approximately 36–46 °C correspond to thermally equivalent depths of approximately 900–1200 m below the seafloor under an independently constrained geothermal model. Clumped isotope compositions are consistent with a predominantly microbial component exhibiting an equilibrium-like signature, while thermogenic mixing remains possible. Combined with seismic observations, the geochemical and geothermal results are consistent with upward methane migration along structurally controlled pathways and accumulation in shallow gas hydrate reservoirs. These preliminary observations constrain possible methane isotopic histories in the analyzed samples; broader regional interpretation requires additional independent hydrate measurements.

title: Olivine solubility in Ca–Mg carbonate melts at 6 GPa: Constraints on the silica content of kimberlite melts
description: Publication date: Available online 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Anton Shatskiy, Daria V. Shatskaya, Yulia G. Vinogradova, Konstantin M. Stepanov, Alisa V. Kovalenko, Arseniy M. Genshpring
abstract: Olivine dominates kimberlites, yet much of it is xenocrystic. To determine whether the primary kimberlite melt was ultrabasic silicate or carbonatitic, the proportion of magmatic olivine must be known. We therefore determined experimentally the solubility of olivine in carbonate melts under mantle P–T conditions, using both simple and natural systems. In the Mg2SiO4–MgCO3–CaCO3 system at 6 GPa and 1500 °C, a magnesiocarbonatite melt dissolves 14 wt% olivine (6 wt% SiO2). In the fertile natural garnet lherzolite system at the same P–T, an alkaline magnesiocarbonatite melt dissolves 22–25 wt% olivine (9–10 wt% SiO2), similar to the kimberlite-relevant system at 6.5 GPa and 1500 °C, where multiple saturation with a garnet lherzolite assemblage yields 26–30 wt% olivine (~11 wt% SiO2; Shatskiy et al. (2017a)). Combining these solubilities with the 14 wt% olivine produced by orthopyroxene carbonation gives a total magmatic olivine content of 28–44 wt%, covering most of the 12–47 wt% range estimated from kimberlite rocks. Natural magmatic olivine exceeds the experimental solubility limit by an amount corresponding to 0.5–4 wt% SiO2; together with the dependence of olivine solubility on H2O, this implies a maximum H2O content of 0.5–3.5 wt% for the primary kimberlite melt. The inferred adiabatic ascent path for kimberlite magma (60 wt% carbonatite melt, 40 wt% mantle solids; Kavanagh and Sparks (2009)) is consistent with SiO2 contents of 2–6 wt% (alkali-poor) and 9–11 wt% (alkali-rich) over 200–30 km. These results support a magnesiocarbonatite composition for the ascending kimberlite melt.

title: Phase-resolved distributions and fractionation of rare earth elements in Daya Bay during spring
description: Publication date: Available online 6 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Yuncong Ge, Yulong Huang, Chunxue Wang, Ziang Li, Zhu Zhu, Wenkai Guan, Cong Zeng, Zhuoyi Zhu, Ruifeng Zhang
abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are widely used to trace land–ocean exchange, boundary inputs and particle–water interactions. Semi-enclosed coastal bays can modify REE signals before export to adjacent shelf waters, but how dissolved–particulate partitioning regulates this transformation remains poorly constrained. Here, we measured dissolved REEs (dREEs), labile particulate REEs (LpREEs) and refractory particulate REEs (RpREEs) in paired surface and bottom waters of Daya Bay, northern South China Sea. Surface dΣREE (234–1210 pM) was more variable than bottom dΣREE, whereas particulate REE pools, turbidity and particulate Al were enriched in bottom waters. Surface dissolved and total particulate REEs generally decreased with increasing salinity, suggesting that low-salinity inputs may influence both dissolved and particulate REE distributions. Superimposed on this bay-wide pattern, localized nearshore anomalies showed non-conservative dissolved REE enrichment, with stronger enrichment of some lighter REEs than heavier REEs, whereas localized refractory, Al-rich particulate REE anomalies were also observed. Refractory particulate REEs were strongly correlated with refractory particulate Al, consistent with a possible lithogenic contribution. In bottom waters, dΣREE showed negative associations with LpΣREE and particle-related variables, particularly LpMn and turbidity. The persistent negative association with LpMn after accounting for salinity and temperature suggests a potential contribution of particle-associated scavenging to dissolved REE distributions in bottom waters. Together, these findings reveal contrasting REE distribution patterns and phase-specific associations in Daya Bay, highlighting the roles of low-salinity-associated enrichment, localized anomalies and particle-associated processes in shaping coastal REE distributions during spring.

title: The geochemistry of uraniferous hyalite from Zacatecas, Mexico: Implications for the origin, timing, and deposition of Electric Opal
description: Publication date: Available online 30 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Bozana Pasic, John Mavrogenes, Ian S. Williams, Dominique Tanner, Peter K.M. Megaw
abstract: Green, daylight-luminescent hyalite from Zacatecas is a rare form of opal containing elevated concentrations of uranium. Through combined in situ isotopic and trace element analyses we investigated the process of uranium sequestration by opal to determine hyalite depositional conditions. Trace element analyses revealed a near perfect 1:1 correlation between uranium and calcium, which we attribute to “trapping” of calcium-uranyl carbonate complexes. Oxygen isotopic analyses and modelling estimate depositional temperatures of between ~23 °C and ~ 64 °C, respectively. Uranium‑lead dating of zoned hyalite indicates three principal generations of growth at 14.2 ± 0.69 Ma, 11.7 ± 0.8 Ma and 9.2 ± 0.7 Ma. Electric Opal was probably deposited from silica supersaturated, alkaline, groundwater-dominated fluids under confined lateral flow, making formation of Electric Opal a product of late volcanic or post-volcanic processes.

title: Hydrological setting and legacy phosphorus decouple algal recovery from catchment nitrogen decline
description: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 683 Author(s): Feilong Shen, Jifeng Li, Miks Valters Vīķis, Zhongbing Chen
abstract: Nitrogen reductions do not necessarily indicate lake recovery when phosphorus and chlorophyll respond differently. We analyzed 5,421 sampling records from 268 monitoring sites in Latvian lakes and reservoirs (1990–2022), combining long-term trends, paired period contrasts, and mixed-effects models. In five core waterbodies, ammonium nitrogen and total nitrogen (TN) declined by 70 % and 51 %, respectively, whereas total phosphorus (TP) showed no significant trend (+41 %; Mann–Kendall P = 0.085). Across 238 waterbodies, paired comparisons between 2007 and 2013 and 2016–2022 showed a 16 % decline in TP, robust to alternative windows. Chlorophyll a (Chl-a) records began in 2002, after most of the nitrogen decline had occurred, so they document conditions after the nitrogen reduction, not algal responses during it. Across 2,252 concurrent samples, TP was more strongly associated with Chl-a than TN (standardized mixed-effects coefficients: 0.252 and 0.003, respectively; at most 0.060 for TN after seasonal adjustment). Site-level Chl-a trends correlated with TP trends (Spearman’s ρ = 0.62; n = 31). The log–log Chl-a–TP slope was 0.98 in 259 natural lakes but −0.17 (not significant) in nine reservoirs. The contrast persisted even after excluding each reservoir in turn or the Daugava cascade. In three run-of-river reservoirs, phosphate accounted for more than half of TP during the growing season. Within sites, TP increased in wetter years (precipitation elasticity 0.21; P = 0.011), whereas TN did not show a detectable response. These results indicate that phosphorus availability and hydrological setting are central to interpreting changes in nutrients and chlorophyll following nitrogen decline.

title: Linking anthropogenic nitrogen and sulfur perturbations to carbon cycling dynamics: a multi-isotopic approach to decipher coupled weathering processes in a typical karst aquifer
description: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 683 Author(s): Wenjing Guo, Pingheng Yang, Zuping Zhang, Yanlu Liu, Changhao Liao, Kejun Qu, Yuechen Li
abstract: Karst watersheds feature unique water–rock–biota interactions and vulnerable biogeochemical cycles, where anthropogenic nitrogen (N) and sulfur (S) inputs profoundly perturb carbonate weathering and carbon (C) cycling. However, the coupled mechanisms of carbon–nitrogen–sulfur cycles and their quantitative controls on carbon export dynamics in karst catchments remain poorly constrained. In this study, systematic hydrogeochemical analyses and multi-stable isotope tracers were combined to elucidate the coupling pathways, driving factors, and flux responses of C–N–S cycles in a typical urbanized karst catchment. The results indicate that groundwater dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is primarily derived from carbonate weathering and direct discharge of wastewater. Hydrochemical stoichiometric evidence shows that anthropogenic HNO3 and H2SO4 extensively participate in carbonate dissolution, in addition to natural H2CO3. Strong acids (H2SO4 and HNO3) jointly mediate 19.5% of the total DIC flux (5.9 g C m−2 yr−1). Of this acid-mediated weathering, the strictly anthropogenically augmented portion, derived from atmospheric acid deposition, manure and sewage, and fertilizer inputs, amounts to 2.6 g C m−2 yr−1 (8.5% of the total DIC export), the remainder being contributed by naturally derived sulfide oxidation and soil-nitrogen nitrification. These findings highlight that human-induced acid inputs substantially reshape natural karst C–N–S cycling. This study establishes a reliable multi-isotope quantitative framework for evaluating anthropogenically modified carbonate weathering and carbon cycling in urban karst systems.

title: Scaling PINNs for field-scale hydrogeology: Comparative analysis of Bayesian optimization and FiLM modulation
description: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 683 Author(s): Mayank Bajpai, Ranveer Kumar, Kamal Singh, Shishir Gaur
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free alternative to traditional numerical groundwater models, but their scalability and structural requirements in data-scarce, real-world field settings remain unclear. This study systematically investigates the architectural and hyperparameter dependencies of PINNs for field-scale hydrogeology by comparing a baseline Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) PINN, the same PINN with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization (Optuna), and a variant incorporating Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM). Applied to the heterogeneous Varuna River Basin in India, the models are trained directly on sparse groundwater-head observations from 37 monitoring wells and simultaneously solve the forward groundwater head prediction and the inverse parameter estimation (hydraulic conductivity and specific yield) of the depth-averaged unconfined flow equation. To evaluate generalization and robustness, the networks were tested across random, temporal-gap and sparse-training validation splits, with hyperparameters selected on a validation partition and performance reported on an independent test partition. Our results demonstrate that uncalibrated baseline PINNs suffer from severe gradient pathologies and fail to capture physical dynamics. Conversely, the Bayesian-optimized standard MLP achieved high predictive accuracy on the test partitions (Kling-Gupta Efficiency of 0.99, 0.98 and 0.88 for the random, temporal-gap and sparse-training splits), bridging chronological gaps and spatial deficits. While the FiLM-integrated architecture reduced internal gradient conflicts and produced highly stable loss convergence, its dynamic temporal conditioning over-smoothed the predictive space, ultimately degrading the resolution of localized hydrogeological transients compared to the standard MLP. A regional MODFLOW-NWT model of the same reach calibrated with the PEST++ iterative ensemble smoother reproduced the matched field observations with a Kling-Gupta Efficiency of 0.25 and a root mean square error of 5.03 m. Furthermore, functional ANOVA of the hyperparameter trials ranked the physical regularization penalties above architectural depth and width, although with wide confidence intervals. This study underscores that for complex, field-scale groundwater systems, rigorous multi-objective loss balancing of continuous, symmetric architectures yields superior predictive fidelity and structural robustness compared to decoupled temporal conditioning through FiLM.

title: Salinity-driven reorganization of bacterioplankton communities across the river–estuary–coast continuum
description: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 683 Author(s): Lei Fu, Xiongdong Zhou, Manjie Li
abstract: The river-estuary-coast continuum is increasingly influenced by climate change and human activities, yet microbial community organization across this transitional system remains poorly understood. In this study, bacterioplankton communities were characterized along a tidal-influenced transect spanning the lower Pearl River, the Pearl River Estuary, and adjacent coastal waters using eDNA-based profiling. Across the continuum, both taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity declined progressively with increasing salinity (Shannon diversity: 5.67 ± 0.08 to 4.06 ± 0.13; phylogenetic diversity: 99.80 ± 3.33 to 51.86 ± 2.40), a pattern that did not exhibit the classical Remane minimum at intermediate salinity. In contrast, network robustness peaked in the estuarine transition zone despite relatively low diversity, whereas the river section with the highest diversity exhibited the lowest robustness. This diversity-stability decoupling indicates pronounced spatial restructuring of bacterioplankton interactions across the continuum. Salinity emerged as the dominant environmental gradient shaping both community composition and assembly processes (direct effect r = 0.91, P < 0.001). Deterministic processes governed community assembly across the entire continuum (69.7 %), whereas stochastic processes became more prominent in the hydrodynamically active estuarine region (ecological drift and other weak processes: 52.4 %). In addition, core bacterioplankton taxa exhibited pronounced turnover along the salinity gradient, with 84 negatively responding taxa dominating the riverine region and 57 positively responding taxa dominating the coastal region, revealing asymmetric replacement of freshwater-associated lineages by salinity-tolerant taxa. Together, these results point to a salinity-driven reorganization of microbial communities that decouples diversity from stability, reshapes assembly processes, and drives asymmetric turnover, providing a conceptual foundation for understanding community dynamics across transitional aquatic ecosystems. These patterns require further seasonal and system-wide testing.

title: A Bayesian approach for modeling temporal variability in urban stormwater event mean concentrations
description: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 683 Author(s): Zhaokai Dong, Pradeep Goel, Clare E. Robinson
abstract: Event Mean Concentration (EMC) is widely used for estimating stormwater pollutant loads. In practice, EMC is commonly treated as a deterministic parameter, overlooking temporal variability associated with seasonal conditions and storm characteristics and potentially underestimating the resulting uncertainty. In this study, we develop a novel Bayesian linear model to represent EMC as a temporally structured parameter, decomposed into global, seasonal, and event-level components. Using soluble reactive phosphorus (SRP) data collected at the outlet of a mixed urban catchment during warm-season events (summer and fall), we demonstrate two applications of the model. The single lumped model directly characterizes temporal variability in catchment-scale EMC and predicts event-specific EMCs based on the estimated temporal relationships, whereas the semi-distributed model extends the framework to infer land use-specific EMCs from catchment-outlet observations when land use-specific monitoring data are limited. Results indicate differences in catchment-scale EMCs between the monitored summer and fall events, with antecedent dry days (ADD) showing a positive association with event-level variation in SRP EMC. Explicitly accounting for seasonal and event-level variability yielded the best predictive performance for event-specific EMCs among the evaluated temporal model structures. Land use-specific EMCs inferred by the semi-distributed model showed limited identifiability of spatial and seasonal patterns across land uses, although the posterior estimates were broadly comparable in magnitude to measured concentrations from grab samples collected at the outlets of individual land use drainage areas. The new framework presented provides a valuable approach for characterizing EMC temporal variability and quantifying the associated uncertainty in stormwater quality modeling.

title: Redox and pH driven divergence in the degradation of hydrophilic and hydrophobic organic matter at the sediment‑water interface
description: Publication date: February 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 683 Author(s): Yaru Feng, Lixin Jiao, Yiru Wang, Liansheng He, Weizhen Zhang
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) regulates nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, and pollutant transport at the sediment–water interface, yet how its hydrophilic (HIM) and hydrophobic (HOM) fractions degrade under varying redox and pH conditions remains unclear. We incubated sediments from eutrophic Lake Dianchi under oxic, hypoxic, and alkaline-hypoxic conditions. DOM was characterized using UV–Vis absorption spectroscopy and excitation-emission matrix parallel factor analysis (EEM-PARAFAC), and the data were further analyzed by principal component analysis (PCA). Our results showed that HIM and HOM followed distinct degradation and transformation pathways. HIM underwent rapid degradation and nitrogen release, which were mainly controlled by redox conditions. Under hypoxic conditions, HIM transformation and nitrogen release were enhanced relative to oxic conditions, accompanied by a 105.7% increase in dissolved organic carbon (DOC) (p < 0.01) and higher biological index (BIX) and ammonium nitrogen (NH4 +-N). HOM was dominated by humification and aromatic carbon preservation. Under oxic conditions, its specific ultraviolet absorbance at 254 nm (SUVA254) was 2.18 times that of HIM, and its humification index (HIX) was highest. Under alkaline-hypoxic conditions, HOM showed limited dissolved release and accumulation, likely due to its retention in the solid phase. These findings help anticipate DOM-mediated nutrient and carbon dynamics and support management strategies targeting DOM composition to mitigate eutrophication and secondary risks.

title: Seasonal hydrologic reversal shifts the dominant reaction location and alters nutrient behavior in lake–groundwater interaction zones
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Ningfei Li, Xiaosi Su, Dong Li, Yongqi Wang, Haiting Liang, Weihong Dong, Hang Lyu, Xiaofang Shen, Xueyu Lin
abstract: Seasonal reversal of lake–groundwater interaction is common in shallow lakes, yet how this reversal shifts the dominant reaction location and alters nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) dynamics in nearshore aquifers remains poorly understood. We investigated a seasonally reversing interaction zone where initial field surveys revealed distinct nutrient behavior between lake-water recharge and groundwater discharge, motivating targeted mechanistic sampling across both exchange states. Under groundwater discharge, reducing groundwater moved toward the lake with limited along-flow variation in dissolved total nitrogen (DTN) and dissolved total phosphorus (DTP), while diffusive gradients in thin films and sediment P data indicated P retention near the sediment–water interface. Under lake-water recharge, oxygenated lake water carrying dissolved organic matter (DOM) entered the nearshore aquifer. The strongest coordinated hydrochemical and redox changes occurred within approximately 20 m of the shoreline, while the farther inland zone showed transitional behavior. Along this recharge flow path, DOM processing and progressive redox reorganization were accompanied by Mn/Fe transformation and nonconservative DTN and DTP enrichment, with concentrations exceeding conservative mixing predictions by 33–133% and 142–247%, respectively. First-order Darcy-based flux estimates showed that the state-specific DTN and DTP transport magnitudes during lake-water recharge were 4.35 and 7.11 times those during groundwater discharge, with the nonconservative component contributing 38% and 63% to DTN and DTP transport, respectively. These findings support a process-based framework linking hydrologic reversal, shifts in the dominant reaction location, coupled DOM–redox processing, and a potential delayed-loading pathway in groundwater-connected shallow lakes.

title: Hydrological model applicability and ensemble prediction under contrasting boundary settings in two semi-humid basins of Northern China
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Qi Kong, Zhijia Li, Cheng Yao, Ke Zhang
abstract: Flood simulation in semi-humid regions remains challenging due to complex hydrological responses. To evaluate model applicability and predictive uncertainty under different hydrological and boundary settings, the Zijingguan headwater basin and the Tanjiafang interval basin in northern China were selected as case studies. A multi-model comparative framework incorporating the Xin’anjiang (XAJ), Grid-Xin’anjiang (Grid-XAJ), Grid-XAJ with Saturation–Infiltration Double Excess (Grid-XAJ-SIDE), and TOPKAPI models was developed, and Bayesian model averaging (BMA) was applied for ensemble prediction. Event-scale results show that relative model advantages vary with basin settings and hydrological conditions, and that greater model complexity is more likely to yield performance gains only when the added structure better represents key response processes. In the Zijingguan basin, under unsaturated conditions, Grid-XAJ-SIDE better reproduces rapid flood responses associated with infiltration-excess runoff; as the basin approaches saturation, differences in runoff generation among models diminish. In the Tanjiafang interval basin, strong upstream inflows partly mask differences in local runoff generation and the effects of spatial heterogeneity, making simulation performance more dependent on upstream inflow routing and its superposition with runoff from the interval basin. Under such conditions, merely increasing the complexity of runoff generation schemes yields limited benefits, whereas TOPKAPI exhibits greater adaptability in representing inflow propagation across different flood magnitudes. For selected historical flood events, BMA improves ensemble mean predictions and overall probabilistic performance, but its gain depends on the diversity and error complementarity of member models. Its prediction intervals generally provide satisfactory coverage but may underestimate predictive uncertainty under extreme conditions.

title: From the Tibetan Plateau to the sea: Contrasting microplastic load trajectories in two Asian mega-rivers
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Sansan Feng, Hongwei Lu, Hengchen Li, Tong Sun, Stefan Krause
abstract: Rivers act as major conveyors of land-derived microplastics (MPs), yet their evolution from remote headwaters through large river networks remains poorly resolved. We combined new field MP measurements in surface water and streambed sediments from 25 Tibetan Plateau headwater sites in the Yangtze, Yellow, and Lancang (upper Mekong) basins with a harmonized synthesis of published downstream studies for the Yangtze and Yellow rivers. Headwater MP concentrations ranged from 133.3 to 933.3 items m⁻3 in surface waters and 8.3 to 116.7 items kg⁻1 in sediments, and were generally lower at remote sites. Fibers and polypropylene dominated headwater assemblages, while multivariate analyses indicated coupled anthropogenic, hydrochemical, and hydraulic gradients. Annualized loads based on non-synchronous downstream MP concentrations and discharge are presented as comparative estimates. Across the reconstructed basin-scale profiles, MP concentrations and estimated annualized loads increased downstream, but followed contrasting trajectories. The Yangtze showed a broadly progressive increase, whereas the Yellow River exhibited a pronounced middle-reach surge, lower-reach decline, and renewed estuary increase. Segment-scale concentration–discharge decomposition indicated a larger discharge-associated marginal term across most Yangtze transitions, whereas concentration-associated changes were more prominent around the main middle-reach increase in the Yellow River. These results highlight contrasting reconstructed longitudinal load trajectories and concentration–discharge signatures across two large rivers with markedly different hydrological settings.

title: External moisture versus local recycling in the Tibetan Plateau summer precipitation dipole
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Fujun Du, Hong Yan, Yongli He, Chao Li, Xiaogang He
abstract: Summer precipitation over the Tibetan Plateau has experienced a pronounced north–south wetting–drying dipole in recent decades, yet the processes driving this hydroclimatic contrast remain unclear. Here, we combine moisture tracking with a source-resolved decomposition of precipitation changes during 1960–2020 into frequency and intensity contributions. We find that the dipole is driven primarily by contrasting intensity changes in precipitation events dominated by externally sourced moisture, while events dominated by locally recycled moisture play a secondary role, reinforcing southern drying through reduced event frequency. The subtropical westerly jet, whose weakening has been linked to anthropogenic aerosol forcing and the Tibetan Plateau summer precipitation dipole, contributes to the dipole mainly through changes in the intensity of externally sourced events. These findings highlight the value of decomposing precipitation changes by moisture source and event characteristics for understanding regional hydroclimate responses to climate change.

title: Forecasting terrestrial water storage anomalies using causal seasonal-trend decomposition
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Ze Yuan, Fuxuan Jiang, Yilin Chen, Sile Li, Zheying Lyu, Guangming Liu, Xiaohong Chen
abstract: Regional terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA) exhibit pronounced nonstationarity. Although decomposition-based forecasting can improve predictive performance, conventional decomposition methods rely on future information and thus violate temporal causality when applied to forecasting. To address this limitation, a novel Causal Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (CSTL) is proposed for causal decomposition and forecasting of GRACE-derived TWSA. CSTL combines offline historical initialization with one-sided causal updating during the forecasting period, thereby preventing information leakage from future observations. An aggregated feature strategy and Dempster–Shafer (DS) evidence theory are further introduced to characterize multiscale memory effects in TWSA and improve feature selection. These components are integrated with four machine-learning models for retrospective forecasting. Validation across nine major river basins in China demonstrates robust predictive performance. At a lead time of one month, the highest forecasting accuracy is obtained in the Southwest River Basin (SWRB), with a Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) of 0.93. Basins with larger contributions from seasonal components exhibit stronger predictability. Compared with TWS change estimates derived from the state-of-the-art numerical climate forecast system, the CSTL-based forecasts achieve higher correlations and reduce RMSE by 18–85%. Ablation results show that CSTL is the key component to stable long-term forecasting. Under a leakage-free forecasting setting, the proposed framework achieves performance comparable to that of the non-causal STL-based model in the Yangtze River Basin (KGE = 0.80). Overall, this study establishes a causality-consistent framework for TWSA forecasting, with potential for real-time operational applications, and provides a methodological basis for hydrological forecasting of nonstationary time series.

title: Seasonal changes in hydrological connectivity regulate nitrate dynamics in a semi-arid saline-alkaline agricultural watershed
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Jimin Huang, Qiannian Fu, Xiangpeng Lin, Junpeng Chen, Lijun Liu, Xuemei Liu, Yao Wu
abstract: Seasonal variations in surface water-groundwater connectivity influence nitrate transport and source composition, yet their role during the transition from spring to early summer in semi-arid saline–alkaline agricultural watersheds remains poorly understood. This study combined hydrochemical analyses, stable isotopes of water and nitrate, and the SIAR Bayesian mixing model to investigate nitrate sources and the influence of hydrological processes on nitrate dynamics in the Huolin River watershed, northeastern China. Nitrate was the dominant nitrogen species in the sampled waters, accounting for approximately 70% of total nitrogen, and the mean nitrate-N concentration was higher in groundwater (3.54 mg/L) than in surface water (1.48 mg/L). SIAR estimates indicated that manure and sewage (MS) had the largest mean source contributions in both water types, accounting for 56.4% in surface water and 46.9% in groundwater in April. In June, the estimated mean contributions of soil organic nitrogen (SON) and chemical fertilizer (CF) increased, whereas those of MS declined to 41.6% and 45.0% in surface water and groundwater, respectively. This shift may reflect the transport of soil-derived and fertilizer-derived nitrogen into surface water and groundwater through rainfall-driven runoff and infiltration. Water hydrogen and oxygen isotopes, together with hydrochemical results, indicated recharge and mixing links between surface water and groundwater, with the groundwater response to recharge potentially lagging behind changes in surface water. Dual nitrate isotope signatures suggested that nitrate formation was primarily associated with nitrification, while some groundwater samples collected in April may have been affected by denitrification. These findings suggest that nitrate pollution control in the Huolin River watershed should strengthen the control of manure and sewage inputs and the management of agricultural nitrogen losses, account for snowmelt and rainfall-driven runoff and recharge, and coordinate the monitoring and management of surface water and shallow groundwater.

title: A scale-aware framework for characterizing multiscale aquifer heterogeneity by coordinating machine learning and stochastic modeling
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Chuanjun Zhan, Jiu Jimmy Jiao, Zhenxue Dai, Mohamad Reza Soltanian, Kenneth C. Carroll
abstract: Aquifer heterogeneity controls groundwater flow and solute transport through structural organization and hydraulic-property variability across multiple scales. Existing characterization methods commonly target scale-specific heterogeneity, such as large-scale sediment–bedrock distributions, sedimentary facies architecture, or continuous hydraulic-conductivity fields; therefore, method selection should reflect the spatial organization, available data, and hydrologic role of each component. This study develops a scale-aware framework that organizes aquifer heterogeneity into three linked scales: the hydrogeologic domain scale, the internal categorical architecture scale, and the property scale. Ensemble machine learning maps sediment–bedrock and weathered–unweathered bedrock structures; transition-probability geostatistical simulation represents clay–sand architecture within sampled sediment domains; and facies-conditioned synthetic pilot points generate illustrative prior hydraulic-conductivity (K) fields. The framework is demonstrated in the Pearl River Delta, a heterogeneous coastal-plain aquifer system containing sedimentary deposits and weathered bedrock. The generated structures are compared with direct four-class models based on machine learning or transition-probability geostatistical simulation using 100 realizations per method. The scale-aware framework closely reproduces the borehole-derived depth-wise class-fraction profiles while jointly retaining regional sediment–bedrock geometry, alternating clay–sand bodies, and coherent weathered-bedrock units. The ensemble statistics and cross-sectional comparisons together support a more coherent overall representation of the intended geological hierarchy. These findings demonstrate the value of matching modeling methods to the spatial characteristics of different heterogeneity components when constructing multiscale aquifer structures and prior hydraulic-property fields from a common borehole database.

title: Predicting complex transport behavior via a hydrofacies-constrained simulation framework
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Chenxi Wang, Zhi Dou, Zeren Ning, Hyoun-Tae Hwang, Walter A. Illman, Zejun Wang, Chaoqi Wang
abstract: Predicting solute and heat transport in highly heterogeneous aquifers remains challenging. Two major limitations hinder borehole-based subsurface characterization: (1) limited capability of downhole logging tests to capture vertical hydraulic conductivity (K) variations across a broad range of particle sizes; (2) conventional interpolation or simulation methods cannot faithfully capture the nested heterogeneity pattern of layered porous media. Here, we establish a simulation framework that uses nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logging to provide decimeter-scale K profiles spanning over five orders of magnitude. To characterize the nested spatial heterogeneity within a glaciofluvial deposit, we performed sequential Gaussian simulation (SGS) within each clustering-defined hydrofacies, yielding equiprobable K realizations that honor the layered geological structure. Thirty-two drawdown records from two pumping tests were used to select realizations that best reproduce groundwater flow dynamics. Spatial K models constructed with various correlation techniques were used to simulate the temperature breakthrough curves of a three-dimensional monitoring network in a forced-gradient heat tracer test. Results show that a standard kriging model conditioned on NMR data captures the general patterns of complex three-dimensional plume behavior. The proposed framework further improves transport predictions. The resulting composite K field from selected realizations outperforms the kriging model by 33.9% and the same selection procedure applied to standard SGS by 50.0%. Hydrofacies constraints enable SGS to generate unit-wise heterogeneity patterns while preserving layered structure, and drawdown-based selection retains realizations better representing K connectivity. This framework circumvents complex calibration and offers an operable approach to high-resolution site characterization for groundwater remediation and geothermal energy use.

title: Hydrodynamic controls on mineral precipitation in porous media: From pore-scale clogging to continuum permeability upscaling
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Yaohui Wang, Fugang Wang, Donghui Wang, Heng Li, Hui Cheng, Yilong Yuan
abstract: Mineral precipitation can sharply reduce permeability in reactive porous media, yet continuum models commonly represent this effect using fixed porosity–permeability relationships that do not account for hydrodynamic controls on precipitation localisation. Here we use pore-scale reactive transport simulations of calcite precipitation in six synthetic two-dimensional porous structures to examine the hydrodynamic contribution of the Péclet number (Pe) to precipitation patterns and permeability evolution under prescribed reaction conditions. The simulations cover diffusion- to advection-dominated regimes. Low Pe promotes reactant consumption near the inlet, producing localised clogging and rapid loss of connected flow paths. By contrast, high Pe transports reactants farther into the pore network, leading to more distributed precipitation and a slower permeability decline. As a result, permeability is not a unique function of porosity: in low-Pe cases, permeability can decline sharply after only a small porosity loss, whereas high-Pe cases can sustain larger porosity reductions before severe hydraulic impairment occurs. We capture this behaviour using a power-law porosity–permeability model with a clogging parameter. Fits to 1,152 pore-scale simulations yield coefficients of determination of 0.82–0.99 and show that the clogging parameter decreases systematically with Pe. Embedding this Pe-dependent parameterisation into a continuum reactive transport simulation allows permeability updates to respond to local flow conditions, unlike fixed Kozeny–Carman or Verma–Pruess relationships. This framework links pore-scale precipitation localisation to continuum-scale permeability evolution and provides a mechanistic basis for predicting precipitation-induced hydraulic impairment in hydrologically heterogeneous subsurface systems.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and compound human pressures on groundwater depletion in the Indus River Basin
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Chunlan Li, Jingping Tian, Huize Xu, Jiansong Peng, Songtao Li, Lijiang Shi, Shijin Wang
abstract: Groundwater depletion threatens water and food security in the Indus River Basin, where irrigated agriculture and expanding settlements place pressure on limited water resources. We examined groundwater-storage changes from 2002 to 2022 using satellite-derived groundwater estimates, nighttime lights, population data, and vegetation observations. The basin-mean groundwater depletion index increased by 13.787 mm yr−1, with major depletion hotspots in the Punjab–Panjnad region and the irrigated plains of northwestern India. Areas with increasing vegetation greenness showed the strongest spatial correspondence with groundwater depletion among the individual indicators, while the combined patterns of vegetation, settlement activity, and population provided a fuller description of regional differences. Agricultural/vegetation associations covered 46.7% of the valid study area, and zones with combined urban and agricultural signals covered another 6.2%. These findings identify irrigated plains as priorities for groundwater monitoring and coordinated water management. Because the groundwater estimates are downscaled and the human-activity indicators do not measure pumping directly, the observed relationships should be understood as spatial associations, not demonstrated causes of groundwater loss.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and teleconnection associations of extreme precipitation in China at the twenty-four solar terms scale
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Jiangkuan Zhao, Ziyan Li, Yimin Wang, Shuai Zhou, Yanru Zhang, Qi Wang, Xiangxu Song, Huixin Shi
abstract: Global warming intensifies extreme precipitation and exacerbates regional disparities, increasing pressures on water resources and ecological security. These pressures depend not only on annual totals but also on intra-annual distribution. To better resolve spatiotemporal dynamics and teleconnection associations that monthly or seasonal aggregation obscures, this study examined ten extreme precipitation indices across China’s seven climatic zones. Using daily CHM_PRE V2 data from 1965 to 2024 and the 24 solar terms as a temporal framework, we analyzed trends at individual solar terms, shifts in precipitation contributions, and overlap between climatological high value windows and strengthening trends to distinguish local changes from annual-cycle reorganization. We further assessed lagged associations with seven large-scale climate indices under low and high states of paired indices. After multiple testing correction, extreme precipitation changes were concentrated in specific solar terms, regions, and metrics, with timing and direction varying across climatic zones. This spatial and temporal heterogeneity is routinely obscured by monthly or seasonal aggregation. Annual precipitation contributions shifted among solar terms in regionally distinct patterns. MangZhong showed the strongest overlap between climatological high values and strengthening trends, highlighting a potentially important phase for precipitation monitoring. Nine of ten significant teleconnection index pairs reversed correlation with extreme precipitation under low versus high states of the second index, indicating state dependence rather than additive effects. These findings demonstrate that the 24 solar terms provide an interpretable temporal framework for characterizing phase-specific precipitation windows and disentangling localized trends, intra-annual redistribution, and conditional teleconnection patterns, thereby informing solar-term-aware precipitation monitoring and regional water-resources planning in China.

title: Modeling groundwater salinity evolution and mitigation strategies under stochastic climate forcings in the Comacchio coastal aquifer (Italy)
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Mattia Gaiolini, Massimiliano Schiavo, Giulia Farina, Nicola Astolfi, Laura Montanari, Nicolò Colombani, Micòl Mastrocicco
abstract: Coastal aquifers are increasingly threatened by salinization due to climate change and sea level rise, particularly in low-lying Mediterranean environments where groundwater systems are strongly connected with saline and brackish surface water bodies. This study presents a three-dimensional variable-density groundwater flow and transport model of the Comacchio coastal aquifer (northern Italy), integrating climatic datasets to investigate groundwater future response to climate forcings. A monthly transient simulation for the period 2024–2025 was calibrated and validated against piezometric heads and salinity observations, achieving R2 values up to 0.98 for heads and 0.97 for salinity concentrations. After this step, predictive simulations up to 2050 incorporated climate change projections, including sea-level rise together with stochastic evapotranspiration and recharge derived from a climate models ensemble. Climate uncertainty and unresolved spatial heterogeneity were propagated through the model via DEM-conditioned stochastic downscaling combined with quantile-based climate forcing scenarios. Results indicate that most of the early salinity increase is related to transient model adjustment, whereas climate change acts as a persistent driver of additional salinity by reducing meteoric recharge and enhancing saline inflows and redistribution of pre-existing saline groundwater by 2050. Simulated mitigation scenarios based on upscaled irrigation areas and increased irrigation loadings proved effective in preventing and delaying groundwater salinization.

title: Depth-resolved phytoplankton pigment structure improves short-term forecasts of surface chlorophyll- a and phycocyanin in a deep lake
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Shenghua Chen, Jingyi Li, Kun Shan, Di Song, Cheng Tang, Qichao Zhou
abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic pressures increasingly threaten water quality and exacerbate algal bloom risks in deep lakes, yet current forecasting frameworks remain constrained by a surface-centric paradigm that overlooks critical vertical heterogeneity regulating phytoplankton dynamics in stratified ecosystems. In such systems, substantial phytoplankton biomass often resides within subsurface layers beyond the reach of surface monitoring. Here, we conducted high-frequency vertical monitoring in Lake Fuxian, a representative deep oligotrophic lake in China, and developed HIS-Phytoplankton (Hybrid Intelligent System for Phytoplankton Forecasting), an interpretable machine-learning framework for one- and two-day-ahead forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a (Chla) and phycocyanin (PC). Generalized-Gaussian descriptors characterized the deep chlorophyll and phycocyanin maxima, while XGBoost-SHAP quantified synchronous associations between pigments, surface conditions and vertical structure. Turbidity and fluorescent dissolved organic matter were important model predictors of Chla, whereas dissolved oxygen and turbidity contributed prominently to PC predictions. Adding subsurface peak magnitude (DM) improved R 2 relative to surface-only models by 26.09% for Chla and 24.93% for PC in one-day-ahead predictions, and by 18.45% and 24.13% in two-day-ahead predictions, respectively. These findings reveal incremental predictive value from depth-resolved pigment information at the monitored station, while not establishing whether vertical transport, biological migration or shared environmental forcing causes the observed associations. HIS-Phytoplankton provides a potentially useful framework for incorporating vertical observations into short-term pigment forecasting in deep lakes.

title: ABiTCN: Asymmetric bidirectional temporal convolutional network for predicting rainfall forecast-integrated flood inflow
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Taesam Lee, Juyoung Shin
abstract: Accurate short-lead-time forecasts of reservoir inflow are essential for dam operation during floods, especially in mountainous catchments affected by monsoons and typhoons. The current study proposes an asymmetric bidirectional temporal convolutional network (ABiTCN) that predicts reservoir inflow 12 h ahead by explicitly incorporating future rainfall forecasts, using Miryang Dam, South Korea as a case study. The model uses three branches as a forward branch that encodes past rainfall, a backward branch that encodes forecast rainfall and converges toward the current time step, and a separate forward branch that encodes past reservoir inflow. This design allows the model use forecast information without leaking future data information into past predictions. Using 24 years (2002–2025) of hourly reservoir data and 18 major flood events, the ABiTCN was tested against a standard TCN and a Transformer model using 5-fold cross-validation. The ABiTCN achieved a much higher Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) than both comparison models, indicating substantially better predictive accuracy. The sensitivity analysis with imperfect rainfall forecast presents that as forecast quality declined, the performance of the ABiTCN dropped gradually rather than sharply, and it still outperformed the other models even when the forecast carried no real skill at all. Across 5-fold cross-validation the ABiTCN reached a mean NSE of 0.93, compared with 0.35 for the TCN and 0.23 for the Transformer. This near-0.93 NSE is obtained with observed precipitation used as a perfect forecast and is therefore an upper bound. When the model is driven by the GEFS version 12 reforecast, the skill is lower but still exceeds the past-only baseline at the operationally important longer lead times. The results indicate that the proposed ABiTCN model has practical value for dam pre-release decisions and downstream flood warning, with performance that improves further as the accuracy of the paired rainfall forecast improves.

title: Coupling of source apportionment with ensemble smoother to identify groundwater pollution source in a chemical industrial park
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Jiyong Tan, Xiao Bian, Bo Sun, Mufeng Cheng, Yujie Chen, Zhenbo Chang, Yang Liu, Huaming Guo
abstract: Accurate and efficient identification of groundwater pollution sources in chemical industrial parks is a critical challenge. This study developed an integrated framework coupling positive matrix factorization (PMF) source apportionment, numerical simulation model, surrogate model, and ensemble smoother with multiple data assimilation (ES-MDA) to identify groundwater pollution sources in a chemical industrial park in Shandong Province, China. The PMF model was applied to identify main source types and their contribution ratios, with these results providing prior constraints for surrogate model training and the ES-MDA inversion. Groundwater flow and solute transport models were constructed to characterize 1,2-dichloroethane (1,2-DCA) migration in aquifers. Given the high computational cost of the numerical model, Kriging (KRG) and multilayer perceptron (MLP) surrogate models were developed and compared. The average relative errors were 12.67% (KRG) and 13.21% (MLP); the KRG model (R2 = 0.944, RMSE = 0.047) achieved accuracy comparable to the MLP model (R2 = 0.942, RMSE = 0.048). The KRG surrogate model was selected for coupling with ES-MDA. The PMF results indicate the presence of five pollution sources in the park: pharmaceutical and chemical sources (18.01%), petrochemical sources (15.59%), mixed sources of salt chemistry and seawater intrusion (29.61%), domestic sewage and nitrogen-containing industrial wastewater sources (17.04%), and geological background sources (19.75%). ES-MDA can effectively identify and estimate the potential source information. The KRG surrogate model reduced computational time and costs by over 90%, enabling the ES-MDA to complete 10 iterations in seconds. This framework provides a highly efficient and transferable solution for source identification in multi-source industrial sites.

title: Implementation of new, asset-specific damage curves for flood risk assessment in wastewater treatment plants: a methodological approach applied to the Metropolitan Area of Barcelona (Spain)
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Guillem Flor-Tey, Eduardo Martínez-Gomariz, Beniamino Russo, Salvador Castán, Joaquín Bosque, Elena Veza
abstract: The frequency and intensity of climate-related disasters have increased in recent decades, posing significant challenges to urban resilience. Sanitation systems, particularly wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), are exposed to flood hazards due to their location in low-lying areas near receiving water bodies. Flood events may cause service disruptions, asset and equipment damage, and associated environmental and economic consequences. To address this issue, this study develops an integrated methodology to quantify hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and damage associated with flood events in wastewater facilities. The main contribution of the research is the development of novel asset-specific damage curves for WWTPs, derived from expert judgement and subjected to a plausibility assessment using information from observed flood events across Spain. The curves are used to estimate potential economic damages resulting from the direct physical impact of water on facility components. A comparison with existing damage curves from the literature shows that the proposed methodology generally produces higher damage estimates, highlighting the relevance of asset-specific modelling for accurate impact evaluation. The methodology has been applied to WWTPs in the metropolitan area of Barcelona, where Aigües de Barcelona is the entity responsible for the sanitation system management and operation. Results identify the facilities most affected by flooding and estimate economic damages that, in extreme scenarios (500-year return period events), may reach approximately 6% of the total value of an individual affected WWTP. These findings support decision-making by utility managers, enabling prioritisation of adaptation measures and planning future investments to enhance the resilience of the metropolitan sanitation infrastructure.

title: Freeze-induced evolution of hydraulic properties in ice-bearing rough fractures
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Xulong Gao, Yuanming Lai, Jiachuan Ran, Wanli Feng, Xinyu Jia, Wenzhe Zhang
abstract: Unfrozen water content and relative permeability are key constitutive variables for describing liquid water retention and hydraulic transport in ice-bearing rough fractures. However, models developed for frozen soils do not explicitly account for fracture confinement, interfacial premelting, or frost-induced aperture changes. This study developed a fracture freezing characteristic curve (FFCC) and a fracture relative permeability curve (FRPC). The FFCC, derived from a second-order generalized Clapeyron relation, partitions unfrozen water into geometrically confined and premelted-film components. The FRPC combines film transmissivities, statistical representations of aperture heterogeneity, and an empirical tortuosity correction to describe effective permeability reduction in ice-bearing rough fractures. Both constitutive relationships include an equivalent frost-heave-induced aperture adjustment. The proposed geometric–hydraulic mapping reproduced the nonlinear saturation–permeability relationships reported for three rough-fracture two-phase flow datasets. The constitutive relationships were further embedded in a transient thermo-hydraulic simulation of an ice-bearing fracture melting experiment, and the simulation reproduced the main macroscopic hydraulic response during melting. Within the investigated parameter ranges, mean aperture primarily shifted the transition locations, and aperture heterogeneity broadened the transition regime. The Hamaker constant mainly affected premelted-film retention at high undercooling, whereas the electrostatic parameters mainly affected the response in the low-to-moderate undercooling range.

title: Integrating NMR relaxation and formation factor for permeability estimation in heterogeneous carbonate rocks
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Behzad Ghanbarian, Silvia L.B. Bermudez, Andre Souza, Gabriel S.S. Ribeiro, Maira C.O. Lima, Paulo Couto
abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logging provides a non-destructive method for characterizing pore structure and fluid distribution in reservoir rocks. Conventional permeability models, such as the Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) and Timur–Coates (TC) equations, have been widely used to estimate permeability from NMR T2 relaxation time distributions. However, these empirical models require calibration against core-measured permeability, and their fitting coefficients often vary substantially among different lithologies and pore systems. In this study, we formulated and evaluated an NMR-informed implementation of a physically-based permeability relationship, i.e. critical path analysis (CPA), by linking the characteristic pore length scale to the dominant NMR relaxation time. We then estimated permeability ( k ) from NMR T2 distribution and formation resistivity factor ( F ) for 14 carbonate rock samples collected from the Morro do Chaves Formation in the Sergipe-Alagoas Basin, Brazil. Its predictive performance was compared against the calibrated SDR and Timur–Coates models. The proposed CPA–NMR formulation achieved an RMSLE of 0.56 for 14 carbonate samples without calibration against measured permeability from the investigated formation. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining NMR relaxation measurements with electrical formation factor for physics-based permeability estimation, although further evaluation using independent datasets is required to establish applicability across different formations and lithologies.

title: Hydroclimatic and catchment controls on drought propagation from climatic water deficits to streamflow drought: A large-sample assessment of GRDC-Caravan basins
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Ting-Yu Liang, Hongey Chen, Chih-Hsin Chang, Hsin-Chi Li, Shih-Chun Hsiao, Wei-Bo Chen
abstract: Drought propagation from climatic water deficits to streamflow drought is mediated by catchment processes, but its controls remain poorly resolved across large basin samples. We analysed 2,451 retained GRDC-Caravan basins during 1981–2020 using non-parametric three-month SPI, SPEI, and SSI. Lagged correlations quantified index coupling, event matching quantified propagation probability, onset lag, amplification, persistence, and recovery, and catchment controls were evaluated using Spearman correlations and random-forest permutation importance. Climatic and streamflow drought indices were widely positively coupled, generally at short lags. Event matching exceeded a substantial structured chance baseline: median observed propagation probability was 0.500 versus 0.375 under a calendar-preserving null model, an excess of 0.125. Under the baseline 12-month matching window, median onset lag, amplification factor, persistence ratio, and recovery lag were 3 months, 1.0, 1.10, and 4 months, respectively; the timing estimates were conditional on the matching window. Higher propagation probability was associated with wetter, more vegetated basins and lower precipitation intermittency. Longer onset delays were associated with snow influence, elevation, relative dryness, and storage, whereas persistence and recovery were more strongly related to basin scale, seasonality, surface-water storage, topography, and regulation. Random-forest importance rankings supported metric-specific within-sample controls, but spatially blocked cross-validation showed little geographic predictive skill. Streamflow drought is therefore not a direct translation of climatic drought, but a probabilistic, delayed, and catchment-conditioned response whose controls depend on the propagation metric considered.

title: DeepPolSARFlood: A dual-polarimetric SAR-Based deep learning framework for transferable flood detection
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Solmaz Khazaei Moughani, Khabat Khosravi, Liangchao Zou, Fernando Jaramillo, Carla Sofia Santos Ferreira, Jonas Olsson, Rares Halbac-Cotoară-Zamfir, Zahra Kalantari
abstract: Accurate detection of flood-affected areas from Earth observation remains challenging due to the transient nature of flooding, complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter responses, and persistent cloud cover. Many existing approaches depend on pre-/post-event change detection or manually defined thresholds, limiting operational efficiency and delaying rapid response. In addition, the generalization of deep learning–based flood models is often assessed through event-specific retraining or fine-tuning rather than direct cross-event transfer, limiting evidence for model transferability across independent flood events. To address these challenges, this study introduces DeepPolSARFlood, a systematic and transferable flood detection framework integrating dual-polarimetric Sentinel-1 SAR data, metaheuristic feature optimization, and deep learning semantic segmentation with its cross-event transferability evaluated on an independent flood event without retraining or fine-tuning. The framework was developed using a 2025 flood event in the Vilaine River basin (France) and evaluated on an independent 2025 flood in Covasna and Brașov (Romania). After SAR preprocessing and dual-polarimetric decomposition, eight metaheuristic algorithms were employed to identify the most informative PolSAR-derived features. Three segmentation architectures, U-Net, Efficient-UNet, and Nested-UNet, were developed, applied and evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, intersection over union (IoU), and balanced accuracy. Findings indicate that the Bat algorithm yielded the highest-performing feature subset, reducing the input feature set from 13 candidate features to five. On the French test subset, Nested-UNet achieved a flood-class IoU of 0.724 and an F1-score of 0.840. In the Romanian full-area evaluation, using a CEMS reference derived from Sentinel-1 imagery acquired on the same date as the model input, it achieved an IoU of 0.580, an F1-score of 0.734, and a balanced accuracy of 0.873. Overall, DeepPolSARFlood demonstrates that an optimization-driven workflow incorporating physically interpretable SAR and PolSAR features can achieve promising cross-event transferability when evaluated on a geographically independent flood event without retraining or fine-tuning, using a CEMS reference derived from Sentinel-1 imagery acquired on the same date as the model input, highlighting its potential for flood mapping in cloud-prone and data-limited regions using freely available Sentinel-1 data.

title: Asymmetric responses of water and carbon fluxes of tall and old trees to flash droughts
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Huan Tang, Zhiwen Guan, Lisheng Song, Jingfeng Xiao, Lingcheng Li, Shaomin Liu
abstract: Climate change is driving more frequent, rapid-onset flash droughts that can disrupt forest carbon uptake and water use, with potential consequences for forest resilience. How photosynthetic and transpiration responses to flash drought vary with key attributes like age and canopy height remains poorly understood. Here, we conducted a regional-scale quantitative analysis of summer flash drought responses across forests in China using multiple remote-sensing derived datasets, including gross primary productivity (GPP), transpiration, vegetation optical depth (VOD), canopy temperature, rooting depth, global solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), forest age and canopy height. Flash-drought-induced declines in GPP intensified with increasing forest age and canopy height, whereas the transpiration response exhibits a weakening-then-recovering trend, concentrating the most pronounced carbon–water decoupling in forests approximately 25–30 m tall and 85–100 years old. After accounting for climate and stand-level covariates, this pattern exhibits strong vegetation specificity, predominantly occurring in deciduous broadleaf forests. Beyond forest structural effects, contrasting associations with atmospheric and root-zone water stress highlight distinct environmental factors linked to carbon and water responses to flash drought. In these tall–old forests, although greater estimated rooting depths, higher VOD, and lower canopy temperatures are consistent with greater water buffering and canopy cooling, the decreases in SIF and water use efficiency indicate that this apparent hydrological advantage does not translate into sustained photosynthetic carbon uptake. Our findings provide insights into improving process representations in terrestrial ecosystem models to better capture forest carbon–water responses to flash droughts.

title: Autoencoder-guided flood-event classification and diffusion augmentation for event-scale flood forecasting in a data-scarce basin
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Tianzhi Wang, Ximin Yuan, Fuchang Tian, Libing Guo, Xiujie Wang
abstract: Limited flood observations cannot fully represent diverse rainfall–runoff responses, constraining data-driven forecasting. We develop an autoencoder-guided framework combining event classification, class-specific diffusion generation and sample selection for 24 h discharge forecasting. Autoencoder representations and K-means define event classes; diffusion models generate paired rainfall–discharge trajectories to train class-specific residual-block convolutional networks. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) selects the forecaster using preceding 12 h rainfall/discharge and given future 24 h rainfall, without future observed discharge. Full-trajectory classification using observed future discharge is a potentially optimistic retrospective reference. Using 25 floods from China’s Huangtai Bridge catchment, five exploratory fixed-split repetitions with 100 randomly selected synthetic events per class yield three-event macro-average Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.698 ± 0.059. Macro-average root mean square error (RMSE) decreases by 36.62% and 34.19% relative to pooled real-data training and global diffusion augmentation. Hydrological prioritization increases observational similarity but reduces sample diversity, without consistently improving forecasts. With MLP classification, leave-one-event-out testing yields mean-window NSE of 0.289 versus 0.147 for pooled training, reducing RMSE by 2.44%, although event-mean NSE improves in only 10 of 25 floods. Reference Classes II and III comprise 19 events with mean NSEs of 0.427 and 0.474. Class I, characterized by prolonged, less concentrated rainfall, averages −0.240; its low scores reflect discharge-level and trajectory errors in three events, with larger NSE penalties in low-variability windows. These results support a potential, event-dependent benefit from class-specific generation; hydrological similarity and sample quantity alone do not determine forecasting value.

title: Future meltwater dynamics and water balance components under climate warming and land use change in a cryosphere-dominated basin of the Tibetan plateau
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Kanon Guédet Guédé, Zhongbo Yu, Huiru Jiang, Xinrong Si, Ghislain Franck Emani, Ousmane Badji, Shoaib Ali
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau is warming at an accelerated rate, driving rapid cryospheric transformation and fundamentally altering the water balance of high-altitude river basins. However, the individual and combined effects of climate warming and land use/land cover (LULC) change on meltwater dynamics and water balance partitioning remain poorly quantified in cryosphere-dominated catchments. Here, we disentangle these effects in the Lhasa River Basin using the physically based Water Balance Simulation Model (WaSiM) with fully coupled snow, glacier, and permafrost modules, calibrated and validated against daily streamflow, MODIS snow cover fraction, and glacier inventory data. Future climate forcing was derived from a five-model CMIP6 ensemble under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 scenarios, and future LULC was projected using a Cellular Automata–Markov model. Our results reveal a fundamental shift in cryospheric water sources: glacier melt contribution to annual runoff rises from 3.26% (1980–2009) to 6.12% (SSP2-4.5) and 7.56% (SSP5-8.5) by 2070–2099, while snowmelt contribution declines from 12.30% to 5.73% (SSP2-4.5) and 4.10% (SSP5-8.5). Glacier melt is projected to surpass snowmelt around 2050 under SSP2-4.5 and 2040 under SSP5-8.5, marking a transition to glacier-dominated meltwater regimes. Under LULC change alone, runoff increases by 3%–6% (2030–2090), while actual evapotranspiration (AET) decreases by 4.0%–7.8% and water storage declines by 4.0%–6.7%. Climate change drives larger runoff increases of 8.4%–42.0% and AET increases of 12.5%–23.1% by 2070–2099, accompanied by water storage losses of 26.2%–48.3%. Under combined forcing, end-of-century runoff increases reach 21.6%–50.6%, AET increases are substantially attenuated to 4.3%–13.8%, and water storage losses intensify to 26.8%–49.6%. These findings demonstrate that LULC nonstationarity exerts a first-order control on future water balance trajectories and must be explicitly represented in hydrological projections for cryosphere-dominated basins across the Tibetan Plateau.

title: Precipitation frequency analysis informed by atmospheric physics: understanding and using the SMEV approach
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Francesco Marra
abstract: Precipitation frequency analysis is fundamental for hydrological risk assessment, infrastructure design, and insurance and reinsurance. The Simplified Metastatistical Extreme Value (SMEV) is an approach to precipitation frequency analysis derived from the Metastatistical Extreme Value distribution. It relies on ordinary events, rather than extremes only, providing estimates of extreme precipitation values with reduced uncertainties compared to traditional methods based on asymptotic statistics. More importantly, SMEV is an approach to precipitation frequency analysis that can be informed by atmospheric physics concepts. It is being increasingly adopted by the hydrology community for calculating extreme precipitation quantiles, for exploratory analyses of heavy precipitation climatology, and for climate change impact studies. Here, we give an overview of the physical and statistical theory underpinning the approach with the aim of framing it within the current physical and statistical understanding of extreme precipitation. We then provide guidelines for an informed use of SMEV, identifying the most common pitfalls and suggesting specific methodological steps. We close by highlighting its limitations and identifying some relevant research directions.

title: Trade-offs and synergies in multi-variable distributed hydrological model calibration in the transboundary Blue Nile Basin
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Mohammed Abdallah, Ke Zhang, Vagner Ferreira, Andrea Libertino, Ahmed Nasr
abstract: Calibration of distributed hydrological models often suffers from parameter equifinality and a lack of internal state realism, particularly in data-scarce transboundary basins. Accurate reconstruction of naturalized streamflow is essential for informed water allocation and cooperative water management in transboundary basins, yet traditional single-variable calibration approaches often fail to capture the full hydrological complexity required for reliable predictions. This study explores the trade-offs and synergies among eight calibration schemes applied to the mesoscale Hydrologic Model (mHM) in the BNB. The schemes range from a default parameterization to single-, dual-, and triple-variable calibrations that incorporate streamflow (Q), remotely sensed soil moisture (SM), and evapotranspiration (ET). Model performance is evaluated using statistical metrics, hydrological signatures, and spatial pattern efficiency indices. Results show that the default (Scheme 1) provides a reasonable baseline (median NSE = 0.72). Q-only calibration (Scheme 2) achieves high streamflow efficiency (median NSE = 0.85) but degrades internal consistency. In contrast, SM-only, ET-only, and SM + ET schemes exhibit “saturated state” errors: high temporal correlation and low RMSE with satellite products mask severe overestimations of peak flows and volumetric biases. Dual-variable schemes (Q + ET and Q + SM) partially improve internal states but retain specific shortcomings. The triple-variable scheme (Scheme 8; Q + SM + ET) delivers the most robust performance, with median NSE = 0.87 and KGE = 0.79 during the validation phase, low spatial RMSE for ET (0.19), SM (0.21), and terrestrial water storage (0.17), and best captures the observed hydrological signatures. By simultaneously constraining the model with streamflow and satellite-derived SM and ET, the triple-variable calibration provides additional constraints on parameter identification and a more physically consistent representation of the basin’s hydrology.

title: Dynamic emergency supply scheduling model for flood disasters based on reactive dispatching
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Jiaping Dong, Rui Shi, Xinyang Li, Gaoxu Wang, Yongxiang Wu
abstract: Flood disasters evolve continuously and are commonly accompanied by changing demand and the phased availability of transport capacity. Conventional fixed-interval dispatching cannot readily synchronize dispatch decisions with the actual availability of vehicles, which may result in vehicle waiting and delayed response. This study therefore proposes a dynamic emergency supply scheduling framework centered on reactive dispatching. The framework triggers a subsequent dispatch when unmet demand remains and at least one dispatchable vehicle is available, and it generates a stage-wise dispatch plan from the updated demand, inventory, vehicle, and travel-condition information at each stage. To support continuous stage-wise optimization under multi-depot, multi-shelter, multi-vehicle, and multi-commodity constraints, the framework further incorporates dynamic clustering, delivery-matrix encoding, and master–subproblem decomposition. In the baseline scenario, which uses identical disaster evolution and solution conditions and a preparation-window length of Δ t = 1 h, reactive dispatching reduces the overall dispatch completion time by 23.70% and the average vehicle waiting time by 76.38% relative to fixed-interval dispatching. These results show that reactive dispatching reduces vehicle waiting and improves continuity between scheduling stages, thereby accelerating emergency supply scheduling for flood disasters.

title: Integrating UAV and satellite remote sensing to improve spatial characterization of total organic carbon in Juzhang river
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 682 Author(s): Yahui Guo, Wei Zhou, Yufeng Gong, Yumei Li, Fanghua Hao, Xuan Zhang, Yongshuo H. Fu
abstract: Rivers are important conduits for terrestrial carbon cycling and material transport, and accurate monitoring of total organic carbon (TOC) is essential for assessing riverine water quality and identifying organic pollution. However, narrow rivers occupy only a limited number of pixels in satellite imagery and are therefore susceptible to mixed-pixel contamination from shorelines and surrounding land features. Meanwhile, TOC lacks a stable and independent spectral response, and the pronounced spatial-scale mismatch between field sampling points and satellite pixels further constrains the accuracy of conventional remote-sensing retrieval methods. To address these limitations, this study focuses on the Juzhang River and proposes a riverine TOC retrieval method that integrates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery with Sentinel-2 imagery. First, random Fourier features (RFF) were combined with a deep neural network (DNN) to develop an RFF-DNN model, thereby enhancing the representation of complex nonlinear relationships between spectral features and TOC. Subsequently, UAV imagery was used as an intermediate scale linking field sampling and satellite observations. UAV-derived TOC predictions were aggregated to generate labels for satellite-scale modeling, and the optimal resampling scheme was identified by comparing six interpolation methods across spatial resolutions from 1 to 10 m. Test-set results showed that, at the UAV scale, RFF-DNN achieved an R2 of 0.811, with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.177 mg/L and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.138 mg/L. For direct modeling between field measurements and Sentinel-2 imagery, the corresponding R2, RMSE, and MAE were 0.631, 0.440 mg/L, and 0.369 mg/L, respectively, outperforming the other comparison models overall. All six interpolation methods achieved their highest accuracy at a 2 m resolution, with cubic B-spline interpolation combined with RFF-DNN performing best, yielding a test-set R2 of 0.903 and an R2 of 0.712 when validated against field-measured TOC concentrations, exceeding the test-set R2 of 0.631 obtained by directly modeling TOC from field measurements and Sentinel-2 imagery. The resulting 2 m TOC distribution preserved the overall concentration level of each river reach while enhancing the representation of local gradients and spatial texture within the channel.
