The results place H. depressa within the broader tropicalization of Mediterranean biota, in which warming relaxes cold-season barriers for thermophilic taxa while increasing summer heat stress at the warm end of their thermal niche.

title: Projected climate warming reduces occurrence probability of the imperiled Athabasca rainbow trout
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Science of The Total Environment, Volume 1058 Author(s): Lee Frank Gordon Gutowsky, Tyana Ashlie Rudolfsen
abstract: Freshwater salmonids often occupy narrow ecological niches defined by tight physiological constraints, limited dispersal pathways, and strong dependence on local habitat conditions. As climate warming, land use, and habitat fragmentation reshape riverine environments, many species may shift distributions or experience population declines, creating species-specific conservation challenges. We integrated two decades of Athabasca rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) inventory data from Alberta, Canada, with geomorphic and anthropogenic predictors in a gradient boosting species distribution model and projected occurrence probabilities under moderate and high future air-temperature scenarios while holding non-climatic predictors constant. Mean August air temperature had the greatest relative influence in the final model, and fitted occurrence probability was highest across an intermediate range of about 12–15 °C. Mean predicted occurrence probability across the stream network declined from 0.205 under current conditions to 0.107–0.068 under future air-temperature scenarios, equivalent to reductions of 47.7–66.9%. Although 54.8–97.4% of future stream-network sampling points fell outside at least one predictor range represented in the training data, increasing uncertainty in the magnitude and spatial distribution of projected change, the direction of change was consistent across all scenarios. These declines are projected across a landscape also characterized by roads and watercourse crossings, highlighting potential conservation conflicts where recovery objectives intersect with ongoing land use. These conditional projections provide a spatially explicit basis for prioritizing monitoring and conservation planning where climate-associated declines and existing landscape pressures coincide.

title: Recycling of terrestrial mercury in the Sumatra subduction zone: constraints from Hg-Sr-Nd-B isotope systematics
description: Publication date: 1 January 2027 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 436 Author(s): Dian-Bing Wang, Ping-Ping Liu, Runsheng Yin
abstract: Mercury (Hg) isotopes, particularly mass-independent fractionation (MIF; expressed as Δ199Hg), serve as a powerful tracer for tracking the recycling of surficial materials into Earth’s deep interior. However, the contribution of terrestrial Hg to modern subduction zones remains poorly understood. Here we present new Hg–B–Sr–Nd isotopic data for volcanic rocks from 8 stratovolcanoes as well as the Toba super-volcanic system, all located along the Sumatra segment of the Sunda arc. All the Sumatra volcanic rocks have negative Δ199Hg values (from −0.19 to −0.02‰), indicating an input of terrestrial Hg. Their mass-dependent fractionation (MDF; expressed as δ202Hg) ranges from −2.08 to −1.07‰, lower than that of the Mesozoic basement of Sumatra (−0.05‰). Together with Sr-Nd isotope constraints indicating minor crustal contamination, these observations rule out a crustal origin for the negative Δ199Hg anomalies and instead reflect a mantle source modified by recycled terrestrial Hg. The Δ199Hg values of the Nicobar Fan sediments (−0.01 to 0.03‰) indicate that the recycled terrestrial Hg in the mantle source of the Sumatra volcanic rocks is unlikely to originate from addition of the Nicobar Fan sediments, but more likely reflects locally derived Sumatran terrigenous sediments. Three-endmember mixing models coupling Δ199Hg with Sr–Nd isotopes further indicate that the contribution of the subducted sediments was dominantly sourced from the Nicobar Fan, with a small proportion of Sumatra terrigenous components carrying the negative Hg-MIF signature, with total sediment additions of <5 wt% beneath the Sumatra stratovolcanoes and ∼5–10 wt% beneath the Toba volcanic system. Boron isotopes indicate slab-derived fluid additions of ∼0.01–1.0 wt% and ∼0.01–0.05 wt% beneath Sumatra stratovolcanoes and the Toba volcanic system, respectively. Mass-balance calculations show that fluids containing ∼20 ppb to 3.3 ppm Hg could reproduce the average Δ199Hg values of the Sumatra volcanic rocks, indicating that slab-derived dehydration fluids are potential carriers transferring terrestrial Hg into the mantle wedge. Near the slab tear zone, sediment melts generated during the diapiric ascent and partial melting of subducted sediments result in the enriched Sr-Nd isotopic compositions of the Toba volcanic rocks. Our results demonstrate that Hg isotopes, when integrated with Sr-Nd-B isotope systematics, serve as a sensitive tracer for distinguishing the recycling of various components in subduction zones.

title: Redox states of the open ocean during the early Ediacaran and Cambrian Ages 1–3: constraints from vanadium isotopes
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): Pei-Shan Sui, Wei Wei, Shao-Bing Zhang, Guang-Yi Wei, Yan-Yan Zhao, Tianchen He, Hong-Fei Ling, Fang Huang
abstract: The early Ediacaran and Cambrian Ages 1–3 witnessed multiphase biological innovations, in which oceanic oxygenation may have played crucial roles. However, detailed marine redox states during this period remain highly debated. Sedimentary vanadium (V) isotope geochemistry is an emerging redox proxy for tracing changes in global marine redox state. Here, we report leachate V isotope compositions (δ51Vleach) of black shales from the lower Ediacaran and Cambrian Stages 1–3 successions in the Yangtze Block, South China. The δ51Vleach variability in the lower Ediacaran succession was caused by changes in local V drawdown efficiency, while that of the Cambrian Stages 1–3 was mainly derived from the open-ocean seawater δ51V (δ51VOSW) variation in response to global marine redox change. Based on these sedimentary δ51Vleach records, we reconstructed temporal δ51VOSW variations during the early Ediacaran and Cambrian Ages 1–3. During the early Ediacaran, the δ51VOSW value (–0.45 ± 0.06‰) is significantly lower than the modern value, and then increases during the Cambrian Ages 1–3, eventually reaching the modern value with an average of 0.26 ± 0.33‰ at ca. 521 Ma. Model-based estimates suggest that the open ocean of the early Ediacaran (ca. 594–582 Ma) may have been extensively euxinic, where early organisms could have survived due to the low oxygen requirements for basic metabolism or local oceanic oxygenation. The oxygenation extent of the open ocean during the Cambrian Ages 1–3 (ca. 539–514 Ma) should have significantly increased, possibly approaching modern-like value under our preferred model assumptions at ca. 521 Ma, which may have promoted the first appearance and radiation of skeletal metazoans and the subsequent Cambrian Explosion.

title: Comparative study of anoxic dissolution of arsenopyrite, loellingite, and pyrite: Crystal structural controls on interfacial reactivity
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): Pei Chang, Xiangyu Zhu, Minghao Tang, Jianchao Zhang, Xiancai Lu, Cong-qiang Liu, H. Henry Teng
abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and redox reactions at mineral–water interfaces fundamentally govern trace metal mobility and geochemical cycles in O2-limited environment. However, predicting how interfacial reactivity and ROS generation shift across compositionally related dichalcogenide minerals, driven by varying anionic frameworks and crystal structures, remains unresolved. Here, we systematically investigated the anoxic dissolution of pyrite, arsenopyrite, and loellingite under varying pH conditions by integrating aqueous H2O2 quantification, macroscopic dissolution kinetics, and surface-sensitive analyses (XPS and zeta potential). We propose that in sulfide-bearing minerals (pyrite and arsenopyrite), alkaline conditions actively promote H2O2 generation, which suppress the passivating effect from nascent Fe(III)-O layers and accelerates dissolution. In contrast, sulfide-deficient loellingite exhibits suppressed H2O2 accumulation and decelerated arsenic release under alkaline conditions due to the formation of a stable Fe(III)-O protective layer. This divergence may reflect loellingite’s narrow band gap and polarizable electronic framework, which together with its edge-sharing structure, may facilitate internal charge redistribution that quenches surface ·OH before H2O2 formation. These findings provide a fundamental physical–chemical framework linking bulk crystal geometry to interfacial ROS dynamics, offering critical insights for predicting mineral-specific dissolution behavior and arsenic mobility in anoxic subsurface systems.

title: N and O isotope fractionation reveals distinct pathways of dissimilatory nitrite reduction to ammonium
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): Guojun Chen, Qinqin Hao, Yan Ru, Andreas Kappler, Raymond Jianxiong Zeng, Xiaomin Li, Zebin Hong, Fanghua Liu, Fujun Yue, Shiwen Hu, Tongxu Liu
abstract: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) is a major pathway of nitrogen (N) retention, yet its isotope systematics remain poorly constrained. Although DNRA and denitrification (DNF) share the same nitrate reductases, they diverge fundamentally at the nitrite reduction step, which represents the key biochemical distinction between N retention and N loss. Understanding N and oxygen (O) isotope fractionation during nitrite reduction is therefore critical for constraining isotopic signatures associated with DNRA pathways. This study systematically investigates dual N and O isotope fractionation associated with fermentative and respiratory DNRA pathways mediated by key nitrite reductases. Using pure-culture experiments spanning cytoplasmic (NirB) and periplasmic (NrfA-based) DNRA pathways, together with a mechanistic kinetic model, we demonstrate that different DNRA pathways generate characteristic and distinguishable N and O isotopic fingerprints. NirB-based fermentative DNRA showed a ratio of the O- and N-isotope effects (the 18 ε:15 ε ratio) of 0.45 ± 0.05, while NrfA-type respiratory DNRA exhibited a ratio of 1.15 ± 0.75. In contrast, multi-subunit NrfA-NrfH and NrfA-NrfB systems displayed negative 18 ε:15 ε ratios (−0.23 ± 0.30 and − 0.25 ± 0.09, respectively), indicating inverse O isotope fractionation linked to complex electron transfer mechanisms. These characteristic isotopic signatures provide a quantitative framework for identifying previously uncharacterized DNRA pathways in biogeochemical N cycling.

title: A continuum formulation for nano-scale mineral dissolution with stepwave-driven surface dynamics
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): M. Starnoni, C. Recalcati, M. Riva, X. Sanchez-Vila, A. Guadagnini
abstract: We develop a continuum-scale framework to describe the evolution of dissolving mineral surfaces directly from nano-scale observations. Quantitative interpretation of mineral dissolution remains challenging because surface evolution arises from coupled actions of terrace retreat and crystallographically controlled step propagation, resulting in experimentally observed surface morphologies that are inherently heterogeneous and dynamic. We represent the fluid-mineral interface as a moving surface whose velocity is decomposed into normal and tangential components associated with terrace retreat and lateral step propagation, respectively. Uncertainty in the corresponding model parameters is quantified through a stochastic Monte Carlo inverse-modeling framework constrained by real-time Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) observations. The approach is applied to the analysis of dissolution of a calcite crystal monitored through time-resolved AFM imaging. Simulations can reproduce the key statistical and spatial characteristics of the evolving surface and the distribution of reaction rates. Inferred parameter distributions reveal a systematic increase in tangential step-propagation velocities during dissolution, highlighting the increasing contribution of lateral step migration to surface evolution. Our formulation is consistent with the established conceptual picture of stepwave-driven surface dynamics and observed surface evolution, and provides a quantitative and physically interpretable link between nano-scale surface morphology and the effective processes governing mineral dissolution.

title: Species-specific strontium distribution and environment in coccolithophores revealed by X-ray fluorescence and spectroscopy
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): Hallam J.M. Greene, Jessica M. Walker, Gerald Langer
abstract: The Sr/Ca ratio of coccoliths is the most developed coccolithophore-related geochemical proxy; used to reconstruct coccolithophore productivity. A process-based understanding of this proxy is limited, because Sr partitioning models are mostly not independently constrained. It has recently been discovered that the lopadoliths of Scyphosphaera apsteinii display stripes of different Sr concentrations, contrary to model predictions. In this study we use XRF imaging to investigate the distribution of Sr across coccoliths from different coccolithophore families. We measured coccoliths from two Coccolithales species, Coccolithus braarudii and Calcidiscus leptoporus, and two Zygodiscales, Pontosphaera syracusana and Helicosphaera carteri. Only P. syracusana showed Sr stripes akin to the ones in S. apsteinii. Thus, we hypothesize that Sr stripiness is an invention of the Pontosphaeraceae. This family produces high Sr muroliths, whereas the other species investigated here produce comparatively low Sr placoliths. All species investigated so far, however, incorporate Sr into Ca sites of the calcite lattice in coccolith calcite, as opposed to other inorganic or organic phases, as evidenced by XANES. We conclude that the Pontosphaeraceae feature a more complex calcification mechanism than placolith bearing species, including time-dependent Sr partitioning, a process that is not captured by our current models.

title: Volcanically driven redox stratification and N–S–C cycling perturbation in a Late Triassic lacustrine system: controls on carbon sequestration efficiency
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): Xianxu Fang, Kelai Xi, Yingchang Cao, Xiujuan Wang, Guanghui Yuan, Yuan You, Miruo Lin, Ke Li, Chao Liang, Keyu Liu, Fang Hao
abstract: Water-column redox structure fundamentally governs ecosystem dynamics, biogeochemical cycling, and ultimately sedimentary responses. Redox stratification recorded in deep-time organic-rich lacustrine shales was frequently perturbed by geological events, particularly volcanism, which enhanced deoxygenation and nutrient loading under recurrent volcanic inputs. However, the biogeochemical pathways by which ecological stress developed and persisted remain poorly constrained. Here we investigate the Upper Triassic Chang 73 Sub-member of the Yanchang Formation in the Ordos Basin, a continuous succession of organic-rich lacustrine shales deposited under episodic volcanic influence. Integrating sedimentological, paleontological and multi-proxy geochemical records, we reconstruct the vertical redox structure of the paleolake and assess its response to contrasting volcanic input fluxes. Our results reveal a stable three-layer redox stratification (oxic, suboxic, and euxinic) that couples nitrogen–sulfur–carbon biogeochemical cycling via a cascade of aerobic respiration, denitrification, anammox, Fe–Mn reduction, and sulfate reduction. Positive δ15Norg values provide direct evidence for a chemocline that restricts denitrification and anammox to the suboxic layer without interference from sulfate reduction below. As volcanic input flux increased from low to high, δ13Corg shifted from negative excursions reflecting internal recycling of 12C to positive excursions driven by Rayleigh fractionation. This shift marks the transition from weakened to efficient carbon sequestration. These contrasting redox states demonstrate that volcanic forcing regulated carbon sequestration through nutrient fertilization that elevated primary productivity, but it was the integrity of redox stratification that ultimately determined carbon burial efficiency. Accordingly, we develop an integrated redox‑ecological model linking the strength of external volcanic forcing, the feedbacks of internal biogeochemical cycling, and the efficiency of lacustrine carbon sequestration into a coherent system. This model provides a process-based explanation of how this integrity mediates ecological stress and governs carbon sequestration efficiency. Drawing on this deep-time eutrophic lake system, this study identifies critical redox thresholds governing ecosystem responses to nutrient enrichment and deoxygenation in modern lakes.

title: Nanoscale mechanisms of mesocrystal formation during non-classical heterogeneous growth of manganese (hydr)oxides on ferrihydrite
description: Publication date: 15 December 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 435 Author(s): Yixuan Yang, Qingze Chen, Chi Zhang, Haozhe Ma, Jing Liu, Jianxi Zhu, Runliang Zhu, Hongping He
abstract: Crystallization by particle attachment (CPA) is an important non-classical pathway of mineral growth that often produces mesocrystals composed of aligned nanoparticles, whose internal interfaces and defects can impart distinctive geochemical reactivity. Given that mineral nucleation and growth in nature commonly occur on pre-existing substrates, a key yet underexplored question is how CPA-mediated mesocrystal growth operates at such heterogeneous interfaces. Herein, we investigated the heterogeneous oxidation of aqueous Mn(II) on ferrihydrite, with a specific focus on the formation of manganese (Mn) (hydr)oxides mesocrystals via CPA. Our results show that Mn (hydr)oxides formed on ferrihydrite grew via oriented assembly into mesocrystalline nanowires. Specifically, Mn (hydr)oxide nanoparticles assembled via end-to-end or side-by-side manners to elongate or widen nanowires, respectively. Misorientations among component nanoparticles led to curved nanowires, whereas straight nanowires resulted from well-aligned interfaces. Mn (hydr)oxide nanoparticles with different crystallographic orientations, and even different mineral phases, can assemble into mesocrystalline nanowires featuring misoriented but crystallographically correlated interfaces. This assembly is rationalized by approximate lattice correspondence at particle junctions and further supported by molecular dynamics simulations revealing energetically favorable interfacial configurations. The assembly of Mn (hydr)oxide nanoparticles was likely initiated by their detachment from ferrihydrite surfaces, driven by the accumulation and release of stress and strain at mismatched Mn (hydr)oxide-ferrihydrite interfaces. Revealing numerous new atomic details of Mn (hydr)oxide CPA, our study links the assembly behaviors of Mn (hydr)oxide nanoparticles to the development of their mesocrystalline structures. We also integrate our new findings with previous studies and synthesize the mechanisms by which different mineral substrates regulate CPA of Mn (hydr)oxides. These findings advance the understanding of heterogeneous growth of Mn (hydr)oxides on iron (hydr)oxides at the nanoscale and contribute to a more integrated view of coupled Mn-Fe cycling in the environment. Our study also highlights the critical roles of substrate mineral surfaces in non-classical mineral growth.

title: Three-dimensional quantification of Ryugu matrix properties and constraints on aqueous alteration heterogeneity
description: Publication date: Available online 26 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Mingqi Sun, Akira Tsuchiyama, Junya Matsuno, Megumi Matsumoto, Masahiro Yasutake, Tomoki Nakamura, Takaaki Noguchi, Akira Miyake, Kentaro Uesugi, Akihisa Takeuchi, Yuri Fujioka, Tomoyo Morita, Shota Okumura, Itaru Mitsukawa, Stefano Rubino, Zelia Dionnet, Alice Aléon-Toppani, Rosario Brunetto, Aki Takigawa, Toru Matsumoto
abstract: Samples returned from asteroid (162173) Ryugu by the Hayabusa2 spacecraft resemble Ivuna-type carbonaceous (CI) chondrites and record extensive aqueous alteration. We analyzed fine Ryugu particles (10–165 µm) using synchrotron radiation X-ray nanotomography (XnCT) with an effective spatial resolution of ∼200 nm, and developed three-dimensional peak analysis (3DPA) to estimate matrix Fe/Mg ratio (Mg#), density, and porosity from peak positions in three-dimensional histograms of XnCT data. This method enables nondestructive characterization of phyllosilicate-dominated matrices containing sub-resolution pores, organic matter, and Fe(–Ni) sulfides. Application of 3DPA to 69 Ryugu particles identified a dominant main group (N = 64) and a minor Fe-rich group (N = 5). The main group has Mg# = 0.84 ± 0.04, density = 1.80 ± 0.23 g/cm3, and porosity = 0.32 ± 0.09, and can be subdivided into high-porosity/low-density (HP-LD) and low-porosity/high-density (LP-HD) subgroups. Comparison with RGB-CT images and previous TEM studies indicates that HP-LD and LP-HD domains are >∼10 µm-scale regions containing different proportions of nanosulfide-rich fine-grained matrix and nanosulfide-poor coarser-grained matrix. These observations reveal multi-scale matrix heterogeneity in Ryugu, from nanoscale to micrometer-scale variations in matrix texture and sulfide abundance to >∼10 µm-scale variations in matrix density and porosity. The HP-LD and LP-HD domains likely record relatively lower and higher degrees of aqueous alteration, respectively, most plausibly reflecting heterogeneity inherited from the accretion of GEMS-like material and ice. The Fe-rich group probably represents compositionally distinct, less-altered clasts incorporated through impact-induced mixing associated with brecciation. CI chondrites are most similar to the Ryugu LP-HD subgroup, suggesting that currently available CI chondrites may preferentially represent relatively more altered materials. In contrast, the Ryugu HP-LD subgroup may represent a more primitive and/or less aqueously altered component that is not represented among CI chondrites available in terrestrial collections.

title: Potassium isotopes reveal the primary role of anatectic fluid regime in leucogranite genesis
description: Publication date: Available online 26 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): You-Shan Xia, Peng Gao, William J. Collins, Hai-Ou Gu, Zi-Fu Zhao
abstract: Leucogranites are crucial for understanding crustal differentiation and rare-metal mineralization, yet the relative roles of source melting and subsequent magmatic evolution in generating their chemical compositions remain debated. Recent studies link potassium (K) isotope fractionation in high‑silica magmas to fractional crystallization of Na‑rich feldspars, as observed along the evolutionary sequence from two‑mica to muscovite leucogranites. However, resolvable K isotope variations are also observed among two-mica leucogranites, which are generally considered to represent the less evolved products. Such variations may arise from multiple geological processes, including source heterogeneity and inherited weathering signatures, isotope fractionation during crustal anatexis, and post-melting processes such as magma crystallization and fluid exsolution. The relative contributions of these processes to the K isotope compositions of two-mica leucogranites remain unclear. Here, we integrate new K isotope data from Himalayan two‑mica leucogranites with published regional data. The compiled dataset shows significant K isotope variation that correlates strongly with key element ratios (e.g., K/Rb, Ba/Rb, Rb/Sr, Nb/Ta and Zr/Hf ratios). Geochemical index and modeling results indicate that source heterogeneity and post-melting processes (such as fractional crystallization and fluid exsolution) cannot adequately explain the observed covariation trends. In addition, the compiled dataset exhibits a relatively restricted range of εNd(t) values (–12.9 to –15.0), whereas (87Sr/86Sr)i ratios vary widely (0.718127–0.756453) and are negatively correlated with δ41K values. Such coupled variations cannot be reconciled with closed-system fractional crystallization and instead point to melting processes associated with addition of external fluid and differential breakdown of micas and feldspars during crustal anatexis. The addition of externally derived fluids with relatively heavy K isotope compositions modifies the K isotope composition of the source and, by increasing H2O availability during anatexis, alters the relative breakdown of micas and feldspars as well as the solubility and partitioning behavior of accessory minerals. These results demonstrate that K isotopes can serve as a powerful tracer of fluid regimes during crustal anatexis. Moreover, by controlling the extent of mica breakdown, the anatectic fluid regime regulates the initial rare-metal budget of granitic melts, thereby establishing the pre-enrichment conditions required for further rare-metal concentration and mineralization during subsequent magmatic evolution.

title: Constraining the effects of source regions and parent-body processes on soluble organic matter in carbonaceous chondrites
description: Publication date: Available online 25 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Mingtan Dong, Wei Yang, Yamei Li, Li Quan, H.G. Changela, Siyu Li, Sen Hu, Yangting Lin
abstract: Soluble organic matter (SOM) in carbonaceous chondrites preserves a molecular record of early Solar System chemical evolution and represents a plausible source of prebiotic molecules delivered to the early Earth. There is a broad consensus that the evolution of SOM was influenced by two primary factors: source-region heterogeneity and parent-body processes. However, it remains unclear how to distinguish the respective influences of these factors. Here, we applied an omics-style workflow based on untargeted ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (UHPLC–HRMS) with positive-ion electrospray ionization [ESI(+)] for comparative molecular profiling of methanol-extractable SOM in nine carbonaceous chondrites spanning CI1, C2-ung, and CM. This approach enabled systematic comparison of molecular composition, relative intensity patterns, and structure-related signatures to investigate the contributions of source-region heterogeneity and parent-body aqueous alteration to SOM diversity. UHPLC–HRMS analysis revealed diverse families of N- and N,O-bearing heterocycles together with organosulfur compounds, while feature-based molecular networking showed modular connectivity among these families through regular mass-difference relationships and similarity between tandem mass spectra (MS/MS). Multivariate analyses further revealed pronounced separation in SOM chemical space among CI1, C2-ung, and CM chondrites. In general, CM2 chondrites exhibited cumulative ESI(+) responses approximately 2–3 times those of the CI1 chondrites and Tarda (C2-ung). Tarda showed relatively higher intensities of alkyl anilines, whereas alkyl pyridines predominated in the ESI(+) responses of CM and CI1 chondrites, highlighting differences in isomer distributions among chondrite groups. Within the CM chondrites, more heavily altered samples (e.g., Winchcombe) showed relatively stronger responses from N-heterocycles with high double bond equivalent (DBE) values and weaker responses from low-DBE N-heterocycles than less altered samples (e.g., Murchison), consistent with progressive condensation and aromatization during aqueous alteration. The association between DBE-dependent N-heterocycle redistribution and bulk Fe valence is consistent with a possible redox link between SOM dehydrogenation and Fe reduction during aqueous alteration. Together, these results provide a comparative framework for evaluating the overlapping contributions of source-region heterogeneity and parent-body processing to SOM evolution. Differences in heteroatom composition, cumulative ESI(+) response, and isomer-family distributions among the analyzed chondrite groups may retain signatures of source-region heterogeneity, whereas DBE-dependent shifts within chondrites point to molecular restructuring associated with parent-body aqueous alteration.

title: Exploring the sensitivity of the vanadium redox proxy to Fe/Mn-(oxyhydr)oxide cycling in a basinal oxic margin setting
description: Publication date: Available online 22 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Nicol D. Udy, Sune G. Nielsen, Maureen Auro, Kasper P. Olesen, Donald E. Canfield
abstract: Vanadium (V) is a promising redox proxy sensitive to the distribution and areal extent of hydrothermal, anoxic, anoxic-sulfidic, and oxic conditions in the ocean. Paleo-redox reconstructions using V rely on observations of V behavior in the modern ocean, across the four depositional contexts highlighted above. Since these reconstructions are dependent on modern marine V data, our understanding of the redox state of the ancient ocean may change if unconsidered V sinks are identified on the modern Earth surface. In the modern ocean, ferromanganese (oxyhydr)oxides accumulating on the pelagic seabed are expected to constitute the largest V sink. The prominence of this oxic sink is expected to decrease when ocean anoxia expands or hydrothermal fluid flux rate increase, because rates of V removal are, on average, 2x and 10x slower from normal oxic seawater than from anoxic and hydrothermally altered seawater, respectively. Decreasing the prominence of the oxic V sink is, in turn, predicted to decrease the δ51V value of seawater (where δ51V = 1000 ‰ * [(51V/50VSample – 51V/50VAlfa-aesar)/(51V/50VAlfa-aesar)]), as the relatively large authigenic δ51V offset of −1.1 ‰ from seawater typically observed in oxic sediments should promote a higher δ51V in seawater than the comparably small offsets of −0.7 ‰ observed for anoxic sediments, and of −0.6 to −0.3 ‰ observed for hydrothermal sediments. Typically, sediments on the oxic continental margin (OCM) reproduce the low V enrichments and large δ51V offsets of the pelagic seafloor. However, recent studies have found high V enrichments on some portions of the OCM independent of anoxia or hydrothermal activity. These findings suggest that non-hydrothermal mechanisms may result in efficient V sinks in modern and ancient oxic settings. To establish the importance of the V-enriched OCM to global V cycling, we first must identify the mechanisms leading to high V enrichments on the OCM, and themagnitude of associated δ51V offsets from seawater. In this study, we explore V enrichment mechanisms and report δ51V values from V-enriched sediments collected from the oxic Skagerrak seaway. Elemental concentrations were measured from porewaters and sequentially extracted sediment solids. Sequential extractions followed a novel method that distinguishes between V bound to Fe- and Mn- (oxyhydr)oxides. Vanadium sequestration rates into the sediments of the deep Skagerrak basin are at least 10x higher than rates reported from typical OCM sediments. The high rates of authigenic V delivery onto the Skagerrak seafloor is primarily driven by an Fe-(oxyhydr)oxide sink, linearly increasing in magnitude from shelf → basin. This primary Fe-driven V sink reproduces the the typical V-(oxyhydr)oxide isotopic fractionation factor of −1.1 ‰. Additionally, in the deep basin sediments of the Skagerrak, there is a secondary V enrichment likely associated with a diagenetic Mn-oxide sink. Deep basin top-sediments, which are hyper-enriched in Mn-oxide, also display a unique authigenic V isotope fractionation relative to seawater <−0.9 ‰, significantly deviating from what is typically expected from OCM settings. Our results suggest that Fe and Mn dynamics, as impacted by basin hydrography, variably control V enrichment and δ51V patterns.

title: Magnesium isotopes reveal diverse clay-water interfacial processes shaping hydrochemical evolution
description: Publication date: Available online 21 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Rui Wang, Xiao-Wei Jiang, John Cherry, Tao-Tao Ji, Ying Tan, Longfei Gou, Guilin Han, Li Wan, Huaming Guo, Zhangdong Jin
abstract: Magnesium (Mg) isotopes are widely used to trace chemical weathering, but processes like cation exchange and surface complexation can disturb weathering signals. It remains challenging to disentangle these clay-water interfacial processes in Mg uptake and isotope fractionation. Here we integrate Mg-Sr isotopes, age tracers (3H and 14C) and hydrochemical data to identify, sequence, and quantify these processes in a sandstone aquifer in the Ordos Basin, NW China. In modern groundwater (age 8,000 years) with pH > 8.40 from the deep part of the discharge area (group DG2), the trend of increasing δ26Mg accompanying Mg uptake is explained by superposition of 24Mg-preferring cation exchange onto surface complexation, and quantitative calculation reveals that surface complexation dominates over cation exchange in removing Mg. By revealing pH-dependent interfacial processes driving Mg isotope fractionation, this study offers new insights into subsurface Mg cycling, and has implications for magnesium isotope budget of the modern ocean

title: Oued Chebeika 002 at the nanoscale: microstructures, composition and comparison with CI-like materials
description: Publication date: Available online 20 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Roberto Conconi, Corentin Le Guillou, Sophie Meuret, Valentine Megevand, Adrien Teurtrie, Sylvain Laforet, Maya Marinova, Hugues Leroux
abstract: Oued Chebeika 002, a CI (Ivuna-type) carbonaceous chondrite recovered in the Moroccan desert in 2024, represents one of the rarest and most pristine samples available to investigate early Solar System processes. In this study, we present a comprehensive nanoscale characterization of the main components of Oued Chebeika 002 (i.e. phyllosilicates, sulfides, magnetite, and carbonates) using transmission electron microscopy, with the aim of resolving its submicrometric mineralogical heterogeneity, constraining the physicochemical conditions of aqueous alteration on its parent body, and comparing these features with those observed in other CI chondrites and samples returned from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu. Our observations reveal a complex mineral assemblage dominated by phyllosilicates intimately associated with Fe-sulfides, magnetite, and carbonates. Overall, the mineral assemblage closely resembles those of CI chondrites and samples from Ryugu and Bennu, suggesting that aqueous alteration processes were broadly similar across their parent body(ies). In particular, the occurrence of dolomite is consistent with precipitation from brines, while its compositional zoning and complex microstructures, including mottled and ribbon-like textures, suggest formation through metastable precursors and subsequent dissolution–reprecipitation and re-equilibration processes. Magnetite spherulites and spherules likewise record distinct non-equilibrium processes. The former is characterized by a radiating microstructure and likely formed through a non-classical crystallization pathway from supersaturated solutions, whereas the latter displays surface etch pits indicative of dissolution. Taken together, the microstructural characteristics of both carbonate and magnetite are indicative of formation and alteration under dynamic, non-equilibrium conditions, highlighting the evolving nature of aqueous solutions in CI parent body(ies).

title: Mineral-specific ligand and redox dynamics of adsorbed platinum: pathway-dependent mobility during terrestrial weathering
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Emily G. Wright, Fernanda M. Loza, Elaine D. Flynn, Jeffrey G. Catalano
abstract: Weathering zones developed above ultramafic rocks, such as oxidized ores, soils, and laterites, concentrate the critical mineral platinum and represent a promising future resource. Prior work has documented Pt accumulation in these zones, including its common association with iron oxides. However, the fundamental mechanisms that control Pt retention versus mobilization during weathering are not well understood, inhibiting resource prediction and our knowledge of Pt environmental behavior. Dissolved platinum is predominantly complexed by chloride and ammonia in surficial waters, but the influence of these environmental ligands on Pt mobilization versus retention by mineral surfaces is currently unclear. We studied how Pt(II) aqueous speciation controls adsorption to hematite and goethite, which typically dominate the reactive mineralogy of laterites, from pH 4 to 8 and for reaction times up to 113 days. Initial speciation is the primary control on the fate of Pt, with slow ligand exchange kinetics inhibiting chemical transformations in solution even when far from equilibrium. Platinum(II)-ammine species are kinetically inert and do not appreciably adsorb to either mineral, even after several months. In contrast, Pt(II)-chloro species readily interact with both mineral surfaces. These dissolved species likely slowly convert to Pt(II)-hydroxo species in solution, further enhancing adsorption. Thus, while chloride ligands mobilize a portion of the adsorbed platinum pool, Pt(II)-ammine complexes are highly mobile and fully unreactive with iron oxide surfaces. Weathering systems hosting active biogeochemical nitrogen cycling or organic matter mineralization may thus strongly mobilize Pt. X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicates that ternary Pt(II)-chloro surface complexes form on both hematite and goethite. Over time, these adsorbed species oxidize and undergo hydrolysis on the hematite surface, but resist redox transformations on goethite. These variations indicate that Pt surface speciation will differ substantially among weathering zones under different climate regimes, which dictate iron oxide mineralogy. Surface-mediated oxidation to Pt(IV), which occurs only in hematite-rich weathering zones, will further inhibit mineral-fluid reactions of platinum due to slower ligand exchange rates for Pt(IV) versus Pt(II) species. Such kinetic inhibition of platinum geochemical reactions will create persistent disequilibrium and result in spatially heterogeneous retention of this critical mineral at the pore scale that varies with fluid residence time.

title: Best Bulk Bennu (B 3 ): elemental compositions of aggregate samples from asteroid Bennu
description: Publication date: Available online 19 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kun Wang (王昆), Katharina Lodders, Piers Koefoed, Megan Broussard, Josh Wimpenny, Jan Render, Quinn R. Shollenberger, Thomas S. Kruijer, Gregory A. Brennecka, Marghaleray Amini, Vivian Lai, Dominique Weis, Kees C. Welten, Kunihiko Nishiizumi, Daniel P. Glavin, Jason P. Dworkin, Conel M.O’D. Alexander, Dionysis I. Foustoukos, Jean-Alix Barrat, Pierre Haenecour
abstract: Ivuna-type (CI) carbonaceous chondrites have long served as proxies for the bulk Solar System composition due to their close agreement with solar photospheric abundances and enrichment in volatile elements relative to other chondrite classes. However, CI chondrites have been subject to terrestrial alteration, which may have modified their original mineralogies and redistributed aqueously mobile elements. NASA’s OSIRIS-REx mission delivered pristine material from the carbonaceous asteroid Bennu, and initial analyses revealed close compositional similarities with CI chondrites. This provides a valuable opportunity to refine estimates of the bulk Solar System composition. We report concentrations of 63 elements in aggregate (bulk, unsorted) Bennu material (representing a combined mass of ∼ 8 g) analyzed across four laboratories. Within analytical uncertainties, we find no statistically significant differences among aliquots of two aggregate samples that were homogenized into powders, or among subsamples (including two previously reported) of a non-homogenized aggregate sample. Nor do we find measurable variations among sample masses ranging from tens of milligrams to several grams. These findings indicate that the material returned from Bennu is well mixed at the aggregate scale. Combining all of the data, we derive an average bulk elemental composition that we term Best Bulk Bennu (B3). Comparison of B3 with an average CI chondrite composition shows excellent agreement within analytical uncertainties, confirming that terrestrial alteration of CI chondrites is effectively isochemical for non-highly volatile elements. B3 and the CI chondrite average composition compare similarly to the solar photospheric composition. Our findings suggest that both CI meteorites and returned samples of carbonaceous asteroids are the best available materials for estimating the bulk Solar System composition of non-highly volatile elements.

title: Triple oxygen isotopes in precipitation reveal kinetic isotopic fractionation driven by turbulence in atmospheric river storms
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Erik J.H. Oerter, Jory Lerback, Jake Harm, Rebecca J. Lazarus, Ate Visser
abstract: Atmospheric river (AR) storms are outsized in their hydrologic importance, especially along continental coastal environments. A better understanding of the physical processes occurring during precipitation generation will improve predictive capabilities of precipitation forecasts. The triple oxygen isotopic composition of precipitation is a useful tracer of the physical processes affecting precipitation because the derived Δ′17O parameter can help distinguish between equilibrium isotope exchange and kinetic fractionation. While the effects of kinetic fractionation have been interpreted from deuterium-excess (d-excess) values, this effect in d-excess is temperature dependent. Because Δ′17O values are relatively insensitive to temperature, the effects of kinetic fractionation are more easily interpretable from the Δ′17O values. Together, the coupled use of both Δ′17O and d-excess values provides complementary information. We collected precipitation at ∼1 hr intervals during a very strong land-falling AR event in mid-latitude west-coast North America, and analyzed these samples for δ2H, δ17O, δ18O, d-excess, and Δ′17O values. We observed a distinct V-shaped pattern (decrease followed by increase) of Δ′17O values through the storm progression, whereas δ2H, δ18O, and d-excess values produced an L-shaped pattern (decrease with no increase). We put these storm data into the context of daily precipitation samples collected at the same site over a 5 year period. Along with complementary meteorological data and analyses, we determined that post-condensation evaporation and re-condensation cycling of precipitation was a dominate process during the Early, pre-frontal passage phase of the AR storm. After frontal passage, we find that Rayleigh-type distillation and equilibrium condensation are the dominant processes in the 2021 AR storm. Thus, the triple oxygen isotope composition of AR precipitation is an important indicator and tracer of physical processes occurring within AR storms.

title: Reconfiguration of natural organic matter by MnO 2 in frozen matrices
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Peizeng Yang, Jingqi Ruan, Jie Chen, Bin Gao, Deyang Kong, Junhe Lu
abstract: While mineral-carbon interactions have been largely studied at ambient temperatures, their dynamics in frozen environments remain unclear. Here, we unveil that the transformation of natural organic matter (NOM) by β-MnO2 was drastically accelerated in frozen matrices under mildly acidic conditions. This enhancement is driven by the freeze-concentration effect, which expels reactants into liquid-like grain boundaries, thus significantly increasing their local concentrations and acidifying the microenvironment. This pH shift profoundly enhances the redox potential of MnO2, facilitating its reactions with NOM, yielding structurally more complex oligomers and polymers, and hydroxylated and quinone-like derivatives. Consequently, extensive molecular reorganization occurs, accompanied by a marked decrease in formula count (from 5130 to 2841) and increase in intensity number-average molecular weight (Mn , from 326.546 to 443.286 Da) but with relatively stable total organic carbon. Concurrently, the reduction of Mn(IV) to dissolved Mn(II) induced by NOM is also accelerated in ice. This previously overlooked cryochemical pathway can alter the reactivity, mobility, and bioavailability of organic carbon. In a warming climate with intensified freeze–thaw cycles, these findings are critical for predicting carbon fate in cold regions.

title: Titanium isotopic insight into variable melt source contributions within the Aleutian Island Arc
description: Publication date: Available online 18 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Emma G. Ling, Sarah M. Aarons, Zhe James Zhang, Linqing Huang, Aleisha C. Johnson, Mauricio Ibañez-Mejia, Gene Yogodzinski, Nicolas Dauphas, Peter Kelemen
abstract: Titanium (Ti) isotopes are a well-established tracer of magmatic differentiation capable of providing useful insight into the magma series and geodynamic setting of rock formation. Titanium isotope fractionation is sensitive to magma conditions such as oxygen fugacity, water content, and the initial geochemical composition of a melt, however during plate subduction the relative contribution of the partial melt from the subducting slab on the Ti isotopic composition of the resulting melt is still under exploration. In this study, we use a suite of samples from two relatively modern, well-characterized sites from the Aleutian arc to probe how formation processes (e.g., partial melting versus fractional crystallization/magma recharge mixing) influence the measured Ti isotope compositions. We present Ti isotopic compositions for 18 volcanic samples from two Aleutian arc sites: Western Aleutian seafloor lavas from the Ingenstrem Depression, and lavas from Korovin Volcano on Atka Island. Samples dredged from the Ingenstrem Depression span a relatively narrow range in Ti isotopic composition (δ49Ti = +0.031 to + 0.147 ‰) with a relatively muted trend in Ti isotopic composition with respect to increasing silica content (SiO2 = 50.41 to 66.30 wt%). The samples from Korovin Volcano span a larger range (δ49Ti = -0.021 to + 0.355 ‰) and include more pronounced Ti isotopic variations with increasing silica content (SiO2 = 50.38 to 64.09 wt%). We use thermodynamic modeling (THERMOCALC software 3.53c) to predict isotope fractionation and show that the rocks from Ingenstrem Depression formed through melt-fluxed melting whereby between 0–70% of cool, hydrous-siliceous partial melt of subducting mid ocean ridge basalt (MORB) in eclogite facies mixes with mantle peridotite as it is heated and decompresses in the mantle wedge. In contrast, the Korovin Volcano dataset is likely formed by fractional crystallization from basalt to dacite with a potential role for recharge mixing of mantle derived melts. The data presented here suggest both a mantle wedge and subducting slab contribution for rocks from Ingenstrem Depression, further highlighting how Ti isotopes can be used to elucidate mass transfer in subduction zones and quantify variable source contributions in arc magmas, thereby providing significant insight into rock formation processes beneath Earth’s surface.

title: Adsorption mechanisms of carbonate on goethite: Density functional theory models of IR spectra and implications for surface complexation modeling
description: Publication date: Available online 17 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): James D. Kubicki, Mario Villalobos, América X. Cruz-Valladares
abstract: Understanding carbonate-goethite (α-FeOOH) surface interactions is crucial for describing adsorption-mediated mechanisms of many anions and cations on goethite, in view of the ubiquitous geochemical nature of both components. In the present work, we investigated, using computational approaches (Density Functional Theory) in conjunction with experimental infrared spectroscopy, possible mechanisms of carbonate adsorption onto goethite. Energy minimization calculations with the VASP code using periodic slab models for the two crystal faces of goethite revealed that there is a slight preference for the monodentate (Mono) complex that interacts with adjoining positively-charged triply-coordinated surface –OH groups, as compared to the bridged bidentate (BB) complex, but within the typical errors of the method, suggesting that both complexes have similar probabilities to form. Additional Gaussian 16 calculations on extended molecular clusters yielded a higher probability of the Mono surface complex to forming on the (101) face, while on (210) (Pnma standard crystallographic setting) the BB complex was largely preferred. The IR signals theoretically generated for each complex on each face yielded three possible surface configurations that matched closely the experimental IR signals of carbonate adsorbed on goethite: A BB complex on face (101), BB complexes on both faces (101) and (210), and Mono and BB complexes on face (101) plus a BB complex on face (210). This latter combination was tested with a unified CD-MUSIC surface complexation model. This model has been successfully applied to goethite for several anions and cations including protons, on goethites of different particle sizes and thus different reactive surface site densities. The CD-MUSIC model yielded adequate simulations of the experimental adsorption data across different conditions, with similar affinity constants for the three complexes, and contributions from each complex that were similar to those predicted by the cluster model. The results of this work tying theoretical models to experimental data revealed the importance of using case-specific surface configurations that are not necessarily applicable to similar environmental minerals, in this case for Fe(III) (hydr)oxides.

title: Hydrological and biogeochemical impact of a dynamic freshwater lens on the carbonate geochemistry in a sandy subterranean estuary
description: Publication date: Available online 16 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jiawei Liu, Zijun Wu, Bradley A. Weymer, Qianqian Wang, Qiyue Gu, Yuanqing Chen, Zhonglin Ma, Yiqing Wang, Bulderxen Huate, Guanlin Li, Jiangtao Li, Nicole Kowalski, Michael Ernst Böttcher
abstract: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) is an important pathway for dissolved carbon delivery to the coastal ocean and a potential driver of coastal acidification; however, the controls on the sources and transformations of SGD-derived carbon remain poorly constrained for sandy beach aquifers under contrasting seasonal conditions. Here, we integrated geochemical, geophysical, and microbial approaches to investigate a permeable subterranean estuary (STE) on the northern coast of the subtropical Beibu Gulf, South China Sea. The contrasting wet and dry seasons provided a natural setting to examine coupled hydrological–biogeochemical processes affecting the dissolved carbonate system. A freshwater lens was observed during the wet season, when precipitation was higher, whereas it was largely absent from the supratidal beach zone during the dry season. This seasonal contrast was associated with changes in salinity distribution, end-member mixing, and carbonate chemistry within the STE. Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), total alkalinity (TA), and Ca2⁺ exhibited non-conservative behavior across salinity zones. Geochemical and microbial evidence suggested sulfate reduction during the wet season, whereas aerobic respiration appeared to be a more important pathway for organic matter degradation during the dry season. CO2 outgassing and carbonate dissolution–precipitation likely further modified the carbonate system in both seasons. SGD-derived DIC fluxes averaged (4.0 ± 0.5) × 105 mol d−1 in the wet season and (5.0 ± 0.4) × 105 mol d−1 in the dry season, comparable to DIC inputs from the adjacent Fengjia River. Most groundwater TA/DIC ratios were below 1 and lower than those of offshore seawater in the Beibu Gulf, consistent with SGD contributing to coastal acidification. The acidifying potential of SGD appeared higher during the dry season, possibly reflecting a larger contribution of inland-derived freshwater SGD and associated shifts in biogeochemical pathways. The estimated [TA–DIC] flux indicates that SGD may have had a stronger acidifying influence than that of the Fengjia River during the dry season. Overall, these findings highlight the seasonal evolution of transient freshwater lenses as a factor that can modulate carbon cycling, export, and acidification potential in sandy beach aquifers, and underscore the need to integrate SGD and its biogeochemical impacts into regional carbon budgets and carbonate chemistry assessments for unvegetated sandy coastal systems worldwide.

title: Spatiotemporal variability of Tungsten-182 in the Hawaiian Plume
description: Publication date: Available online 14 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lori N. Willhite, Nicole M.B. Williamson, Valerie A. Finlayson, Dominique Weis, Richard J. Walker
abstract: As a product of the decay of short-lived 182Hf (t½ = 8.9 Myr), 182W isotopic compositions in Earth’s rock record reflect processes that occurred during the first ∼60 Myr of the Solar System. Modern mantle plume-derived ocean island basalts have µ182W values (parts-per-million deviation from the bulk silicate Earth; BSE) that range from BSE estimates to values as low as ∼-25. The range of µ182W in some mantle plume-derived systems indicates variable contributions of an ancient component with low μ182W. The expression of the anomalous component in mantle plumes has implications for its size, viscosity, fusibility, distribution, and density. The Hawaiian mantle plume is well characterized with respect to chemical and isotopic variations for a range of elements, as well as magmatic flux, over the ∼5 Myr rock record represented by the volcanoes of the Hawaiian archipelago. To examine the physical nature of the anomalous component in this major plume system, we analyzed 35 basalts from across the archipelago for μ182W values and paired these data with complementary major-trace element and other isotopic data. These data, together with previously published data, indicate that Hawaiian plume-derived lavas were characterized by pulses of isotopically anomalous material, such that the component that hosts negative µ182W was either not always present or did not always contribute to melt production over the 5 Myr period. Of greatest note, the Hawaiian plume expresses large µ182W deficits during distinct time periods, at approximately 5 Ma in Kaua‘i and at present-day Kamaʻehuakanaloa, creating an inverted “u” shaped pattern of µ182W versus distance along the archipelago. Bulk Silicate Earth-like to moderate negative µ182W values (+1 to −14.5) appear at ∼1 Ma in Lānaʻi. Hawaiian volcanic centers lack clearly resolved µ182W anomalies at West Ka‘ena, Wai‘anae, Ko‘olau’s Makapu‘u section, Haleakalā, and Kohala. The negative µ182W anomalies at ∼5 Ma and present day correspond with rapid increases in magmatic flux of the Hawaiian plume, suggesting that the entrainment and expression of anomalous µ182W could be related to variations in the thermal structure of the plume. The Loa and Kea trends that are characterized by distinctive variations in the compositions of long-lived radiogenic isotope systems do not show resolvable differences between their µ182W systematics, indicating that the diverse contributions of recycled materials to the plume did not strongly affect the µ182W values of plume melt products. The attenuation of µ182W anomalies due to mixing with components with normal µ182W is unlikely to account for the distribution of µ182W along the archipelago. During the intervals when µ182W anomalies were minimal, the region of melting did not sample the anomalous component, most likely because it was irregularly entrained in the mantle plume.

title: Manganese-mediated ROS amplification drives oxidative dissolution of stibnite under dark abiotic conditions
description: Publication date: Available online 13 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Tongliang Wu, Linfang Zhu, Meiying Huang, Cun Liu, Yihang Huang, Song Wu, Zimeng Wang, Peixin Cui, Yujun Wang
abstract: Although oxidative dissolution of stibnite (Sb2S3) governs antimony (Sb) mobilization in many subsurface environments, the abiotic mechanism responsible for sustained oxidation in dark systems remains unresolved. Here, we show that interfacial activation of molecular oxygen (O2) on Sb2S3 generates surface-derived superoxide (O2 •−), which is coupled to Mn-mediated reactive oxygen species (ROS) reactions and markedly accelerates oxidative dissolution under dark conditions. Kinetic experiments showed that dissolved Mn(II) substantially enhanced Sb2S3 weathering, increasing the apparent Sb(V) release rate from 1.45 ± 0.52 × 10−10 mol m−2 s−1 in the absence of Mn(II) to 7.69 ± 1.13 × 10−10 mol m−2 s−1 at 1 mM Mn(II). Electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy confirmed O2 •− generation on the Sb2S3 surface, and density functional theory calculations showed favorable electron redistribution from surface Sb sites toward adsorbed O2, supporting an interfacial electron-transfer mechanism. In the presence of Mn(II), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) accumulation was greatly enhanced, consistent with Mn-mediated conversion of O2 •− to H2O2. This process was accompanied by the formation of poorly crystalline mixed-valence Mn (oxyhydr)oxide phases, progressive elemental sulfur accumulation, and increasing Sb–O coordination, indicating coupled oxidation of both reduced sulfur species and Sb(III). This O2 •−-initiated, Mn-mediated pathway provides a mechanism for accelerated Sb2S3 oxidation under dark, Mn-rich, mildly alkaline conditions.

title: Low-Ca olivine antecrysts as fingerprints of recycled oceanic crust and possible pyroxenite destruction beneath the southern East Pacific Rise region
description: Publication date: Available online 13 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Annie Chien, Peng Jiang, John M. Sinton, Zhaoshan Chang, Shiqiang Huang, Ethan Warnes, Jacqueline E. Dixon
abstract: Lavas from the 13°S to 23°S southern East Pacific Rise (SEPR) exhibit significant compositional heterogeneity along and near the ridge axis, as well as the off-axis Rano Rahi Seamounts and the west-northwest trending Pukapuka Ridge. This heterogeneity has been attributed to “plume-like” materials or “entrained mantle heterogeneity”, likely involving recycled components. However, whether recycled oceanic crust (ROC) is a major recycled component and whether the mantle beneath the SEPR is lithologically heterogeneous (i.e., presence of pyroxenite) remains poorly constrained. In this study, we examine textures and geochemical (major, minor, and trace element) compositions of olivine phenocrysts in lavas from the representative SEPR regions, via integrated EPMA and LA-ICP-MS techniques and fractional crystallization (FC) modeling. Our results reveal distinct olivine populations characterized by their zoning patterns and Ni-Ca compositions. FC modeling of the Ni-rich olivine endmember (the high-Ni trend) favors high-pressure FC at approximately 1.0 GPa, potentially reaching 1.5 GPa, under relatively oxidized conditions (up to ΔQFM +2) and with initial H2O contents of up to approximately 0.5 wt.%. A distinct group of reversely zoned olivines exhibit low-Ca cores (∼310 to ∼1160 ppm Ca) that plot along the high-Ni trend and cannot be explained by repeated mafic recharge or diffusion-driven re-equilibration. These low-Ca, reversely zoned olivine cores are interpreted as olivine antecrysts and occur exclusively in the isotopically anomalous region at 18°–19°S, characterized by elevated 87Sr/86Sr and low 143Nd/144Nd. Together with evidence from other trace elements (Li, Zn, Sc, Ti), these low-Ca olivine antecrysts can be best explained by crystallization from deep-sourced, Ca-poor melts derived from ROC-metasomatized mantle. Despite the inferred involvement of ROC, olivine first-row transition-element ratios, including Mn/Fe, Zn/Fe, and Mn/Zn, provide no clear evidence for a preserved pyroxenite source lithology but instead support a peridotite-dominated source. The apparent absence of a recognizable pyroxenite signature despite ROC involvement may reflect either insufficient ROC relative to peridotite to form pyroxenite initially or possible pyroxenite destruction through complete melting and assimilation into the surrounding peridotite, thereby forming refertilized peridotite. In the latter scenario, ROC-derived chemical and isotopic signatures may persist after the original lithological identity has been erased. These findings highlight the value of olivine textures and in situ geochemistry as complementary to glass and whole-rock analyses, revealing potential olivine-scale fingerprints of ROC involvement and providing insights into ROC fate and associated mantle processes that may be obscured by bulk compositions. Together with studies of pyroxenite in other geological settings, our findings raise the possibility that pyroxenite destruction may be a globally widespread process that contributes to mantle geochemical and lithological heterogeneity in both plume-influenced and plume-absent oceanic and continental settings.

title: Oxygen isotopic and chemical composition of chromites in the unique Washington County iron meteorite and implications for classification
description: Publication date: Available online 12 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Manfred Vogt, Daniel Mahr, Andreas Pack, Mario Trieloff
abstract: The ungrouped iron meteorite Washington County, so far unique for hosting solar-wind derived He and Ne within its metal, contains previously undocumented µm-sized chromite inclusions, extremely enriched in Mn and with highly variable oxygen isotopic compositions. The chromites of ≤ 13 µm in diameter occur as isolated, angular to subangular grains, which are erratically but frequently distributed within the metal of the iron meteorite. 76 inclusions were characterized by SEM–EDS, micro-Raman spectroscopy and electron microprobe analyses as Mn-bearing chromites (FeCr2O4), containing several wt% MnO, and manganochromites ((Mn,Fe)(Cr,V)2O4) with up to ∼ 27 wt% MnO, representing the Mn-richest natural chromite ever reported. δ18O, δ17O and Δ17O values of ten Mn-bearing chromites and five manganochromites were determined by Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) to reveal potential genetic associations with other meteorites. The δ18O values of individual chromite inclusions, with spatial distances of only a few millimeters, range from −3.52‰ to + 20.38‰, defining a huge measured isotopic spread – unprecedented among differentiated meteorites – while the mean Δ17O value of −0.07 ± 0.13‰ (2σ) is indistinguishable from the Terrestrial Fractionation Line (TFL). The measured oxygen isotopic spread shows no systematic relationship with chemical composition of the inclusions as both low- and high-Mn chromites show δ18O variations of ∼ 22‰ and ∼ 24‰, respectively. However, because potential matrix-dependent and other analytical effects cannot be fully quantified, the magnitude of the intrinsic isotopic variability remains uncertain. If a substantial component is intrinsic, the δ18O and δ17O variations are consistent with kinetic isotope fractionation during oxygen diffusion when chromites formed by solid-state exsolution within the FeNi metal upon cooling. Δ17O values overlap with those of enstatite chondrites, aubrites, and other non-carbonaceous (NC) meteorites but differ from most carbonaceous (CC) meteorites. A comparative analysis of oxygen isotope trends in NC versus CC meteorites shows that Δ17O values support classification of Washington County as NC-iron, suggesting a common formation region in relation to the NC population. Further literature review reveals additional NC-irons (i.e., irons of groups IIAB, IIG, IIIAB, IVA and IAB) that might, like Washington County, contain volume-correlated solar-type noble gases, potentially consistent with more intense exposure to solar irradiation in the inner solar system and incorporation of solar signatures preferentially into NC parent bodies.

title: Role of alkalis in carbonatite melt-mediated rare earth element mineralization
description: Publication date: Available online 12 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jia-Dong Ma, Hao-Cheng Yu, Isra Ezad, Li Zhou, Xing Ding, Ming-Qian Wu, Yi-Xue Gao, Zhong-Hai Fan, Shan-Shan Li, Kun-Feng Qiu, Jun Deng
abstract: Although recent studies have established a melt–fluid evolutionary framework for REE mineralization in carbonatitic systems, the role of sodium (Na), a principal alkali component, in fluid saturation, REE partitioning between melt and fluid, and REE mineral crystallization remains incompletely constrained. To evaluate the role of Na during REE mineralization, we conducted high-pressure, high-temperature experiments at 550–650 °C and 100 MPa, investigating the crystallization of REE minerals and fluid saturation in a simplified CaCO3-Na2CO3-LaF3 system containing 10 or 20 wt% bulk Na2CO3, with corresponding CaCO3 contents of 70 or 60 wt% at a fixed LaF3 content of 20 wt%. Experiments were run either as anhydrous compositions or fluid-bearing with the addition of pure H2O, a 3.3 mol L−1 NaCl aqueous solution, or a 1.7 mol L−1 Na2SO4 aqueous solution. Run products contained calcite and quenched carbonatitic melt, together with variable assemblages of bastnäsite, carbocernaite, and a Ca–F phase. Vapor cavities in fluid-bearing runs are interpreted as evidence of a separate fluid phase. Comparative experiments showed that, at a given temperature, increasing the bulk Na2CO3 content from 10 to 20 wt% results in increasing carbonatitic melt fraction. The higher bulk Na2CO3 content is also associated with greater inferred H2O retention in the carbonatitic melt. In fluid-bearing experiments, REE minerals crystallized within the quenched carbonatitic melt rather than within vapor cavities. Fluid–melt partition coefficients calculated from mass balance ranged from 0.05 to 0.13 for La and 0.09 to 0.31 for F. Chlorine- and sulfur-bearing components introduced through the addition of fluids were also detected in the quenched carbonatitic melt. These results show that REE are preferentially retained in the melt and that REE minerals crystallize primarily within the carbonatitic melt during melt–fluid coexistence. In bastnäsite-bearing experiments, carbonatitic melts with higher Na2O contents also contained higher La2O3 concentrations, suggesting that higher Na may enhance the capacity of carbonatitic melts to retain dissolved REE during REE mineral crystallization. The species of crystallizing REE minerals in the carbonatitic melts varied with bulk Na2CO3 content and temperature. In the high-Na system (20 wt% bulk Na2CO3), carbocernaite was dominant (12.9 vol%) at 550 °C, whereas only minor bastnäsite crystallized (2.9 vol%) at 600 °C. In the low-Na system (10 wt% bulk Na2CO3), bastnäsite crystallized from 550 to 650 °C (4.8–9.9 vol%). These relations suggest that higher Na availability favors alkali–REE carbonate crystallization, whereas lower Na availability favors bastnäsite crystallization in carbonatitic systems. Together, these findings indicate that primary REE mineralization remains melt-dominated during melt–fluid coexistence rather than shifting toward hydrothermal control. Within this melt-dominated framework, Na influences melt persistence, fluid saturation, REE retention in carbonatitic melts, and the crystallization of REE minerals during melt–fluid evolution in carbonatitic systems

title: Crystallographic controls and growth-rate effects on trace-element uptake in natural sphalerite
description: Publication date: Available online 11 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Chen Wei, Max Frenzel, Richard Wirth, Joachim Krause, Viktor Bertrandsson Erlandsson, Lin Ye, Frank Melcher, Zhilong Huang
abstract: Compositional zoning in minerals is increasingly exploited to reconstruct growth histories and decipher the processes and mechanisms of ore formation. Sphalerite is an important host of the critical metals Ga, Ge, and In, and commonly exhibits complex compositional zoning that may record the incorporation and partitioning of these elements during crystal growth. However, growth texture, such as sector zoning, can produce remarkable compositional differences among crystallographically nonequivalent but time-synchronous growth sectors. So far, this texture and its key control factors have been largely overlooked. Here, we combine electron backscatter diffraction, electron microprobe analysis, laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry, and transmission electron microscopy to investigate sector-zoned sphalerite crystals from Gorno (Italy), Huize (China), and Elmwood (USA). The results show clear elemental partitioning of tri- and tetra-valent cations (e.g., Ga3+, Ge4+, and Sb3+) between crystallographically distinct but time-equivalent growth sectors. Specifically, these elements are preferentially incorporated into different crystallographic face families in the following order: {111} > {110} > { 1 ¯ 1 ¯ 1 ¯ } > {100}. Monovalent cations (e.g., Cu+, Ag+, and possibly Tl+) are positively correlated with the highly charged cations, probably due to incorporation for charge compensation. In contrast, divalent cations generally show weak sectoral partitioning, with Cd2+ and Hg2+ showing somewhat opposite enrichment patterns. These selective elemental uptakes appear to be governed by the crystallographic structure of sphalerite and modulated by the kinetic effects imposed by hydrothermal growth environments. They can arise without changes in bulk fluid compositions, thermodynamic conditions (incl. T, p, pH, fS2), with no detectable involvement of accessory phases. This impacts trace element-based thermodynamic proxies and hydrothermal history reconstructions, complicates the use of experimental partition coefficients, and warrants evaluation of crystallographic effects on isotope fractionation. Our study provides a framework to recognize and evaluate such textures in sphalerite, applicable to other minerals with analogous textures, improving the robustness of trace element (isotope)-based interpretations.

title: FROM slab dehydration to arc magmatism: tracing continuous fluid release with molybdenum isotopes in forearc serpentinite
description: Publication date: Available online 11 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Fu-Qiang Dai, Yi-Xiang Chen, Ren-Xu Chen, Zi-Fu Zhao, Yu Wang, Jie Li, Thomas Pettke, Trevor J. Falloon
abstract: Isotopic evidence remains scarce for the contribution of forearc serpentinite to the source of arc magmas. In this study, we present new Mo contents and isotopic ratios for serpentinites from the Tonga-Kermadec forearc, to explore the behavior of Mo during forearc serpentinization and its role in arc magma formation. Our results reveal that the Tonga-Kermadec forearc serpentinites are enriched in fluid-mobile elements (e.g., U, As, Sb, Mo), and most samples exhibit heavy Mo isotopic compositions with δ 98/95MoNIST3134 ranging from −0.27‰ to 1.84‰. Molybdenum-As-Sb-Sr-U contents in these serpentinized peridotites show two different variation trends with their δ 98/95Mo values, indicating that their protoliths were metasomatized by different-stage forearc fluids with divergent Mo systematics. Rayleigh dehydration modelling using proximal oceanic crust materials indicates that forearc fluids released from sediments and/or altered oceanic crust at various depths can effectively account for the Mo isotopic endmember compositions observed in these serpentinites. We suggest dragged-down forearc serpentinite is the most important heavy Mo carrier for fluid-rich arc front magmas (especially in cold subduction zones). This study offers new insights into the Mo cycling process in subduction zones and highlights the role of forearc serpentinites in the formation of arc magmas.

title: Chromium isotope systematics of ferromanganese nodules: implications for the marine chromium cycle
description: Publication date: Available online 10 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Xi Yu, Ziyao Fang, Xiaoqing He, Liang Yi, Chenglong Deng, Huiqiang Yao, Liping Qin
abstract: Ferromanganese nodules play a crucial role in the marine cycle of many trace metal elements and significantly affect the isotope composition of these elements in seawater. Chromium (Cr) is a redox-sensitive element, and its isotope system has been widely used to trace the redox conditions of paleo-environments. Previous studies have shown that the Cr isotope compositions of ferromanganese nodules are notably lower than those of seawater, but the mechanisms behind this isotope fractionation and their implications for the marine Cr cycle are still debated. In this study, we examined ferromanganese nodules from the Western Pacific Ocean along with Cr adsorption experiments, and combined selective leaching, scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, and laser ablation-inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry analyses to explore the sources of Cr in the nodules and the geochemical processes that influence their Cr isotope compositions. The adsorption experiments show that during the uptake of Cr(VI) by manganese (Mn) oxides, lighter Cr isotopes are preferentially incorporated into the solid phase, leading to an equilibrium Cr isotope fractionation of about − 0.90‰ (Δ53CrMnOx−solu). However, this process alone cannot fully explain the low Cr isotope values and their substantial variability observed in our nodule samples (δ53Cr, −0.82‰ to − 0.20‰). Selective leaching results indicate that only a limited fraction of Cr is associated with readily leachable mineral phases, indicating the presence of additional Cr reservoirs. Iron (Fe) oxides may incorporate isotopically light dissolved Cr(III), potentially contributing to the negative bulk δ53Cr values. Meanwhile, in situ analyses reveal substantial Cr enrichment in Si- and Al-rich components, including authigenic clays and detrital materials, suggesting that these components represent additional important Cr reservoir. Our findings suggest that the Cr isotope compositions of ferromanganese nodules reflect the combined influences of multiple processes involving different Cr species and mineral phases. Consequently, the relationship between nodule and seawater δ53Cr is more complex than previously assumed, making it difficult to directly reconstruct paleo-seawater Cr isotope compositions from ferromanganese nodules. These findings highlight the importance of Cr speciation and mineralogical controls when interpreting Cr isotope records in Fe-Mn-rich sediments as proxies for past ocean redox conditions.

title: Hydrated mantle source and low-pressure differentiation control the formation of gold-enriched magmas
description: Publication date: Available online 9 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Deng-Yang He, Hao-Cheng Yu, David Hernández-Uribe, Olivier Namur, Meng-Fan Yang, Shan-Shan Li, Guo-Long Yan, Kun-Feng Qiu, Jun Deng
abstract: Crustal magmatism is widespread on Earth, yet only a relatively small proportion of magmatic systems become enriched in gold (Au) during differentiation to form Au deposits. How mantle source properties and crustal differentiation jointly control this selectivity remains poorly quantified. Here, we combine thermodynamic modeling with trace element mass-balance calculations to trace the generation and preservation of Au-fertile magmas from mantle source to upper crust. Our results show that high Ba/Zr ratios in Au-related magmas are source-controlled rather than differentiation-driven, indicating the hydrated, metasomatized mantle as a prerequisite for generating Au-fertile magmas. This is consistent with an extensive positive correlation between Au concentrations and Ba/Zr ratios of natural arc magmas. Hydrous and oxidized melting of metasomatized mantle can accelerate residual sulfide exhaustion at low melting degrees and generate primary mantle melts containing tens of ppb Au. Modeled magmas with H2O > 4–6 wt% reproduce the U/Yb and Nb/Y signatures of natural Au-related magmas and favor delayed sulfide saturation, indicating that H2O-rich melts are critical for maintaining Au fertility during crustal differentiation. Consistent with this, mass balance calculations show that, in evolved melts containing 1 wt% MgO, the 8 wt% H2O-rich model retains an additional 26% of the initial Au inventory relative to the 2 wt% H2O-poor model. Modeled Cu/Zr and Cu/Y systematics further reveal that, compared to high-pressure differentiation in thick crust, low-pressure magma evolution in thin crust suppresses premature sulfide saturation and FeO depletion, exerting a first-order control on the preservation of magmatic Au fertility. Along the hot-zone path in thick crust, >82% of the initial Au is removed, whereas low-pressure paths allow magmas to ascend to <5 kbar without substantial Au depletion (<10%). Cu/Zr and Cu/Y ratios also identify different evolution and formation processes for magmas associated with Au and Cu mineralization, respectively. The decreases in both ratios of modeled magmas caused by sulfide saturation during fractional crystallization reproduce the low Cu/Zr and Cu/Y array of Au-related magmas, whereas assimilation of 10%–20% pre-existing sulfide-bearing cumulates reproduces the high Cu/Zr and Cu/Y array of Cu-related magmas. Collectively, our findings establish a hierarchical framework, in which hydrated fertilized mantle generates Au-rich parental melts, and high melt H2O contents and low-pressure differentiation in thin crust preserve Au fertility during ascent to shallow crust.

title: Vanadium isotopic compositions in organic-rich sediments and the implications for constraining ancient marine redox evolutions
description: Publication date: Available online 9 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Siqi Li, Sean Newby, James McManus, Silke Severmann, Jeremy D. Owens
