abstract: As a novel redox proxy, authigenic sedimentary vanadium isotope signatures (δ51Vauth) have been suggested to be sensitive to benthic redox conditions and have the resolution to identify low-oxygen environments. Importantly, these low-oxygen environments are associated with ecological significance due to increased oxygen stress on marine ecosystems. However, some aspects of V isotopes remain poorly constrained, including the potential influence from early diagenetic processes under varying redox gradients, which could complicate the interpretation of sedimentary V isotopic signatures in reconstructing ancient marine redox conditions. In this study, sedimentary δ51Vauth values were measured across a range of depositional environments that have varying levels of bottom water oxygenation and early diagenetic processes. Sediments and pore fluids were collected from six sites located around the eastern Pacific oxygen minimum zone along the California and Mexico continental margins, encompassing a range of benthic redox conditions from oxic to anoxic, as well as having variations in organic carbon burial rates. The data show that sedimentary δ51Vauth values appear relatively consistent with core depth at each site, regardless of the potential for V remobilization between sediments and pore fluids. We interpret this vertical consistency reflecting limited V release from sediments during early diagenesis. Thus, variations in sedimentary δ51Vauth across the studied sites dominantly correspond to the local redox conditions. In the oxic settings at Patton Escarpment and San Clemente Basin, V is primarily scavenged by manganese (Mn) and iron (Fe) oxides, and sedimentary δ51Vauth values range from approximately –1.10‰ to –1.40‰. This variability is plausibly influenced by specific oxide mineralogy or the relative abundances of Mn and Fe oxides. At low-oxygen (bottom water [O2] <∼20μM) and anoxic sites—Catalina Basin, San Pedro Basin, San Blas Basin, and Soledad Basin—authigenic V has previously been suggested to be mainly delivered via organic particles, although contributions from Fe oxides may also play a role in authigenic V enrichment. A general trend of higher sedimentary δ51Vauth values occurring with more reducing conditions suggests a redox-dependent isotope fractionation. Notably, sites with similar bottom water redox conditions, i.e., near anoxic (bottom water [O2] at ∼3 μM) and fully anoxic, but different organic carbon burial rates and Fe enrichments, display similar sedimentary δ51Vauth values. Furthermore, the sedimentary δ51Vauth values documented at Soledad Basin, where no significant V depletion is observed in either bottom waters or pore fluids, closely approach the values reported for surface sediments in the euxinic Cariaco Basin. This suggests that, in Cariaco Basin, V isotope fractionation is not primarily driven by water column H2S accumulation or Rayleigh fractionation derived from V depletion as proposed in previous research. Therefore, anoxic and euxinic environments both exhibit an isotope offset of around -0.4‰ relative to seawater. Overall, our findings demonstrate that sedimentary δ51Vauth signatures are sensitive to local redox conditions—particularly across the oxic to anoxic conditions—and are relatively resistant to alteration during early diagenesis, across a wide range of porewater redox conditions from oxic to sulfidic conditions. These findings highlight the potential of V isotopes as a robust proxy to diagnose local redox variations. Integration with other local and global redox proxies can provide a more comprehensive framework for reconstructing ancient marine redox evolution.

title: Zinc behavior during carbonated peridotite melting
description: Publication date: Available online 7 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Zhongxing Sun, Xiaolin Xiong, Jie Tang, Chunguang Wang
abstract: The characteristic high δ66Zn (≥0.3–0.4‰) of intraplate alkaline basalts indicate derivation from carbonated peridotite or a mixed peridotite + carbonated eclogite source. Moreover, these basalts also exhibit high Zinc (Zn) contents. Zn behavior should thus offer strong potential for tracing carbonated peridotite involvement in their genesis. A significant knowledge gap exists, however, as mineral-melt Zn partition coefficients (D Zn) during carbonated peridotite melting are scarce. Here D Zn between mineral and carbonate/carbonated silicate melt were experimentally determined at 3 GPa and 1300–1450 °C. Integrating our results with literature data reveals that melt MgO and SiO2 contents well correlate with mineral-melt D Zn. We quantified these relationships by parameterizing mineral-melt D Zn as function of melt MgO and SiO2 contents. Using our new D Zn values, we modeled Zn behavior during carbonated peridotite melting. The modeling results indicate that partial melts derived solely from carbonated peridotite consistently contain less than ∼100 ppm Zn. This is insufficient to explain the high Zn contents (∼120 ppm) observed in high-δ66Zn intraplate alkaline basalts. In contrast, mixing of peridotite-derived melts with melts derived from eclogite + Zn-rich carbonate provides a viable mechanism to account for the high Zn contents in these high-δ66Zn intraplate alkaline basalts. Therefore, a mixed peridotite + carbonated eclogite mantle source might represent a suitable origin for intraplate alkaline basalts exhibiting high δ66Zn values.

title: Zircon saturation in damp hot rhyolites
description: Publication date: Available online 6 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Julian-Christopher Storck, Ben Ellis, Edgar A. Cortes-Calderon, Marcel Guillong, Olivier Bachmann
abstract: Zircon is a key mineral for understanding evolved magmatic systems, yet its presence in hot, silicic magmas challenges conventional models of zircon saturation. Volcanic rocks of the Columbia River–Snake River Plain–Yellowstone hotspot track, for example, contain notable quantities of zircon despite having high temperatures, low crystallinities, and moderate zirconium (Zr) contents, conditions under which magmas are theoretically predicted to be zircon-undersaturated. This study investigates how and where zircon forms and persists in such seemingly unfavorable environments. We focus on the Castleford Crossing ignimbrite, one of the youngest and hottest eruptions in the Central Snake River Plain, to reconstruct the final stages of its thermal and crystallization history. New time–temperature constraints are derived from an integrated approach combining zircon U–Pb geochronology, mineral thermometry, and thermodynamic modeling. Two-Fe-Ti-oxide and pyroxene thermometry yield magmatic temperatures of > 910 °C and ∼ 930 °C, respectively. These estimates converge with calculated zircon saturation temperatures, consistent with the low pre-eruptive H2O contents (∼1–2 wt%) of these rhyolites. Textural observations show that over 75% of zircon crystals are attached to or included within oxides, pyroxenes, and plagioclase. This spatial association suggests that zircon nucleation is facilitated in microns-thick, supersaturated diffusive boundary layers enriched in Zr and characterized by a lower “M factor” (major-element cation ratio) adjacent to growing major phases. U–Pb dating by LA-ICP-MS across multiple units reveals very little scatter beyond analytical uncertainty, indicating a minimal antecrystic component, a finding corroborated by ID-TIMS data from the same units. While most zircons crystallized in near equilibrium with the evolving host melt, a small fraction, distinguished by high U and Ti contents, likely reflects fast disequilibrium growth. Collectively, our results demonstrate that zircon saturation in these hot magmas is possible, although it is achieved primarily through the creation of transient, Zr-rich microenvironments. This mechanism reconciles the presence of largely autocrystic zircon in these hot Snake River Plain rhyolites and has broader implications for interpreting zircon geochronological data in terms of magma fluxes in high-temperature silicic systems. In particular, the short zircon crystallization histories recorded by the large ignimbrites of the Snake River Plain and Yellowstone province are likely due to poor preservation potential of zircons in such high-T, and relatively dry rhyolitic magmas, not to unusually high magma production rates.

title: Dehydration processes of stagnant slab within the mantle transition zone revealed by geochemistry of olivine-hosted melt inclusions
description: Publication date: Available online 4 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Junfu Zhang, Yang Yu, Jie Tang, Feng Wang, Wenliang Xu
abstract: Nearly 50% of subducted plates may stagnate in the mantle transition zone (MTZ), forming the big mantle wedge (BMW) structure. Fluids or melts released by subducted stagnant slab within the MTZ intensively influence the physical–chemical nature and evolution of the upper mantle in a BMW system. However, dehydration processes of stagnant slab within the MTZ are unclear. Here, we present geochemical and H-B isotopic data of olivine-hosted melt inclusions from Early Oligocene-Miocene basalts in eastern Northeastern China (ENC), with an aim of constraining the dehydration processes of subducted stagnant slab in the MTZ within the BMW system. The olivine-hosted melt inclusions in OIB-like basalts (33–21 Ma) exhibit low water contents in primary melts (545–965 ppm) and mantle sources (116–202 ppm), coupled with low H2O/Ce ratios (7.96–13.6) and low δD values (−406 ‰ to −191 ‰), implying that the water in mantle sources is mainly contributed by ancient sediment-dominated dehydration in the MTZ. The olivine-hosted melt inclusions in weak-arc like basalts (11 Ma) exhibit relatively high water contents in primary melt (5780–6381 ppm) and mantle source (354–390 ppm), with elevated H2O/Ce ratios (135–166) and upper mantle-like δD values (−119 ‰ to −78 ‰), suggesting that the water in mantle source is mainly contributed by the young lower oceanic crust-dominated dehydration in the MTZ. Additionally, the melt inclusions in the ENC basalts also exhibit variable δ11B values (−17.10 ‰ to −0.08 ‰). The heavy B isotopic compositions of a small amount of melt inclusions from 33 Ma and 11 Ma basalts indicate the contribution of subducted serpentinite dehydration. The water contents in mantle sources of 33 Ma and 21 Ma basalts are lower than those in mantle sources of the early Cenozoic basalts, which is consistent with the transition from an active continental margin setting to trench-arc-basin system and formation of the northeastern (NE) Asian BMW, whereas the increase of water contents in mantle sources from 33 Ma to 11 Ma basalts could reflect the initial stagnance of subducted Pacific slab to formation of the NE Asian BMW as well as the transformation from ancient sediment-dominated dehydration to young lower oceanic crust-dominated dehydration, which is closely related to the evolution of the NE Asian BMW.

title: Beyond bulk sediments: extracting salinity signals from Sr/Ba ratios in complex marginal-marine settings
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Xia Zhang, Xiaotian Zhang, Yue Cai, Rong Hu, Guyue Tan
abstract: Sedimentary successions in modern to sub-modern marginal-marine environments are valuable archives of climatic and environmental change. However, paleosalinity reconstruction in these settings is often compromised by lithological heterogeneity, complex sediment sources, hydrodynamic processes, and diagenetic overprinting. Using a well-constrained postglacial succession (∼15 ka to present) from the Qiantang River coastal system, we test and refine Sr/Ba-based salinity proxies, that have been widely used in fine-grained siliciclastic successions. To investigate occurrence modes and interfering factors of Sr and Ba, we analyzed bulk sediments, grain-size fractions, and selective chemical extracts using dilute acetic acid (HAc), ammonium carbonate (AC), sodium acetate (NaAc), and ammonium acetate (AA). Our results show that Sr/Ba ratios in the 1.50) environments. Nevertheless, this ratio tends to overestimate salinity in high-energy settings, where clay winnowing preferentially removes exchangeable Ba. We therefore apply a correction using the relative proportion of the coarse-grained sensitive end-member (FEI). The FEI-normalized SrAC/BaHAc ratio shows enhanced sensitivity to relative sea-level variations and successfully identifies the MFS. This refined multi-proxy framework is well-suited for modern to sub-modern marginal-marine settings where exchangeable fractions are largely preserved, and confounding influences can be corrected through integration with sedimentological analyses. For ancient or diagenetically altered successions, where exchangeable fractions are severely modified but within a closed system, bulk Sr/Ba proxies in fine-grained successions remain a promising alternative, provided that carbonate-rich and/or barite-bearing intervals are treated with caution. This conclusion is supported by the general consistency observed between the Si/Al-normalized Sr/Ba<10μm ratios and the refined exchangeable proxies. Overall, this multi-proxy approach circumvents confounding factors and offers practical utility for paleoenvironmental and relative sea-level reconstruction in complex modern to sub-modern marginal-marine settings. More broadly, the methodological framework might offer a reference point for analogous investigations in other contexts, depending on site-specific preservation conditions of exchangeable fractions.

title: Potassium isotope dichotomy in hydrogenetic ferromanganese crusts: phase-specific archives of seawater signatures or authigenic processes?
description: Publication date: Available online 3 November 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jiayang Chen, Weiqiang Li, Tianyu Chen, Yang Qu
abstract: Stable potassium (K) isotopes offer valuable insights into K cycles at various scales. Hydrogenetic ferromanganese (Fe-Mn) crusts, precipitated from seawater and enriched in K, could serve as potential marine K isotopic archives. To evaluate this potential, we conducted detailed investigations of the elemental and isotopic characteristics of K in two hydrogenetic Fe-Mn crusts from the northwestern Pacific Ocean floor over the past 80 million years. Sequential extractions reveal two major K-bearing phases: exchangeable K mainly in Mn oxyhydroxides (62.8 ± 8.9%) and structural K in silicates (32.6 ± 9.3%), with other phases contributing less than 5%. The δ41K values of the exchangeable K, ranging from −0.09 ± 0.04‰ to 0.35 ± 0.05‰, are higher than those of silicate K, which range from −0.71 ± 0.06‰ to −0.34 ± 0.05‰. Notably, the δ41K values of exchangeable K in the two crusts exhibit inconsistent temporal variations. This indicates that exchangeable K in Fe-Mn crusts is susceptible to local diagenetic processes, undermining its reliability as a proxy for long-term seawater δ41K changes. In contrast, the δ41K values of silicate K show consistent temporal trends, correlating with changes in distances between the sample sites from the Hawaiian hotspot. This suggests that the isotopic ratios of silicate-bound K in Fe-Mn crusts can record seafloor authigenic processes, and the growth of authigenic minerals in Fe-Mn crusts appears to be mainly influenced by basaltic volcanic detritus from hotspots. This study reveals a fundamental elemental and isotopic dichotomy of K in Fe-Mn crusts, demonstrating that 1) hydrogenetic Fe-Mn crusts are unlikely to be robust recorders of seawater K isotope evolution, and 2) silicate-bound K can be a sensitive tracer for seafloor authigenic processes and hotspot-related volcanism.

title: Lithospheric mantle derivation and depth-dependent endowment of Neoarchean orogenic gold in the Yilgarn Craton
description: Publication date: Available online 30 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qingfei Wang, David I. Groves, Runsheng Yin, Shiyu Liu, Carl Brauhart, Lin Yang, Huajian Li, Neal J. McNaughton, Kunfeng Qiu, Yongbo Peng, Jun Deng
abstract: The Yilgarn Craton represents one of the largest Precambrian orogenic gold provinces globally. The Kalgoorlie and Kurnalpi terranes, dominated by mesozonal-epizonal deposits, host the bulk of the gold, whereas the South West and Youanmi terranes, dominated by hypozonal deposits, are far less endowed. The source of auriferous fluids has long been debated between models involving crustal metamorphic devolatilization at mid-crustal levels and magmatic-hydrothermal processes near the crust-mantle boundary, whereas the causes for the marked regional endowment contrast remain poorly understood. Here we present integrated Hg, multiple S, and Sr isotope data to reveal that these four terranes share a common lithospheric mantle source and that their contrasting gold endowment relates to distinct depth-controlled mineralization processes. Non-zero Δ33S values of gold-related sulfides (−0.09 to 0.81 %) are comparable to those of granites across all terranes. This implies that lower-crustal components were involved in the source, arguing against a model involving a mid-crustal metamorphic fluid source. The Δ199Hg values of native gold and sulfides range from negative to positive and center near zero, indicating that lithospheric mantle metasomatized by oceanic sediments with significant input of continental crust is the most plausible source for the auriferous fluid. This is supported by elevated (87Sr/86Sr)i ratios of hydrothermal apatite. Critically, Δ199Hg values are similar between the well-endowed Kurnalpi Terrane and the poorly endowed South West and Youanmi terranes, confirming a common lithospheric mantle source. In striking contrast, δ202Hg values are markedly higher in mesozonal-epizonal deposits (0.11–1.79 %) than in hypozonal deposits. This distinction is attributed to fluid phase separation during mesozonal and epizonal mineralization at middle-upper crustal levels, whereas isotopically light Hg was preferentially partitioned into the vapor phase and lost, leaving the residual fluids enriched in heavy Hg isotopes. In contrast, the greater depths of hypozonal mineralization effectively inhibited such phase separation. Collectively, these interpretations suggest that the primary control on gold endowment is not source heterogeneity but rather the current exposed crustal depths of the terranes.

title: Dissolved organic matter decouples Fe(II) oxidation from arsenic immobilization: radical localization, mineral disorder and colloid stabilization
description: Publication date: Available online 30 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Junhao Niu, Valentina Erastova, Xinghao Wang, Yanwei Wang, Juan Gao
abstract: Arsenic contamination of paddy soils and shallow aquifers threatens drinking-water safety and staple-crop production worldwide, and its severity is set by Fe-As coupling at subsurface oxygenation fronts. Where oxygen periodically infiltrates reduced layers, Fe(II) oxygenation generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) and fresh Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides that jointly oxidize mobile As(III) and sequester the resulting As(V). How dissolved organic matter (DOM), a ubiquitous constituent of redox-dynamic environments, disrupts this natural attenuation circuit remains insufficiently resolved at the molecular scale. We examined straw-derived DOM across C/Fe molar ratios of 0–10 during aerobic oxidation of 1 mM Fe(II) in synthetic solutions at pH 5.5–7.5, combining radical quenching, kinetic modelling, XRD, Fe K-edge XAS and STEM-EELS. Converging quenching and modelling evidence indicates that As(III) oxidation proceeded predominantly via hydroxyl radicals generated at the Fe-mineral – water interface (·OHsurf) rather than via the freely dissolved pool. Increasing DOM progressively relocated ·OH generation to aqueous Fe(II)-DOM complexes, where radicals were scavenged before reaching surface-associated As(III); the Fe(II) utilization efficiency for As(III) oxidation accordingly declined from 0.33% to 0.13%. A transition near C/Fe ≈ 5 for rice straw-derived DOM separated two geochemical regimes: below it, micron-scale lepidocrocite aggregates settled and retained arsenic, whereas above it, ferrihydrite–organic nanocolloids of 160–360 nm carrying approximately 40% of total As remained suspended. We identify that DOM controls As fate through coupled effects on the spatial partitioning of radical generation, iron mineral transformation, and colloidal stabilization, and propose C/Fe stoichiometry as a governing chemical parameter for predicting arsenic fate in redox-fluctuating environments.

title: Aspartic acid-responsive Leifsonia shinshuensis mitigates imidacloprid phytotoxicity in Brassica oleracea
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Chunran Zhou, Tao Zhang, Jingyi Deng, Peijuan Miao, Canping Pan, Dong Li
abstract: Plants recruit rhizosphere microorganisms to alleviate pesticide stress, but the chemical signals governing this process remain unclear. We show that imidacloprid (IMI) stress triggers aspartic acid accumulation in root exudates of cabbage, restructuring the rhizosphere bacterial community with enriched Actinomycetes. We isolated a bacterial strain B3 from the treated rhizosphere, identified as Leifsonia shinshuensis, and confirmed that aspartic acid acts as both a chemoattractant and growth promoter for this strain. Inoculation with strain B3 accelerated IMI degradation, reducing pesticide residues in plant tissues by 7.9–43.0%. This was accompanied by enhanced plant amino acid metabolism and enrichment of beneficial rhizobacterial taxa, collectively alleviating IMI-induced oxidative damage. Together, our findings identify aspartic acid as a candidate signal linking root metabolic stress to beneficial bacteria and demonstrate a plant-microbe feedback mechanism that enhances pesticide detoxification under IMI stress.

title: Influences of soil metabolites and microbial successions on methylmercury production in terrestrial soil environments
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Runnan Lyu, Martin Tsz-Ki Tsui, Ganxing Liu, Xizi Yang
abstract: Vegetated ecosystems are important sinks of mercury (Hg), but predicting methylmercury (MeHg) distribution remains a major challenge due to complex biogeochemical conditions and diverse environmental and ecosystem drivers (e.g., precipitation and vegetation covers) in terrestrial ecosystems. Here, we examined MeHg production in a 90-day soil incubation study assessing untargeted metabolomics and shotgun metagenomics, which simulated wet-season rain pulses under diverse organic inputs (e.g., carbon, nitrogen, thiols and/or phenols sources). Results revealed a biphasic pattern of soil MeHg dynamics. During the initial wet phase (Day 3–40), elevated soil moisture stimulated rapid increases in net MeHg production, which was driven by key enzymatic pathways that decomposed complex soil organic matter (SOM) to unlock labile nutrients (e.g., organic acids, nucleotides, and short-chain lipids). This process was found to be tightly coupled with the expansion of one-carbon metabolism, carbohydrate utilization and fermentation, which collectively acted as molecular factories supplying essential substrates, electron shuttles, and methyl donors to anaerobic hgcAB-bearing hosts (e.g., Bacteroidota and Acidobacteriota). However, during the subsequent attenuation phase (Day 40–90) when labile nutrients were largely depleted, net MeHg production declined drastically, coinciding with reduced methylation activity and the pervasive presence of merAB-carrying heterotrophic lineages across dominant background phyla (e.g., Pseudomonadota and Verrucomicrobiota). Ultimately, these multi-omic successions indicate that moisture-induced soil MeHg surges are influenced by the metabolic priming of microbial Hg methylators and counteracted by a persistent heterotrophic detoxification potential in soil environments.

title: Determination of the vapor pressures and Henry's law constants of fluorotelomer alcohols as a function of temperature for COSMO-RS prediction
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiaoyu Liu, Shubin Liu, Peter P. Egeghy, Joseph M. Martin, Edgar E. Folk, Kevin D. Culver
abstract: Concerns about per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have increased due to their persistence and potential health effects. Accurate physicochemical data, including vapor pressure (VP) and Henry’s law constant (HLC), are essential for understanding their environmental fate and transport. In this study, static micro-chamber and headspace methods coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry were used to measure the VPs and HLCs of four fluorotelomer alcohols (FTOHs) at 25–37 °C. These compounds were selected because they are commonly present in consumer products, building materials, household dust, and indoor air. The measured average VPs (Pa) at 25, 32, and 37 °C were 59.8, 89.5, and 134.8 for 4:2 FTOH; 8.9, 8.6, and 21.5 for 6:2 FTOH; and 0.66, 1.14, and 2.69 for 8:2 FTOH. For 10:2 FTOH, values were 0.02, 0.03, 0.11, and 0.16 at 25, 30, 35, and 37 °C. The corresponding dimensionless HLCs at 25 and 35 °C are 0.005 and 0.012 (4:2 FTOH), 0.065 and 0.090 (6:2 FTOH), 0.224 and 0.291 (8:2 FTOH), and 0.028 and 0.034 (10:2 FTOH). These results showed good agreement with COSMO-RS predictions (root mean square error ≤ 0.26) and may improve exposure modeling and our understanding of the role of FTOHs in human exposure to PFAS.

title: Soil moisture dynamics drive antibiotic resistance gene propagation through redox-mediated ROS accumulation and microbial community shifts
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jiajia Zhang, Zihu Ma, Wenxuan Wang, Yutong Li, Hu Li, Tiecheng Wang
abstract: Soil moisture fluctuations are increasingly recognized under climate change, yet their mechanistic role in antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) dissemination remains unclear. Here, riparian soils were exposed to continuous drying (D), constant wetting (W), and wet-dry alternation (DW) to investigate hydro-redox regulation of resistome dynamics. Wet-dry cycling induced synchronized Fe(II)/Mn(II) redox oscillations and enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production (H2O2, •OH), generating periodic oxidative stress. Compared with D and W treatments, the DW regime significantly increased ARGs abundance and conjugative transfer potential, particularly multidrug resistance genes, alongside elevated mobile genetic elements (MGEs). Metagenomic and network analyses revealed that Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, and Actinobacteria were major potential hosts associated with ARGs, and their relative abundances varied substantially under different water regimes. ROS levels and Fe/Mn redox-active species showed significant positive correlations with ARGs and MGEs, indicating coupled physicochemical regulation of horizontal gene transfer. Overall, water regime fluctuations were associated with changes in MGEs and ARGs profiles through alterations in soil oxygen diffusion and redox conditions, accompanied by Fe/Mn cycling, ROS accumulation, and microbial community restructuring, thereby forming a coupled ecological response network linking hydrological perturbations with ARGs transfer.

title: Melatonin-mediated activation of citrate efflux contributes to aluminum tolerance via CsMATE23 and CsMATE46 transporters
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Junjun Huang, Mengdie Song, Ying Yuan, Zhaoxin Hai, Yatong Zhu, Zhixian Sun, Huahua Wang
abstract: Aluminum (Al) toxicity represents a major abiotic constraint limiting crop productivity in acidic soils, yet the mechanisms underlying Al tolerance in cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.) remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the role of melatonin (MT) in Al tolerance using two cucumber cultivars (FY-35 and YM-18) with contrasting Al sensitivity. We found that the Al-tolerant cultivar YM-18 exhibits higher endogenous MT accumulation, reduced Al accumulation, and enhanced citrate secretion compared with the Al-sensitive cultivar FY-35. Exogenous MT application significantly alleviated Al-induced root growth inhibition and cellular damage by promoting citrate efflux and reducing Al accumulation in root apices. Furthermore, we identified two Al-responsive CsMATE proteins, CsMATE23 and CsMATE46, which localize to the plasma membrane and function as citrate transporters. Both genes were root-specifically induced by Al, with stronger expression responses in YM-18 than in FY-35. Functional validation in Xenopus laevis oocytes and transgenic Arabidopsis demonstrated that CsMATE23 and CsMATE46 enhance citrate secretion, decrease Al accumulation, and improve Al tolerance. Notably, MT increased the expression of CsMATE23 and CsMATE46 under Al stress. Collectively, our findings reveal a novel MT-mediated regulatory pathway that enhances cucumber Al tolerance by upregulating CsMATE23/CsMATE46-dependent citrate secretion, providing promising strategies for improving crop performance in acidic soils.

title: Rational engineering of a cofactor-independent P450BM3 peroxygenase for sustainable transformation of fluorinated phenolic pollutants
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qianqian Wang, Xingchen Yan, Mingyan Yan, Di Yan, Lingsen Kong, Fang Wang, Dong Li, Jiakun Xu
abstract: Fluorophenols (FPs) are persistent aromatic contaminants associated with industrial wastewater and agricultural activities. The high stability of their C–F bonds renders them resistant to conventional remediation processes, highlighting the need for efficient and sustainable treatment strategies. Here, we engineered a cofactor-independent P450BM3-based peroxygenase for the rapid H₂O₂-driven transformation of 3-fluorophenol (3-FP), 4-fluorophenol (4-FP), and 2,4-difluorophenol (2,4-DFP). Through rational active-site remodeling, the optimized F87A/T268D/A328F mutant achieved > 99% conversion of 3-FP and 4-FP within 1 min, and > 98% conversion of 2,4-DFP within 5 min. Kinetic analysis showed that active-site engineering improved the apparent catalytic efficiency of selected mutants in a substrate-dependent manner. UPLC-MS/MS analysis of the transformation products suggested substrate-dependent hydroxylation and oxidation pathways, with product masses consistent with putative defluorination-related products. This study demonstrates the potential of engineered P450BM3 peroxygenases for the rapid transformation of fluorinated aromatic contaminants.

title: Interception efficiency and driving mechanisms of bioretention facilities for microplastics in urban road rainwater runoff
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Wang Xiaojuan, Zhou Jianqiang, Song Xichen, Li Hao, Yan Yaping, Liu Xiuyun, Yue Cheng, Zhang Tingting, Gao Suxia, Ma Fengfeng, Yao Guirong, Liu Jianlin, Li Wei, Wei Bigui
abstract: Bioretention facilities are important measures for urban stormwater management and runoff pollution control. To elucidate the interception efficiency and driving mechanisms of bioretention facilities for microplastics (MPs) in urban road rainwater runoff. In this study, the on-site bioretention facilities were taken as the research object. By collecting rainwater runoff and substrate soil samples, the response of the facilities to rainwater runoff MPs was analyzed, the key driving factors affecting the interception efficiency were identified, and its mechanism was clarified. The removal rate of MPs (20–500 μm) by bioretention facilities was 46.51%-73.56%. Among them, the substrate soil interception rate was 20.33%-43.89%, and the non-substrate pathway interception rate was 2.62%-45.55%. pH, Urease, Sucrase, Verrucomicrobiota, Myxococcota, and Basidiomycota are potentially important internal factors affecting the retention of MPs in facilities. Maximum rainfall intensity, rainwater runoff microplastic input, particle size (20–100 μm) and polymer type (PE, PU, ACR) are potential important external factors. In the future, the research on the migration and removal of MPs under continuous rainfall and long-term operation conditions should be strengthened to provide a scientific basis for the continuous control and optimal operation of microplastic pollution in bioretention facilities.

title: Metabolomic trend-curve modeling: distinguishing defense and damage responses and points of departure for enniatin B toxicity in HepaRG cells
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Charlène Gendre, Blandine Gendre, Sylvie Huet, Pierre-Jean Ferron, Ludovic Le Hégarat, Estelle Dubreil-Chéneau
abstract: Enniatin B (ENNB) is an emerging foodborne mycotoxin whose molecular mechanisms of hepatotoxicity remain poorly understood. Untargeted metabolomics combined with concentration-response modeling was applied to characterize metabolic perturbations in HepaRG cells exposed for 48 h to ten ENNB concentrations (0.00781–4 µM; IC10 maximum). Omics-derived benchmark concentrations (BMCs) identified sensitive molecular responses and derived points of departure (PODs) within a New Approach Methodology (NAM) framework. Among the significant unannotated features, biphasic concentration–response curves predominated (73%). BMC analysis revealed high metabolome sensitivity, with biphasic responses (hypothesized to be adaptative-related) occurring at lower concentrations (median BMCs: 0.084 and 0.021 µM for bell- and U-shaped trends, respectively) than monotonic responses (hypothesized to be damage-related) (1.914 and 2.014 µM for increasing and decreasing trends, respectively). Putative defense-related metabolites were mainly lipids, whereas putative damage-associated metabolites were primarily amino acids and acylcarnitines. Pathway enrichment identified disruptions in glutathione metabolism, taurine and hypotaurine metabolism, steroid hormone biosynthesis, and pantothenate and coenzyme A biosynthesis. Redox imbalance and ionic homeostasis disruption emerged as a potential mechanistic link between adaptive and adverse metabolic responses. These findings establish a hypothetical mechanistic connecting adaptive and adverse metabolic responses to ENNB exposure and support metabolomics-derived PODs for next-generation risk assessment.

title: Solvent-free hydrogels with confined charge regulation for high-capacity and ultra-selective cesium removal from wastewater and seawater
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xin Wang, Zhaolong Niu, Rao Fu, Kun Zhou, Hengyi Gong, Yanli Li, Zhiwei Niu, Weiguo Ding, Wangsuo Wu, Peizhuo Hu
abstract: Radioactive cesium removal from nuclear wastewater and seawater remains a major environmental challenge because many adsorbents have limited capacity or poor selectivity in high-salinity systems. A cupric ferrocyanide-loaded composite hydrogel was prepared by combining solvent-free emulsion templating with confined charge regulation. Negatively charged polymer domains preconcentrate Cu2 + and direct the confined nucleation of cupric ferrocyanide nanoparticles within the hydrogel network. Theoretical calculations show that confined charge regulation increases accessible Cu2+ binding sites, explaining the enhanced loading capacity at the molecular level. The hydrogel is stable over pH 1–8, exhibits rapid adsorption equilibrium within 80 min, and achieves a maximum Cs+ capacity of 167.8 mg∙g−1. It also shows remarkable selectivity in complex matrices, with a Cs/Sr separation factor of 7536. Even in real seawater containing only 1.37 ppb Cs, it maintains highly selective adsorption at a solid–liquid ratio of 1.5 g∙L−1, with an efficiency of 54.23%. Mechanistic analysis indicates that Cs+ uptake proceeds mainly via K+/Cs+ exchange within the cupric ferrocyanide lattice and is promoted by size-matched channels favoring selective Cs+ transport. This strategy provides a practical route to high-capacity, ultra-selective adsorbents for radioactive wastewater and seawater treatment.

title: Steering atomic hydrogen production at zero-valent iron-water interface via proton-coupled electron accumulation for efficient dechlorination
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Tong Wang, Lisha Yang, Tong Hu, Zheqi Pan, Dingjiang Chen, Wenjun Zhou, Daohui Lin, Lizhong Zhu
abstract: Ambient hydrogenation induced by atomic hydrogen (*H) in the zero-valent iron (Fe0)-water system holds great promise for deep dechlorination of refractory chlorinated organic compounds (COCs), yet sluggish proton transfer and mismatched electron delivery at the interface limit efficient *H supply for hydrodechlorination. Inspired by bifunctional metalloenzymes, bismuth/nitrogen co-modified Fe0 (4Bi-1N-Fe0) was designed to simultaneously gather protons and electrons at the Fe0-water interface via coupled accumulation, steering *H generation toward targeted dechlorination. N sites strengthen interfacial hydrogen bonding, enabling relay proton accumulation, stabilizing *H, and enhancing dechlorination selectivity. Meanwhile, Bi sites construct fast interfacial charge-transfer channels and optimize Fe electronic structures via p-d orbital hybridization, enhancing electron density and surface *H binding. Driven by Bi-N cooperativity, 4Bi-1N-Fe0 delivers a dechlorination rate of 2.69 h−1 (trichloroethylene, TCE), which is 59.8 and 268.9 times that of singly modified Bi-Fe0 and N-Fe0, respectively. Furthermore, 4Bi-1N-Fe0 exhibits broad-spectrum dechlorination (for 4-CP, 2,4-DCP, FF, and CAP), remarkable 150-day stability, and low ecological risk, as confirmed by unimpaired survival of E. coli and unaffected germination and growth of rice and wheat upon leachate exposure. This strategy resolves the trade-off between sluggish *H generation and rapid *H loss, providing a new avenue for remediating COC-contaminated wastewater.

title: Fluorophilic AIE-active conjugated polymer nanoparticles for enhanced detection of PFOA and PFOS in environmental water via fluorous-mediated capture
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Chunqiang Liu, Yi Hao, Ziyu Yue, Sami M. Alharbi, Xuemeng Tian, Xueyi Liu, Yue Wang, Sameer Hussain, Ruixia Gao
abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) are two widely occurring per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in water, and rapid, sensitive and selective screening toward them is important. Herein, we adopt a modular design route for conjugated polymer (CP) probes based on a “Capture-Reaction-Response” cascade, in which fluorophilic interactions facilitate PFAS capture for improved sensitivity and selectivity. The fluorinated (F-NPs) and non-fluorinated (C-NPs) aggregation-induced emission-active CP nanoparticles were prepared. Via a turn-off proton-transfer mechanism, F-NPs show an ∼10-fold higher Stern-Volmer quenching constant (Ksv) than C-NPs. Mechanistic studies indicate that fluorinated alkyl chains improve analyte affinity and capture, and proton-transfer-induced exciton traps disrupt exciton transport in confined polymer networks for signal amplification. Furthermore, the fluorophilic interactions effectively enhance the selectivity toward PFAS, enabling it to overcome interference from common acids and anionic surfactants. The F-NPs achieve detection limits of 1.22 nM for PFOA and 1.76 nM for PFOS with a rapid response (20.0 s). Though not yet meeting drinking water ppt-level requirements, the probe serves as a rapid screening tool complementary to liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry. This work employs AIE-CP to suppress aggregation-caused quenching of nanoparticles, establishing and validating a probe design strategy with simultaneously enhanced sensitivity and selectivity.

title: Arsenic exposure induces cellular senescence and Alzheimer's pathogenesis via FBXO40-STING axis
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Tong Zhang, Wangqian Zhang, Jing Wang, Beixing Yang, Xushen Chen, Hui Kan, Rong Zhou, Xiaodong Ying, Wanxuan Hu, Yanxi Chai, Yulan Qiu, Meng Wang, Xuefeng Ren
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a leading cause of dementia, with cellular senescence implicated as a primary contributor to its pathogenesis. Chronic arsenic (As) exposure is associated with increased AD risk and accelerated biological aging, yet the causal link and mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify the E3 ubiquitin ligase FBXO40 as a critical regulator of As-induced neurotoxicity and senescence. Sprague–Dawley rats exposed to NaAsO₂ (0, 30, and 100 ppm) via drinking water from gestation through postnatal day 185 showed hippocampal AD-like pathology, disrupted FBXO40 expression, and enriched pro-inflammatory and senescent signatures. In vitro, FBXO40 knockdown exacerbated, whereas overexpression rescued, As-induced senescence and amyloidogenic markers. Mechanistically, FBXO40 prevents aberrant STING activation by ubiquitinating STAT1 for proteasomal degradation, thereby regulating endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD). The findings were validated in C57BL/6 J and ApoE4 transgenic mice exposed to NaAsO₂ (0, 0.5, and 50 ppm) for 36 and 24 weeks, respectively. Collectively, this study links As exposure to elevated AD risk under a gene–environment nexus and delineates a novel FBXO40/STAT1/ERAD/STING axis driving cellular senescence and AD pathogenesis, identifying the FBXO40–STING node as a potential intervention target for environment-associated neurodegeneration.

title: Coupling of acid-etched, stacked Ti microchannel cathodes and electron shuttles for enhancing Cr(VI) reduction
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yuchen Zhao, Lu Li, Sifan Zhang, Weilong Wang, Hongtao Yu
abstract: Electrochemical reduction may directly use cathodic electrons to detoxify Cr(VI). The bottleneck for improving efficiency is the electrostatic repulsion of cathodes to negatively charged Cr(VI) oxyanions. To overcome this bottleneck, this study reports an acid-etched, stacked Ti microchannel cathode (Ti-MC), enhancing Cr(VI) reduction through combining acid-etched Ti surface, stacked Ti-mesh microchannels, and NO3 −/NO2 − electron shuttles. After acid etching, the Ti mesh cathode exhibited a 2.3-fold increase in double-layer capacitance relative to pristine Ti mesh, consistent with an enlarged electrochemically accessible interface. After 120 s of polarization, the normalized fluorescence intensity inside Ti-MC was 3.30 times that near a single-layer Ti mesh, consistent with greater retention of the anionic tracer within the stacked cathode. During electrochemical Cr(VI) reduction over Ti-MC, Cr(VI) concentration decreased from 500 mg L−1 to below the discharge limit within 125 min. When the mass ratio of NO3 −-N/Cr(VI)-Cr was 6.7%, the residual Cr(VI) concentration was 45% of that without nitrate addition after 25 min. In the continuous-flow tests, the effluent Cr(VI) concentration remained below 0.5 mg L−1 for at least 380 h. Furthermore, a simple acid-washing process effectively mitigated cathode deactivation caused by Cr(III)-containing deposits covering Ti surface. These results demonstrate that Ti-MC is a promising cathode for the electrochemical treatment of Cr(VI)-containing wastewater.

title: Endophyte SaMR12 reduces tomato Cd accumulation and restores Sedum alfredii phytoextraction in tomato– Sedum alfredii intercropping
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Luyao Ma, Yinhua Ji, Weiwei Zhou, Haofeng Lv, Bin Liang, Ying Feng
abstract: The endophyte SaMR12 improves vegetable–Sedum alfredii Hance intercropping performance, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We established a hydroponic tomato–S. alfredii intercropping system with SaMR12 inoculation to elucidate the metabolic mechanisms involved. In tomato, intercropping expanded root length, surface area and tip number, accompanied by higher shoot and root Cd concentrations. SaMR12 inoculation reshaped tomato root architecture by decreasing root length and tip number while maintaining higher root diameter and volume, suggesting a smaller Cd-exposed absorptive interface and coinciding with reduced tomato Cd concentrations. In S. alfredii, intercropping suppressed biomass and shoot Cd concentration, whereas SaMR12 partially restored both traits. Untargeted metabolomics revealed species-specific root metabolic responses. In tomato roots, intercropping decreased trehalose and tagatose abundance and activated a Cd-associated stress response, with increased amino acid-, polyphenol- and flavonoid-related metabolites and elevated CAT, POD and PAL activities. SaMR12 partially returned sugar-related metabolites and reduced several amino acid- and phenolic-related responses while maintaining high antioxidant enzyme activities. In S. alfredii roots, SaMR12 increased citric acid and dihydrozeatin abundance, linking Cd tolerance and cytokinin-related growth regulation with restored biomass and shoot Cd accumulation. Therefore, these findings provide a mechanistic basis for validation and optimization of SaMR12-assisted tomato–S. alfredii intercropping under field conditions.

title: Composite source inputs and subsurface biochemical processes driving elevated ammonium in groundwater
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Fangyuan Cheng, Jingshuang Cui, Linyi Fan, Lijuan Yang, Fei Li, Jiao Qu, Wengeng Cao, Ya-nan Zhang
abstract: Groundwater ammonium-nitrogen (NH4 +-N) contamination threatens regional water resource security, yet its sources and formation mechanisms remain poorly constrained in resource-based regions. This study integrated stable isotopes, dissolved organic matter (DOM) molecular profiling, and microbial functional gene sequencing to elucidate the sources and formation mechanisms of NH4 +-N in a high-NH4 +-N aquifer in Songyuan, Jilin Province. Spatial analysis showed a localized NH4⁺-N enrichment pattern, while the pronounced decrease during the wet-season campaign likely reflected hydrological dilution together with changes in aquifer biogeochemical conditions. Stable-isotope signatures suggested multiple potential nitrogen sources, while local petroleum extraction activities could represent an additional anthropogenic influence. DOM molecular signatures showed that nitrogen-containing low-molecular-weight compounds accounted for 30–39% of DOM, identifying them as an important mineralizable nitrogen reservoir. Microbial community analysis identified Comamonadaceae as the most abundant bacterial family (23.59% on average), while metagenomic analysis revealed the presence of ammonification-related ure and ansA genes. Their positive associations with Comamonadaceae suggest the microbial community composition is associated with ammonification potential. Overall, the results indicate that groundwater NH4⁺-N enrichment reflects the coupled influence of multiple external inputs, DOM transformation, microbial ammonification potential, and reducing hydrogeochemical conditions, providing a mechanistic basis for groundwater nitrogen management in resource-intensive regions.

title: Amyloid fibril-ceramic membrane for efficient removal of lead from perovskite solar cells leachate
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yanxin Li, Chunhui Zhang, Peidong Su, Qiuqiong Wang, Xunchang Fei
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have attracted considerable attention due to their optoelectronic performance and technological advancements. However, Pb leaching from discarded PSCs into aquatic systems raises environmental concerns. Here, an amyloid fibril-ceramic membrane was fabricated on an Al2O3 ceramic substrate, with phytic acid acting as an electrostatic gelation agent to mediate the self-assembly of amyloid fibrils into a cross-linked surface network. Under optimized conditions, the membrane achieved a Pb2 + removal efficiency exceeding 99.9% in aqueous solution. When applied to actual PSC leachate containing competing metal ions (such as Cs+, Mg2+, K+, Na+, and Ca2+), it maintained a Pb2+ removal efficiency above 99%, demonstrating high selectivity with minimal interference. Molecular dynamics simulations and experimental characterization revealed that Pb2+ removal primarily relied on coordination and electrostatic interactions. Pb2+ exhibited more diverse coordination geometries and stronger electrostatic interactions with amyloid fibrils than competing ions, explaining the membrane’s selectivity. This study provides an efficient strategy for mitigating the environmental impact of discarded PSCs and advancing membrane materials for water purification.

title: Efficient oxygen cycle driven by strong V–O–Nb interactions for enhanced catalytic oxidation of chlorobenzene
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Shilong Li, Rongbing Nie, Qi Zhong, Xuan Wang, Zhengmao Cao, Xue Fang, Yu Xie, Mingzhi Wang, Jinyan Cao, Jianjun Chen, Qiulin Zhang, Ping Ning
abstract: Catalytic oxidation is a promising route for eliminating chlorinated volatile organic compounds, yet conventional V/TiO2 catalysts are often limited by insufficient oxygen activation and deactivation caused by intermediate accumulation. In this study, a Nb2O5-doping strategy is developed to construct strong V-O-Nb interactions that modulate the electronic structure of V species. The optimized 3V/Nb2O5-TiO2 catalyst achieved a T90 of 280 °C for chlorobenzene (CB) oxidation, a low activation energy of 49.9 kJ/mol, and significantly enhanced CO x (CO + CO2) yield and stability compared with pristine 3V/TiO2. A series of characterizations combined with theoretical calculations reveal that the strong V-O-Nb interaction not only facilitates the deep oxidation of CB via the formation of highly reactive oxygen species, but also enables Nb species to serve as an electron pool that suppresses electron localization of V active sites and promotes gaseous oxygen activation. The resulting highly efficient oxygen cycle enhances CB catalytic oxidization, and its broad applicability is further validated in toluene and CO catalytic oxidation reactions. This work provides mechanistic insights into the promotion effect of Nb2O5 and offers an effective catalyst design strategy for the abatement of carbon-containing pollutions via catalytic oxidation.

title: Deriving a proxy for highly reactive VOCs from satellite formaldehyde: Application to a Chinese megaregion
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Heng Yao, Saisai Chen, Fuhua Mao, Chunyan Zhou, Ruizhi Chen, Wei Wei
abstract: Formaldehyde (HCHO), a key volatile organic compound (VOC) oxidation intermediate, is a proxy for VOC reactivity, yet substituting ΩHCHO for VOCs is uncertain. We propose a novel satellite-based approach to estimate highly reactive VOCs (HRVOCs) over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region, a global HCHO hotspot, during July 2018–2022. Our approach first extracts secondary HCHO (ΩHCHO_SEC) by subtracting primary (ΩHCHO_PRI) and background (ΩHCHO_BACK) HCHO from ΩHCHO; then simulates the HCHO yield coefficient from HRVOCs using a box model considering composition, NOx, and meteorology; finally derives ΩHRVOCs via a steady-state equation for secondary HCHO. For July 2018–2022, ΩHRVOCs were 12.71–16.57 × 1015 molecules·cm−2 in urban areas, 2.42–5.41 × 1015 molecules·cm−2 in mixed areas, and 0.95–1.45 × 1015 molecules·cm−2 in vegetation areas. The retrievals show expected mechanistic relationships: ΩHRVOCs variation in vegetation areas correlates with temperature, and ΩHRVOCs exhibits a positive spatial association with surface ozone; uncertainty propagation shows CVs of ΩHRVOCs ranging from 23.26% to 43.64% across regions. This study bridges the spatial gap between surface VOC concentrations and space-based observations, offering novel insights into spatiotemporal quantification of VOCs.

title: Molecular fingerprint insights into microplastic‑derived dissolved organic matter mediating phosphate immobilization on microplastic‑goethite complexes
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiaojun Song, Jiannan Ding, Jiaxin Yang, Wen Jiang, Yi Peng, Hua Zou
abstract: Microplastic‑derived dissolved organic matter (MP‑DOM) is pervasive in aquatic systems, yet its polymer‑specific controls on nutrient cycling remain poorly understood. This study investigated orthophosphate adsorption on pre-synthesized MP-goethite complexes in the presence of MP-DOM leached from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polylactic acid (PLA). Batch experiments showed that MP-DOM competed with orthophosphate for goethite adsorption sites, with PET-DOM exerting a stronger inhibitory effect (60.0% adsorption reduction) than PLA-DOM (57.1%). Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry results revealed preferential depletion of lignin-, protein-, and lipid-like molecular formulas, reflecting distinct compositional traits: PET-DOM is enriched in carboxyl-rich protein and lipid components, whereas PLA-DOM is dominated by tannin-like and condensed aromatic constituents. Mechanistic fraction‑based tests confirmed that DOM components enriched in oxygen‑containing groups, potentially including carboxyl‑ and phenolic‑hydroxyl‑related structures, may exhibit stronger competitive effects for phosphate adsorption on goethite. Beyond site competition, MP-DOM reduces surface Fe(III) and induces goethite amorphization, with more significant mineral alteration under PET-DOM exposure. This study provides molecular‑level insights into how MP‑DOM alters phosphate retention in the sediments, highlighting that polymer‑driven MP‑DOM effects should be considered when assessing internal phosphorus loading in MP‑polluted aquatic systems.

title: Incense-derived particulate exposure impairs social behavior through suppression of Nptx2 in the amygdala
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ngoc-Anh-Thu Le, Zih-Chan Lin, Yen-Yue Lin, Chiang-Wen Lee, Hsin-An Chang, Miao-Ching Chi, Jian-Yu Chen, Yue-Ling Chen, Zhu-Qian Wen, Jian-Ting Hong, Yi-Chun Huang, Jyun-Yan Lu, Pei-Yi Wu, I-Lin Wu, Guo-Jen Huang, Kuo-Ti Peng, Yao-Chang Chiang, Cathy Chia-Yu Huang
abstract: Air pollution is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for neurological disorders. Incense burning, a widespread source of indoor pollution, generates complex mixtures of particulate matter and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). However, the mechanisms linking incense exposure to brain dysfunction remain unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of incense-derived particulates on brain function and behavior in mice. Mice were exposed to incense particulates of different sizes three times per week for 7 weeks. Incense exposure impaired social novelty preference without affecting sociability in both sexes, in the absence of robust neuroinflammatory responses. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses revealed downregulation of activity-dependent genes, including reduced Nptx2 and Fos mRNA and protein levels in the amygdala. This was accompanied by reduced AMPA receptor GluA4 expression in parvalbumin (PV) interneurons. In vitro exposure to representative PAHs suppressed Nptx2 expression, supporting a potential contribution of pollutant-associated PAHs to Nptx2 dysregulation. Finally, adeno-associated virus–mediated Nptx2 overexpression in the amygdala improved incense-induced deficits in social novelty preference. These findings identify amygdalar Nptx2 signaling as a potential neuronal mechanism linking incense-derived air pollution to social behavioral dysfunction.

title: Metagenomic and mineralogical evidence of microbial community restructuring across a natural radiological-geochemical gradient
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Rashmi Priya, Santosh K. Sahu, Owais M. Bhat, P.R. Vivek Kumar, Divyalakshmi Saini, Rohit Verma, Rakesh Shukla, Vinita Grover, Sangeeta J. Sartandel, Prateek Chandrani, Vinay Jain, Santosh K. Sandur, Deepak Sharma
abstract: Naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORM), including thorium and uranium, together with associated heavy metals, represent persistent environmental contaminants that exert chronic radiological and chemical stress on soil ecosystems. To investigate microbial adaptation under long-term exposure, we integrated mineralogical characterization with metagenomic-sequencing of monazite-rich soils from the High-Level Natural Radiation Area (HLNRA) of Kerala, India, spanning a natural radiation gradient of 0.6–150 mGy/year. Mineralogical analyses revealed enrichment of thorium and uranium with elevated titanium, aluminium and iron concentrations, while X-ray diffraction indicated lattice disorder in high-radiation soils. Despite > 1000-fold variation in radionuclide concentrations, microbial alpha diversity remained stable. However, significant community reorganization and species-level turnover were observed, although dominant bacterial phyla remained conserved. Fourteen species, including Egicoccus halophilus and Woeseia oceani, were positively associated with radiation dose, whereas 44 species linked to carbon degradation and nitrogen transformation were negatively associated. Functional profiling revealed shifts along the radiological-geochemical gradient. Taxa enriched in high-radiation soils were associated with aromatic-compound degradation, heavy-metal resistance and oxidative-stress tolerance. BacMet annotation identified resistance determinants for arsenic, copper, and oxidative stress-related compounds. These findings indicate that microbial community restructuring can occur without substantial changes in overall diversity across a natural radiological-geochemical gradient. The observed patterns provide insights into microbial resilience in NORM-contaminated environments.

title: Metabolomic bridges between selenium and schizophrenia: A mediation model uncovers potential metabolic pathways
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Lailai Yan, Yuanli Liu, Yuming Guo, Bing Cao
abstract: Lower selenium (Se) is associated with schizophrenia (SZ), yet metabolic pathways remain unclear. We tested whether lower serum Se relates to SZ via metabolic pathways and whether metabolites mediate this link. In 98 first-episode, drug-naive SZ patients and 99 healthy controls, serum Se was measured by ICP-MS and untargeted metabolomics by UHPLC-HRMS. Serum Se was lower in SZ (p 1) positive, indirect associations with SZ. These findings suggest a Se-metabolite-SZ axis spanning neurotransmitter, oxidative-stress, inflammation and energy metabolism. Given the cross-sectional design, these are statistical, not causal, mediations requiring validation. External Se was not measured, so these are candidate intermediate phenotypes, not environmental hazards; pairing soil, drinking-water and dietary Se with longitudinal metabolomics is warranted.

title: Mechanochemical construction of graphene-confined Fe 3 O 4 nanocomposites with interfacial electronic reconstruction for efficient Hg 0 capture from oxy-fuel combustion flue gas
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ziyao Yang, Lina Liu, Mantang Chen, Xuehui Sun, Cong Nie, Lin Du, Qingzhu Zhang, Yujin Tong, Yang Xu
abstract: Efficient removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) is often limited by the insufficient exposure of active sites and sluggish interfacial electron transfer in conventional sorbents. Herein, graphene-confined Fe3O4 nanocomposites (GCF) were mechanochemically constructed from graphite oxide and iron powder (Fe0) for Hg0 removal under oxy-fuel combustion conditions. During ball milling, graphite oxide was simultaneously exfoliated and reduced into graphene, while Fe0 was oxidized into Fe3O4 nanoparticles uniformly confined within the graphene layers. This nanoconfined architecture effectively suppressed Fe3O4 nanoparticle aggregation and strengthened the interfacial coupling between graphene and Fe3O4. The optimal Fe0/graphite oxide mass ratio and milling time were 2 and 13 h, respectively. Under these conditions, GCF exhibited high Hg0 removal performance and improved tolerance to SO2 and H2O. Mechanistic analyses revealed that Hg0 removal over GCF was mainly dominated by chemisorption, where Fe3+ and adsorbed oxygen species served as active sites. Density functional theory calculations revealed that spontaneous electron transfer from graphene to Fe3O4 induced interfacial electronic reconstruction, which modulated the electronic structure of Fe active sites and strengthened Hg0 adsorption. This work highlights the critical role of confinement-engineered interfacial electronic structures in enhancing Hg0 capture and provides a scalable strategy for designing advanced sorbents with regulated interfacial properties.

title: Aggregating nanoplastics transport with nonlinear attachment: Model evaluation against published experimental data
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Vasileios E. Katzourakis, Shadi W. Hasan, Maryam R. Al Shehhi, Ibrahim (Abe) M. Elfadel, Constantinos V. Chrysikopoulos
abstract: The established transport model of Katzourakis and Chrysikopoulos is extended to aggregating nanoplastics in water-saturated porous media under one dimensional flow. Nanoplastics may remain suspended or attach to the solid matrix through reversible and/or irreversible retention. To capture particle size evolution, the Smoluchowski population balance equation is coupled with the advection dispersion attachment equations, accounting for the effect of aggregate size on attachment and retention. The model was evaluated using published batch and column data for nanoplastics (10–30 mg/L) in seawater-saturated sea sand, including surface functionalized particles with humic acid and pristine particles with algae polysaccharides. Unlike conventional approaches that assume constant size colloids, the transport model is constrained by aggregation parameters derived independently from batch experiments and held fixed during fitting. The model also accounts for aggregation in the source container during injection, so the inlet particle size distribution may evolve with time. These extensions link the batch and transport experiments in one consistent framework. Aggregation can strongly influence breakthrough behavior, and information criteria comparisons with non-aggregating models showed that fixed size models may fail to reproduce complex breakthrough profiles. The model provides a more physically realistic basis for analyzing nanoplastic fate and transport in porous media.

title: Contrasting mechanisms of oxalic acid-activated manganese oxides for enhanced 17β-estradiol oxidation: Dissolved versus surface-complexed Mn(III)
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jun Wu, Shuang Liu, Shengpeng Zhang, Erdan Hu
abstract: Manganese oxides are ubiquitous oxidants in natural environments. While extensive research has centered on ligand-driven activation of highly reactive Mn(IV) phases, whether the less oxidizing Mn(III) minerals can be activated by natural ligands remains unknown. Here, we contrasted the oxidation of 17β-estradiol (E2) by δ-MnO2 (Mn(IV)) and Mn2O3 (Mn(III)) in the presence of oxalic acid (OX). In the δ-MnO2/OX system, reductive dissolution facilitated the release of a short-lived aqueous Mn(III)-OX complex, driving stepwise hydroxylation of E2. Conversely, the Mn2O3/OX system produced no soluble Mn(III) but formed a surface-bound >Mn(III)-OX complex via bidentate chelation (supported by FTIR and EXAFS), exhibiting a longer lifetime and promoting E2 dehydrogenation-hydroxylation and dimerization. Molecular orbital and electrochemical analyses revealed that these divergent pathways stem from the labile d 4 configuration of Mn(III) (Jahn-Teller active, fast ligand exchange) versus the inert d 3 state of Mn(IV) (electron transfer). Reactive Mn(III) generation was strongly pH-dependent, favored under acidic conditions but suppressed under neutral to alkaline conditions. Our findings challenge the conventional emphasis on Mn(IV) phases, demonstrating that Mn(III) minerals, long considered inert, can be effectively activated by ligands through surface complexation, thus expanding the understanding of organic pollutant attenuation in ligand-rich ecosystems.

title: An assessment of the annual effective dose rate due to radon inhalation from phosphogypsum stacks in the SW of Spain
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Israel Lopez-Coto
abstract: Phosphogypsum (PG) stacks in Huelva (SW Spain) cover ≈ 1000 ha less than 1 km from the city center, representing a potentially significant source of atmospheric radon (²²²Rn) due to ²²⁶Ra decay. This study quantifies the annual effective dose from radon inhalation to workers and surrounding populations using a conservative, climatological source term with a maximum exhalation rate of 1 Bq m⁻² s⁻¹, modulated monthly, coupled with Lagrangian atmospheric dispersion modeling for 2017. Doses were estimated using the UNSCEAR framework (with equilibrium factor = 0.8, dose conversion factor = 9 nSv (Bq h m⁻³)⁻¹, occupancy factor = 8760 h a−1). The annual mean radon concentration directly over the stacks was 2.9 Bq m⁻³, yielding a median effective dose of ≈ 170 μSv a⁻¹ for uncovered zones. For nearby towns (Huelva, Palos de la Frontera), mean stack contributions ranged from 0.15 to 0.60 Bq m⁻³, corresponding to median doses of 10–25 μSv a⁻¹. Maximum doses in any populated area remained below 50 μSv a⁻¹. All values are well below the ICRP public dose limit of 1000 μSv a⁻¹ and represent only a small fraction of the natural background radon dose (≈ 400 μSv a⁻¹). Reaching the public dose limit would require stack emissions 12–25 times higher. We conclude that while the Huelva PG stacks produce measurable local radon enhancements, their contribution to public and worker effective doses is modest, and total exposure to radon outdoors is dominated by natural background sources, even under conservative assumptions.

title: Visible-light-driven activation of free available chlorine via Fe(III)-mediated photochemistry for enhanced micropollutant abatement
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Limiao Cai, Bang Lan, Kejin Tang, Shaoxiong He, Jingyun Fang
abstract: The coupling of visible-light-driven Fe(III) photochemistry with free available chlorine (FAC) activation remains largely unexplored, despite the frequent coexistence of Fe(III) and FAC in engineered water systems. This study reveals enhanced micropollutant abatement through the coupling of visible light, Fe(III), and FAC. Carbamazepine (CBZ) removal increased from 40% to 92% within 15 min in the ternary system, with a kinetic-based synergy factor of 16.9 indicating substantial kinetic enhancement. The observed CBZ-associated photochemistry is consistent with a ligand-to-metal charge transfer pathway involving Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling and subsequent FAC activation, enabling complementary chlorine-mediated transformation and radical-mediated oxidation pathways. The enhanced degradation was further promoted by chloride addition, while effective performance was maintained at low natural organic matter concentrations. Screening of 41 coexisting pharmaceuticals and personal care products showed that 37 compounds achieved higher removal in the ternary system than in the best-performing binary system, with 19 exhibiting additional removal exceeding 20%. This study provides new insights into the coupling of pollutant-associated Fe(III) photochemistry with FAC activation and its potential for enhanced micropollutant abatement under acidic conditions.

title: Defect-electronic structure coupling in vanadium nitride enables rapid room-temperature NO 2 sensing
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ruihan Zhang, Jiaxin Li, Chonghui Zhu, Ji Li, Yuan Liang, Minghui Yang
abstract: Reliable room-temperature monitoring of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is crucial for environmental monitoring and public health. Transition metal nitrides offer an attractive platform for electrochemical gas sensing due to their high electrical conductivity and tunable defect chemistry. However, it is not yet fully understood how defect evolution induced by the nitridation process regulates the interaction between NO2 and the electrode. Here, we developed a vanadium nitride (VN) electrochemical sensor by controlling the nitridation temperature of the V2O5 precursor. The resulting samples were denoted as VN-500 ℃, VN-550 ℃, and VN-600 ℃, corresponding to nitridation temperatures of 500, 550, and 600 °C, respectively. The optimized VN-550 ℃ sensor generates a response current of 4.3 μA at a NO2 concentration of 50 ppm, with response and recovery times of 4.6 and 6.8 s, respectively. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses indicate that the optimized distribution of nitrogen vacancies and the surface coordination environment enhance NO2 adsorption and interfacial charge transfer, thereby promoting the surface activation and electrochemical reduction of NO2. These findings establish the defect-surface chemistry relationship governing NO2 sensing in VN and provide a rational strategy for designing high-performance room-temperature nitride-based gas sensors.

title: Mechanistic analysis of the neurotoxic effects of combined exposure to Bisphenol S and triclocarban in zebrafish
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qian Wang, Xiao Yang, Zhongjin Chen, Zhengzhang Xu, Ruoyi Peng, Ningyu Jiang, Ying Zhu, Jin Yan, Qiuhui Qian, Xuedong Wang, ZeJun Wang, Huili Wang
abstract: Triclocarban (TCC) and Bisphenol S (BPS) are widely coexisting endocrine-disrupting contaminants; however, the neurotoxic effects and underlying mechanisms of their combined exposure remain poorly understood. This study systematically investigated the neurotoxicity of single and combined TCC/BPS exposure at environmentally relevant concentrations in zebrafish. Integrated transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, and gene expression validation identified fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (KDR) as potential upstream molecular targets. Mechanistically, disruption of the FGFR3/KDR–MAPK/ERK–AP-1 signaling axis suppressed the expression of genes involved in neuronal differentiation and neurotransmitter synthesis, which was supported by pharmacological rescue with γ-linolenic acid (GLA). Multi-level analyses showed that TCC/BPS exposure impaired neuronal differentiation, inhibited neural progenitor cell proliferation, disrupted astrocyte development and blood–brain barrier integrity, and reduced monoamine neurotransmitter levels, ultimately leading to locomotor and cognitive dysfunction in adult zebrafish. Comparative transcriptomic analysis further revealed substantial overlap between TCC/BPS-responsive genes and Alzheimer's disease-associated molecular signatures, suggesting that chronic environmental exposure may increase susceptibility to neurodegenerative processes. Overall, this study identifies the FGFR3/KDR–MAPK/ERK–AP-1 axis as a candidate pathway in TCC/BPS-induced neurotoxicity, providing a framework for further investigation of coexisting phenolic contaminants.

title: Immunotoxicity of BHT in Manila clams ( Ruditapes philippinarum ): Pyroptosis pathways and mechanisms of hemocytes
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yaobing Li, Qilong Liao, Ruyue Ma, Xin Yu, Qiuhong Xu, Luqing Pan
abstract: Human activities have led to increasing levels of synthetic phenolic antioxidants (SPAs) in global environments. However, the immunotoxic mechanisms of SPAs in aquatic invertebrates remain unclear. This study established butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) exposure and co-exposure to BHT and Vibrio harveyi in Ruditapes philippinarum. BHT exposure inhibited the immune behavior of hemocyte phagocytosis and exocytosis, and significantly downregulated total hemocyte count, phagocytic rate, and antibacterial/bacteriolytic activities. Under BHT stress, reactive oxygen species and expression of antioxidant enzymes in clams' hemocytes initially decreased and then increased, resulting in significant DNA damage. Meanwhile, hemocyte pyroptosis signaling was activated under long-term BHT exposure, primarily involving ROS-mediated NF-κB/NLRP3 transcription and mitochondrial stress-induced NLRP3 inflammasome activation pathway. The expression of gasdermin E (GSDME) and ninjurin-1 (NINJ1) was significantly upregulated at the later BHT exposure period, accompanied by increased PI+ cell ratio, LDH release, and pro-inflammatory factor expression. After 15 days of BHT stress, the clams were challenged with V. harveyi. Hemocyte pyroptosis signaling was suppressed under 7-day co-exposure to BHT and V. harveyi, undermining immune defense levels and reducing survival rates. Our study elucidated the pathways and mechanisms of pyroptosis induced by SPAs in aquatic invertebrates, establishing a foundation for research on the immunotoxicity of SPAs.

title: Molecular complexity and cross-phase emissions during sludge wet oxidation
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jun Zhan, Fan Lü, Yuyao Xu, Yangbing Wei, Hua Zhang, Pinjing He
abstract: Release of particulate matter (PM) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) during sludge wet oxidation treatment raises concerns regarding atmospheric pollution. However, limited molecular level knowledge of these emissions constrains the development of effective control strategies. Here, the transformations and characterizations of organic matter across sludge, PM, and VOCs during the whole process in a full-scale plant were systematically investigated using ultrahigh resolution Orbitrap mass spectrometers. Wet oxidation transformed complex molecules into smaller, more hydrophilic, oxidized, and energetically constrained compounds. More than 80% compounds detected in PM samples were classified as intermediate-volatility organic compounds and semivolatile organic compounds. Subsequent dewatering increased the molecular richness and diversity of VOCs, and enhanced the abundance of CH-compounds. Molecular property analyses revealed phase dependent differentiation but molecular continuity, with stepwise decreases in molecular weight, aromaticity, and oxidation state from sludge to PM and VOC. Formula overlapped between sludge and PM suggests potential partitioning, whereas gas phase compounds originated from more selective volatilization of less oxidized, less aromatic, CHO-dominated species. Our work establishes a cross-media molecular framework for understanding air pollutant formation during sludge wet oxidation treatment and could provide a theoretical basis for optimizing sludge management technologies to minimize atmospheric pollutant emissions.

title: From disinfectants to endocrine disruptors: Unveiling the inhibitory potential of oxygenated benzalkonium analogues on gonadal 3β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases via enzyme kinetics analysis and computational simulations
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zulipiyamu Tuoheti, Mengyao Yin, Lubin Xie, Yang Zhu, Ping Duan, Ren-shan Ge, Linxi Li
abstract: Oxygenated benzalkonium analogues (OBAs) are ubiquitous disinfectants with poorly characterized endocrine-disrupting potential. Here, we assessed seven OBAs for inhibition of human 3β-HSD2 and rat 3β-HSD1, pivotal enzymes in progesterone biosynthesis. Four candidates (miramistin, methylbenzethonium, benzethonium, and benzoxonium) exhibited mixed/noncompetitive inhibition for substrate pregnenolone, with IC₅₀ values ranking 21.33, 22.16, 23.91, 36.77 μM against 3β-HSD2, and 6.54, 7.88, 9.40, 22.77 μM against 3β-HSD1, respectively. Miramistin and methylbenzethonium showed competitive inhibition against the NAD⁺ cofactor of 3β-HSD2. In intact KGN granulosa cells, active OBAs significantly suppressed progesterone secretion at 10 μM with negligible cytotoxicity. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that OBAs preferentially occupy the conserved NAD⁺-binding pocket, stabilized by hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic contacts. Furthermore, 3D-QSAR modeling identified lipophilicity and steric bulk as critical determinants of potency, while network toxicology linked OBA exposure to ovarian dysfunction pathways. Collectively, this work establishes a mechanistic paradigm for evaluating the endocrine risks of OBAs and offers structural insights for designing safer disinfectant alternatives.

title: Spatially heterogeneous linear covariation of arsenic- fluoride in the Yellow River, the world’s most turbid river: Isotopic insights
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Bailing Fan, Pei Dou, Xiangqin Yang, Wenjing Dai, Junwen Zhang, Zhiqi Zhao
abstract: Although the co-occurrence of arsenic (As) and fluoride (F) in low-quality groundwater has received considerable attention, their covariation and coupled transport mechanisms in large river systems remain poorly constrained. This study investigated the spatial distribution of As across the Yellow River Basin, clarified its geochemical associations with other hydrochemical constituents, and specially examined the As-F concentration relationship. By integrating multiple isotopic tracers (87Sr/86Sr, δ18O, δ34SSO4) with comprehensive hydrochemical data, we reveal the distinct geochemical behaviors of As and F and identify their controlling mechanisms. In comparison to the low concentrations of dissolved As in the Yellow River, As was significantly enriched in suspended particulate matter (SPM) with a mean contamination factor of 3.74. A linear yet spatially inconsistent As-F correlation was observed along the Yellow River mainstream: As concentrations correlate positively with F in the upper basin, whereas an inverse relationship occurs in the downstream.
