This spatial inconsistency arises from the non-conservative behavior of As, which is strongly regulated by adsorption onto suspended particulate matter (SPM) where Fe- and Al-bearing phases play a pivotal role. In contrast, groundwater discharge acts as an important contributor to the downstream geochemical evolution of F. The natural laboratory of "Jing-Wei River system" unambiguously demonstrates the critical role of SPM in As biogeochemistry and its negligible influence on F. The work highlights that trace elements covariations can provide critical insights into aquatic geochemical processes and the evolution of river water chemistry.

title: Stable antimony isotope and rare earth element fingerprinting of legacy mining in natural waters: Insights from an underground water management system in a former mining district of the Upper Harz Mountains, Germany
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Andreas B. Kaufmann, Sebastian Viehmann, Selina Hering, Moritz D. Wellisch, Felix Marxer, Wilfried Liessmann, Stefan Weyer, Dennis Kraemer
abstract: Legacy mining districts are important sources of metal contamination, yet tracing water sources and contaminant pathways remains challenging. We combine rare earth element and yttrium (REY) systematics with stable antimony (Sb) isotopes to investigate hydrogeochemical processes in the Upper Harz (Germany), a historic Zn-Pb and fluorite-barite mining district. Deep mine water from flooded workings shows elevated dissolved Fe concentrations, isotopically light Sb, and weak or absent shale-normalized Ce anomalies, consistent with potentially oxygen-depleted conditions. Along the drainage system, changes in Fe concentrations, REY patterns, and Sb isotope compositions indicate mixing, water-rock interaction, and secondary mineral formation. Primary Sb-bearing minerals show variable δ¹²³Sb values (0.11–1.16‰), whereas dissolved and suspended particulate Sb range from −0.07–0.77‰ at low dissolved Sb concentrations (0.03–1.15 μg L-1). Particulate Sb is isotopically heavier than coexisting dissolved Sb by up to 0.65‰, potentially reflecting temporally integrated Sb uptake rather than simple equilibrium adsorption. Three water types are distinguished: (i) meteoric dump-influenced drainage, (ii) ascending deep mine water, and (iii) mixed and subsequently hydrogeochemically modified drainage water. Together, REY signatures and Sb isotopes provide complementary information for water-mass fingerprinting, water-rock interaction, mixing and weathering processes in mining-affected catchments.

title: Multiple factors drive intermediate volatile organic compounds from construction machinery in China: From fresh emission to aged formation
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Cui Min, Yu Junyao, Zhuang Wanting, Fan Zhang, Yingjun Chen, Piao Zhe
abstract: Implementing control measures for non-road diesel machinery may significantly affect the formation and environmental impacts of intermediate volatile organic compounds (IVOCs). This study investigated multiple factors driving fresh and aged of IVOCs from 10 pieces of construction machinery. For diesel-fueled construction machinery, machine type, emission standard, engine load, and working mode all affected IVOCs emissions, with China IV machinery exhibiting a higher potential for aged IVOCs formation. This degree is set jointly determined by aging time, NOx level, and precursor concentration rather than by the emission standard alone. For the biodiesel blends, fresh IVOCs emission factors initially increased and then decreased with increasing biodiesel proportion, whereas aged IVOCs emission factors gradually decrease. The chemical composition of the IVOCs changed significantly after aging, with an unresolved complex mixture (UCM) accounting for 87.7% of the aged IVOCs and a shift toward long-chain, less volatile compounds. The 2022 national emission inventory indicates that the total aged IVOCs formation from biodiesel-powered machinery was only 7.07 Gg, which is much lower than that from diesel-powered machinery. Therefore, priority should be given to promoting biodiesel in high-emission regions and key scenarios such as construction sites and ports to maximize the emission reduction benefits.

title: Legacy arsenic- and antimony-bearing gold mine waste shapes the microbial community of Giant Mine sulfate-rich wetlands, promoting metal(loid) cycling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Hailey A. Jack, Carol J. Ptacek, David W. Blowes
abstract: Legacy As- and Sb-bearing wastes at mine sites contribute to long-term contamination of surrounding terrestrial and aquatic environments. The microbial communities in wetland sediments impacted by As- and Sb-rich fugitive tailings and airborne particles at the Giant gold mine were examined. Sediment and porewater samples were analyzed using aqueous and solid-phase geochemistry techniques, bulk As and S K-edge XANES, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing, and functional predictions. Four wetland sediments were impacted by legacy mine wastes, but each location exhibits distinct geochemical conditions and microbial communities. Sediment porewaters were circumneutral and moderately oxidizing, with elevated SO4 2- and variable Fe, As, and Sb concentrations. Synchrotron-based XANES analyses show co-occurrence of mixed oxidized and reduced As and S species, indicating sediment redox heterogeneity. Microbial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Bacteroidota, Thermodesulfobacteriota, Bacillota, Acidobacteriota, and Chloroflexota, with community structure varying with geochemical conditions. Metabolic functional predictions indicated element and metal(loid) cycling, demonstrating microbially mediated reactions within the wetland environments promote contaminant transformation, mobilization, and attenuation. Greater potential for sulfate reduction and sulfide generation was observed in sediments from the Foreshore Tailings Area and Northwest Tailings Containment Area, suggesting microbially mediated As and Sb immobilization as a potential bioremediation strategy at Giant Mine.

title: Ambient air pollution exposure before and during pregnancy and risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: A large cohort study in Sichuan, China
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ning Ma, Wangnan Cao, Jie Yin, Furong Wang, Chunrong Li, Shengzhi Sun
abstract: Evidence linking ambient air pollution to hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) remains inconsistent, particularly regarding exposure timing and pollutant mixtures. We examined associations between six air pollutants (O3, SO2, NO2, CO, PM2.5, and PM10) and HDP in a multi-center retrospective cohort of 1,330,109 singleton pregnancies in Sichuan, China (2013–2022). Residential exposures from 13 weeks before pregnancy through gestational week 20 were estimated using geocoded addresses and gridded pollution data. Multivariable logistic regression and quantile g-computation assessed predefined exposure windows; distributed lag nonlinear models (DLNMs) assessed weekly associations. For O₃, each interquartile range increase was associated with higher HDP risk during the 13-week pre-pregnancy period (OR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.29–1.42) and gestational weeks 1–4 (OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.26–1.34). The air pollution mixture was associated with increased HDP risk during the pre-pregnancy period (OR = 1.53, 95% CI: 1.46–1.60) and gestational weeks 1–4 (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.21–1.30). DLNM analyses indicated that exposure during several pre-pregnancy weeks was associated with increased HDP risk for all six pollutants, with associations during early gestation also observed for O₃, SO₂, and PM₂.₅. Overall, pre-pregnancy and early-gestation air pollution exposure was associated with higher HDP risk, with associations varying by pollutant and exposure window.

title: Trace xanthates in mining-impacted soils: Dispersive solid-phase extraction (DSPE)-LC-MS/MS method validation, matrix effects, and field evidence
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Hong-Lian Yu, Hai-Rong Chen, Yan-Wen Li, Yu Zhang, Hai-Ming Zhao, Quan-Ying Cai, Xiao-fei Tan, Hai-jun He, Ce-Hui Mo, Lei Xiang
abstract: Xanthates are widely used as collectors in mineral flotation, but their fate and risks in soils remain poorly understood because reliable analytical methods are lacking. Here, we developed a dispersive solid-phase extraction coupled with LC-MS/MS for simultaneous determination of ethyl, isopropyl and butyl xanthate (EtX, IpX and BuX) in soil. Analytes were extracted twice with 30% ammonia in methanol (4 + 4 mL, 8 min each) and cleaned up with 50 mg C18, achieving satisfactory extraction efficiency. Quantification was performed in negative ESI-MRM using the [ROCSS]⁻ precursor-to-product transition, while identification relied on the ion-intensity ratio of the RO⁻ product ion to its H₂-elimination fragment, improving selectivity of the analytes. The method showed good linearity (10–1000 μg/L, R² > 0.998), low detection limits (0.07–0.83 μg/kg), and recoveries of 62.5%-105.4% with RSDs < 10% across different soils. Matrix effects were associated with integrated soil-property gradients, requiring matrix-matched calibration to offset analytical interference. Field investigation revealed ongoing xanthate release in active mining areas and persistent residues in abandoned areas, implying profound impacts of xanthates in soil. The developed method provides an analytical basis for sensitive monitoring, risk assessment, and remediation evaluation of xanthates in mining-impacted soils.

title: Nile Red-positive submicron event burden in induced sputum is associated with eosinophilic inflammation and remodeling-related biomarkers in severe asthma
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Agnes Hernandez Biette, Leandro Tapia Barredo, Raquel Guillamat Prats, Ignasi Garcia Olive, Paula Goncalves Romeu, Jordi Petriz, Antoni Rosell Gratacos, Carlos Martinez Rivera
abstract: Human exposure to microplastics and nanoplastics has raised concerns about respiratory health, but evidence linking airway particulate signals to severe asthma remains limited. This cross-sectional study quantified Nile Red-positive submicron events in induced sputum from 32 patients with severe asthma and 11 healthy controls using chemical digestion, fluorescence staining, and flow cytometry. Clinical characteristics, inflammatory phenotypes, and immunological biomarkers were assessed. Nile Red-positive events were detected in all samples. Event burden per gram of sputum dry weight was higher in severe asthma than in controls in unadjusted analysis (median 3232 versus 1730 events/g; p = 0.042), but the association was not statistically significant after adjustment for age, body mass index, and smoking status (B = 0.364; p = 0.122). Among severe asthma phenotypes, eosinophilic T2 asthma exhibited the highest event burden. Positive correlations were observed with blood and sputum eosinophilia and with MMP-3, MMP-9, and PDGF-BB, biomarkers related to airway remodeling. However, Nile Red fluorescence does not establish polymer identity, and the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. These exploratory findings warrant confirmation using polymer-specific analytical methods and appropriately matched cohorts.

title: Phosphate-solubilising bacteria enhance Cd and Pb immobilisation using phosphate rock powder: Distinct regulation by pH and urea supply
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jinpeng Yu, Xirui Kang, Yan Zhang, Wenchi Guo, Yaping Li, Fei Han, Hui Wang, Hong Pan, Quangang Yang, Yanhong Lou, Yuping Zhuge
abstract: Phosphate rock powder (PR) effectively immobilises cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) in acidic soil but exhibits limited solubility under alkaline conditions. Phosphate-solubilising bacteria (PSB) may overcome this limitation by promoting PR dissolution. Herein, Bacillus megaterium (BM) and Bacillus subtilis (BS), two PSB, were evaluated using a 154-day pot experiment with wheat as well as shake-flask experiments across pH 4.0–7.0 and urea supplies of 22.5–90.0 mg/L to elucidate the synergistic Cd and Pb immobilisation mechanisms of PR–PSB and verify their remediation potential in weakly alkaline soil. Increased pH and urea supply enhanced Cd and Pb immobilisation by PSB–PR. Higher pH primarily strengthened weak-acid-extractable fraction, whereas increased urea supply favoured oxidisable fraction and residual fraction. Cd immobilisation was dominated by residual fraction (47.74%), whereas Pb immobilisation was driven by weak-acid-extractable fraction (35.05%) and oxidisable fraction (25.43%). In the pot experiment, BM–PR reduced soil-available Pb and Cd by 48.91% and 14.69%, respectively; lowered Cd and Pb concentrations in wheat shoots and roots; and increased shoot and root biomass by 36.35% and 39.08%, respectively. Thus, combined PSB–PR application is effective for Cd and Pb immobilisation in weakly alkaline soil.

title: Prevalence and transmission of the tet (X4) gene in Escherichia coli : A genomic and plasmidome study of isolates from food origin in Hunan, China
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jian-Chao Yuan, Ruan-Yang Sun, Yi-Han He, Heng Heng, Qin-Lu Lin, An-Ping Li, Bo Zhou, Xiao-Bo Liu, Jin-Wang Li, Sheng Chen
abstract: The dissemination of the tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) raises concerns about antimicrobial resistance along the food chain. We integrated genomic and plasmidome analyses of 151 tet(X4)-positive E. coli isolates recovered from food in Hunan, China, with 1160 publicly available NCBI genomes. Among the 1311 isolates, 75.90% originated from China, swine was the predominant host source (37.38%), and phylogroup A was most common (67.35%). Genomic analyses identified closely related isolates within and between Chinese provinces and across geographic regions and host sources, suggesting potential clonal dissemination rather than confirmed transmission. Phylogeographic reconstruction indicated greater inferred connectivity involving East and Southeast Asia than other regions within the available, geographically imbalanced dataset. Pan-genome analyses revealed regional differences in gene-family accumulation patterns, although these differences were attenuated after equal-size subsampling. Plasmidome analyses identified IncFIA(HI1)-IncHI1 and IncX1 as common tet(X4)-associated plasmid types. Conjugation experiments supported the transfer of tet(X4)-associated genetic material to E. coli EC600, while the association of tet(X4) with ISCR2 and the proximity of IS26 suggested potential involvement of mobile elements in its mobilization. These findings provide genomic insights into food-associated tet(X4)-positive E. coli and support broader food safety and One Health surveillance.

title: Preconceptional parental air pollution exposure and clinical pregnancy after assisted conception: Identifying parent-specific vulnerability windows and high-risk subpopulations
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jiahao Zhu, Jing Wang, Zhe Zhang, Huanzhuo Mai, Aijun Yang, Li Guo, Xianan Zhang, Guolei Niu, Yushuang Gao, Jiajia Wang, Qingtao Meng
abstract: The impact of ambient air pollution on clinical pregnancy following assisted conception and its parent-specific exposure windows remain unclear. We investigated 19,358 assisted conception cycles from 9943 couples in Shandong, China (2014–2024). Daily parental exposures to PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, and O3 were estimated at 1-km resolution during gametogenesis. Multilevel logistic regression assessed clinical pregnancy failure risk. Parental PM2.5, PM10, NO2, and SO2 exposures were associated with increased pregnancy failure risk, with NO2 showing the strongest adverse association (maternal adjusted odds ratio = 1.410, 95% confidence interval: 1.339–1.486 per 10 μg/m3 increase), whereas O3 exhibited an inverse association. Key sensitive exposure windows were identified at maternal days 180–86 (preantral follicle phase) and paternal days 69–15 (advanced sperm growth phase) prior to treatment. Susceptibility was heightened in couples undergoing in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection, those with secondary infertility, and parents aged ≥ 35 years. Preconceptional air pollution exposure is associated with compromised assisted conception outcomes, with susceptibility windows aligning with specific maternal and paternal gametogenesis stages. These observational findings support the potential relevance of preconception environmental counseling, although clinical benefits require prospective confirmation.

title: Can we justify the environmental and human health costs of reducing PFAS in drinking water? A life cycle assessment in Sweden
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Sabrina Altmeyer Mendes, Magdalena Svanström, Philip McCleaf, Lutz Ahrens, Gregory Peters
abstract: PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) contamination of drinking water is a critical environmental and public health concern. As regulations become more stringent, water utilities are increasingly evaluating treatment technologies to ensure safe drinking water supplies. This study applies life cycle assessment to compare five treatment trains for PFAS-contaminated groundwater, each including pre-treatment, PFAS removal, post-treatment and PFAS destruction steps. Beyond traditional LCA, a net human health benefit (NHHB) approach is developed and tested to capture health impacts not reflected in traditional LCA. NHHB assesses whether the avoided PFAS-related human health impacts achieved through water treatment outweigh the life cycle impacts induced by treatment systems operations. For NHHB, characterization factors (CF) based on rodent and epidemiological studies are calculated and applied to estimate human lifetime cancer and non-cancer effects from PFAS ingestion. PFAS removal was generally the main driver of overall impacts, while pre- and post-treatment were also substantial contributors in some systems. Closed-circuit membrane filtration showed the highest impacts across most categories, while the relative performance of the other systems varied by impact category. NHHB results are highly sensitive to the CF choice. With rodent-based CFs, treatment burdens outweigh benefits, while epidemiological CFs indicate net health benefits. Although treatment reduces exposure, it shifts impacts upstream via energy, chemicals, and materials production. This burden-shifting raises environmental justice concerns, as the populations receiving the health benefits of cleaner drinking water may differ from those bearing treatment-related impacts. These findings suggest that prioritizing policy changes by enforcing comprehensive restrictions on PFAS may be more sustainable than relying on downstream water treatment.

title: Engineering the electronic structure of LaCoO 3 nanofibers via Cu doping for efficient electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Bingyan Shi, Mingze Xia, Siqi Zhang, Cheng Fan, Shengji Tian, Chade Lv, Xiaofeng Lu
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) to ammonia is a promising alternative to the Haber-Bosch process, but suffers from slow kinetics, complex mechanism, and competing reactions. In this work, B-site Cu-doped LaCoO3 (ABO3-type) perovskite nanofibers (NFs) are successfully fabricated through a high-voltage electrospinning-calcination technique for NO3RR. The optimized 5% Cu-LaCoO3 NFs catalyst exhibits an outstanding Faradaic efficiency (FE) amounting to 98.7 ± 0.5% under –0.483 V vs. RHE. An NH3 generation rate of 27.6 ± 0.6 mg cm⁻2 h⁻1 is recorded at –0.683 V vs. RHE, significantly exceeding that of pristine LaCoO3 NFs. Moreover, when employed as the cathode in an assembled aqueous cell, the catalyst delivers a peak power density of 5.58 mW cm⁻2 and shows reasonable long-term charge-discharge stability. Through physicochemical analyses and density functional theory (DFT) computations, it is demonstrated that substituting Cu at the B‑site of LaCoO3 enhances orbital mixing between Cu 3d and O 2p states, tunes the adsorption behavior of Co, and modifies the electronic configuration of LaCoO3, thereby lowering the activation barrier for NO3RR. This work presents an innovative strategy for designing advanced electrocatalysts capable of both NH3 electrosynthesis and power generation, offering a promising route toward sustainable energy conversion.

title: Biochar and melatonin alleviate antimony toxicity in sesame through coordinated regulation of photosynthesis and rhizosphere microbiota
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Muhammad Umair Hassan, Dai Zhenlin, Waqar Ahmed, Muhammad Talha Aslam, Tahir Abbas Khan, Zhang Man, Faizah Amer Altihani, Shifaa O. Alshammari, Su Qitao
abstract: Biochar (BC) and melatonin (MT) are recognized as important amendments for mitigating metal and metalloids toxicity, but the effects of combined MT and BC in mitigating antimony (Sb) toxicity remain unexplored. This study examined the effects of BC and MT in mitigating Sb toxicity in sesame. The study included the following treatments: T1; control, T2; Sb stress (100 mg kg−1), T3; Sb stress + MT (100 µM), T4; Sb stress + BC (2%), and T5; Sb stress + BC (2%) + MT (100 µM). Antimony decreased sesame growth and yield while BC + MT enhanced sesame growth and yield (48.71%) by improving photosynthetic pigments (chlorophyll-a: 63.15%, and chlorophyll-b: 62.19%), antioxidant activities (50.99% average), soil nutrients availability (TN, AP, AK: 41.16% average), and decreasing soil Sb availability. Biochar + MT also up-regulated chloroplast organization, polysomal ribosome function, cell wall organization and biogenesis, 6-phosphogluconolactone activity, methionine biosynthetic processes, and photosynthetic electron transport in photosystem I. These transcriptomic patterns were associated with better growth under Sb stress. In addition, BC + MT increased the abundance of Chloroflexota and Acidobacteriota and altered the complexity of the bacterial co-occurrence network. These results demonstrate that the combined application of BC and MT offers an effective strategy to mitigate Sb toxicity in sesame.

title: Shared anthropogenic drivers of nitrate and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons: Implications for terrestrial-aquatic source tracing and integrated watershed management
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zihan Zhao, Jiayu Zhao, Hao Sun, Xueyi Yuan, Wenhao Li, Zucong Cai, Yanhua Wang
abstract: Nitrate (NO3 −) contamination in surface water and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in soil pose environmental challenges in the rapidly urbanizing upstream watershed of Taihu Lake. However, pollutants are commonly investigated independently, limiting understanding of their shared anthropogenic controls. Here, isotopic analysis, Bayesian mixing models, receptor modeling, and risk assessment were integrated to investigate aquatic NO₃⁻ and soil PAHs across three contrasting river-network regions. NO3 − concentrations peaked in the industrial-agricultural area (TGRA; 1.81 ± 0.33 mg L−1), followed by the agricultural lakeside area (LRA) and highly-urbanized area (CDRA). Soil ΣPAH16 concentrations exhibited spatial heterogeneity, ranging from 989.14 to 8184.38 ng g−1, with the highest value observed in the TGRA. Beyond co-occurrence, aquatic NO3 − and soil PAHs exhibited regionally corresponding source profiles, indicating overlapping anthropogenic pressures across environmental compartments. Fertilizer-derived NO3 − (66.0% ± 13.8%) and coal/coke combustion-derived PAHs dominated the TGRA, which exhibited the poorest water quality and highest ecological and health risks. In LRA, manure-derived NO3 − (72.1% ± 16.8%) and biomass-burning PAHs predominated, whereas the CDRA was characterized by mixed NO3 − sources and traffic/petroleum-related PAH. Soil erosion further provided a potential terrestrial-aquatic linkage for PAH transport. These findings highlight the value of cross-media source tracing for integrated, region-specific watershed pollution management.

title: Microbial and geochemical controls on selenium methylation and volatilization by bacteria from Hg–Se contaminated paddy soils
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qingqing Wu, Hua Zhang, Chaofa Chen, Haiyan Hu, Chuanyu Chang, Kang Mao, Xuefeng Yang, Baolin Wang, Kevin Bishop
abstract: Selenium (Se) is essential at trace levels but can become hazardous when accumulated in mining-impacted soils. Microbial Se volatilization offers a potential remediation strategy, but its efficacy under mercury (Hg)–Se cocontamination remains uncertain. We compared Se(IV) methylation among 20 aerobic bacterial isolates from Hg–Se-impacted paddy soil in Wanshan and examined the effects of Se loading, temperature, sulfur species, and Hg coexposure in Aeromonas hydrophila D15. All isolates produced dimethyldiselenide (DMDSe) as the only detected volatile methylated species, with recovered amounts varying by approximately 86-fold. In independent D15 experiments, DMDSe production responded nonlinearly to Se(IV), was inhibited by sulfate, and was stimulated by 0.01 mM methionine. At 37 °C, DMDSe production decreased by 87% relative to 30 °C. Hg and Se coexposure at a molar ratio of 2:1 reduced recovered DMDSe by 98% and coincided with Hg–Se-rich particles whose XRD features were compatible with an HgSe-like phase. These observations motivate a testable, non-exclusive hypothesis that Hg-associated solid formation may compete with microbial Se volatilization for transformed Se, while direct metabolic inhibition remains possible. The findings identify factors constraining Se volatilization in controlled bacterial cultures and a potential trade-off between volatile and solid Se products, informing evaluation of remediation strategies for Hg–Se-cocontaminated soils.

title: Biofilm-mediated accumulation and release of microplastics and nanoplastics in potable water pipes: experiments and kinetic modeling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Atif Bashir, Dibya Kanti Datta, Chao Luo, Binbin Wang, Maryam Salehi
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) are increasingly detected in tap water; however, the role of biofilms in their retention and release within premise plumbing remains poorly understood. This study investigated the accumulation and release of polystyrene MPs (15 µm) and NPs (500 nm) in 15-month biofilm-laden and initially virgin PEX-A pipes under flow and stagnant conditions. Significantly more MPs accumulated on biofilm-laden pipes. After 48 h accumulation under flow, MP loading was 4.7 ± 0.3 versus 2.9 ± 0.2 µg/cm2 on biofilm-laden and initially virgin pipes, respectively; the corresponding 120 h cumulative release fractions were 45.3 ± 4.3% versus 92.1 ± 8.1%, indicating enhanced retention by the heterogeneous biofilm matrix despite unfavorable electrostatic interactions. In contrast, NPs accumulated more on initially virgin pipes, while a greater fraction of retained NPs was released from biofilm-laden pipes. Thus, MPs and NPs exhibited contrasting accumulation and release behaviors, although interactions between particle populations cannot be excluded. Greater MP accumulation was found under flow and greater NP accumulation under stagnation exposure conditions. Langmuir attachment–detachment and multi-rate release models reproduced the observed accumulation and release trends and provided a quantitative framework for comparing particle–surface interactions across pipe and hydraulic conditions.

title: Oxygen vacancy-rich iron cathode for efficient degradation of polylactic acid microplastics via electro-Fenton
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ting Wu, Yilin Zhao, Mengxue Liu, Xiaoping Li, Yangzhi Liu, Xiaohan Du, Wangbo Wang, Zhihua Li, Weihuang Zhu
abstract: Electro-Fenton technology is widely used to remove aquatic organic pollutants, but its feasibility for microplastic remediation remains underexplored. Herein, a low-cost AFe-OV cathode enriched with oxygen vacancies and Fe-P/Fe-O active sites was fabricated through the calcination of ferrous precursors pre-reduced by crude tea extract. The as-prepared cathode achieved outstanding performance in polylactic acid microplastics (PLA-MPs) degradation. Such superior performance stems from the lowered energy barriers for cathodic hydrogen peroxide adsorption and activation, which facilitates high-yield hydroxyl radical (•OH) formation. This led to the reduced particle size, enhanced hydrophilicity, decreased molecular weight, and lower negative zeta potentials of PLA-MPs. The constructed electro-Fenton system efficiently removed aqueous PLA-MPs over a wide pH range, with maximum removal efficiencies reaching 91.2% and 96.5% at pH 3.0 and 9.0, respectively. Investigation results revealed that PLA-MPs degradation involved the synergistic hydrolysis and oxidation, with ester bond hydrolysis predominant in alkaline environments and •OH-driven oxidation prevailing under acidic conditions. Meanwhile, the microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter exhibited negligible acute, chronic biotoxicity, and phytotoxicity. This study develops a simple and efficient vacancy-engineered electro-Fenton approach for removing biodegradable microplastics, and offers in-depth insights into the effects of cathodic generated reactive oxygen species on microplastic transformation and degradation.

title: Indigenous functional microbiome-augmented bagasse-biochar composite drives carbon metabolism for detoxification and ecological remediation of rare earth tailings
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Haipeng Yang, Yang-Guo Zhao, Xiangyu Yang, Zeyun Cui, Jiale Wang
abstract: Rare earth element (REE) tailings are characterized by extreme acidity, high ammonia toxicity, and severe organic matter deficiency. These harsh conditions intrinsically hinder ecological remediation and preclude the colonization of traditional exogenous microbial inoculants. To overcome this bottleneck, we engineered a biochar-bagasse-microbiome (BBM) composite. Specifically, an indigenous microbiome was directionally enriched from tailing soils and homogeneously mixed with a bagasse-biochar matrix for stable colonization. The composite was subsequently applied to REE tailings in phytoremediation trials. Results demonstrated that the BBM amendment effectively ameliorated the hostile soil microenvironment, elevating soil pH, organic matter, and available phosphorus, while reducing ammonia toxicity. Concurrently, it activated key soil enzymes governing C, N, and P cycling. Consequently, this habitat restoration promoted ryegrass (Lolium perenne) growth. The treatment enhanced seedling emergence and biomass accumulation, while reducing plant malondialdehyde (MDA) content to mitigate oxidative stress. Correlation analyses elucidated robust covariation patterns linking physicochemical detoxification, microecological activation, and plant physiological enhancement. Finally, economic evaluations indicate a low application cost of 1.62–2.70 $·m−2. This suggests strong potential for field-scale remediation, pending long-term in situ validation.

title: Modeling brake wear particle emissions under diverse driving conditions: A data-driven time-series approach
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Changyu Wang, Xin Wang, Jianwei Tan, Lijun Hao, Aihong Li, Wanyi Chen, Yitu Lai, Sheng Su, Yachao Wang, Yunshan Ge
abstract: With the forthcoming Euro 7 regulation, the representativeness of brake particle emissions measured under the WLTP-Brake cycle has received increasing attention. In this study, two pad materials from different vehicles were tested on a brake dynamometer under multiple driving conditions. Although PM10 emissions under the WLTP-Brake cycle complied with the regulatory limit, exceedances occurred under other conditions. Variations in PN emissions among cycles reflected the cumulative effects of preceding brake events, indicating strong temporal dependence. Machine-learning models were therefore developed to predict PN emissions and identify influential brake features. Under time-series inputs, the Transformer achieved the best predictive performance, with an R2 of 0.85 ± 0.03, while XGBoost also showed acceptable accuracy. SHAP analysis showed that high-emission tests were mainly associated with positive contributions from temperature and brake power, whereas low-emission tests were characterized by negative contributions from features such as vehicle speed. Speed was positively related to PN emissions, and brake power amplified its influence. Overall, the proposed approach enables brake particle emissions to be evaluated under diverse driving conditions and may support future brake-emission assessment and regulation.

title: Phosphate-solubilizing fungus synergistically promotes Cr(VI)–pyrene transformation and nutrient cycling to drive ecological recovery in co-contaminated soil
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jiajie Wang, Tao Jin, Liping Wang, Wenjie Chen, Xiang Yan, Ruirui Qu, Simin Huang
abstract: Phosphate-solubilizing fungi offer a promising strategy for the ecological restoration of heavy metal–polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon co-contaminated soils, yet their role in coupling contaminant transformation with nutrient cycling remains unclear. A 42-day incubation experiment was conducted to investigate the effects of Talaromyces verruculosus PF1 on Cr(VI)–pyrene transformation, soil properties, indigenous microbial communities, and C–N–P cycling. PF1 decreased the proportion of Cr in the acid-soluble/exchangeable fraction (F1-Cr) from 38.93% to 0.85% and increased pyrene removal to 66.38%. Soil available P reached 80.21 mg/kg, 2.12-fold that of the control, while dissolved organic C, hydrolyzable N, and enzyme activities also increased. Microbial community composition changed substantially, accompanied by the enrichment of functional taxa associated with aromatic degradation and Cr detoxification. Metagenomic analysis further revealed enhanced reductive Cr(VI) detoxification, characterized by increased chrR and azoR abundances and enhanced antioxidant capacity. Genes associated with pyrene degradation indicated greater potential for salicylate–catechol metabolism. Meanwhile, C–N–P cycling functions were also altered, with alleviated P limitation, enhanced organic C degradation, reduced nitrification, and strengthened nitrate reduction potential. These findings demonstrate that PF1 promotes synergy between contaminant attenuation and nutrient cycling, offering an attractive approach for the ecological restoration of co-contaminated soils.

title: Desulfurization mechanisms and sulfur re-fixation in simulated lead-zinc mixed ores during roasting under gas diffusion constraints
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiaolong Zhao, Yonggang Wei, Chen Zhao, Shiwei Zhou, Bo Li, Yongxing Zheng, Hua Wang
abstract: Efficient utilization of complex lead-zinc mixed ores requires a clear understanding of sulfur transformation pathways to control residual sulfur. This study elucidates the sulfur pathways and gas-diffusion constraints determining desulfurization depth during roasting. Thermodynamic calculations and a gas-diffusion model were verified by roasting experiments using the ZnS–PbSO4 system under air and argon. At a 0.5:1 ratio, vigorous interaction occurred at 900 °C. The low-melting PbO–PbSO4 eutectic melt promoted mass transfer and SO2 escape. By 1000 °C, the desulfurization rate reached 99.22% under air, forming metallic Pb and ZnO. Gas release expanded the pore size to 51.63 nm, with Knudsen number (K n ) dropping to 2.83, placing the system in the transition diffusion regime. At a 2:1 ratio, excess ZnS was converted into network-like aggregates of refractory ZnO microcrystals which shrank the pore size below 16 nm. This structural change confirmed the diffusion model prediction, driving gas transport into the Knudsen regime (K n = 14.19) and building up an internal SO2 pressure of 0.084 atm. Excess ZnS and high local sulfur potential drove secondary sulfur fixation via solid-state exchange and reverse gas-metal interaction, lowering desulfurization to 57.29%. Mass balance confirmed zero Zn volatilization, while Pb loss ranged from 12.59% to 49.13%. With 30 wt% gangue (CaO + SiO2), the 0.5:1 ratio maintained 87.95% desulfurization and suppressed Pb loss to 4.01%, whereas 2:1 raised Pb loss to 25.57%. These findings improve the understanding of sulfur transformation and diffusion limitations during roasting of mixed sulfide-oxide lead-zinc ores.

title: Comparative ecotoxicity of aluminium-based galvanic anodes and impressed current on the Pacific oyster ( Crassostrea gigas ) larvae: A dose-response study
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Nesrine Zitouni, Katherine Costil, Jean-Luc Boudenne, Bruno Coulomb, Gaël Martin, Matthieu Dussauze, Antoine Serpentini, Christelle Caplat
abstract: Cathodic protection through aluminium-based galvanic anodes (Al-GACP) or impressed-current cathodic protection (ICCP) are widely used to prevent corrosion of submerged steel structures in seawater. These processes release cocktail of compounds, whose impact on the surrounding environment remains poorly documented. In this study, the effects of the metal cocktail released by Al-GACP and of by-products formed by the ICCP system were assessed in Crassostrea gigas oyster D-larvae. The ICCP released chlorination and bromination by-products, such as trihalomethanes, haloacetonitriles, and haloaldehydes. Both cathodic protection systems induced dose-dependent responses on embryonic development and larvae unable to develop normally at concentrations above thresholds of 117 to 187 μg L⁻¹ for Al-GACP, and with the slightly diluted (1.6-fold) stock solution of by-products for the ICCP produced after 4 h under non-renewed water conditions. Embryotoxicity tests further demonstrated interindividual variability in the sensitivity of C. gigas broodstock to Al-GACP, with an EC50 ranging from 63.4 to 110 μg L−1. These preliminary results highlight the need for further research on the ecological effects of chlorination byproducts (generated by the ICCP system) in ecotoxicological studies, in order to strike the right balance between decisions regarding the protection of offshore structures against corrosion and the conservation of marine wildlife.

title: Tracking antibiotics in farmed bullfrogs and their culture environment across different aquaculture systems through multiphase monitoring and toxicokinetic modelling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Wang Qian, Shi Hanyang, Fan Jiahang, Huang Yupeng, Wen Luting, Li Juan-ying
abstract: The bullfrog (Lithobates catesbeianus) is an important aquaculture species in China, and antibiotics might be used in its production. A two-compartment toxicokinetic model incorporating full-cycle monitoring of antibiotics was used to quantify the bioaccumulation in bullfrogs from industrial, traditional, and ecological farms. The toxicokinetic model estimated that feed-associated exposure contributed 89.9% of the antibiotic burden in the industrial farm case, followed by waterborne exposure (7.3%). In the traditional farm case, the estimated contributions of feed, water, and solid-phase exposure were 71.8%, 19.2%, and 9.0%, respectively. The corresponding estimated contributions in the ecological case were 65.7%, 28.0%, and 6.3%. The culture environment affected antibiotic bioaccumulation in the bullfrogs. A system-level mass balance was estimated to resolve the sources and fates of antibiotics in different culture environments. The results indicated that influent water was the dominant source in the culture environment (56.6–98.3%), while effluent discharge (56.7–91.9%) and dissipation (5.6–42.5%) were the main pathways of removal. Overall, regulations for feed quality and influent water quality should be prioritized. Microbial based remediation is also a potential option for the industrial and traditional farms. In the ecological farm, the antibiotics were removed by natural dissipation, minimizing their dietary risk.

title: Novel swirl core nozzle enhances atomization and suppresses hazardous byproducts of next-generation fire extinguishing agents
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhilei Yu, Junchao Zhao, Haibin Dong, Song Lu, Guohui Li, Xuelei Xian, Heping Zhang
abstract: Efficient delivery of high-boiling-point fire extinguishing agents requires effective atomization at low operating pressures while limiting hazardous combustion byproducts. Numerical simulations and experiments compared nozzles with identical external dimensions but different internal swirl core geometries. Atomization was evaluated at 0.3–0.6 MPa, with three independent replicates at each pressure. The turbine vane Type C nozzle provided the best combination of flow uniformity and atomization, achieving a mean D0.5 of 210.370 μm at 0.6 MPa. Across the tested pressures, mean D0.5, D0.9, and D0.99 were 268.73, 412.94 and 554.93 μm, respectively, representing reductions of 31.6%, 28.4% and 28.4% relative to Type A. The conventional Rosin–Rammler model poorly represented the coarse tail of measured droplet size distributions. Recalibration using zero-intercept least-squares regression in logarithmic coordinates yielded D0.99/D0.5 = (D0.9/D0.5)1.73, increasing R² from 0.867 to 0.963. In fire-suppression tests at 0.6 MPa, Type C reduced the peak carbon monoxide (CO) concentration by 35.3% compared with Type A, and reduced thermal exposure near the fire. These results demonstrate that internal swirl-core redesign improves atomization and mitigates combustion hazards under the tested conditions. The turbine vane core offers a promising architecture for improved delivery efficiency and hazard control performance of high-boiling-point fire extinguishing agents.

title: Combining target and nontarget screening to reveal PFAS contamination profiles and health risks in aquatic products
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Shuai Wu, Xiao Liu, Shuang Liu, Dawei Chen, Jianwen Li, Sheng Wen, Jiaying Liu
abstract: Despite global restrictions reducing legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), the prevalence of emerging alternatives continues to escalate. This study employed target and nontarget screening to assess PFAS in market aquatic products from Hubei Province, China. A total of 41 PFAS were detected, 15 with detection frequencies (DF) > 50%, with the ∑15 PFAS concentration ranging from 1.07 to 49.2 ng/g dry weight (dw). Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) was the most abundant, with a geometric mean (GM) concentration of 2.55 ng/g dw, accounting for 54% of ∑15 PFAS. Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA; GM concentration: 0.38 ng/g dw) exhibited higher contamination than perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (NTf2; GM concentration: 0.015 ng/g dw), an emerging PFAS used in lithium-ion batteries, showed high DF. Monte Carlo simulation-based dietary exposure model indicated children aged 3–6 and 7–12 years had significantly higher estimated daily intake (EDI) of ∑15 PFAS than other age groups, and their median EDI of ∑PFOA + PFNA + PFHxS + PFOS via aquatic products exceeded tolerable daily intake. For the general population, the median risk quotient of perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA) was 50. Of the 15 highly detected PFAS, 8 still lack reference doses for risk assessment.

title: Systemic coordination underpins wheat cultivar-specific tolerance to oxytetracycline: A multi-omics perspective
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiaojun Wu, Songyan Wei, Gan Li, Weihua Ding, Hao Jiang, Tiezhu Hu, Xiangdong Chen, Zhengang Ru
abstract: Oxytetracycline (OTC) readily accumulates in agricultural soils, threatening wheat productivity and food safety; however, the mechanisms underlying cultivar-specific OTC tolerance remain unclear. In this study, we used the relatively tolerant cultivar Bainong 4199 (BN) and the relatively sensitive cultivar Yannong 21 (YN) as experimental materials. Integrating phenotypic, physiological, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, we elucidated the differential regulatory mechanisms underlying their responses. OTC primarily inhibited root growth in both cultivars, more strongly in YN, whereas BN showed hormetic shoot stimulation at low OTC concentrations. In both cultivars, reactive oxygen species and malondialdehyde levels increased with increasing OTC concentration. Multi-omics suggested YN had less concordant cross-omics patterns, while BN maintained coordinated regulation of energy, protein, antioxidant, and secondary metabolism. Specifically, BN showed greater citrate accumulation with coordinated glycolysis-TCA upregulation, likely supplying intermediates for protein repair and defense. Under stress, energy compensation was limited, with skewed secondary metabolites and reduced signaling-metabolism coupling, potentially contributing to cellular damage. Multi-omics analyses revealed that OTC tolerance in the two tested cultivars involved multi-layered metabolic coordination, not single-pathway activity. This study characterizes cultivar-specific adaptive strategies, offering insights into assessing antibiotic risks in farmland, breeding OTC-tolerant wheat, and safe crop production in contaminated soils.

title: Graphitic nitrogen dominates direct electron transfer in peracetic acid activation by nitrogen-doped biochar: Revealing the structure-activity relationship
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhuoran Li, Hongxuan Chu, Kaitian Zhang, Yue Lei, Ruiyong Feng, Kaige Li, Liang Hao, Jianhua Qu, Ying Zhang
abstract: Peracetic acid (PAA) activation using carbon-based catalysts has emerged as a promising strategy for water purification, however, the structure-activity relationship governing non-radical oxidation remains unclear. Herein, nitrogen-doped biochar (NBC) was developed to activate PAA for 2,4-dichlorophenol (2,4-DCP) removal. The optimized N1BC800/PAA system achieved 96.8% removal with a k obs value of 0.141 min−1. Through quenching experiments, in situ Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical characterization, and density functional theory calculations, it was demonstrated that the direct electron transfer (DET) mediated by the N1BC800-PAA* complex was the main pathway for 2,4-DCP removal. The relative fraction of graphitic N content correlated strongly with ln k obs (R 2 = 0.9038), indicating that graphitic N was the key structure that mediated the DET process. Conversely, the relative fraction of -COOH content had a highly negative correlation with ln k obs (R 2 = 0.9533), since excessive -COOH suppressed the interactions between the catalyst and PAA, thereby hindering the formation of surface-complex and DET process. N1BC800/PAA system retained more than 80% 2,4-DCP removal across pH 5.1–10.8 and resisted common anions and real-water matrices, while preferentially oxidizing electron-rich contaminants. This study reveals how surface structure governs PAA-mediated DET process and provides molecular-level guidance for direct catalysts design and selective water purification.

title: Linoleic acid secreted by maize root system regulates endophytic bacterium Serratia sp. NS8: Enhances nicosulfuron degradation by upregulating dadA and katG
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Kuo Liu, Yulin Wu, Yubo Ding, Fuqiang Guo, Qibing Yan, Donghui Liu, Hao Zhang
abstract: Nicosulfuron residues threaten maize growth and ecological sustainability, whereas plant–endophyte-mediated remediation represents a promising strategy, but the regulatory mechanisms linking host metabolites and bacterial degradation remain poorly understood. Here, an endophytic bacterium Serratia sp. NS8 was investigated to elucidate the interaction between maize metabolic responses and bacterial degradation of nicosulfuron. Metabolomic analysis revealed that nicosulfuron stress induced metabolic reprogramming in maize roots and promoted linoleic acid accumulation. Chemotaxis assays and functional analyses demonstrated that linoleic acid enhanced NS8 chemotactic response and promoted D-amino acid metabolism by upregulating dadA, thereby improving nicosulfuron transformation efficiency. Heterologous expression and enzymatic characterization further confirmed that KatG participated in nicosulfuron degradation through sulfonylurea bridge cleavage, producing an ASDM-like transformation product. In planta experiments showed that NS8 inoculation reduced nicosulfuron residues, alleviated oxidative stress, and improved maize growth performance. Integrated microbiome and metagenomic analyses indicated that NS8 modified rhizosphere microbial composition, functional potentials, and species-level co-occurrence patterns associated with degradation-related functions. This study reveals a metabolite-mediated regulatory mechanism linking maize, endophytic bacteria, and rhizosphere microbiota, providing an ecological framework for enhancing microbial remediation of herbicide contamination.

title: Air quality benefits and carbon reduction potential of future ultra-low emission retrofits in the chinese coking industry
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Fen Liu, Shu Xu, Yufei Tan, Zongshuang Wang
abstract: China, the world’s largest coke producer, emits substantial air pollutants and CO₂ from coking. Although ultra-low emission standards are being implemented, their emission reductions, remaining mitigation potential, and air quality benefits remain unclear. This study developed a nationwide, plant- and sector-level emission inventory of air pollutants and CO2 for China’s coking industry for 2023. Compliance rates for particulate matter (PM) and sulfur dioxide (SO2) concentrations exceeded 99.6% across all emission stages, whereas the nitrogen oxides (NOx) compliance rate at the coke oven stack stage was 86.52%. In 2023, coking industry emitted 16.01, 26.55, 88.16, and 129.33 kt·yr−1 of PM, SO2, NOx, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), respectively, and 227.80 Mt·yr−1 of CO2. Under the synergistic air pollutant-CO2 mitigation scenario, emissions of PM, SO2, NOx, VOCs, and CO2 would be reduced by 43.3%, 4.1%, 18.0%, 77.9%, and 54.7%, respectively. Air quality simulations indicated that the coking industry’s contributions to ambient PM2.5, SO2, NO2 and O3 concentrations could be reduced by 53.5%, 20.7%, 40.0%, and 15.8%, respectively. These findings reveal substantial differences in emission characteristics and remaining mitigation potential across coking processes and pollutants, providing new sector-specific insights for developing targeted air pollutant and CO2 mitigation strategies in China’s coking industry.

title: Legacy and emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances profiles in the two largest tributaries of the Yellow River: Roles of industrial structures and hydrodynamical condition
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yawen Li, Wenjing Lv, Yanan Li, Yitao Pan, Fengfeng Dong, Qiusheng He, Yang Cui, Xiang Ren, Yanfeng Zang, Jiayin Dai, Jianhui Tang
abstract: Seasonal hydrology regulates contaminant transport and fate, yet hydro-sedimentary controls on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in sediment-rich rivers remain poorly understood. This study investigates how industrial structures and hydro-sedimentary dynamics shape PFAS distribution, phase partitioning, and transport in the Fen (FR) and Wei (WR) Rivers, the two largest tributaries of the Yellow River. PFAS concentrations in water, suspended particulate matter (SPM), and sediments generally increased from upstream to middle reaches before declining downstream. ΣPFAS concentrations were higher in WR (1.12–8873.6 ng/L; mean: 441.8 ng/L) than in FR (3.55–415.1 ng/L; mean: 53.5 ng/L), with traditional PFAS dominating FR (82.5%) and perfluoroalkyl ether carboxylic acids (PFECAs) contributing 43.1% in WR, reflecting distinct industrial signatures. In FR, wet-season hydrology reduced dissolved-phase concentrations but increased SPM-associated PFAS. With increasing downstream streamflow and sediment flux, partition coefficients (Kd) and particle-associated fractions (f particle) decreased for short-chain PFAS but increased for long-chain homologues. This reveals chain-length-dependent SPM behavior, characterized by particle dilution of short-chain PFAS and enhanced transport of long-chain homologues under intensified sediment transport. Statistical analyses further showed that dissolved PFAS were primarily influenced by meteorological and socioeconomic factors, whereas SPM-associated PFAS were predominantly controlled by hydro-sedimentary processes.

title: Freeze-thaw aging enhances microplastic phytotoxicity in rice via root metabolism and DNA methylation
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zongyu Wang, Zikun Gao, Zhong Wang, Mengjun Wang, Zhangchao Yao, Zhixu Huang, Tanke Yu, Jiahui Li, Huijun Liu, Zhiheng Li, Jie Chen
abstract: Freeze-thaw cycling (FTC) accelerates microplastic (MP) aging in cold-region soils, yet the mechanisms underlying their amplified phytotoxicity remain elusive. This study integrated physicochemical characterization, metabolomics, and DNA methylation sequencing to evaluate the root toxicity of pristine and FTC-aged polystyrene, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polyethylene in rice (Oryza sativa). FTC aging induced surface oxidation and structural fragmentation, increasing hydrodynamic diameters by 8.8–26.7% and elevating negative surface charge by 5.17–5.36 mV. The aged PVC elicited the most severe phytotoxicity, disrupting root membrane integrity and suppressing superoxide dismutase activity by up to 54%. Metabolomic profiling revealed pronounced malate depletion coupled with lactate accumulation, indicating alterations in central carbon metabolism consistent with a potential shift toward glycolysis-associated metabolism, alongside significant perturbations in branched-chain amino acid and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Whole-genome bisulfite sequencing demonstrated that DNA methylation reprogramming was dominated by the CHH context, accounting for > 96% of all differentially methylated regions. Correlation network analysis revealed that aged PVC induced targeted CHH promoter hypermethylation in key redox hubs (e.g., NTRC, Trx M3), effectively decoupling antioxidant defense signaling from core energy metabolism. The work pinpoints that FTC-aged MP induced CHH methylation could connect to root metabolic reprogramming, establishing a basis for assessing risks of MPs in cold-climate agriculture.

title: Novel insights into BPS-induced neurodevelopmental toxicity in the octopus: Excitation/inhibition imbalance associated with GRM5 dysregulation potentially impairs learning and memory function of Amphioctopus fangsiao
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Lihua Wang, Jian Zheng, Penglong Zhang, Yifan Huangfu, Xiaodong Zheng
abstract: Bisphenol S (BPS) is widely detected in aquatic environments, yet its neurodevelopmental toxicity mechanisms in marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. Octopuses, the most intelligent invertebrates with sophisticated nervous systems, serve as ideal model organisms for neurodevelopmental research. In this study, Amphioctopus fangsiao embryos were exposed to 1, 10, and 100 μg/L BPS to evaluate its neurodevelopmental toxicity. The results showed that BPS exposure reduced hatching rates, and induced structural atrophy in the vertical lobe, a core region responsible for learning and memory, accompanied by oxidative stress, neuronal apoptosis, and synaptic damage in brain tissue. Behavioral assays confirmed that 10 μg/L BPS was associated with altered light habituation behavior, suggesting a potential impact on non-associative learning. Through transcriptomic analysis and molecular docking, we prioritized glutamate receptor 5 (GRM5) as a candidate neurotoxic target. BPS was predicted to interact with GRM5 and to upregulate its expression, which was associated with disruption of neuronal excitatory/inhibitory balance, inhibited the ERK/CREB pathway phosphorylation and downregulated synaptic plasticity-related genes. These findings propose a putative mechanistic framework linking GRM5 dysregulation to potential learning and memory impairment, providing an integrated assessment of BPS-induced developmental neurotoxicity in a cephalopod with complex cognition and a basis for future risk assessment.

title: Efficient solar spectrum partitioning in a photoelectrochemical-Fenton process for synergistic hydroxyl radical generation solely from water
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Seungmok Han, Ho-Sub Bae, Seok Kim, Sukhwa Hong, Chang Won Yoon, Kangwoo Cho, Wonyong Choi
abstract: We herein propose a solar-irradiated photoelectrochemical (PEC) system that achieves synergistic ·OH radical generation both from anodic and cathodic reactions for advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) in ambient air-equilibrated conditions. This system, based on a self-doped blue TiO2 (BT) nanotube photoanode, a carbon paper cathode and an infinitesimal Fe redox mediator (50 μM), achieves outstanding aqueous pollutant degradation efficiencies. The complex reaction mechanisms were disentangled by quantitative ·OH measurements in single- and divided-cell with comparison to an electrochemical system with boron-doped diamond (BDD) anode. The ·OH generation by BT was exclusively ascribed to trapped holes oxidizing water, while the oxygen reduction to H2O2 on carbon cathode (utilizing O2 generated by BT) was comparable ·OH source via Fenton reaction in an ambient condition. The hole-driven Fe2 + oxidation on BT elevated the photocurrent and H2O2 generation on the carbon paper, while elongated the service life of photoanode. In parallel, the residual solar photons after absorption by the BT could effectively induce facile photolysis of Fe(OH)2+ to regenerate Fe2+ to continue the Fenton reaction. Accordingly, the PEC BT-Fe-Carbon system without external chemicals except for a minute Fe (50 μM) exhibited a rapid aqueous pollutants degradation efficiency, irrespective of the initial Fe valency. This system demonstrates efficient pollutant mineralization in both synthetic and real wastewater matrices without a gas purging, along with sustained durability enabled by Fe redox cycling. These advancements broaden the practical applicability of PEC AOPs with homogeneous redox mediators for diverse (waste)water remediation applications.

title: Low-level background antibiotic mixture exposure and gestational diabetes mellitus: An exploratory indirect association analysis involving serum lipopolysaccharide
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ziyuan Qi, Yubin Ma, Yihui Wu, Ruixin Zhang, Bixia Peng, Pablo Gago-Ferrero, Zhaoxia Liang, Jing Liu
abstract: Although antibiotics are emerging contaminants with potential effects on gut microbiota and metabolic health, their role in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) remains unclear. This nested case-control study (264 GDM cases and 264 matched controls) within a prospective cohort examined early pregnancy exposure to 39 antibiotics and GDM risk. Serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) was measured to assess an indirect association. Total urinary antibiotic concentrations were higher in GDM cases than in controls (median: 62.16 vs. 45.16 ng/mL, P < 0.001), with β-lactams predominant. Higher concentrations were associated with increased odds of GDM (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.90, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.60–2.24 per doubling). Quantile g-computation revealed a positive joint association, with each one-quartile increase in mixture exposure associated with 22.3% higher odds of GDM (aOR = 1.223, 95% CI: 1.095–1.367). Among 134 participants with serum LPS measurements, exploratory mediation analysis identified a statistically imprecise indirect association involving LPS (71.4%; 95% CI: 20.3%-170.4%). Urinary antibiotics and serum LPS were measured concurrently, so temporal order could not be established. These findings suggest an association between low-level background antibiotic mixture exposure and higher odds of GDM, highlighting the potential relevance of such exposure to maternal metabolic health.

title: Reductive bioleaching of metals from spent lithium-ion batteries using corn silage slurries
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qu Wen, Angela Gil, Xu Li
abstract: Recovery of metals from the cathode materials of spent lithium ion (Li-ion) battery is important to achieve circular economy and environmental sustainability. The objective of this study was to explore the feasibility of using corn silage (CS) to leach metals from spent Li-ion batteries in a two-stage process, fermenting stage and bioleaching stage. Lactic acid and acetic acid were the dominant carboxylic acids in the CS slurry during the fermenting stage. Increasing CS content in the slurry enhanced metal recovery, achieving max leaching efficiencies of 96.70 ± 3.22% for Li, 89.47 ± 4.09% for Ni, 70.55 ± 4.95% for Co, and 83.65 ± 6.25% for Mn after 31 days of bioleaching with 6% CS. Following the addition of the cathode materials to the CS slurry, reducing sugars were released from CS solids. The consumption of reducing sugars, along with the detection of the potential oxidation products of the reducing sugars (e.g., glyceric acid), coincided with the release of metals from the cathode materials, suggesting that reducing sugars might contribute to metal leaching as reductants during bioleaching. Overall, this work demonstrated corn silage as a novel and effective bioleaching agent to recover valuable metals from spent Li-ion batteries.

title: Microplastics, endocrine disruption, and hormone-responsive cancers
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Destiny Tiburcio, Jon Swedenborg, Kalise Coffee, Michal Toborek
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging concern in human health as plastic production continues to accelerate, resulting in increased global pollution. Exposure to MPs spans the entire lifetime, from ingestion and inhalation to more indirect contact through placental barriers. The endocrine system and hormone-responsive organs, including breast, endometrium, thyroid and prostate could be especially vulnerable to the harmful effects of MPs as they carry additives with endocrine-disrupting activity. Furthermore, the highly metabolic nature of these organs, which are often enriched in lipids, supports the retention of hydrophobic MP-associated additives, and creates a pro-oxidative environment, which favors genotoxicity and carcinogenesis. This review examines emerging data on the potential association between MP exposure and the onset of hormone-responsive cancers, such as breast, endometrial, thyroid, and prostate cancers. The reported findings aim to inform future research directions in endocrine-related cancer etiology and population health, and may help prioritize research and exposure reduction.

title: AI-assisted high-throughput screening of MOFs for formaldehyde capture
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Kevizali Neikha, Amrit Puzari
abstract: Formaldehyde (FA) is a hazardous indoor volatile organic compound that poses risks to human health, demanding efficient adsorbent materials. Functionalized Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) offer structural tunability; however, functionalization can alter the framework, increase heterogeneity, cause pore blockage, and increase cost. Identification of pristine MOFs for FA adsorption is crucial for understanding adsorption mechanisms, framework topology, chemical composition, and unfunctionalized structures. In this work, we present an AI-assisted high-throughput screening framework that combines Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)-based text mining, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations, and Machine Learning (ML) to accelerate the discovery of MOFs for FA capture. Four MOF features were extracted using GAI text mining, and 1208 MOFs were selected from the CoRE MOF 2019 database. GCMC simulations evaluated FA uptake, while atomic, geometric, chemical, and thermodynamic descriptors were extracted for ML analyses. Seven regressors were developed to predict FA uptake based on these descriptors. An SVR-based denoising method was introduced during preprocessing to reduce simulation noise and improve predictions. The SVR model showed the best performance with an R² value of 0.94 and predicted FA uptake in 500 hMOFs. Validation of GAI responses, feature analyses, and experimental data also confirmed the reliability of this approach.

title: Intrinsic phytate and minerals lower arsenic bioaccessibility in brown rice: Mechanistic insights via machine learning
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Guobing Lin, Wenjie Dong, Yuan-Chen Zhang, Chenjing Liu, Lena Q. Ma
abstract: Whole-grain diets are promoted by substituting white rice with brown rice, which confers health benefits but increases arsenic (As) exposure. Based on 104 paired samples, brown rice exhibited 51% higher total As but 19% lower As bioaccessibility than white rice. Machine learning models identified As, S, Mg, and phytate contents as key determinants of bioaccessible As. Sequential extraction showed that 88–96% of As was associated with proteins, while 54 −92% of P existed as phytate. While phytase-induced phytate hydrolysis elevated As bioaccessibility by 33–54%, exogenous phytate reduced it by 7.5–22%. Similarly, in an aqueous system, phytase increased water-soluble S and As by 16–35% and 12–19%. Conversely, supplementing phytate and Mg reduced water-soluble As. These results suggest that phytate and minerals may contribute to As retention in rice grains, probably through the phytate-mineral-protein ternary association, which potentially makes As-bearing proteins less available to enzymes and thereby restricts As release. In this context, 90 −300% greater phytate and Mg contents in brown rice than white rice may enhance its As retention, contributing to its lower As bioaccessibility. Overall, this study proposes a working model to evaluate As release from rice grains and provides a possible explanation for lower As bioaccessibility in brown rice.

title: Aging-dependent pathogen loading and intestinal toxicity discrepancies between petroleum-based and biodegradable microplastics in zebrafish
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yuhang Dou, Ke Ye, Boyan Nie, Jie Liu, Lei Wang, Zhenghua Duan
abstract: Although biodegradable plastics are widely promoted as eco-friendly alternatives to conventional petroleum-based plastics, their ecological risks following environmental aging remain poorly understood. Herein, microplastics (MPs) of conventional polyethylene (PE) and biodegradable PLA/PBAT were prepared from commercial packaging plastic bags via mechanical and insect-mediated fragmentation, yielding two groups of MPs subjected to mechanical aging and biological aging, respectively. All aged MPs were incubated in kitchen waste leachate to compare biofilm formation and pathogen enrichment profiles, followed by toxicological tests using zebrafish. The results demonstrated that the pathogen-loading capacity and biological toxicity of aged MPs were jointly shaped by aging patterns and polymer types. Compared with mechanically aged MPs, biologically aged MPs facilitated the colonization and intestinal transfer of pathogenic microbes in zebrafish, thereby triggering stronger inflammatory responses. Aged PLA/PBAT MPs accumulated more in the gut but caused milder histological damage, lower mortality, and weaker developmental inhibition than aged PE MPs. A possible explanation involves energy compensation, whereby fish may utilize their degradation products. This study offers novel insights into the aging- and material-dependent risks of MPs, supporting ecological safety assessment and rational application of biodegradable plastics in aquaculture ecosystems.

title: Selenium-doped red carbon dot nanozymes for dual-mode tetracycline detection and synergistic antibacterial inactivation
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Shan Huang, Silin Li, Wei Ni, Guixin Li, Yutong Zhao, Fuxiang Wei, Yi Fang, Qi Xiao
abstract: Multifunctional nanozyme platforms integrating pollutant detection and antibacterial action are highly desirable for environmental monitoring and food safety. Herein, red-emissive selenium-doped carbon dots (Se-CDs, λ em = 615 nm) were synthesized via a one-step hydrothermal strategy. The Se-CDs exhibit excellent photostability and pronounced peroxidase-mimetic activity. A dual-readout colorimetric/fluorescence platform was thus constructed for total screening of tetracycline-class antibiotics, achieving detection limits of 0.22 μM and 0.23 μM, both reaching the maximum residue limit for tetracycline in milk (approximately 0.22–0.23 μM) stipulated by the EU and China’s GB 31650–2019. Density functional theory calculations, including implicit solvation and pH-relevant protonation states, revealed that tetracycline adsorption in the Se-associated catalytic environment was protonation-state-dependent, suppressing catalytic oxidation and enabling dual-channel signaling. The method was applied to tetracycline quantification in commercial milk with recoveries of 93.74%–107.60%. Moreover, the Se-CDs showed low cytotoxicity and potent antibacterial efficacy against both Gram-negative Escherichia coli and Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus, achieving 97.98% and 99.93% inactivation within 30 min via synergistic peroxidase-like reactive oxygen species generation and membrane disruption. This method is intended as a rapid screening tool for total tetracycline-class antibiotics, and provides an integrated paradigm for rational design of CD-based nanozymes with dual-functional capabilities in hazard monitoring and antibacterial applications.

title: The mobile resistome of Aeromonas : An underrecognized taxon in the global dissemination of antimicrobial resistance
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Dong-Won Lee, Sang-Gyu Kim, Do-Hoon Lee, Yong-Seok Kim, Chang-Jun Cha, Dae-Wi Kim
abstract: The genus Aeromonas is ubiquitous in aquatic environments and has been recognized as an important reservoir of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), yet its contribution to global ARG dissemination across taxonomic barriers remains unclear. We analyzed 1,569 publicly available Aeromonas genomes to characterize its mobile resistome and connectivity with the broader Pseudomonadota resistome. Among 109 non-singleton ARGs detected across five major Aeromonas species, 62 exhibited conserved Aeromonas ARG context (AAC) sequences across multiple species, suggesting extensive inter-species circulation within the genus. Extending AAC analysis to four major bacterial phyla identified 68 Aeromonas-derived Pseudomonadota inter-genus ARGs whose conserved contexts were predominantly shared with clinically important genera belonging to Enterobacteriaceae and were frequently associated with mobile genetic elements (MGEs). A complementary Pseudomonadota-wide network analysis based on inter-genus Pseudomonadota ARG context (PAC) clusters revealed strong connectivity between Aeromonas and clinically important Pseudomonadota species. Both Aeromonas-derived Pseudomonadota inter-genus ARGs and inter-genus PAC clusters increased markedly after 2000, with each increase mirrored by parallel increases in their MGE-associated contexts. These findings extend the view of Aeromonas beyond an aquatic ARG reservoir and suggest its potential role as an environmental exchange node in the dissemination of clinically relevant mobile ARGs across One Health sectors.

title: Coupled sulfur cycling and bioelectrochemical regulation of lead in carbon-limited constructed wetlands: Immobilization pathways and microbial responses
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Fengxiang Zhu, Jiale Li, Dongmei Cai, Haiying Yu, Jianjun Lian, Shanshan Hu, Bo Hu, Zhongbing Chen
abstract: Constructed wetlands (CWs) are important nature-based systems for sustainable wastewater management, but simultaneous removal of lead (Pb) and conventional pollutants under low C/N conditions remains limited by electron donor deficiency and Pb-induced biological stress. This study investigated the effects of integrating microbial fuel cells (MFCs) and elemental sulfur on nutrient purification, Pb transformation, microbial responses, and bioelectricity generation in CWs planted with Iris pseudacorus. Results showed that coupling MFCs with sulfur overcame electron donor limitation under low C/N conditions, achieving removal efficiencies of 90.7%, 82.2%, and 82.7% for total phosphorus, total nitrogen, and chemical oxygen demand, respectively, and enhancing Pb removal to 87.9%. Pb was predominantly associated with the root cell wall fraction, and its extraction profile shifted toward the acetic-acid-extractable Pb fraction, consistent with restricted translocation to shoots. Microbial analyses showed that MFC and sulfur reshaped microbial community assembly and enriched functions related to carbon transformation, denitrification, sulfur cycling, and Pb immobilization. Sulfur amendment also improved bio-electrochemical performance by reducing internal resistance and increasing maximum power density. These findings indicate that integrating sulfur-driven metabolism with bioelectrochemical regulation provides a hybrid low-carbon strategy for simultaneous nutrient removal and Pb stabilization in carbon-limited wastewater treatment.

title: Divergent fates of PAHs during reductive soil disinfestation: Activation versus sequestration dictated by biochar pyrolysis temperature
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Siyi Hu, Ran Wei, Weifeng Chen, Jinzhi Ni
abstract: Reductive soil disinfestation (RSD) and biochar amendment are established strategies for soil improvement and pollution remediation, respectively, but their combined effects on polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) fate remain unclear. A 56-day RSD incubation was conducted on PAH-spiked, pre-aged Anthrosol amended with wheat straw- and pine sawdust-derived biochars produced at 300 ℃ and 750 ℃. By combining sequential extraction with density fractionation, we separated soil PAHs into available, extractable, and alkaline-extractable bound (AE-bound) fractions to characterize PAH redistribution and mechanisms. Biochar pyrolysis temperature exerted stronger control on PAH redistribution than feedstock. Within 7 days, RSD lowered redox potential, increased pH, promoted metal oxide dissolution, and disrupted aggregates, thereby remobilizing a previously sequestered PAH pool. Low-temperature biochars (LT-BCs, 300 ℃) promoted an activation pathway, decreasing AE-bound PAHs by 39.26–52.70% and increasing the extractable fraction by 15.46–54.37%; remobilized PAHs associated with LT-BCs transferred into the light fraction. In contrast, high-temperature biochars (HT-BCs, 750 ℃) promoted a sequestration pathway, with decreased available PAHs accounting for most of the total extracted PAH reduction and HT-BC particles incorporating into the heavy fraction, rendering associated PAHs non-extractable. Collectively, these findings reveal pyrolysis-temperature-dependent activation and sequestration pathways during RSD, with LT-BCs increasing PAH extractability and potentially facilitating biodegradation.

title: Cesium hydroxide aerosols causing acute upper respiratory tract irritation and epistaxis following the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant accident: Deductive research evidence
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Masao Hattori, Harukazu Hirano, Yoshimi Tanaka, Masashi Nishiya, Junko Endo, Eiji Asari, Eiichi Momotani
abstract: Following the accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant (FDNPP), residents reported symptoms including inflammation of the upper respiratory tract mucosa, eyes, and skin, as well as nosebleeds, headaches, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, and psychological distress. In response to these concerns, a non-profit organization held free medical consultation sessions staffed by physicians in various locations. The authors investigated the actual health impacts from a medical perspective using an anonymized database compiled from the records of 509 consultation participants. Based on the characteristic symptoms observed, the authors concluded that these health issues stemmed from the chemical toxicity of radioactive cesium hydroxide (R-CsOH) aerosols, which are highly alkaline and corrosive. This study revealed for the first time that these aerosols—which accounted for 90% of the cesium released during the plant's explosions—can cause adverse health effects even at extremely low concentrations. The study presents inductive evidence regarding atmospheric pollution caused by R-CsOH aerosols.
