The characteristic clinical symptoms identified in this study are noteworthy as a new indicator for assessing human exposure and could serve as a novel warning sign of internal radiation exposure.

title: Heavy metal contamination of industrial soil revealed by Cu, Zn, and Pb isotopic ratios of sequential extraction fractions
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Dae-Gyu Im, Duk-Min Kim, Nok Il Kwak, Seong-Taek Yun
abstract: The sources and mobility of metals in contaminated industrial soils are difficult to resolve from total concentrations alone. Four of the 11 soils from a railway maintenance facility in Seoul, South Korea, were sequentially extracted, and Cu, Pb, and Zn isotopes were measured in each fraction of the most contaminated soil (S5). S5 contained 7130 mg kg−1 Pb, and As, Cd, Cu, and Zn also exceeded the Korean Worrisome Levels for Area 1. Its Fe-oxide spherules, anomalous magnetic susceptibility, and thermally refractory carbon are consistent with a waste input from metallurgical operations. Less than 1% of Cu, Pb, and Zn was exchangeable in all four soils. The 207Pb/206Pb of all five fractions (0.889–0.894), including the residual, fell outside Korean stream-sediment and subsoil ranges, so anthropogenic Pb dominated every fraction. These ratios differed from coal-combustion and urban Pb but overlapped Korean smelter emissions, consistent with imported ore. In contrast, δ65Cu and δ66Zn varied among the fractions. Relative to the mass-balance bulk, carbonate-bound Zn was heavy (Δ66Zn = +0.29‰) but Cu light (Δ65Cu = −1.29‰). Because Pb varied less among fractions than its offset from geogenic Pb, these differences are interpreted as in-soil partitioning rather than a distinct source for each fraction.

title: Post-operative exposure to air pollution and colorectal cancer survival: A multi-center cohort study in southwestern China
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Lang Wang, Chang Liu, Xiong Zhou, Jinshan Liu, Jian Xie, Man Zhang, Zhihu Xu, Botian Chen, Xiaoyu Liu, Rongbin Xu, Dong Peng
abstract: Evidence linking post-operative air pollution to colorectal cancer (CRC) survival remains limited. This multi-center cohort study included 7068 patients undergoing radical resection for CRC at four hospitals in Chongqing, China. Over a median follow-up of 56 months, 1540 all-cause deaths occurred. Residential exposures to fine particulate matter (PM2.5), inhalable particulate matter (PM10), ozone (O3), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and carbon monoxide (CO) were obtained from CHAP, whereas PM2.5 constituents, including sulfate (SO4 2-), nitrate (NO3 -), ammonium (NH4 +), organic matter (OM), and black carbon (BC), were obtained from TAP. Time-varying Cox models assessed associations between 1-year lagged moving-average exposures and all-cause mortality. In fully adjusted models, each 5 μg/m3 increase in PM2.5 and PM10 was associated with higher mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.079 (95% CI: 1.045–1.115) and 1.050 (95% CI: 1.027–1.074), respectively. These associations were generally consistent across two-pollutant and sensitivity analyses. The inverse association observed for O₃ warrants cautious interpretation. Among PM2.5 constituents, OM showed the most consistent positive association (HR per IQR increase: 1.088; 95% CI: 1.028–1.152) and remained significant in residual and remaining-mass models. These findings link particulate pollution to CRC survival and highlight the potential relevance of PM2.5 constituents, particularly OM.

title: Redox-differentiated bank filtration is associated with enhanced sulfamethoxazole transformation but sustains persistent transformation products
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Jimmy Köpke, Caglar Akay, Simon Klaes, Julia Huchthausen, Luise Henneberger, Lorenz Adrian, Chang Ding, Aki Sebastian Ruhl
abstract: Sulfamethoxazole (SMX) is a frequently detected antibiotic that challenges drinking water production by bank filtration and managed aquifer recharge. Although redox conditions influence antibiotic transformation, their long-term effects on transformation products (TPs), microbial communities, and residual toxicity remain poorly understood. This long-term study integrates parent compound attenuation, TP formation, microbial community composition, and cytotoxicity to provide a comprehensive assessment of SMX fate during continuous-flow subsurface treatment. Laboratory-scale bank filtration columns were operated for 589 days under initially oxic and subsequently redox-differentiated conditions. No SMX transformation occurred under fully oxic conditions. Following methanol amendment and redox differentiation, SMX transformation was consistently observed, peaking in the oxic–anoxic transition zone and continuing under anoxic conditions. Twenty TPs, predominantly derived from modifications of the isoxazole and aniline moieties, exhibited distinct spatial formation and persistence patterns. Endpoint microbial community composition differed among sampling zones and SMX treatments, including enrichment of Meiothermus (class Deinococci) in the high-concentration treatment. Despite partial SMX attenuation, enriched influent and effluent extracts from the high-concentration treatment showed comparable cytotoxicity. These findings demonstrate that long-term redox differentiation is associated with enhanced SMX attenuation but also persistent TP formation and residual cytotoxicity, highlighting that parent compound removal alone is insufficient to evaluate micropollutant attenuation and environmental risk in bank filtration and managed aquifer recharge systems.

title: Environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, toxicity and priority of fluorinated liquid crystal monomers
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yawen Yuan, Jiawei Cheng, Zihao Li, Yuhe He, Kenneth M.Y. Leung, Yunsong Mu, John P. Giesy
abstract: Fluorinated liquid crystal monomers (FLCMs) constitute the largest and most widely used subgroup of liquid crystal monomers (LCMs), accounting for more than half of known LCMs. They are important components of high-performance liquid crystal mixtures used in displays because of their excellent dielectric anisotropy, low viscosity, and thermal stability. With the large-scale production, use, and disposal of liquid crystal displays, FLCMs are continuously released into the environment and have been widely detected in air, dust, water, sediments, wastewater, biota, and human samples. Compared with non-FLCMs, FLCMs generally exhibit stronger environmental persistence, higher bioaccumulation potential, and greater ecological and health risks, and therefore represent potential emerging contaminants. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on the sources, environmental occurrence and fate, transformation, bioaccumulation, exposure, and toxicity of FLCMs, and compares their PBT characteristics with those of non-FLCMs to assess the relative priority of FLCMs and non-FLCMs as two groups. Overall, FLCMs show risk characteristics similar to persistent organic pollutants, but knowledge gaps remain regarding their environmental behavior, transformation-product toxicity, actual exposure hazards, and life-cycle risk assessment. Future studies should strengthen multimedia monitoring, mechanism-based toxicology, exposure assessment, and green molecular design to support risk identification, priority control, and sustainable management of FLCMs.

title: Quantitative analysis of geochemical boundaries for controlling mobile cadmium speciation in soil of high geological background regions
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Kunling Zheng, Bingtao Li, Yinxian Song, Tengjie Cui, Junfeng Ji, Zhongyao Chen, Godwin A. Ayoko
abstract: Accumulation and mobilization of cadmium (Cd) in high geological background regions threaten agricultural and ecological security, yet the dynamic evolution and quantitative thresholds of mobile Cd during weathering pedogenesis remain unclear. This study, for the first time, coupled the PROFILE with multi-surface model, together with machine learning, to conduct a comparative analysis of karst and black shale high geological background regions, with the Yangtze River Delta for comparison. Results show that Cd leaching risk is highly region specific: water-soluble Cd dominates black shale (46%) and non-high geological background regions (51%), whereas karst regions exhibit a stronger mineral bound buffering. Although the critical pH range governing Cd immobilization and mobilization generally falls within the classical geochemical range of 6.0–7.0, it varies with parent material and pedogenic processes. Critical dissolved organic carbon thresholds show a decreasing gradient of black shale (250–300 mg/kg) > karst (200–250 mg/kg) > non-high geological background (150–200 mg/kg), correlating positively with indigenous soil DOC levels to optimize organic fertilizer dosage. Weathering pedogenesis induces seasonal Cd “release and mineral re-immobilization” dynamics, and high temperature and precipitation in summer significantly enhance Cd leaching. This study provides a quantitative basis for differentiated Cd risk management in comparable high geological background regions.

title: Field-deployable ZnO/ZIF-67 heterostructure sensor: Enabling rapid, highly sensitive, and humidity-tolerant NO 2 detection
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Huimin Chen, Xiangyi Deng, Li Lv, Shuyan Cao, Liang Yin, Xiangqun Chu, Shicai Yan, Pinhua Zhang, Bin Liu
abstract: Real-time nitrogen dioxide (NO2) detection is critical for both environmental monitoring and ecological agriculture, but its practical deployment is still limited by low sensitivity, slow response speed and severe humidity interference. Herein, a porous p-n heterostructure based on ZnO/ZIF-67 was prepared via in-situ growth of ZnO on ZIF-67. Benefiting from the synergistic effect between the porous structure and the built-in heterogeneous interface, the as-prepared composite material delivers exceptional NO2 sensing performance. The optimized ZnO/ZIF-67 sensor exhibits a high response of 8.29 ( | I g / I a | ) to 10 ppm NO2 with fast response/recovery times of 5/6 s (25℃). The sensor also enables clear detection down to 200 ppb and maintains stable sensing performance over 35 days. Furthermore, it displays excellent humidity tolerance: as relative humidity increases from 45% to 85%, the sensing response toward 1 ppm NO2 only varies by 18.51%. To investigate the practical application performance of the sensor in real-world scenarios, a portable sensing platform was constructed for real-time NO2 monitoring in humid agricultural environments. Experiments verified that the sensor system can effectively detect nitrogen-derived gases in the soil. This work supplies a feasible material design methodology for low-power NO2 sensing and ecological agriculture monitoring application.

title: Engineered titanium-coated iron oxide nanocomposites alleviate nickel-induced phytotoxicity in maize through integrated physiological, ultrastructural, and transcriptomic protection
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Muhammad Rehman, Sajid Muhammad, Bahar Ali, Zulqarnain Haider, Abdul Salam, Yinbo Gan
abstract: Nickel (Ni) contamination of agricultural soils threatens crop productivity, food safety, and human health. Although individual nanomaterials have been explored to alleviate Ni stress, little is known about the integration of complementary oxides within a single core-shell platform, and the transcriptomic basis of such protection remains poorly understood. We engineered titanium-coated iron oxide core-shell nanocomposites (Ti@Fe3O4 NCs), combining the redox-modulating capacity of the Fe3O4 core with the ROS-scavenging properties of the Ti-based shell, and evaluated their foliar application against Ni toxicity in maize. Relative to Ni-stressed plants, NCs + Ni improved shoot length (36%), root length (54%), and biomass, reduced Ni accumulation, and restored shoot Ca (65%), P (45%), Mg (29%), and Zn (35%). NCs + Ni re-established redox homeostasis by lowering H2O2 (29%), O2•− (33%), and malondialdehyde (24%) and by increasing SOD (35%), POD (42%), CAT (42%), and APX (14%) activities. Transcriptome profiling showed that, instead of hyper-activating stress signaling, NCs + Ni buffered Ni-induced transcriptional disruption, reducing differentially expressed genes from 2462 to 1654 and downregulated known genes from 425 to 146. NCs + Ni also enhanced photosynthesis-, cell wall-, and phenylpropanoid-related pathways. Collectively, Ti@Fe3O4 NCs alleviate Ni toxicity through redox protection, ultrastructural preservation, and transcriptional regulation, offering a nano-enabled strategy for crops in Ni-contaminated agroecosystems.

title: Structural insights and mutational validation of a novel α/β hydrolase acting on oxidized polyethylene-derived substrates
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Yanzi Sun, Yi Xiao, Sufang Wang, Dunpeng Liu, Yishu Wang, Lina Qiu, Yixin Liu, Haihong Jia, Feng Ding, Dengyue Sun, Mingguan Yang, Piwu Li
abstract: Polyethylene (PE) accumulates environmentally due to its inertness and recalcitrance. PE biodegradation is generally considered a multistep process in which abiotic or enzymatic oxidation generates oxygen-containing intermediates subsequently transformed by downstream enzymes. However, the structural basis and catalytic roles of hydrolases in these downstream processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identified a novel α/β-hydrolase (HvH) from Vreelandella venusta, investigated using UV-oxidized and native PE films. Physicochemical characterization revealed that active HvH altered surface morphology, hydrophilicity, crystallinity, and molecular-weight distribution, whereas heat-inactivated controls showed substantially reduced effects. Site-directed mutagenesis of computationally predicted key residues further highlighted their contributions to catalytic activity and the observed changes in the UV-oxidized PE system. The crystal structure of HvH, determined at 2.71 Å resolution, revealed a canonical α/β-hydrolase fold containing a catalytic triad (S122–D223–H252) and a flexible loop–helix lid region regulating access to the substrate-binding pocket. Molecular dynamics, Markov state model analysis, and QM/MM simulations suggested a dynamic substrate-recognition mechanism and provided hypotheses regarding substrate recognition and catalysis that may guide further investigation. Collectively, these findings indicate that HvH may contribute to the transformation of materials associated with UV-oxidized PE and provide structural and mechanistic insights into hydrolase-mediated plastic biodegradation pathways. Synopsis This work provides structural and functional insights into a novel α/β hydrolase involved in the transformation of oxidized polyethylene-derived fragments.

title: Unravelling PFAS disruption of thyroxine transport by transthyretin using machine learning-augmented modelling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Aikaterini Theodori, Konstantinos D. Papavasileiou, Haralampos Tzoupis, Danae Zareifi, Andreas Tsoumanis, Francesco Dondero, Georgia Melagraki, Iseult Lynch, Antreas Afantitis
abstract: Thyroid-disrupting chemicals (TDCs) pose a significant risk to human health and are associated with adverse neurological and cardiovascular effects. Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been shown to bind to transthyretin (TTR), disrupting thyroid hormone homeostasis and leading to adverse outcomes. We present a refined workflow for modelling and predicting PFAS activity toward TTR, where training compounds were labelled Active or Inactive based on experimental activity values (binding affinities) exceeding 50% relative to the control, thyroxine (binding partner of TTR). Curation of experimental datasets from published studies resulted in 131 unique PFAS structures for modelling. The dataset was augmented with molecular descriptors and molecular docking-derived scores, followed by model optimisation and evaluation through an automated machine learning (AutoML) approach. Among the tested classification algorithms, XGBoost demonstrated the strongest overall performance, achieving a held-out test accuracy of 0.818. Structure-activity insights, molecular docking calculations and Shapley value analysis indicated an association between higher PFAS lipophilicity and Active predictions, consistent with the hydrophobic nature of the TTR binding pocket and previous experimental observations. In accordance with the FAIR principles for data and models, the curated dataset is publicly available through ChemPharos (https://db.chempharos.eu/datasets/Datasets.zul?datasetID=ds21). The final model is implemented as a user-friendly web application (https://enaloscloud.novamechanics.com/scenarios/thyrotox/).

title: Interpretable machine learning assessment of morphological traits and genetic factors associated with cadmium transfer to rice grains during grain filling
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhong Tang, Meng-Jie Fu, Chuan-Jun Zhang, Bing-Ying Zou, Yi-Bo Wu, Min Liang, Peitong Wang, Qing Zhu, Jianlong Xu, Fang-Jie Zhao, Xin-Yuan Huang
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice grains threatens food safety and human health. Although root uptake and root-to-shoot translocation have been extensively characterized, the aboveground processes that determine Cd delivery to the grain remain poorly resolved. Here we combined in vitro detached panicle tracer-based transport phenotyping, aboveground morphological analysis, genetic haplotype analysis, and interpretable machine learning to dissect the determinants of grain Cd transfer capacity. Grain Cd transfer capacity varied 303-fold (phloem) and 233-fold (xylem), revealing extensive natural variation in aboveground Cd allocation. Twenty morphological and organ transfer traits of the node I, flag leaf and panicle and haplotypes of seven Cd allocation genes provided 27 input features for four machine learning models trained on 264 observations. The multilayer perceptron achieved the highest predictive accuracy with R2 = 0.67 and R2 = 0.63 for grain Cd transfer capacity relative to phloem and xylem transport, respectively. SHAP analysis ranked the flag leaf and panicle Cd transport capacity, seed-setting rate, and OsDEF8 haplotypes as the most influential predictors. Our results highlight that aboveground translocation processes, rather than organ morphology, are central to grain Cd loading. This integrative framework offers potential mechanistic insight and practical tools for breeding low-Cd rice, reducing dietary Cd exposure and improving food safety.

title: Sonic hedgehog pathway activation mitigates the anti-neurogenic effects of Bisphenol-A in the rat brain hippocampus
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Ranjeet Kumar Yadav, Shraddha Tiwari, Phoolmala, Saurabh Tiwari, Tanya Jamal, Rajnish Kumar Chaturvedi
abstract: Bisphenol-A (BPA) causes neurochemical and neurobehavioral abnormalities in humans. Our previous studies showed that BPA inhibits hippocampal neurogenesis. Our current in-silico studies suggest that BPA interacts with key proteins of the Sonic hedgehog (Shh) pathway. Postnatal BPA exposure caused alterations in Shh pathway associated gene expression and protein levels (RGMA, NEO1, and Gli1) in the rat hippocampus. BPA significantly reduced neural stem cells (NSCs) proliferation (reduced co-localization of NEO1 and Gli1 with Sox-2 and nestin) and neuronal differentiation (reduced co-localization of NEO1/β-Tubulin-III in the hippocampal NSCs-derived neuronal cultures and Gli1/NeuN and RGMA/NeuN in the hippocampus. Pharmacological inhibition of Shh pathway transcription factor (Gli1) by cyclopamine caused reduced NSCs proliferation and neuronal differentiation in NSCs culture. Pharmacological activation of canonical Shh signalling by Smoothened agonist SAG mitigated BPA-mediated inhibition of NSCs proliferation and neuronal differentiation in-vitro and in-vivo. Shh pathway activation reduced inhibitory effects of BPA on dendritic spines, mitochondrial and synaptic ultrastructure, and apoptosis in the hippocampus. Activation caused improved NSCs proliferation (increased number of neurospheres and size, and Gli1&Sox2/nestin co-localization), neuronal differentiation (Gli1/NeuN co-localization), neuronal growth cone formation (MAP2/GAP43 co-localization), and synaptic markers (MAP2&SYP/PSD95) co-localization leading to improved learneing and memory. Thus, activation of the Shh pathway mitigates the deleterious effects of BPA on neurogenesis, and cognitive impairments.

title: Integrated multi-omics and molecular modeling analyses of indaziflam distribution, ecological risks, and biological responses in a water–sediment system
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiaoqian Song, Ruolin Wu, Hongyuan Zhang, Lei Zheng, Xiuguo Wang, Yiqiang Li, Tong Liu
abstract: Indaziflam is an alkylazine herbicide that inhibits cellulose biosynthesis, yet its environmental safety remains poorly understood. Indaziflam concentrations decreased in water under static exposure but remained relatively constant under semi-static exposure, while its concentrations in sediment increased under both exposure conditions. It exhibited moderate acute toxicity to zebrafish, Daphnia magna, and Chironomus kiiensis. During the 28-day exposure at 0.1 and 0.5 mg/L, indaziflam induced oxidative stress, disrupted antioxidant and detoxification enzyme activities, and affected neurochemical responses in zebrafish. Sediment microbial richness and diversity were significantly reduced, with altered community composition. Integrated microbiome and metabolomic analyses showed increased relative abundances of Pontibacter, Lysobacter, and Flavisolibacter following indaziflam exposure, indicating that these genera responded to indaziflam exposure. Zebrafish transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses showed altered pathways related to energy and nucleotide metabolism, cellular homeostasis, and neuroactive ligand–receptor interactions, alongside differential expression of neuronal signaling and detoxification genes. Molecular docking based on AlphaFold2 models and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a stable association between UGT5G2 and indaziflam, identifying UGT5G2 as a candidate detoxification protein. Collectively, this study characterizes the distribution and biological effects of indaziflam in a water–sediment system and identifies UGT5G2 as a candidate detoxification protein, providing evidence for its environmental risk assessment.

title: Thiram exposure impairs tibial chondrocyte maturation and ECM synthesis by disrupting the NAD+/Sirt1-driven glycolytic checkpoint
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Kai Liu, Xiaomei Wu, Junhong Hou, Yuanliang Li, Ying Li, Zhaoxin Tang, Quazi T.H. Shubhra, Yung-Fu Chang, Hui Zhang
abstract: Thiram, a dithiocarbamate pesticide, induces tibial dyschondroplasia (TD) in broilers, but its metabolic toxicity mechanism remains unclear. Using thiram‑exposed broilers (100 mg/kg feed) and primary chondrocytes (10 μM thiram), we investigated whether thiram disrupts chondrocyte maturation and extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis by impairing NAD+‑dependent glycolysis. Thiram reduced the NAD+/NADH ratio and Sirt1 activity in tibial growth plates and downregulated glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) and glycolytic enzymes (HK2, ENO1, LDHA). This metabolic crisis, evidenced by decreased glucose uptake, lactate production, ATP, and sulfated glycosaminoglycan synthesis, was accompanied by impaired chondrogenic markers (Sox9, Runx2, Aggrecan, Col2A1) and abnormal cartilage histology. Rescue experiments showed that GLUT1 overexpression partially reversed glycolytic defects and chondrocyte dysfunction caused by Sirt1 knockdown; Sirt1 knockdown attenuated, but did not abolish, GLUT1-mediated protection, and GLUT1 inhibition aggravated these impairments, indicating GLUT1 is a downstream mediator of Sirt1-driven glycolysis. Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), an NAD+ precursor, elevated NAD+, reactivated Sirt1, upregulated GLUT1‑mediated glycolysis, and reversed thiram‑induced ECM loss and maturation arrest. We identify the NAD+/Sirt1/GLUT1 axis as a critical checkpoint that thiram targets to suppress chondrocyte glycolysis and differentiation, revealing a novel toxicological pathway, and suggest NAD+ replenishment may mitigate pesticide‑associated skeletal disorders, with implications for environmental health risk assessment.

title: Environmentally relevant imidacloprid impairs juvenile scallop growth via a dual constraint on energy acquisition and utilization
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qiaoqiao Wang, Xianming Tang, Wenhao Zhang, Lu Wang, Manni Wu, Luqing Pan, Jingjing Miao
abstract: Neonicotinoid insecticides are now ubiquitous in coastal waters, yet their chronic hazard to non-target marine invertebrates remains poorly defined. Juvenile scallops (Chlamys farreri) were exposed to imidacloprid (IMI) at environmentally relevant concentrations (0.5 and 5 μg/L) and a high level (50 μg/L) for 21 days, and growth, feeding physiology, neuroendocrine signalling, energy reserves and untargeted metabolomics were integrated to resolve the basis of growth inhibition. IMI severely suppressed the scope for growth and condition index at concentrations as low as 0.5 μg/L, at tissue burdens of 13.6–28.3 μg/kg. Mechanistically, IMI disturbed cholinergic, serotonergic, and insulin/NPY neuroendocrine circuits, leading to feeding suppression. Unexpectedly, this feeding suppression did not cause classical energy reserve depletion. Instead, IMI induced abnormal lipid accumulation together with reduced ETS activity and pronounced late-stage AMPK activation. Growth impairment may thus have arisen from a dual constraint, coupling suppression of energy acquisition with restricted energy utilization, a pattern consistent with cellular energy imbalance despite abundant stored lipids. This study reveals an overlooked hazard of sublethal neonicotinoid contamination to the growth performance of juvenile bivalves, emphasizing the need to incorporate early-life-stage energetic endpoints into ecological risk assessment.

title: Serendipita indica reshapes early metal allocation and root-associated transcriptional responses in Sedum alfredii under combined cadmium-lead stress
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Siyi Li, Jie Zhao, Xiaoqi Zhu, Yiming Ma, Xiaorui Zhang, Baoping Xie, Qianwen Fei, Yuanyuan Shao, Kuan Xu, Xini Liu, Yabei Qiao, Meng Fan, Shengke Tian
abstract: Mechanistic studies of plant-microbe interactions under heavy metal stress have focused predominantly on single metal exposure, whereas contaminated soils commonly contain multiple metals whose combined effects cannot be predicted directly from responses to individual contaminants. Here, we investigated how the root endophytic fungus Serendipita indica (S. indica) influences metal acquisition, allocation, and root transcriptional responses in the hyperaccumulator Sedum alfredii (S. alfredii) exposed to individual or combined cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) stress. Metal quantification was integrated with RNA sequencing, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and RT-qPCR validation. Under combined stress, S. indica increased root Cd and Pb concentrations, enhanced root-normalized shoot metal accumulation, and promoted root-to-shoot translocation. Combined Cd-Pb exposure elicited a transcriptional response distinct from those induced by either metal alone, while fungal inoculation further reshaped gene expression patterns associated with metal detoxification, redox regulation, protein homeostasis, and energy metabolism. Co-expression analysis identified gene modules associated with fungal inoculation and combined metal exposure, and RT-qPCR supported the RNA-seq expression trends of CSP4, atp2, SPBP35G2.11c, and RPS21. These findings demonstrate that S. indica modifies both metal acquisition and host stress responses under Cd-Pb co-stress, providing mechanistic insight into microbe-assisted phytoremediation of multi-metal-contaminated soils.

title: Occurrence, temporal trends, and associations of tetrabromobisphenol A/S and their analogs with fatty-acid profiles in cetaceans from the Northern South China Sea
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhenhui Xie, Yanling Gan, Bin Sun, Qiang Xie, Xiyang Zhang, Yuping Wu
abstract: Despite the increasing concerns about the health risks arising from the continuous detection of TBBPA/S and their analogs in biota, studies on their occurrence and potential risks in marine cetaceans remain limited. Here, we investigated the bioaccumulation characteristics and potential risks of 10 TBBPA/S and their analogs in 9 cetacean species (n = 40) from the NSCS during 2006 −2023. All target compounds were detected in at least one cetacean species, with the summed concentrations of the 10 target compounds ranging from 39.6 to 278.4 ng/g ww, indicating their widespread occurrence in the NSCS. Compared with TBBPA, its analogs, such as TBBPS-BME, TBBPS-BDBPE, and TBBPA-BHEE, predominated in these cetaceans. Target compound concentrations in N. phocaenoides showed no significant age- or sex-related differences. Although TBBPA concentrations remained stable from 2006 to 2023, its analogs (i.e., TBBPA-BHEE and TBBPA-BME) increased significantly. These trends are consistent with changing use patterns of BFRs, but cannot presently be attributed to a specific cause. Preliminary results suggested significant associations of TBBPA/S and their analogs with several individual FAs and/or FA group ratios (e.g., ∑n-6/∑n-3 PUFAs and SCD-16). These findings highlight the need for continued monitoring of these compounds to protect this vulnerable species.

title: Field-deployable sensors for PFAS detection: Current advances, emerging trends, and future opportunities
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Minshu Chen, Xin Lu, Tyler Maddox, Chujun Zhou, Shang Jia, Lei Guo
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants whose effective analysis, characterization, and remediation heavily rely on sensitive, reliable, and field-deployable monitoring technologies. Although liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) remains the benchmark for PFAS analysis, its reliance on centralized laboratories, specialized instrumentation, and extensive sample preparation limits its utility for rapid screening and on-site decision making. This review critically evaluates recent progress in non-mass-spectrometry PFAS sensors from the perspective of field deployment. We first define key design criteria for practical PFAS sensing, including regulatory-relevant sensitivity, selectivity, matrix tolerance, stability, and portability. We then summarize optical, electrochemical, and other sensing modalities that achieve limits of detection (LODs) at or below current U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) drinking water limits for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), highlighting the recognition and signal-transduction strategies that enable ultralow PFAS detection. Beyond regulatory-relevant sensitivity, we discuss emerging trends in PFAS sensing, including emerging PFAS recognition mechanisms, detection of emerging, short and ultrashort chain PFAS, ratiometric quantification, PFAS differentiation, and smartphone-assisted readouts. Finally, we highlight persistent barriers to on-site PFAS sensing, including inconsistent LOD/LOQ reporting, limited assessment of specificity and selectivity, and challenges in translating laboratory proof-of-concept sensors into credible tools for routine field monitoring. Rather than replacing LC–MS/MS, field-deployable PFAS sensors are best positioned as complementary tools for rapid screening, source tracking, treatment monitoring, and early-warning detection. Future advances will require standardized performance evaluation, mechanism-guided sensor design, realistic field validation, and integration with portable data-processing platforms.

title: Distinguishing groundwater quality degradation from potentially toxic element risks in coastal aquifers: An integrated hydrogeochemical analysis and risk assessment framework
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Zhibin Li, Chengpeng Lu, Guangdong Wu, Bo Liu, Longcang Shu
abstract: Coastal plains are highly vulnerable to groundwater quality degradation driven by natural processes and human activities. Yet links among hydrochemical evolution, groundwater quality degradation, and potentially toxic element (PTE) risks remain poorly understood. This study integrates hydrogeochemical analysis, positive matrix factorization (PMF), the entropy water quality index (EWQI), partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), and an integrated potentially toxic element risk index (IPTE-RI) to investigate groundwater quality evolution in a coastal plain in eastern China. Groundwater hydrochemical evolution is primarily controlled by water-rock interaction, ion exchange, evaporation, and seawater intrusion. Hydrogeochemical processes associated with water-rock interaction and ion exchange account for up to 80% of the solute sources. Groundwater quality is favorable, although alternative weighting schemes produce an average difference of 51.34% in EWQI results. IPTE-RI reveals that groundwater quality degradation and PTE risks represent distinct dimensions of groundwater deterioration. All samples with IPTE-RI of 0.5–1.0 fall into the “medium” EWQI, while samples classified as “poor” or “very poor” have IPTE-RI values below 0.5. As, Cr (Ⅵ), and Ni are the major risk-contributing elements. This study provides a transferable approach for distinguishing groundwater quality degradation from specific toxic element risks, offering broad applicability for groundwater management in coastal plains.

title: Physiological and molecular responses of Enterococcus faecium IB-1 to Cd stress: Insights from transcriptional regulation and extracellular immobilization
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Min Zhu, Jing Sun, Ruobing Ren, Feng Zhao, Xinqi Lv, Juntao Cui, Yu Zhang, Kai Sun
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a highly toxic, mobile, persistent, and bioaccumulative heavy metal pollutant of major concern in agricultural environments. In this study, Enterococcus faecium IB-1, which has environmental adaptability and heavy metal tolerance, was selected as the target microorganism to explore its Cd tolerance mechanisms and immobilization potential. The results showed that Cd inhibited bacterial growth and induced adaptive responses. Specifically, visible colonies decreased by 63.9% in the 10 mg/L Cd2+-treated group, while a proportion of cells remained viable. Particulate deposition and cellular morphological alterations were observed under Cd stress. At the transcriptional level, 70 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 34 upregulated and 36 downregulated genes, were identified in E. faecium IB-1 treated with 10 mg/L Cd2+, while urea cycle and pyrimidine metabolism were enhanced. Oxygen-containing functional groups, carbonate-related species, and phosphate-associated components participated in Cd2+ binding and immobilization. Consistently, the highest Cd removal efficiency reached 44.72% under the conditions of this study. Moreover, CaCO3, CdCO3, and Ca4.03Cd0.97(PO4)3OH were formed and stabilized in localized alkaline microenvironments. Overall, Cd tolerance and immobilization involve physiological adaptation, cell-surface adsorption/complexation, urea production and hydrolysis, and carbonate/phosphate-associated mineral formation. This study provides mechanistic insights into Cd stress adaptation and biomineralization-associated Cd immobilization in E. faecium IB-1.

title: Geogenic Ni redistribution and soil-to-rice transfer during flooding and drainage in a basalt-derived paddy soil
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Xiupei Zhou, Wenting Chi, Kaiyi Huang, Shan Wang, Feng Gong, Zebin Hong, Guojun Chen, Shiwen Hu, Qi Wang, Guoyong Huang, Dandan Pan, Yang Yang, Xiaomi Li, Tongxu Liu
abstract: Geogenic nickel (Ni) in basalt-derived paddy soils is redox-responsive, but its redistribution and soil-to-rice transfer remain unresolved. A full-season pot experiment combined sequential extraction, interfacial characterization, and stage-specific kinetic modeling. During flooding, labile Ni (exchangeable and specifically adsorbed), Fe/Mn oxide-bound Ni, and organic matter-complexed Ni decreased from 2.70% to 1.55%, 5.74% to 3.82%, and 2.64% to 2.23%, respectively, whereas residual Ni increased from 84.47% to 86.82%, indicating net immobilization. These shifts coincided with reductive transformation of Fe-bearing phases, mobilization of mineral-associated organic matter, and altered mineral–organic interfacial properties. Plaque-associated Ni rose from 1.24 to 2.50 mg kg–1, and tissue Ni remained concentrated in roots. Modeling suggested a labile Ni → Fe/Mn oxide-bound Ni → residual Ni redistribution pathway during flooding, with possible transfers from organic matter-complexed and sulfide-bound pools to residual Ni. During drainage, labile Ni recovered to 1.82%, whereas organic matter-complexed and sulfide-bound Ni increased, indicating limited remobilization. Unified soil–plant modeling suggested apparent redistribution pathways, although several were weakly constrained. Interfacial changes and root-surface retention were associated with limited Ni transfer to grain; grain Ni was 0.34 mg kg–1, providing context for assessments of geogenic Ni mobility and soil-to-rice transfer across a flooding–drainage sequence.

title: Redirecting sulfur metabolic flux by Fe(II) in a simulated composting system: From H 2 S emission to oxidative immobilization
description: Publication date: 1 December 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 520 Author(s): Qinghao Han, Yali Zhang, Junxing Zhu, Jingwen Jia, Qianhan Liang, Caihong Song, Zimin Wei
abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) from food waste composting is a major odor pollutant. This study investigated H2S source reduction via iron regulated sulfur metabolism during food waste composting. Using a quartz-sand simulation system, two Fe(II) (ferrous chloride) concentrations (0.05%, 0.5%) were tested. In the blank control (CK), H2S peaked at 812 mg/m3, cumulatively emitting 2454 mg/m3 over 21 days. The optimal 0.5% Fe(II) completely suppressed H2S emission. Mechanistically, Fe(II) precipitated sulfide as FeS (partially converted to pyrite, 8.81 mg/kg) and may form a microbially mediated Fe(II) regeneration cycle, enabling continuous sulfide immobilization without inhibiting microbial activity. Functional gene analysis revealed that 0.5% Fe(II) suppressed dissimilatory sulfate reduction genes Sat and Apr (peaks falling to 47.3% and 27.3% of CK), reducing sulfide ion content by 94.5%. Conversely, sulfide oxidation gene Sqr was upregulated 212.4%-258.3% (days 3–5), shifting sulfur metabolic flux from reduction to oxidation. Metabolomics identified 210 differential metabolites, with reduced intermediates downregulated (e.g., bisulfite, thiosulfate) and oxidized/stable compounds upregulated, with significant enrichment in cysteine/methionine, sulfur, and taurine metabolism. In conclusion, 0.5% Fe(II) efficiently reduced H2S by redirecting sulfur flux toward oxidative immobilization, establishing a benign Fe(II) cycle.

title: Mercury isotopic fingerprints in human blood and hair from Amazonian riverine populations
description: Publication date: Available online 26 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Gabriel N. Cezarette, Juliette Esplugas, Océane Asensio, Warren T. Corns, Pascale Louvat, Fernando Barbosa Junior, Maïté Bueno, Zoyne Pedrero
abstract: Amazonian riverine populations are chronically exposed to methylmercury through local fish consumption and are among human groups with the highest mercury (Hg) exposure levels worldwide, representing a relevant population-model to investigate Hg internal handling. Despite the recognized Hg toxicity, questions remain about its internal transport, species transformation, and excretion pathways in humans, including the potential influence of selenium (Se). Hg stable isotopes are powerful tracers of Hg sources and metabolic processes, but human studies remain limited and, to date, data in human blood are completely lacking. This work reports Hg isotopic signatures in blood and hair of 107 individuals from Tapajós region, Brazilian Amazon. Hair displayed generally higher δ²⁰²Hg values than blood, whereas Δ¹⁹⁹Hg remained similar in the two matrices (median ~0.54‰). In 56 paired blood–hair samples, the hair–blood δ²⁰²Hg shift reached up to ~1.5‰, potentially reflecting internal Hg processing. This hair–blood shift also decreased with increasing blood Se concentration, leading us to hypothesize that this essential element, long proposed to mitigate Hg toxicity, despite unresolved mechanisms, may modulate internal Hg fractionation and/or detoxification through hair excretion. Overall, this study provides the first Hg stable isotope measurements in human blood, opening new perspectives on Se–Hg interactions beyond the Amazonian context.

title: Molecularly Imprinted PFOA Sensing Using Defect-Scheelite La 2 (MoO 4 ) 3 /Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene Heterostructures with Zn-Ion Energy-Storage Functionality
description: Publication date: Available online 26 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Fouzia Mashkoor, Mohd Shoeb, Saman Zehra, Changyoon Jeong
abstract: Persistent perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) contamination demands highly sensitive analytical platforms, while multifunctional electrode materials offer opportunities for their independent application in environmental sensing and electrochemical energy storage. Herein, defect-scheelite La2(MoO4)3-Ti3C2Tx heterostructures were prepared by microwave-assisted synthesis and composition-controlled assembly. Composites with different Ti3C2Tx contents were evaluated to identify an optimized electrode for Zn-ion hybrid supercapacitors, which was subsequently used as the transducer for a molecularly imprinted poly(o-phenylenediamine)-based PFOA sensor. Structural, morphological, and spectroscopic analyses confirmed preservation of the La2(MoO4)3 framework, strong oxide-Ti3C2Tx interfacial coupling, and uniform oxide distribution on conductive Ti3C2Tx nanosheets. The optimized Lm-Mx3 electrode exhibited a charge-transfer resistance of 0.43 Ω. The Lm-Mx3//Zn device with PVA-ZnSO4 gel electrolyte delivered 318.72F/g at 1.5A/g and 86.76Wh/kg at 1050W/kg, retaining 68% capacitance with approximately 96% Coulombic efficiency after 50,000 cycles. The sensor showed a linear range of 1.260-1000nM, R2 = 0.997, and a detection limit of 0.212nM. Recoveries of 89.60-99.64% were achieved in water and food samples. Conventional interferents caused less than 5% signal variation, whereas related PFAS produced 7.85-23.24% changes, revealing measurable structure-dependent interference during selective recognition. These findings establish the materials-level multifunctionality of the optimized La2(MoO4)3/Ti3C2Tx heterostructure for electrochemical sensing and energy storage applications, demonstrated through two independently configured electrochemical systems.

title: Combined effects of PVC micro-nanoplastics (MNPs) and environmental pollutants (EPs) on lettuce and wheat: Mechanistic insights and food safety implications
description: Publication date: Available online 26 November 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials Author(s): Mandeep Kaur, Milton Das, Sarah Alotaibi, Eshun Gaddi, Sudhir Sharma, Satwik Majumder, Alexander Moser, Glen DeLoid, Omowunmi Sadik, Philip Demokritou, Jason C. White, Nubia Zuverza-Mena
abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are an emerging threat to food security and environmental health. However, the effects of MNPs ageing on pollutant uptake in crops remain largely unexplored. To address this gap, we evaluated the effects of pristine, UV-aged and incinerated polyvinyl chloride (PVC) on the uptake of environmental pollutants (EPs) As, Cr, Pb, boscalid, and perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) in hydroponically grown lettuce and potting-mix grown wheat. Biomass responses were plant species- and PVC-forms, with decreased lettuce shoot and wheat grain mass. Among the co-exposure treatments, only UV-aged PVC enhanced contaminant accumulation in edible tissues relative to EPs alone (except for As in wheat): UV-aged PVC-EPs co-exposure increased Cr, Pb, PFOS and boscalid uptake by 9.1, 10.4-, 1.74- and 4.2-folds in lettuce, and by 1.5-, 1.0-, 0.50- and 3.1-folds in wheat grains, respectively. Accumulation of all plastic types in lettuce shoot (1.13-1.18-fold) and roots (1.11-2.15-fold) was increased with EPs co-exposure. In wheat grains, only unaged PVC MPs uptake was increased (1.46-fold) under EPs co-exposure. The enhanced uptake was associated with high oxidative stress, aquaporin downregulation, compromised root barrier integrity, and potential PVC-EPs associations (Trojan horse effect). These findings show PVC ageing alters crop contaminant transport, requiring aged-plastic co-exposure risk assessments.

title: Distinct cotransport behaviors of antiviral drugs with perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and diethyl phthalate (DEP) in contrasting porous media under saturated conditions
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Qi Liu, Peng Peng, Yating Hua, Qianyuan Huang, Yingyu Chen, Hui Feng, Haoxiang Yang, Shaolin Wang, Yun Zhang
abstract: Antiviral drugs are widely detected in aquatic environments due to their large-scale consumption and incomplete removal, with an estimated 30–50% of administered doses excreted unmetabolized. Their transport behavior in porous media, particularly under coexisting contamination scenarios, remains poorly understood. This study investigated the transport of two representative antiviral drugs, ribavirin (RBV) and remdesivir (RDS), in quartz sand and paddy soil, and examined their cotransport behavior with a coexisting contaminant, perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) or diethyl phthalate (DEP), under saturated flow conditions. In single-solute systems, transport was governed by compound hydrophobicity, ionization state, and medium properties: RBV and anionic PFOA exhibited near-conservative transport in quartz sand, while their retention increased moderately in organic-rich paddy soil. The moderately hydrophobic RDS and weakly hydrophobic DEP showed stronger retention, particularly in paddy soil, where abundant organic matter and fine particles enhanced sorption. Under cotransport conditions, three distinct interaction mechanisms were suggested: independent transport (RBV–PFOA), competitive adsorption (RBV–DEP), and synergistic co-retention (RDS–DEP and RDS–PFOA). These interactions were negligible in quartz sand but substantially amplified in paddy soil, indicating that medium heterogeneity mediates cotransport behavior. These findings demonstrate that the transport of antiviral drugs in porous media may differ substantially under coexisting contamination scenarios, highlighting the need to account for both compound interactions and medium heterogeneity in environmental risk assessment.

title: Integrating soil-gas tracers and Laser-Induced Fluorescence for spatial characterization of potential LNAPL secondary source zones
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Giulia Felli, Livio Ruggiero, Paolo Rizzetto, Marco Petrangeli Papini, Paolo Ciampi
abstract: Light non-aqueous phase liquids (LNAPLs) represent persistent sources of groundwater contamination, and their spatial delineation remains a major challenge for contaminated-site characterization. This study presents an integrated framework combining soil-gas tracers (222Rn, CO2, and CH4) with high-resolution Laser-Induced Fluorescence (LIF) investigations to characterize potential LNAPL secondary source zones. The approach was applied at a former military site in southern Sardinia (Italy) affected by multiple historical JP-8 fuel releases. A multiplicative Combined Index (CI_mult) was developed by integrating normalized maximum LIF fluorescence with inverted normalized 222Rn concentrations, while additional soil-gas parameters were used as supporting tracers. The derived CI_mult surface showed strong spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I = 0.984, p = 0.001), and Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) identified High–High areas covering 34,250 m2. At the P80 operational threshold, high LIF responses characterized 91.4% of the High–High area, 222Rn-depletion anomalies 47.3%, and their simultaneous occurrence 40.4%. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that component-overlap estimates were threshold-dependent, whereas the main high-CI_mult spatial patterns were largely preserved under an alternative arithmetic integration rule. Because LIF and 222Rn are components of the CI_mult, their spatial correspondence reflects internal spatial consistency rather than independent validation. Overall, the framework provides a quantitative integration of direct and indirect indicators that can support spatial prioritization of areas potentially associated with LNAPL secondary source zones and guide targeted site investigations.

title: Modeling nitrate–nitrogen fate in the deep vadose zone of the North China Plain under long-term irrigation and precipitation
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Hanchang Li, Yue Li, Yunhan Chang, Dongyang Ren, Xu Xu, Junwei Tan, Guanhua Huang
abstract: Intensive agriculture in the North China Plain has caused massive nitrate–nitrogen (NO3 −–N) accumulation in the deep vadose zone, posing a serious threat to groundwater quality. However, the long-term effects of climate variability, irrigation, and N fertilization on NO3 −–N transport and leaching through the deep vadose zone remain poorly understood. Using the winter wheat–summer maize rotation system in the Shijiazhuang area of the North China Plain as a representative case, this study systematically quantified NO3 −–N migration and depth-dependent leaching dynamics along a 4400 cm deep soil profile from 2004 to 2024 and assessed the long-term mitigation potential of different irrigation and N fertilization strategies. The calibrated model results showed that the synergistic effect of extreme precipitation and excessive irrigation accelerated the downward migration of NO3 −–N peaks. NO3 −–N leaching from the soil above the 1000 cm rapidly responded to precipitation and irrigation, requiring only 1–2 years to leach beyond this depth, whereas NO3 −–N leaching in deeper layers exhibited a substantial lag effect. Under the influence of extreme precipitation events, NO3 −–N required continuous N fertilization for 12 years to migrate below 3500 cm, increasing annual leaching at the 4300 cm depth from 5 to 28 kg ha−1. Reducing irrigation and N input effectively mitigated soil NO3 −–N leaching, while the mitigation effect was delayed by 1–2 years for every 500 cm increase in depth. Below the 3500 cm depth, a notable reduction in leaching (ranging from 0.01% to 77%) required 12 years. Notably, compared with the current strategy (an annualized irrigation of 400 mm and an annualized N application of 620 kg ha−1), a 25% reduction in irrigation and N application was found to be the optimal strategy among the simulated scenarios at this site. Under this strategy, crop yield losses remained below 5% in most years, while NO3 −–N leaching decreased by 46%–77%. It substantially suppressed the “pulse-like” heavy leaching triggered by extreme precipitation, thereby effectively mitigating groundwater contamination risks. Our insights provide a useful basis and practical guidance for developing targeted groundwater protection and pollution control strategies in intensive agricultural watersheds where winter wheat–summer maize rotation is practiced under conditions similar to those in this study.

title: Remote-sensing-derived declines in ammonia-nitrogen across the river network of Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area under water pollution controls
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Jiahui Hao, Ni Wen, Xingda Chen, Yun Zhang, Guorong Yu, Jinyue Chen, Mingjie Duan, Qianling Ci, Yida Lu, Guanxi Ou, Shuisen Chen, Dan Li, Richen Ye, Xia Zhou, Chongyang Wang
abstract: Ammonia nitrogen (NH₃-N) is a key parameter in the ecological assessment of urban river network systems. Owing to its lack of distinct spectral features and the influence of complex environmental factors, long-term spatiotemporal monitoring of NH₃-N remains challenging. In this study, a machine learning model was developed to retrieve NH₃-N concentrations in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) using Sentinel-2 MSI imagery. The model was evaluated using 48 independent validation samples (R2 = 0.636, RMSE = 0.366 mg·L−1, MAE = 0.204 mg·L−1). It was then applied to 398 Sentinel-2 scenes to estimate NH₃-N concentrations during the dry seasons from 2015 to 2025 and analyze their spatiotemporal variations. The results showed that the annual mean NH₃-N concentration decreased from over 1.50 mg·L−1 in 2015 to approximately 1.00 mg·L−1 in 2025. Class III waters (0.5–1.0 mg·L−1) were widespread across the GBA, while higher concentrations (≥1.0 mg·L−1) were mainly observed along the Guangzhou–Dongguan boundary and in eastern Jiangmen. NH₃-N concentrations also showed seasonal differences, with higher levels during October–December (0.97–1.36 mg·L−1) than during January–March (0.79–0.96 mg·L−1). The Guangzhou–Dongguan region consistently exhibited relatively high concentrations. The observed reductions in NH₃-N concentrations, particularly during 2017–2020, were temporally consistent with the implementation of water pollution control policies, the river chief system, and integrated watershed management measures since 2015–2016. These findings provide useful information for identifying pollution hotspots, assessing changes in water quality, and supporting water quality management in complex river network–estuarine systems.

title: Physicochemical characterization and phytotoxic potential of lysimeter leachates derived from hard coal mine waste and combustion ash
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Dominika Dąbrowska, Marek Sołtysiak, Wojciech Rykała, Aleksandra Wdowczyk, Agata Szymańska-Pulikowska, Bernard Gałka
abstract: Leachates from coal mine waste and combustion ash may contain high concentrations of soluble constituents, but chemical composition alone does not establish their biological effects. The aim of this study was to characterize the physicochemical burden of lysimeter leachates from a coal mine waste–ash mixture and compare chemical pollution indices with phytotoxicity and acute earthworm responses. Four flow-weighted composite samples were analyzed. Sodium concentrations were 700–1000 mg/L, boron concentrations were 15–19 mg/L, and sulfate reached 3550 mg/L in sample XII. Nitrogen species and phosphate were low or below their quantification limits. The comprehensive pollution index (CPI) and Nemerow pollution index (PN), calculated using groundwater thresholds as comparative benchmarks, indicated a high chemical burden, dominated by boron and, in sample XII, sulfate. Sinapis alba and Lepidium sativum showed species- and sample-dependent responses, with moderate phytotoxicity (GI 50–80%) in four of eight species–sample combinations and no cases of high phytotoxicity (GI <50%). In the 14-day Eisenia fetida soil test, mortality was limited to one individual in the undiluted XII treatment (2.5%), and body-mass changes did not differ significantly among treatments. The plant responses are consistent with stress from a mineral-rich mixture, but the contribution of individual constituents was not established. The contrasting biological responses show why chemical characterization should be combined with multiple test species and endpoints when assessing these leachates; low short-term earthworm mortality does not demonstrate environmental safety.

title: Hydrochemical controls on uranium mobility and its redox-dependent coupling with dissolved organic matter across multilayer aquifers in the Datong Basin, China
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Hanyue Wang, Qin Ge, Junpeng Zhang, Xinyan Li, Haiyan Liu, Jianing Fan
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) can influence uranium (U) mobility through complexation, surface interactions, and redox processes, but its role across vertically stratified alkaline aquifers remains uncertain. Groundwater samples (n = 46) were collected from the Datong Basin, China, and hydrochemical analysis, nitrate isotope analysis, EEM-PARAFAC, Visual MINTEQ modeling, and correlation analysis were integrated to evaluate U mobility and its association with DOM. Groundwater U concentrations ranged from below the reporting limit to 322 μg·L−1, and 32.61% of samples exceeded the World Health Organization guideline of 30 μg·L−1. Mean U concentrations decreased from 86 μg·L−1 in the shallow phreatic aquifer (Zone I) to 11 and 8 μg·L−1 in the semi-confined and confined aquifers (Zones II and III), respectively, together with generally lower ORP at depth. PARAFAC resolved fulvic-like C1, humic-like C2, and tryptophan-like C3; the model explained 98.46% of fluorescence variance and had a core consistency diagnostic (CORCONDIA) of 65.76%. Ca–U–CO₃ complexes dominated the modeled aqueous U speciation in Zones I and II, whereas modeled organic-bound U species accounted for less than 0.5%. In Zone I, U was strongly correlated with total organic carbon (TOC) (r = 0.80, p < 0.001), but TOC-controlled correlations between U and C1-C3 were not significant in any zone. Zone III combined low U concentrations and lower mean ORP with nonsignificant negative partial-correlation trends between U and the three fluorescence components. This pattern is compatible with redox-sensitive and mineral-associated U retention but does not directly demonstrate U reduction or component-specific DOM control. Variations in nitrate isotopes and localized enrichments of NO3 −, SO4 2−, and TOC in several deep samples further indicate hydrochemical heterogeneity. Overall, the vertical distribution of dissolved U was associated with differences in aquifer hydrochemistry and redox conditions. Although Ca-U-CO₃ complexes dominated the modeled aqueous U speciation, their predominance did not fully explain the zonal variation in dissolved U concentrations. DOM-U coupling was more closely associated with bulk organic matter abundance, whereas component-specific associations with individual fluorescent components were comparatively weak.

title: Occurrence and ecological risk of carbamate insecticides in river surface water and adjacent shallow groundwater across urban and agricultural catchments
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Haixin An, Xiaocui Wang
abstract: Carbamate insecticides (CBs) occur widely in aquatic environments, yet their ecological thresholds remain poorly defined due to limited chronic toxicity data and insufficient knowledge of contamination across contrasting land-use watersheds. The occurrence, ecological thresholds, and ecological risks of CBs were systematically investigated in the urbanized Licun River and the predominantly agricultural Wulong River. Species sensitivity distributions (SSDs) were established for 12 representative CBs using a comprehensive toxicity database, while acute toxicity data were converted to chronic endpoints through acute-to-chronic ratios (ACRs), thereby extending the toxicity dataset in a manner analogous to completing missing pieces of a puzzle for more robust ecological threshold derivation. A total of 22 CBs were detected in surface waters, whereas 20 CBs were identified in groundwater. The Licun River exhibited substantially higher contamination levels than the Wulong River, with aldicarb reaching a maximum concentration of 350.26 ng L−1, while dioxacarb predominated in the agricultural watershed (mean 12.98 ng L−1), revealing distinct contamination fingerprints driven by divergent land-use patterns. Furthermore, 12 HC₅ and PNEC values were successfully derived. Deterministic risk quotients identified aldicarb, carbaryl, and propoxur as highest-risk, with chronic RQ > 1.0 for aldicarb at three urban Licun River sites; probabilistic joint probability curves showed catchment-scale chronic risk concentrated in a few compounds whose exposure ranges overlap the steep part of their sensitivity distributions. This study derives robust water quality thresholds for representative CBs and offers an integrated framework for watershed-specific pesticide management.

title: Spatiotemporal patterns and driving mechanisms of Total nitrogen in a typical agricultural watershed based on remote sensing: A case study of the Yiluo River Basin
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Zhengqiong Liu, Cangjie Shi, Chengzhi Sun, Qiang Xu, Weiqiang Chen, Guangxing Ji, Yuan Li, Zhubin Zheng, Yulong Guo
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying agricultural production and escalating rural resource exploitation, farmland nutrient leaching has emerged as a critical bottleneck constraining the improvement of rural habitats and aquatic ecological security. As surface water serves as the primary carrier for nitrogen (N) migration and transformation, understanding the spatiotemporal evolution of total nitrogen (TN) concentrations in agricultural watersheds and their response mechanisms to rural production activities remains crucial yet poorly understood. This study utilized the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform combined with 785 sets of in-situ TN data from 11 automatic water quality monitoring stations to retrieve TN concentrations across the entire Yiluo River Basin (YRB) from 2019 to 2024, employing three machine learning algorithms (eXtreme Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine). Results showed that the XGBoost model achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.75, RMSE = 1.22 mg/L), enabling rapid and comprehensive monitoring of non-point source pollution in agricultural watersheds. Spatially, TN levels exhibited a distinct “low in the west, high in the east” pattern, with hotspots near confluences, urban centers, and the Luhun Reservoir, while temporally following a “stable-peak-decline” trajectory peaking at 3.933 mg/L in 2022–2023 before declining to 3.231 mg/L in 2024. Driver analysis revealed that cropland (r = 0.75) and impervious surfaces (r = 0.64) were the land-use variables most strongly correlated with TN, whereas forest and grassland were negatively correlated with TN; Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis identified four key driving modules-agricultural production, urban interference, weather-driven transport, and ecological barriers-highlighting the composite nature of nitrogen pollution. This study establishes a reliable and cost-effective framework for TN monitoring via GEE platform, creating a complete analytical loop from spatial monitoring to driver identification and policy formulation, thereby offering a replicable model for managing similar agricultural rivers in the Yellow River Basin.

title: Physics-guided deep learning for watershed-scale prediction of streamflow and Escherichia coli dynamics
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Do Hyuck Kwon, Dae Seong Jeong, Jin Hwi Kim, Heewon Jeong, Minjeong Kim, Keooudone Latsachack, Olivier Ribolzi, Laurie Boithias, Kyu-Tae Lee, Seok Min Hong, Kyung Hwa Cho
abstract: Fecal contamination in surface water poses a major public-health risk, particularly in tropical catchments with limited sanitation infrastructure and monsoon-driven rainfall. While hydrological model, soil and water assessment tool (SWAT), has provided valuable hydrological insights, it faces challenges in capturing nonlinear and event-driven microbial transport. In contrast, deep learning models demonstrate strong predictive capabilities for complex environmental processes but often lack physical consistency and interpretability. To address these limitations, a novel physics-guided deep learning framework was developed by integrating hydrological knowledge from SWAT simulations into a deep learning architecture. The framework combines a long short-term memory (LSTM) network for temporal features with a convolutional neural network (CNN) for spatial feature extraction. A physics-guided loss function based on SWAT simulations was incorporated to guide model training. The physics-guided LSTM-CNN achieved a Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) of 0.96 for streamflow and 0.96 for Escherichia coli (E. coli) contamination during the test period, outperforming both SWAT and standalone LSTM-CNN models. Furthermore, explainable artificial intelligence analysis showed that the contributions of input variables in the physics-guided LSTM-CNN were consistent with domain knowledge on hydrological and microbial dynamics. These findings of this research demonstrated that the potential of integrating hydrological knowledge into deep learning could enhance predictive accuracy for practical water risk management in aquatic ecosystems

title: Quantitative monitoring of DNAPL source-zone evolution in heterogeneous sand-clay aquifers via deep learning fusion of time-lapse ERT and induced polarization
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Fansong Meng, Jinguo Wang, Yun Yang, Yaping Qi
abstract: Dense non-aqueous phase liquids (DNAPLs) form highly irregular source zones in saturated heterogeneous sand-clay media, where conventional single-method geophysical surveys are limited by insufficient spatial resolution and clay-induced electrical background interference, and standard inversion remains inadequate for quantitative characterization of contaminant distributions. This study develops a data-model integration framework that couples petrophysical constraints with a U-Net architecture, fusing time-lapse cross-borehole electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) and time-domain induced polarization (TDIP) to map multi-source electrical parameters directly to DNAPL saturation. Because clay distribution governs DNAPL migration pathways, chargeability and normalized chargeability are incorporated as petrophysical medium-background constraints. For the demonstration case, time-lapse fusion outperforms static fusion by a wide margin, raising the intersection over union from 0.27 to 0.63 and reducing the boundary displacement distance from 0.81 to 0.23 m. Across a fixed subset of 150 stochastic realizations, the normalized-chargeability constraint further reduces the boundary displacement distance by 6.65–7.50% relative to unconstrained time-lapse fusion, and its advantage in image-domain MSE emerges at the 5–10% observation-noise levels representative of field acquisition. Increasing observation noise from 1% to 10% raises the image-domain MSE by 28–34%, while ±10% single-factor perturbation of the petrophysical parameters changes the evaluation metrics by at most 2.34%. In the synthetic sand–clay scenarios considered here the framework shows promising performance for monitoring source-zone evolution, and provides a basis for future laboratory and field validation.

title: The importance of eventflow sampling for river load estimation of trace contaminants
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Nikolaus Weber, Steffen Kittlaus, Katarina Kozlica, Radmila Milačič Ščančar, Jörg Krampe, Matthias Zessner, Ottavia Zoboli
abstract: The accurate quantification of riverine contaminant loads is essential for assessing mitigation measures, pollution transport to downstream recipients (lakes, seas, countries) and for substance balance model validation. However, monitoring programmes based on regular, low-frequency grab samples often fail to adequately capture high-flow events (hereinafter referred to as eventflow). Ignoring these periods introduces significant bias into load estimation. To address this limitation, we developed and validated a targeted sampling strategy that combines high-frequency in-situ measurements with flow-type composite sampling, enabling accurate load estimation with reduced analytical effort. We tested this approach across three rivers with varying catchment characteristics and applied it to quantify seasonal and annual loads of trace contaminants representing different emission pathways and transport behaviours, including total and dissolved potentially toxic elements (PTEs), such as Hg, Ni, Pb, Cu, Cr, Zn, Cd, and As; pharmaceuticals; perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs); and perfluoroalkyl sulfonic acids (PFSAs). We derived the eventflow contributions to annual loads and quantified the potential bias from conventional sampling that misses eventflow periods. Our results demonstrate that eventflow sampling and its proper representation in load estimation are essential for particle-bound and hydrologically responsive contaminants. Excluding eventflow samples led to substantial underestimation of total PTEs loads ( ∼ 50% on average). For river systems dominated by diffuse inputs, PFCA loads were underestimated by ∼ 30% and pharmaceuticals by 28%–55%. In contrast, for river systems with substantial wastewater treatment plant inputs, the bias of dissolved PTEs, pharmaceuticals, and PFSA remained modest (typically within ± 15%), reflecting the dominance of steady point pathway contributions. The results demonstrate that our targeted sampling strategy provides a validated, cost-effective solution for accurate load estimation of trace contaminants.

title: Source-zone-informed numerical modeling of DNAPL transport and remediation in fractured media: From process representation to credible prediction
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Yuqing You, Fuyun Huang, Xiaoqing Shi, Chuanyin Jiang, Di Deng, Jie Zhou, Xiaoguang Wang
abstract: Dense non-aqueous phase liquids (DNAPLs) in fractured media remain difficult to predict because the source-zone architecture controlling dissolution, matrix storage, and remediation response is rarely directly observable or uniquely identifiable. This review frames numerical modeling of DNAPL transport and remediation as a source-zone-informed hydrological prediction problem. We synthesize the spatiotemporal lifecycle of contamination and compare continuum, discrete-fracture, and hybrid representations alongside inverse and surrogate-assisted approaches. Across the reviewed studies, prescribed source architectures, scale-dependent constitutive relations, and scarce independent field validation limit predictive credibility. Greater geometric or process detail therefore does not necessarily improve forecasts. For pump-and-treat, surfactant-enhanced remediation, thermal treatment, chemical oxidation, and enhanced bioremediation, we assess how process representation, treatment-induced feedbacks, and observation requirements affect prediction. Cross-domain comparisons with karst hydrology, radionuclide migration, petroleum reservoir simulation, and geological carbon storage identify transferable strategies for inferring hidden structure, representing long-term exchange, and updating coupled models. The resulting fit-for-purpose framework links prediction targets to model structure, priority observations, and uncertainty outputs. It emphasizes independent testing and iterative model-observation-inversion workflows, treating remediation operations as diagnostic perturbations as well as interventions. Future priorities are shared lifecycle datasets, cross-scale tests of effective relationships, and efficient inference across alternative source and process hypotheses. These developments are needed to distinguish sustained source depletion from temporary concentration suppression and strengthen the evidence supporting hydrological and remediation decisions.

title: Driving mechanisms of rainfall recharge intensity on hydrological response and nitrate source evolution in a karst spring system
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Shuna Sun, Mingming Luo, Xiangyu Peng, Wenhui Zhao, Haoyang Li, Xiaoyang Liu, Hengquan Wang
abstract: Karst groundwater is a vital global freshwater resource, and rainfall-driven recharge plays a critical role in controlling groundwater flow and solute transport. This study investigated the Qinglongkou Spring (QLK Spring) system in western Hubei Province, China. Hydrological responses and nitrate sources under different rainfall intensities were examined using high-frequency hydrological monitoring, hydrochemical analyses, dual nitrate isotopes (δ15N-NO3 − and δ18O-NO3 −), and the MixSIAR Bayesian mixing model. Results indicate that rainfall intensity is a major factor influencing hydrodynamic responses and nitrate transport in the karst system. The high-intensity rainfall event (mean intensity 9.5 mm·h−1) activated conduit flow and preferential flow pathways, resulting in a 1.5 h response lag and a peak spring discharge of 2990.7 L·s−1. In contrast, the low-intensity rainfall event (mean intensity 2.4 mm·h−1) showed a 7.5 h response lag and a lower peak spring discharge of 1347.9 L·s−1, reflecting slower recharge with a greater contribution from diffuse infiltration and fracture flow. Hydrochemical variations were jointly controlled by dilution and water-rock interactions. Solute fluxes responded synchronously to discharge during the high-intensity rainfall event, whereas stronger water–rock interactions during the low-intensity rainfall event produced relatively high solute concentrations but low fluxes. Ammonium-based fertilizers and soil organic nitrogen were identified as the primary potential nitrate sources. During the high-intensity rainfall event, the sum of the posterior mean contributions from these two sources exceeded 65%, whereas during the low-intensity rainfall event, the posterior mean contribution of ammonium-based fertilizers decreased to 15.7%–16.4%, accompanied by increased contributions from atmospheric deposition and manure/sewage. The high-intensity rainfall event was associated with rapid mobilization and high-flux export of agricultural nitrate, whereas the low-intensity rainfall event showed greater source mixing and biogeochemical buffering, resulting in a more balanced source contribution pattern. These findings indicate that rainfall intensity can substantially influence nitrate source contributions and transport dynamics by modifying recharge pathways, hydraulic connectivity, and water residence times, providing insights for groundwater quality management and non-point source pollution control in karst regions.

title: Virus transport mediated by microorganisms and micro-nano bubbles in soil
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Weipeng Liu, Fengxian Chen, Liqiong Yang
abstract: Public health threats from pathogenic viruses remain a persistent societal concern. Viruses enter soils through irrigation, manure application, or aquifer recharge, with their subsurface transport and fate determining the associated public health risk. While soil microorganisms are a key ecosystem component, their role in virus transport remains a critical knowledge gap. This study aims to investigate the influence of soil microorganisms on virus transport and to evaluate the feasibility of using micro-nano bubbles (MNBs) to mitigate virus transport. We selected two model viruses with different isoelectric points (MS2 and ΦX174) and performed column experiments, varying microbial activity (native vs. inhibited) and the presence of MNBs (with vs. without MNBs). We observed enhanced transport for both viruses in soil with repressed microbial activity, which was attributable to the lower abundance of microbial cells. The virus with the higher isoelectric point (ΦX174) exhibited more pronounced transport changes, with recovery differing by ~62.49 percentage points between the two treatments. Furthermore, MNBs could hinder virus transport by providing air–water interfaces. This effect was more pronounced when microbial activity was inhibited, with MNB addition reducing MS2 recovery by ~14.52 percentage points. This study reveals the distinct roles of microorganisms and MNBs in virus transport and underscores the importance of considering biological processes when assessing the fate of viruses in soil.

title: Lacustrine groundwater discharge drives antibiotic fluxes in large shallow lakes: From a hidden sink to a secondary source
description: Publication date: January 2027 Source: Journal of Contaminant Hydrology, Volume 284 Author(s): Jiamei Zhang, Yu Wang, Gege Cai, Fazhi Xie, Yuyang Zhu, Zhiqiang Xie, Xing Chen, Guolian Li, Shan Li, Xin Luo
abstract: Intensified human activities have exacerbated antibiotic pollution in large freshwater lakes. Although multiple pathways can transport antibiotics into lakes, the contribution of lacustrine groundwater discharge (LGD) to surface water contamination remains insufficiently understood. This study investigated the migration of antibiotics across surface water and groundwater in Chaohu Lake, the fifth-largest freshwater lake in China, with a specific focus on LGD contributions. Overall, antibiotic concentrations were higher in surface water than in groundwater, with both water bodies exhibiting elevated levels during the dry season.
