Governance correspondingly shifted from localized adaptation toward basin-scale coordinated regulation, water–sediment management, and ecological restoration. These stage transitions reflect changing feedbacks among climatic variability, human interventions, ecological conditions, fluvial processes, and institutional arrangements, offering a long-term socio-hydrological perspective on hydrological vulnerability and sustainable management in the Yellow River Basin.

title: Afghanistan's water security crisis: Coupled hydroclimatic stress, groundwater depletion, water quality risks, and institutional constraints
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Sajid Ullah, Rujun Chen
abstract: Study region Afghanistan is an arid to semiarid country where river flow variability, precipitation fluctuations, limited groundwater recharge, irrigation demand, and snow and glacier dynamics constrain water availability. Changes in these processes at the basin scale directly affect national water security. Study focus This review synthesizes peer-reviewed and gray literature published from 2017 to 2025, integrating hydrogeological, water-quality, remote sensing (RS), geographic information system (GIS), and hydroclimatic studies. It evaluates surface-water availability, groundwater quantity and quality, and the impacts of climate variability and water-management practices on Afghanistan’s water resources. New hydrological insights for the region The reviewed studies demonstrate significant spatial variability across Afghanistan’s major river basins. The Kabul River Basin (KRB) is the most well-documented hotspot of groundwater stress, with reported declines of up to 1.5 m yr⁻¹ , reduced storage, excessive abstraction, and deteriorating water quality. In contrast, the Helmand River Basin (HRB) and Panj-Amu River Basin (PARB) are strongly controlled by cryospheric processes, with snowmelt contributing approximately 77% and 74% of annual river flow, respectively. Changes in snow persistence, glacier conditions, runoff timing, and drought patterns threaten surface-water reliability and groundwater recharge. Overall, Afghanistan’s water crisis stems from the combined effects of hydroclimatic variability and anthropogenic pressures. Significant uncertainties persist in poorly monitored basins, underscoring the need for improved monitoring networks, recharge assessments, and integrated water-resource management.

title: Estimating reference evapotranspiration across major agricultural seasons in Bangladesh’s croplands: Ground data to spatio-temporal insights using machine learning
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Sabyasachi Niloy, Ajoy Kumar Saha, Pinki Debnath, Raj Kiron Kishan
abstract: Study region In Bangladesh’s seasonally variable climate, reference evapotranspiration (ETₒ) across cropland is vital for agricultural water management. This study used a spatio-temporal approach for ETₒ mapping in Bangladesh. Study focus This study produced spatially explicit, agricultural season-based cropland ETₒ maps (500 m) using historical observations (1998–2023) from 35 meteorological stations for spatio-temporal analysis. Traditional interpolation methods were compared with Bayesian-optimized Machine Learning (ML) models, including Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), XGBoost, and weighted ensembles. New hydrological insights for the region ML approaches outperformed conventional interpolation methods, while incorporating spatio-temporal information improved traditional models. Based on error metrics and the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, XGBoost was selected for seasonal mapping (MAE: 0.16, RMSE: 0.21, and R²: 0.91). SHAP analysis indicated strong seasonal contributions to ETₒ prediction. ETₒ was highest in Kharif-I/pre-monsoon (4.16–4.96 mm/day), followed by Kharif-II/monsoon (3.52–3.92 mm/day) and Rabi/winter (2.54–3.50 mm/day). Kharif-II showed more widespread ETₒ increases; however, trends were non-uniform and spatially concentrated, with recent peaks. ETₒ hotspots shifted mainly from southern and southwestern regions in Kharif-I to northern and northwestern regions in Kharif-II, and to southeastern coastal and hilly regions in Rabi. K-means clustering identified four seasonal ETₒ regimes. The generalized additive model (GAM) indicated higher associations of solar radiation, temperature, and wind speed with ETₒ. Findings support climate-resilient irrigation planning and sustainable agricultural water management in Bangladesh.

title: Influence of extreme rainfall during Cyclone Boris on the water quality of the urban Tócó Stream in Hungary
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Imre Boczonádi, Sándor Kun, Edina Baranyai, Zsófi Sajtos, János Tamás, Attila Nagy
abstract: Study region Tócó Stream located in Debrecen, Hungary. Study focus The increasing frequency of extreme precipitation events significantly impacts the water quality of urban streams, especially small watercourses. In this study, we examined the effects of Cyclone Boris, which affected Debrecen in September 2024, on the water quality of the Tócó Stream at two sites with different land uses (near-natural and urban areas). New hydrological insights for the region Our results indicate that water quality parameters experienced more moderate fluctuations at the near-natural site, whereas significant deterioration and extreme fluctuations became evident at the urban site, particularly concerning organic load (BOD5), nutrient forms (NO2 -, NO3 -, PO4 3-), and microbiological parameters. At this site, due to the large volume of excess water, a dilution effect was noted in several parameters (including conductivity and nutrients), reflecting the dominance of continuous background loading. The statistical analysis revealed that water quality trends are influenced by precipitation-driven input of nutrients and organic matter, as well as changes in oxygen levels. Sediment analyses indicated episodic metal loading in the urban site, particularly for Cd, Cu, and Zn, which revealed a decreasing trend following precipitation events. A key outcome of the study was the development of a comprehensive water and sediment quality assessment system suitable for small watercourses, enabling the consistent evaluation of various parameters.

title: Snow Water Equivalent Index (SWEI): A non-parametric approach for snow drought assessment in Iran
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Somayeh Hajivand Paydari, Mohammad Saligheh, Bohloul Alijani, AliReza Karbalaee
abstract: Study region The snow domain of Iran (about 545,000 km2), comprising the Alborz and Zagros, the north-western and north-eastern highlands and isolated central mountains, where snowmelt sustains spring streamflow and aquifer recharge in a semi-arid climate. Study focus The non-parametric Standardized Snow Water Equivalent Index (SWEI) of Huning and AghaKouchak (2020), Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 117, (1975)3–(1975)9) was applied to 0.1° ERA5-Land data for 1980–2025. Because SWEI depends only on within-pixel ranks, it is insensitive to time-invariant reanalysis bias. The domain was defined independently from MODIS snow cover, and ERA5-Land was evaluated against 23 stations and an independent land-surface product. Snow-drought characteristics were compared between water years 1982–2003 and 2004–2025 and tested for trends with the Mann–Kendall test. New hydrological insights for the region ERA5-Land reproduced the timing and spatial ranking of snow water equivalent (SWE) but not its magnitude. Snow-drought frequency rose from 0.21 to 0.41, and the share of severe-to-exceptional classes roughly tripled. Increasing trends in duration and risk were significant over about 78% of the domain, with no significant decrease anywhere. Snow-season temperature rose by 1.4 °C, whereas total precipitation declined by only 5.3% (not significant); snowfall and SWE declined by 22% and 41%. This mismatch shows that warm snow drought, undetectable by precipitation-based indices, dominates. The hotspots are the central–southern Zagros and Kopet Dagh–Binalud, headwaters of major rivers and aquifers.

title: Sediment reduction or elevated risk? Vertical Heterogeneity in saturated hydraulic conductivity shapes the hydrological trade-off between erosion control and shallow landslide susceptibility on the Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Honglei Tang, Yuxin Li, Ju Chen, Qihua Ran, Zheng Lu, Yunhao Lai, Jihui Gao
abstract: Study region The Chinese Loess Plateau has undergone extensive vegetation restoration, reducing soil erosion but raising concerns about shallow landslide susceptibility under extreme rainfall. Study focus We coupled the Integrated Hydrology Model (InHM) with an infinite-slope stability model in Shejiagou catchment to examine how vegetation-induced changes in saturated hydraulic conductivity (K sat ) profiles shaped runoff, erosion and stability. Forty vegetation-associated simulations based on measured profile-values together with thirty-two controlled simulations with fixed surface-layer conductivities or average conductivities were conducted. Responses of surface-subsurface hydrological processes, soil erosion and slope stability to the vertical heterogeneity of K sat were compared under high/low rainfall conditions and dry/wet antecedent conditions. New hydrological insights for the region Under high-intensity rainfall on dry soil, profiles with higher near-surface conductivity reduced discharge by 15.8%–68.6% and hydraulic sediment yield by 15.2%–66.6%, yet diverted water was stored at depth and forest profiles developed deeper potential instability than same-age grass profiles, a contrast amplified under wet conditions. Controlled profiles matched in surface conductivity and thickness-weighted mean isolate this mechanism. Altering internal conductivity allocation cut sediment yield by 19.7%–26.7% but enlarged the potentially unstable area from 31.0% to 33.6% and from 45.3% to 53.2%. Erosion-control benefits from vegetation restoration in the Loess Plateau cannot be judged from reductions of runoff and soil erosion alone. Future strategies must jointly weigh erosion control against the increasing depth-dependent potential instability.

title: Increasing fragility of groundwater sustainability across the Tibetan Plateau revealed by a RRV (reliability, resilience and vulnerability)-based framework
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wenhao Ren, Jianping Han, Hui Qian, Zongjie Li, Panpan Xu, Jie Chen, Xianmin Ke, Mengna Li, Qiying Zhang, Yuting Zhang, Yanyan Gao
abstract: Study region The Tibetan Plateau (TP). Study focus Groundwater is a critical component of the TP, and its sustainability has become an important scientific and environmental concern. However, comprehensive assessments of groundwater sustainability that simultaneously consider groundwater reliability, recovery capacity, and deficit severity remain limited. In this study, a RRV (reliability-resilience-vulnerability)-based framework was applied to evaluate groundwater sustainability across the TP during 2003–2025 using GRACE-derived groundwater storage anomaly (GWSA) data. New hydrological insights GWSA across the TP exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with increasing trends mainly distributed in the central and northern plateau and decreasing trends concentrated in the southern regions. During 2003–2025, the TP experienced an average of 12.49 unsatisfactory events, with a mean event duration of 5.14 months and a cumulative duration of 47.21 months. During the recent decade (2016–2025), both the frequency and duration of unsatisfactory events decreased across most subbasins. Reliability increased from 0.63 in 2003 to 0.83 in 2025, whereas resilience decreased markedly from 0.65 to 0.28. Vulnerability fluctuated but decreased overall from 0.44 to 0.21. Consequently, the GRACE-based sustainability index (GSI) increased from 0.55 in 2003 to 0.63 in 2008, followed by an overall decline after 2015 and reaching 0.56 in 2017, with a short-term recovery during 2018–2021. Spatially, GSI values were generally higher along the humid eastern margins (>0.70) and lower in the arid central and southwestern endorheic basins (<0.40). These findings highlight the increasing sensitivity of groundwater and emphasize the necessity of incorporating recovery capacity and vulnerability into future groundwater management and water-resource sustainability assessments in high-altitude regions.

title: Spatiotemporal reconfiguration of estuarine multi-reservoir systems under extreme saltwater intrusion: A distributionally robust approach
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Chang Yu, Kang Xie, Ruimin He, Qian Cheng, Cuishan Liu, Guoqing Wang, Junliang Jin, Jianyun Zhang
abstract: Study region The Yangtze River estuary, China, specifically focusing on the interconnected municipal water supply network comprising the estuarine Qingcaosha and Chenhang reservoirs, alongside the inland Jinze Reservoir. Study focus Estuarine freshwater resources face severe threats from intensifying saltwater intrusion. Under nonstationary hydrological dynamics, traditional stochastic management fails to fully comprehend distributional shifts, leaving water systems vulnerable to extreme anomalies. We propose an adaptive Wasserstein distributionally robust optimization (WDRO) framework to explicitly quantify deep distributional uncertainty. This approach shifts regional water management from expected cost efficiency toward dynamic system stability, optimizing fundamental tradeoffs among water shortages, operational costs, and salinity tail risks. New hydrological insights for the region: Under escalating extreme saltwater threats, estuarine water infrastructure must rely on critical spatiotemporal reconfiguration rather than static dispatch rules. The robust framework autonomously executes adaptive spatial decoupling, leveraging the inland Jinze Reservoir as a reliable hydrodynamic buffer and maximizing preemptive strategic storage in the massive capacity Qingcaosha Reservoir. Independent validation against the extreme 2022 saltwater intrusion event demonstrates that accepting a quantifiable cost of robustness significantly suppresses extreme salinity tail risk vulnerabilities (measured by conditional value at risk). Ultimately, these insights translate into actionable, tiered (economic, balanced, and conservative) emergency dispatch protocols, providing a quantitative decision support foundation for safeguarding megacity water security under volatile climatic environments.

title: Urban flood prediction and economic loss assessment under drainage pipe siltation: An integrated hydrodynamic and IBWO-IRCNN-Informer framework
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Danyang Di, Hao Jia, Zhaoyang Zhang, Jingbo Xu, Chang Wang, Meiqin Qi, Haoyu Meng
abstract: Study region A highly urbanized catchment in Zhengzhou, central China, with aging drainage infrastructure, recurrent pluvial flooding, and pronounced topographic and urban-development contrasts. Study focus This study developed an integrated framework to assess drainage-pipe siltation effects on urban inundation and economic losses. A coupled 1D–2D InfoWorks ICM model incorporated a comprehensive siltation coefficient (CSC), and its outputs trained an IBWO-IRCNN-Informer surrogate for rapid spatiotemporal inundation estimation. Depth–loss functions, asset exposure, and vulnerability were integrated to estimate losses under different rainfall and siltation scenarios. New hydrological insights for the region The hydrodynamic model reproduced observed hydraulic responses (independent-validation NSE: 0.747 for discharge and 0.761 for water level). Under R2 rainfall, surrogate predictions had a mean absolute inundation-depth error (MAE) of 0.035 m against InfoWorks ICM simulations at eight selected flooding points and a temporal NSE of 0.971 for time-series predictions. With CSC = 0.3, inundation extent increased by 83.27%, 91.62%, and 13.56% under the 10-, 20-, and 200-year rainfall scenarios, respectively, relative to clean pipes; estimated economic losses increased by 71.65%, 71.01%, and 10.21%. Zone 4 was the primary risk hotspot, accounting for 37.9% of total probability-weighted potential economic loss across the evaluated design rainfall scenarios. These findings highlight the substantial effects of pipe siltation, particularly under more frequent rainfall, and the importance of drainage maintenance for urban flood-risk management.

title: An integrated hydrogeophysical workflow for identifying buried lower-salinity groundwater targets in the Ebro coastal delta
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ignacio Martín Nieto, Cristina Sáez Blázquez, Miguel Ángel Maté-González, Javier Carrasco García, Joaquim Enric Roset Piñol, Diego González-Aguilera, Pedro Carrasco García
abstract: Study region The Ebro Delta (NE Spain), a low-lying Mediterranean delta with intensive irrigated agriculture; the study site is an agricultural property at Sant Jaume d′Enveja where shallow groundwater is brackish and the deltaic succession is dominantly saline. Study focus We tested whether a compact hydrogeophysical workflow can identify a buried groundwater-bearing interval of comparatively low salinity within a saline deltaic succession and guide the completion of a production well. A 390 m pole–dipole electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) profile and two 75 × 75 m time-domain electromagnetic (TDEM) soundings were interpreted before drilling. A 61.7 m well, located 7 m from the ERT profile and 30 m from one TDEM sounding, was then logged (fluid electrical conductivity, temperature, natural gamma) and sampled at discrete depths (1, 40 and 55 m), and a pumping-test sample was measured. An Archie-type conversion was evaluated with a sensitivity analysis of the formation factor (F = 1.5–9). New hydrological insights for the region ERT and TDEM consistently resolve a thin surface unit, a highly conductive fine-grained unit (≈0.4–0.6 Ω m) between ≈ 5 and 25–34 m, an intermediate resistive gravel-dominated unit (≈7–20 Ω m) and a deeper conductor. In the screened part of the intermediate unit, groundwater electrical conductivity (EC) is 3.5–4.0 mS cm⁻¹ : brackish, but about one order of magnitude less saline than seawater, whereas EC rises to 9.1–12.4 mS cm⁻¹ at 55–61 m. A formation factor of ≈ 2 calibrated in clay-rich shallow sediments underestimated the pore-water EC of the gravel unit by a factor of ≈ 2.7; the sample-calibrated apparent F is ≈ 5.4. The lower boundary of the target is a salinity transition within the same gravels rather than an aquitard. Lower-salinity groundwater can therefore persist in semi-confined coarse units of the Ebro Delta, but its identification requires lithology-specific calibration with direct water samples, and its use requires screens ending above the salinity transition and EC-monitored abstraction to prevent upconing.

title: Linking legacy phosphorus accumulation and hydrological vulnerability to catchment-scale phosphorus leaching in an agricultural watershed of eastern China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Hao Wu, Zhihan Cheng, Jia Zhou, Yucang Wang, Xinyi Jiao, Zheqi Pan, Xiaochen Liu, Lingzao Zeng, Minpeng Hu, Ming Shan, Dingjiang Chen
abstract: Study region This study was conducted in the Yongan watershed, eastern China, a mixed forest-agricultural humid subtropical watershed. Study focus Phosphorus (P) leaching is a critical pathway to transfer legacy soil P to groundwater and surface waters, yet field evidence and watershed-scale estimates remain scarce. We combined long-term P budgets, soil P accumulation and fractionation, in situ lysimeter monitoring, and hydrological upscaling in the Yongan watershed to reveal P leaching mechanisms and estimate spatial variation of soil P leaching potential. New hydrological insights for the region Long-term positive cropland and orchard P budgets resulted in large cumulative P surpluses (mean 1321.8 and 1248.6 kg P ha−1). Long-term increases in soil TP and Olsen-P demonstrated long-term P enrichment, while contemporary labile and moderately labile P pools and elevated P saturation indicated substantial mobilization potential. At 30 lysimeter sites, leachate TP averaged 0.50 mg L−1, and dissolved P accounted for about 75% of TP, with higher values in dryland and orchard than in forest soils. Combining source-zone concentrations with Xinanjiang (XAJ)-derived equivalent subsurface drainage yielded estimated annual sub-catchment P-leaching intensities of 0.02–0.35 kg P ha−1 yr−1. The two concentration scenarios retained the same deterministic group of candidate high-leaching sub-catchments. This framework integrates historical P accumulation, soil P and hydrological transport to identify potential leaching source areas and inform spatially targeted management.

title: Water insecurity, governance and environmental justice in Iran: A spatial, bibliometric and thematic synthesis
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Vahid Karimi, Marzieh Keshavarz, Elham Ahmadifard, Hossein Azadi, Ali Sadian, Yan Tan, Sheida Jahangiri, Masoud Yazdanpanah
abstract: Study region Iran, a predominantly arid and semi-arid country with strongly uneven water endowment and important transboundary dependencies, notably the Helmand/Hirmand basin shared with Afghanistan. Study focus Water conflict is often attributed to scarcity alone, yet similar hydrological stress produces different social outcomes. We combine three sequential methods to examine how water insecurity becomes contested in Iran: a province-level Water Insecurity Index (WII) based on precipitation deficit, drought frequency and land subsidence probability; bibliometric mapping of 207 publications on water conflict, governance and environmental justice; and a thematic synthesis of 79 studies. New hydrological insights for the region The WII reveals pronounced spatial inequality in exposure, highest in central and southeastern provinces, whereas research attention concentrates in Khuzestan, Isfahan and Fars. Scholarship has shifted from scarcity-centred explanations towards governance, justice, vulnerability and adaptation. The thematic synthesis identifies four interacting pathways: unequal exposure and environmental injustice, institutional legitimacy and governance capacity, risk perception, and behavioural and collective capacity to respond. A differentiated assessment shows that Iran's governance record combines substantial achievements in domestic water supply, mixed outcomes in coordination and regulation, and persistent shortcomings in groundwater sustainability and equitable allocation, while transboundary dependencies, particularly in the Helmand/Hirmand basin, limit what domestic governance alone can achieve. The resulting framework is a conceptual synthesis, not a tested causal model, and supports context-specific reforms in allocation rules, groundwater regulation and basin-level participation.

title: A foundation-model-based hybrid framework with geophysical feature learning for watershed flood forecasting
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ruiqi Wang, Yanlai Zhou, Tianyu Xia, Jinzhou Chen, Fi-John Chang, Chong-Yu Xu
abstract: Study region The Jianxi River Basin, a watershed characterized by saturation-excess runoff generation in southeastern China. Study focus A key obstacle in data-driven hydrology is that conventional artificial neural networks struggle to capture the spatiotemporal dependencies of rainfall-runoff transformations. This mismatch between model architecture and physical process structure produces systematic bias and time-lag phenomena, especially for large floods. This study proposes a hybrid watershed flood forecasting framework combining a foundation model with geophysical feature learning. It integrates a Fourier neural network-based feature learning module and a graph attention network guided by basin hydrological and geographic priors, together with a pre-trained Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (FG-TabPFN), enhancing the representation of complex spatiotemporal dependencies in rainfall-runoff processes. New hydrological insights for the region FG-TabPFN was evaluated in the Jianxi River Basin using 3-hourly flood-season hydrometeorological data from 2008 to 2023, divided into training (including validation) and testing sets for 1- to 7-step-ahead forecasting. The results show that FG-TabPFN outperforms LSTM and Transformer in forecasting accuracy and stability. Relative to LSTM and Transformer, average percentage improvements are 1.9% and 3.4% in Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency, 13.8% and 21.9% in root mean square error, 13.4% and 20.4% in mean absolute error, and 10.9% and 20.4% in volume error, respectively. These findings highlight the potential of combining geophysical feature learning with task-adapted pre-trained knowledge to support flood early warning and risk management.

title: Elevation-dependent drought vulnerability and spatio-temporal drought dynamics in the East African Rift System
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Minyahel Tilahun, Solomon G. Tesfamichael, Takehiro Sasaki, Jianshuang Wu, Elhadi Adam, Ayana Angassa
abstract: Study region The East African Rift System (EARS), spanning 13 countries across eastern and central Africa, is characterized by elevation gradients and diverse hydroclimatic conditions ranging from humid highlands to arid lowlands. These contrasting environments influence drought characteristics and vulnerability across the region. Study focus This study investigated elevation-dependent drought dynamics across the EARS using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) for 1950–2022 and a 1-km digital elevation model to classify elevation bands. Drought frequency, duration, and intensity were analyzed across elevation bands. A Composite Drought Vulnerability Index (CDVI), integrating multiple drought hazard characteristics, was developed and projected for 2023–2052 using a trend-based statistical framework. New hydrological insights for the region Elevation emerges as a key modulator of drought dynamics across the EARS. Lowlands below 1000 m display persistent long-term aridification (−0.1 to −0.032 decade⁻¹), where as elevations above 2000 m exhibit significant wetting trends (0.060–0.148 decade⁻¹). Below 1000 m, short-term drought occurrence increased after the 1990s, from 3.8% to 26.9% below 500 m and from 3.3% to 33.3% at 500–1000 m by the 2010s. The 2001–2500 m band emerges as a regional drought hotspot, with the strongest drought duration–intensity coupling (β = 0.10), while historical CDVI values ranges from 0.01 to 0.89, with the highest values occurring above 2501 m and at mid-elevations (p = 0.007 for differences among groups). Future projections indicate an increasing CDVI across timescales, with the projected CDVI at SPEI01 increasing by 49.7% decade-1 (β = 0.23; R² = 0.92). These findings suggest that topographic gradients regulate drought dynamics and vulnerability across EARS, informing drought risk mitigation and water resource management.

title: A future tidal condition-guided HLF-Net model for multistep tidal level forecasting at Xuliujing in the Yangtze River Estuary
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Xu Zhao, Feng Ding, Shengping Wang, Zhigao Chen
abstract: Study region Xuliujing Hydrological Station, Yangtze River Estuary, China. Study focus Runoff and meteorological forcing modify tidal propagation and introduce nonstationary water-level variations, complicating tidal level forecasting. Existing deep learning models often extract historical information without explicitly considering future tidal states. This study proposes HLF-Net, a hybrid model integrating harmonic analysis (HA), long short-term memory (LSTM), and future tidal condition-guided attention (FTCA). HA provides future harmonic tidal levels as the forecasting baseline, allowing LSTM to focus on residual variations. FTCA uses future tidal conditions derived from harmonic information as attention queries, enabling the model to retrieve historical hydrological information relevant to each anticipated tidal state. The model was compared with conventional HA and seven deep learning models at forecast horizons of 24, 72 and 120 h. New hydrological insights for the region HLF-Net outperformed all benchmarks at each forecast horizon. Relative to HA, root mean square error (RMSE) decreased by 31.14%-54.34% and mean absolute error (MAE) by 33.98%-56.88%. Corresponding reductions relative to LSTM were 16.67%-28.67% and 16.47%-27.03%. These findings suggest that the predictive relationship between historical hydrological conditions and future tidal levels varies with tidal state. FTCA’s effectiveness highlights the value of tidal predictability for representing this dependence and improving multistep forecasts of nonstationary water-level variations in tidal rivers. The proposed framework offers an approach to multistep tidal level forecasting in dynamic tidal river environments.

title: Groundwater storage anomalies on the Loess Plateau: Nonlinear evolution, spatial heterogeneity, and links to vegetation restoration
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Huayu Guan, Mingliang Gao, Huili Gong, Min Shi, Lin Zhu, Yunxiao Liu, Jie Wang, Rong Shen, Zheng Chen
abstract: Study Region The Loess Plateau (34–41° N, 101–114° E), a semi-arid region of about 640,000 km² in northern China, where ecological restoration began in 1999 and groundwater is critical but poorly monitored. Study Focus This study characterizes the nonlinear, stage-dependent evolution and spatial heterogeneity of groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) across the Loess Plateau during 2003–2024, and examines their association with vegetation greening and precipitation. GWSA was derived from GRACE/GRACE-FO CSR mascon data by removing GLDAS-simulated soil moisture, snow water equivalent and canopy water storage. The series was segmented into five stages and decomposed into trend, seasonal and residual components. New Hydrological Insights GWSA declined at −0.94 cm/year [−1.07, −0.88], but not monotonically: depletion peaked in 2015–2017 (−1.67 cm/year), the interval of peak greening, giving way to a final stage whose trend is not statistically distinguishable from zero while residual variability increases. Depletion formed a west-to-east gradient, from −0.35 cm/year in the western hilly zone to −1.08 and −1.89 cm/year in the central–eastern plateau and the Guanzhong Plain and southeastern river valleys. After 2015 the association between GWSA and both NDVI and precipitation weakened and no month-scale precipitation lag is resolvable. These results suggest a potential trade-off between surface ecological gains and subsurface water security, indicating that groundwater monitoring should be integrated into restoration planning in semi-arid regions.

title: Research on the fusion and applicability of multi-source precipitation data in the Kaidu River Basin based on various bias correction methods
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Tongxia Wang, Fulong Chen, Chaofei He, Fengnian Zhao, Jing Yang, Chaonan Zhang, Xiangdong Xu
abstract: Study region The Kaidu River Basin is in the arid inland region of northwest China. Study focus In the arid mountainous areas of northwest China with scarce ground observations, accurate estimation of precipitation remains a core challenge for multi-source precipitation data in terms of precision assessment and bias correction. This study systematically evaluated the accuracy and bias characteristics of multiple precipitation products, including TRMM, IMERG, ERA5-Land, MSWEP, CN05.1, and CMFD, in the Kaidu River Basin. We employed three bias-correction methods: DBC (Distribution Bias Correction), QDM (Quantile Delta Mapping), and DLS (Delta Local Scaling), and analysed the improvements in precision indicators, empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF) characteristics, and the ability to capture the onset and cessation of the rainy season before and after correction, constructed a high-precision multi-source merged precipitation dataset and conducted an in-depth analysis of the basin’s precipitation variation characteristics and influencing mechanisms from 1998 to 2023. New hydrological insights for the region (1) The multi-source precipitation products exhibited significant applicability differences, with reanalysis datasets generally outperforming satellite-based remote sensing products overall. (2) All three bias correction methods significantly improve the accuracy of multi-source precipitation data. DLS and QDM perform comparably and outperform DBC overall. The multi-source merged dataset constructed using DLS correction exhibits high reliability, with R² values mostly exceeding 0.9, NSE and KGE above 0.8, and RMSE below 2 mm. (3) From 1998–2023, annual precipitation at stations across the basin exhibits periodic fluctuations. High-elevation areas show a slight increasing trend, while low-elevation areas display a slight decreasing trend. The basin experienced a total of 153 precipitation events exceeding 10 mm, with extreme events (>50 mm) being rare. (4) The spatial distribution of precipitation in the basin results from the synergistic effects of multiple factors, with elevation and slope aspect exerting the strongest controlling influence. The findings of this study provide a scientific basis for selecting and optimizing multi-source precipitation data in arid regions of northwest China. They also deliver high-precision data support for flood risk assessment, sustainable water resources planning, ecological conservation, and climate change adaptation in the basin, offering significant regional application value. The analytical framework developed here can be extended to other similar arid mountainous basins in future studies, providing strong support for regional hydrological model simulations and policy-making.

title: Hydrogeochemical evolution across the Lushan-Poyang Lake mountain-lake continuum: A wet-season multi-tracer study of water sources, weathering, and anthropogenic inputs
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zuobing Liang, Yumei Yan, Yi Jin, Yifan Xu, Tao Hu, Xin Xiong
abstract: Study region The Lushan–Poyang Lake continuum, Jiujiang City, Jiangxi Province, southeastern China (115.85–116.13°E, 29.29–29.69°N), spanning sampling elevations from 10 m at the shore of Poyang Lake, the largest freshwater lake in China, to 1173 m in the Lushan massif. Study focus During one wet-season campaign we sampled 100 sites (63 groundwater, 29 river, 4 spring and 4 lake) and measured field parameters including dissolved oxygen (DO) and redox potential (ORP), major ions, stable isotopes of water (δ¹⁸OH₂O, δ²HH₂O) and δ¹ ³C of dissolved inorganic carbon. Isotopes, ion stoichiometry, PHREEQC saturation indices and multivariate statistics (principal component analysis with KMO and Bartlett tests, hierarchical clustering) were used to evaluate water sources, evaporation, solute acquisition by weathering and strong acids, nitrogen inputs and redox status. New hydrological insights for the region (1) All waters are of meteoric origin. Deuterium excess is positive in springs, rivers and groundwater (median +12 to +15‰) and falls to + 0.6 to + 6.1‰ at the lake sites, so evaporative enrichment is confined to the lake margin and a few lowland river reaches. (2) Solute enrichment increases strongly from the mountain zone (median TDS 42 mg L⁻¹) to the lowland zone (237 mg L⁻¹) in Ca–HCO₃ waters; ion ratios place upland waters closest to the silicate end-member and lowland groundwater between the silicate and carbonate end-members, and Ca²⁺ + Mg²⁺ is balanced by HCO₃⁻ + SO₄²⁻ + NO₃⁻ (slope 1.13), indicating strong-acid participation. (3) Nitrate, sulfate and chloride are highest in lower-DO lowland groundwater, pointing to anthropogenic inputs, but nitrate is not significantly related to elevation and only 2 of 58 groundwater samples exceed the WHO guideline (50 mg L⁻¹). (4) DO differs strongly among compartments (groundwater 3.0, lake 10.6 mg L⁻¹) whereas ORP does not, so reductive metal release in the lake is not supported. The wet-season snapshot and the small spring and lake groups (n = 4 each) limit generality; the dataset provides a baseline for multi-season monitoring of this mountain–lake system.

title: Impact of climate change on total organic carbon of major rivers in South Korea using deep learning
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): SeungHyeon Lee, JunGi Moon, JeongHwan Baek, ChanHae Ok, MyeongJin Jung, HyungTae Kim, HyoSeon Kim, SangJin Jung, DaEun Yun, JongCheol Pyo
abstract: Study region This study examines the Han, Nakdong, Geum, and Yeongsan River basins, South Korea’s four major river systems, which span diverse climatic, hydrological, and water quality conditions. Study focus We developed a total organic carbon (TOC) prediction framework using multiple one-dimensional convolutional neural network architectures trained on 38,715 observations from 2008 to 2022 with 24 water quality and climate-related predictors. The best-performing model was applied to Shared Socioeconomic Pathway projections for 2030, 2050, 2070, and 2090 to assess climate-driven TOC changes while holding baseline water quality conditions constant. New hydrological insights for the region The proposed deep learning model showed that TOC exhibited distinct spatial and seasonal patterns across the four river basins, reflecting their contrasting hydrological, water quality, and climatic characteristics. In addition to chemical and biochemical oxygen demand, extreme temperature and dry climate indices were identified as important predictors, suggesting that TOC variability may be sensitive to hydroclimatic conditions. Under future climate scenarios with baseline water quality conditions held constant, high TOC events were projected to become more frequent despite relatively modest changes in mean TOC concentrations. These findings highlight the importance of considering the potential risks associated with high TOC concentrations, alongside mean TOC concentrations, when developing regional water quality monitoring and management strategies for South Korea’s four major river basins.

title: Surface water connectivity under drought stress: Spatiotemporal variations and scenario-based correction coefficients
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Lanshu Jing, Xuejun Zhang, Shanjun Zhang, Yanyun Wang, Zhicheng Su, Hui Gao, Xixi Chen
abstract: Study region Three representative subbasins of the Nenjiang River Basin (NRB), Northeast China, with limited regulation by large control reservoirs. Study focus This study examined waterbody connectivity during the 2007–2009 typical drought event. Monthly water bodies were extracted from Landsat imagery. Connectivity was quantified using the connectivity function value (CFV) and cumulative CFV. Seasonal and Trend decomposition using Loess (STL) decomposition and correlation analysis were used to identify temporal components and hydroclimatic associations. Multiple linear regression and generalized additive models (GAM) were compared to examine responses to Water Surplus Deficit Index (WSDI), precipitation, and temperature. Monthly connectivity correction coefficients were then derived for five drought scenarios. New hydrological insights for the region Waterbody connectivity showed seasonal, interannual, and spatial variations. Connectivity generally increased during spring snowmelt and the summer rainy season, but its timing and magnitude varied among sub basins. HHS_QS showed large temporal fluctuations, HS_QS was characterized by shorter connectivity distances, and XAM_BC maintained connectivity over longer distances. The trend component was positively correlated with WSDI, while the seasonal component was positively correlated with precipitation. GAM improved model performance in HS_QS and XAM_BC, indicating nonlinear hydroclimatic responses. The correction coefficients decreased with increasing drought severity, with the strongest response in HHS_QS and the weakest in HS_QS. These coefficients provide a quantitative reference for future integration of drought-induced connectivity changes into water resources allocation models.

title: Spatiotemporal variations and multi-scenario projections of streamflow and river water temperature in the Upper Yangtze River under climate change
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wanyu Wang, Huanghe Gu, Xiaoyan Wang, Yubo Yan, Ruifeng Zhang, Weiguang Wang, Zhongbo Yu
abstract: Study Region The Upper Yangtze River Basin (UYRB), China Study Focus A one-way coupled PCR-GLOBWB–DynWat framework was developed to simulate streamflow and river water temperature in the UYRB. The model was evaluated against observations driven by bias-corrected projections from five GCMs under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Future hydrothermal changes were assessed for three future periods relative to 1976–2005, and the roles of air temperature and streamflow in river warming were examined. New Hydrological Insights for the Region The coupled framework reproduced historical streamflow and water temperature with reasonable accuracy, although water-temperature performance was weaker at the headwater station. Ensemble projections indicate basin-mean streamflow decreases in the near- and mid-century but increases by 3.18% under RCP4.5 and 4.46% under RCP8.5 in the late century. River water temperature increases persistently, with basin-wide warming of 1.75 °C to 4.99 °C across scenarios and periods, and stronger warming in the middle and lower reaches. The regression analyses consistently indicate a stronger association of projected river warming with air temperature than with streamflow. The ensemble projections further imply marked shifts in the thermal conditions for fish spawning, with the spawning threshold date for the Four Major Chinese Carps advancing by 7 days and that for Chinese sturgeon delayed by 20 days in the near-future period under RCP4.5. Results support climate-adaptive reservoir and ecosystem management.

title: Patch identities and drought patch chains resolve internal event evolution and cross-sub-basin connectivity in the Upper Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Minshen Wang, Hanbo Yang, Changming Li, Quan Quan
abstract: Study region The study was conducted in the Upper Yangtze River Basin (UYRB), southwestern China. Study focus This study focuses on resolving the internal spatiotemporal structure of regional drought events from their constituent monthly patches. Three-dimensional (3D) drought identification establishes patch continuity, but event-level summaries alone do not resolve the histories of concurrent internal branches. A patch-level information layer was added that assigns each drought patch (DP) a persistent identity and organizes directed month-to-month connections into drought patch chains (DPCs). The representation distinguishes one-to-one continuation from merge/split reorganization and diagnoses internal stages without changing event boundaries. New hydrological insights for the region During 1960–2024, 298 events comprised 1702 DPs and 1459 directed links. DP centroids shifted from western headwater concentration towards a more spatially distributed pattern. Regional severity shares revealed recurrent directions of spatial redistribution. High-frequency decrease–increase scenarios included spatially separated sub-basins, whereas frequent paired increases mainly involved neighbouring pairs. High recurrence did not coincide with the largest absolute changes in total DP severity. Links involving merging or splitting accounted for 44.4% of all connections. In a 34-month event, five DPCs resolved five node-exclusive diagnostic stages and reconstructed monthly severity without double counting. These results distinguish where connected drought development recurs from how strongly severity changes, while exposing branch succession within a continuous event.

title: Migrating alternate bars during an extreme flood in the Chikuma River, Japan simulated using an Eulerian-type nonequilibrium sediment transport model
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Naoki Kamata, Riku Kubota, Takashi Inoue, Rintaro Fujino, Yasuo Nihei
abstract: Study region The Chikuma River in Nagano Prefecture, Japan Study focus The movement of alternating sandbars is a type of damage caused to river structures by floods, and this can lead to levee breaches. Therefore, understanding the physical mechanisms of alternating sandbars during flooding is important. This study aims to develop an Eulerian-type nonequilibrium sediment transport model that can reproduce the dynamics of alternating sandbars and clarify the physical mechanisms of alternating sandbar during floods. Two-dimensional shallow-water flow and riverbed deformation analyses were conducted on large-scale channel changes that occurred in the Chikuma River in Nagano Prefecture, Japan. New hydrological insights for the region The calculation results indicated that the migration speed of alternating sandbars during floods differed significantly between the top and bottom of the sandbar. Moreover, the longitudinal distribution of the water level around the sandbar was affected by the sandbar shape. Furthermore, we revealed that deposition occurred in front of the sandbar, erosion occurred on the sandbar, and the movement speed of the sandbar depended on the magnitude of the difference between the pick-up and deposition on the riverbed by comparing the erosion and deposition characteristics on the riverbed with the positional relationship of the sandbar shape. These findings are expected to become important for river management technologies such as predicting and monitoring changes in water impact within river channels during floods.

title: HydroTG-STAGNet: A topology-guided spatiotemporal adaptive gating network for flood forecasting
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wen-chuan Wang, Zong Li, Xiao-xue Hu, Yi-yang Wang, Dong-mei Xu
abstract: Study region This study selected the watersheds controlled by the Lushi, Loude, and Beiwang stations in the Yellow River Basin, China, as the study area. In addition, flood data from the Ningxiang station in the Yangtze River Basin are selected for external basin validation. Study focus To address the challenges of physical consistency and interpretability faced by data‑driven flood forecasting models, this paper proposes HydroTG‑STAGNet, a hydrological topology‑guided spatiotemporal graph neural network. Methodologically, the model employs a coupled architecture of multi-scale temporal convolutional networks (TCN) and graph attention networks (GAT) to jointly model temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies of hydrological processes. On this basis, a feature allocator mechanism is designed to perform directed information aggregation according to the river network topology, enabling message passing to explicitly follow the watershed structural prior. Meanwhile, a hybrid loss function, a spatiotemporal gating fusion mechanism, and a target‑attention mechanism are introduced to enhance forecast robustness and decision‑making transparency thereby enhancing forecast robustness and transparency through both the loss design and the architecture. New hydrological insights for the region The results show that HydroTG-STAGNet achieves single-step Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) values of 0.9409, 0.9730, and 0.9562 at the Lushi, Loude, and Beiwang stations, respectively, representing improvements of approximately 3.84%–68.08% compared with the standalone temporal convolutional network (TCN) model. These results demonstrate that topology constraints are crucial for improving flood forecasting accuracy in the region. Quantitative analysis of the internal model weights further reveals stable statistical associations between the average gating states and the observed discharge as well as the intensity of hourly discharge variations, while the target-node attention weights exhibit clear basin-specific differences. These findings further reveal the dynamic response characteristics of the model during different flood processes from the perspectives of internal information allocation and feature fusion states.

title: Late Holocene paleoflood events and their quantitative hydrological reconstruction in the Yellow River source area, NE Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zikun Li, Yuzhu Zhang, Yan Zhu, Ninglian Wang, Yao Jin, Mengting Li, Runang Liu, Ting Qi, Chun Chang Huang, Jiangli Pang, Jibao Dong
abstract: Study area The Kesheng Reach, located in the Yellow River source area on the northeastern (NE) Tibetan Plateau, is characterized by a high-altitude alpine and cold environment. Increasing global climate extremes have enhanced the frequency and magnitude of extreme floods in this region, highlighting the importance of paleoflood records for extending short instrumental records and improving extreme flood risk assessment. Research focus Two typical slackwater deposit (SWD) layers were identified in the Kesheng Reach and investigated through field observations and laboratory analyses, including magnetic susceptibility, grain-size, geochemical elements, and optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating. This study aimed to identify paleoflood events and their regional hydroclimatic background, and to reconstruct the corresponding peak flood stages and discharges. New hydrological insights for the region Two paleoflood events, dated to 1.13 ± 0.05 ka–0.82 ± 0.07 ka and corresponding to the Medieval Warm Period (MWP), significantly enrich the extreme flood records in the Yellow River source area. Under the warm climate, extreme rainstorm and enhanced glacial meltwater from glaciers and permafrost jointly constituted the regional hydrological background for the paleoflood events. The paleoflood peak stages were reconstructed based on the elevation of the end points of SWD; combined with HEC-RAS model, the peak discharges were estimated to range between 7310 m3/s and 8150 m3/s. A power-law relationship, Q = 0.2D 0.93, was further established between peak discharge and drainage area for rainstorm-generated paleofloods in the Yellow River mainstream. This study provides the first reconstruction of paleoflood peak discharges in the Yellow River source area and offers a quantitative basis for extreme flood hazard assessment and hydraulic engineering design in this high-altitude alpine and cold region.

title: Event-scale controls on precipitation isotopes revealed by explainable machine learning: Evidence from the Urumqi River Basin, Central Asia
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Siqi Wu, Fang Feng, Shuang Jin, Zhongqin Li, Michael A. Urban, Qiaohua Huang
abstract: Study region Urumqi River Basin, Central Asia Study focus Precipitation isotope research has long been a central topic in isotope hydrology and atmospheric sciences. However, systematic quantitative investigations into the controlling factors of precipitation isotope variability remain relatively limited. Based on long-term event-scale precipitation isotope observations and explainable machine learning techniques, this study aimed to systematically analyze and quantify the major factors controlling precipitation isotope variations. New hydrological insights for the region Three machine learning algorithms, namely Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron Neural Network, were employed to establish predictive relationship models linking precipitation isotope variability to its potential driving factors. All three models demonstrated satisfactory predictive accuracy and generalization capability. By integrating explainable machine learning technique (SHapley Additive exPlanations), the relative contributions of individual predictors to model outputs were further quantified. The results indicate that temperature is the dominant controlling factor affecting precipitation isotope variations. In addition, relative humidity, upper-atmospheric wind components, cloud cover, and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) also exert significant influences on precipitation isotope variations within the basin.

title: Climate warming and wetting-driven hydrological evolution in a typical alpine watershed on northeastern Tibetan Plateau: Driving mechanisms and runoff hysteresis
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yong Xiao, Xu Guo, Jie Wang, Jiahao Liu, Hongming Peng, Wanping Wang, Jiahua Wei, Youjing Yuan, Yan Ren, Peiyuan Zhan, Jing Ning
abstract: Study region The Buha River watershed is an alpine basin on northeastern Tibetan Plateau, where cryospheric processes and groundwater storage jointly regulate runoff generation. Study focus This study focuses on the long-terms hydro-meteorological changes and associated driving mechanisms of the high-altitude alpine watershed on northeastern Tibetan Plateau under the influence of climate warming and wetting. New hydrological insights for the region A marked climate shift took place in 1996, whereas abrupt runoff change occurred in 2001, yielding a five-year lag. Precipitation dominated runoff variability across the watershed, explaining 80.94% of total attributed variation. Increased precipitation offset the negative hydrological effects of rising evapotranspiration throughout the period of 1956–2024. The underlying-surface parameter maintained a high and stable value (n = 9.99), and catchment conditions exerted steady control over local runoff generation. Temporal differences in runoff responses corresponded closely to watershed storage-replenishment processes. Elevated precipitation firstly replenished soil moisture and groundwater deficits that formed during previous dry periods before generating substantial runoff in the watershed. Regional hydrological conditions have been affected by ongoing cryospheric degradation and lake expansion. Inundation events of riparian infrastructure have occurred within the study region, and local water resource planning requires full consideration of changing hydrological regimes. This work provides an effective framework for partitioning independent climatic and catchment controls on runoff dynamics in cold alpine watersheds.

title: Satellite-observed rise in groundwater storage masks recurrent drought in the Horn of Africa
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jinping Liu, Maoyu He, Qingfeng Hu, Yanqun Ren, Run Zhang
abstract: Study region: The Horn of Africa: Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Eritrea, and Djibouti. Study focus: Piezometric networks across this drought-exposed region are sparse. Monthly groundwater storage anomalies for 2003–2024 are derived by subtracting GLDAS-Noah soil moisture and snow storage from Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On mascon terrestrial water storage, tested against alternative GRACE and soil-moisture products and surface-water screening, and related to rainfall. Groundwater drought is assessed with the GRACE Groundwater Drought Index in full-record and trend-relative frames, and a reliability–resilience–vulnerability (RRV) analysis stratified by country and hydrogeology. New hydrological insights for the region: Regional storage rose at 0.71 cm yr−1 (annual means; 95% confidence interval 0.55–0.88) and 0.26–0.68 cm yr−1 across these alternatives. Gains follow accumulated rainfall surpluses, concentrated in the wettest water years (2020, 2024). Against full-record climatology, drought effectively ends in 2013; against the trend line, low-storage episodes recur through 2020, the largest in 2018–2019, and this contrast holds in every configuration. Rising storage masks drought-scale anomalies rather than ending them, so the frame alone reverses whether drought is over. Recovery is slow everywhere (one-month drought-exit probability 0.19 versus a 0.69 random-order null), slowest in Eritrea (0.11) and in local and shallow aquifers of medium-to-very-low mapped recharge. Under cell-wise rank standardization the RRV composite degenerates to a resilience transform. Groundwater drought indicators should report both frames.

title: Divergent impacts of anthropogenic nitrogen input on water-carbon use efficiencies
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wenbing Ouyang, Binghao Jia, Lei Cai, Ruixueer Wu
abstract: Study region The Dongting Lake Basin in subtropical southern China comprises forested uplands and intensively managed agricultural lowlands with contrasting nitrogen inputs. Study focus Basin-scale responses of water use efficiency (WUE) and carbon use efficiency (CUE) to anthropogenic nitrogen input (ANI) remain insufficiently resolved. We combined controlled Community Land Model version 5 experiments, XGBoost–SHAP, and structural equation modeling for 1990–2020, comparing time-varying nitrogen inputs with a control fixed at 1990 levels to assess changes in WUE, CUE, gross primary productivity (GPP), net primary productivity (NPP), and evapotranspiration (ET). New hydrological insights for the region ANI increased simulated CUE by 15.3% and WUE by 2.44%. NPP increased by 19.6%, compared with 3.8% for GPP and 1.3% for ET. The stronger CUE response reflected a larger fraction of GPP retained as NPP, whereas the accompanying ET increase limited the WUE gain. Biomass was the leading predictor of both efficiencies; WUE was more strongly associated with vapor pressure deficit, whereas CUE was more closely associated with temperature. Combined nitrogen inputs produced smaller gains in both efficiencies than the summed single-source responses. These findings show that nitrogen-related improvements in plant carbon use efficiency do not translate into comparable gains in carbon uptake per unit water loss, informing joint assessment of carbon production and water use in regional nitrogen management.

title: Wind-conditioned short-lead typhoon rainfall forecasting at inland-plain and coastal sites in northeastern Taiwan
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Chih-Chiang Wei
abstract: Study Region Northeastern Taiwan, where the Lanyang Plain and adjacent coast are frequently affected by western North Pacific typhoons. Yilan is an inland-plain site, whereas Suao is more coastally exposed. Study Focus This study integrates hourly land-station observations, offshore buoy data, and typhoon parameters to evaluate supplementary 1–6 h rainfall guidance during official typhoon warning periods in Taiwan. Direct rainfall forecasting (DRF) is compared with two-stage wind-conditioned forecasting (WCF), which predicts target-lead mean wind speed before using it as auxiliary input for rainfall at the same lead. Gated recurrent unit (GRU) and multi-head self-attention recurrent neural network (MSA-RNN) models provide consistent architectures for assessing the added wind information. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Wind conditioning provided station- and lead-dependent benefits. At coastal Suao, WCF-MSA-RNN reduced root-mean-square error (RMSE) by approximately 2.5–6.2% across 1–6 h leads relative to DRF-MSA-RNN, with the largest reduction at 6 h. Mean absolute error (MAE) decreased by approximately 9.7% at 3 h, and event-wise RMSE improved in seven of eight test typhoons. At inland-plain Yilan, the WCF advantage was concentrated at 1 h. These findings support station-specific selection and calibration of auxiliary wind information and refinement of rainfall-intensity representation. Integrated observations could provide supplementary rainfall guidance for disaster-management agencies in Taiwan. The comparison offers an evaluation framework for similar typhoon-affected regions through local calibration and verification.

title: Revisiting the meteorological-to-agricultural drought propagation under compound conditions: The contribution of heatwaves merits closer attention
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Qianzuo Zhao, Xuan Zhang, Shuyou Liu, Chong Li, Fanghua Hao, Yongshuo Fu
abstract: Study region Yangtze River Basin, the largest river basin in China and the third-largest in the world. Study focus Climate change has intensified heatwaves during meteorological drought (MD), increasing compound drought and heat extreme events. The role of heatwaves in shifting propagation characteristics remains poorly quantified. This study systematically compares drought propagation from MD to agricultural drought (AD) under heatwave and non-heatwave conditions using partial correlation analysis, intensity propagation ratios, and Vine-Copula-based conditional probabilities. Compound thresholds integrating both drivers were derived from a Generalized Additive Model. New hydrological insight (1) Under non-heatwave conditions, 99.8% of the Yangtze River Basin showed attenuation in propagation, whereas heatwaves weakened this attenuation and induced propagation amplification in 26.36% of the Yangtze River Basin. (2) Heatwaves nearly doubled the probability of agricultural drought occurrence, with the mean onset probability of moderate drought increasing from 0.37 to 0.73. (3) Agricultural drought depended on compound SPI-STI thresholds. In the Poyang Lake Basin, agricultural drought was observed under heatwave conditions even when SPI did not indicate concurrent meteorological drought, with 28.6% of no-MD heatwave samples developing moderate-or-worse agricultural drought. Across all extreme drought thresholds, STI values consistently exceeded 0.5, indicating the important role of heat stress in extreme agricultural drought development. These findings improve understanding of drought propagation under global warming and support the development of integrated heat-drought early warning systems.

title: Significant regional contrast in multidecadal rainfall variability and drying trends in Tasmania, Australia
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): T.A. Nilusha T. Perera, Tessa R. Vance, Anthony S. Kiem, Kirsten Adams, Poul Christoffersen, Neil J. Holbrook
abstract: Study region Tasmania, Australia’s southernmost state, and Macquarie Island, a sub-Antarctic island 1500 km southeast of Tasmania, lie within the Tasman Sea sector of the southwest Pacific, spanning subtropical, temperate and sub-Antarctic environments. Regional climate is influenced by both tropical Pacific variability and Southern Ocean atmospheric circulation. Study focus Tasmanian long-term rainfall variability (1900–2024) was analysed using 24 rain gauge stations to examine spatial patterns, trends, and relationships with the Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO). Principal component analysis (PCA) identified dominant spatial patterns, while trend, change point, and IPO phase composite analyses assessed long-term rainfall variability. Macquarie Island was included as a complementary sub-Antarctic comparison. New hydrological insights for the region PCA revealed that 53% of rainfall variance was explained by a coherent Tasmania wide mode, while significant drying trends of 13–19% occurred at one-quarter of stations, concentrated in southeastern Tasmania. Negative IPO phases were associated with 10–30% higher rainfall than positive phases at several northern and eastern stations, demonstrating a statistically detectable and spatially structured IPO-rainfall relationship. Interestingly, Macquarie Island exhibited significantly lower rainfall during negative IPO phases (from a shorter instrumental record) highlighting contrasting IPO responses across the Tasmania – sub-Antarctic region in the Tasman Sea sector. Crucially, we observe centennial-scale rainfall declines in the highly populated and agriculturally important region of southeastern Tasmania, comparable to the well-documented declines observed in southwest Western Australia.

title: Deep learning and statistical models quantify the protective value of coastal wetlands against typhoon damage in Taiwan
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Spandana Vadloori, Mei-Hua Yuan, Hoda Fakour, Hsiao-Wei Chen
abstract: Study region Taiwan, a typhoon-prone region where coastal wetlands may mitigate storm-related economic losses. Study focus Coastal wetlands are vital nature-based solutions for mitigating storm damage, and understanding their protective role is essential to disaster risk management. This study quantifies the extent to which wetlands reduce typhoon-induced economic losses, using structural equation modeling, Bayesian analysis, and a Transformer-MLP predictive model applied to 74 typhoon events from 1960 to 2022. New hydrological insights Total wetland area had a significant negative effect on economic losses (β = −0.315, p = 0.0098). Each additional 1 km2 of wetland reduces losses by about TWD $0.30 million per event, and existing wetlands provide an estimated annual protective value of TWD $415 million. Under low-wind conditions, areas with small wetlands had average losses of TWD $151 million compared with TWD $88 million and TWD $29 million in areas with medium and large wetlands, respectively. Under high-wind conditions, losses exceeded TWD $1115 million in small-wetland areas, compared with TWD $309 million in large-wetland areas. Under high-storm conditions, losses exceeded TWD $494 million in small-wetland areas compared with TWD $161 million in large-wetland areas. The Transformer-MLP achieved R2 values of 0.947, 0.920, and 0.483 for training, internal testing, and external testing, respectively. These findings highlight that preserving coastal wetlands is a cost-effective strategy for minimizing typhoon-induced damage and enhancing coastal resilience.

title: Reservoir-cascade regulation is homogenizing the flow regime of the middle–lower Yangtze River: Concurrent flood attenuation and low-flow amplification
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ruiyuan Li, Feng Yao, Jing Guo, Bo Zheng, Zhen Xu, Jianping Yuan
abstract: Study Region The middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River basin, China. Study Focus Most assessments of how the Three Gorges Dam and upper-Yangtze cascade altered downstream extremes target only the flood tail. From daily discharge (1960–2022) at five mainstem gauges and three less-regulated tributary controls, we tested high-flow, low-flow and variability indices with modified Mann–Kendall and Pettitt tests, quantified homogenization through flow-duration-curve (FDC) flattening, intra-annual variability, the high/low-flow ratio and dual-tail frequency analysis, and tested the change against basin precipitation and each catchment's degree of regulation. New Hydrological Insights for the Region The mainstem regime is being homogenized, not merely de-peaked: the annual minimum 7-day discharge rose 23–54% (field-significant, p < 0.001) while the mean annual maximum fell 4–18%, so the intra-annual coefficient of variation (−9 to −18%), high/low-flow ratio (−24 to −39%) and FDC mid-slope (−1 to −31%) declined. Both design extremes migrated inward at Yichang (10-year low flow +25%, 10-year flood −13%); at Datong only the low-flow tail moved. Homogenization is strongest below the dam and weakens downstream; the mainstem low-flow rise exceeds the controls' by 23 points (90% CI 8–35), is unmatched by precipitation, scales with reservoir storage across the eight catchments and deepens after 2009. Stationary flood-only frequency analysis therefore misstates the regime change; non-stationary two-tailed analysis and the loss of flow variability, not lowered floods alone, should anchor ecological-flow, navigation and water-resource planning.

title: Longitudinal patterns and transformation of hydrologic alteration under cascade regulation: Evidence from the Datong River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wanqi Wang, Hao Wang, Feng Wang, Xiaoyan Wei, Kang Li, Guoxin Chen, Yilang Wen, Yonghong Tan, Weixuan Yang, Tengbo Li
abstract: Study Region The Datong River is a cold, high-altitude tributary on the northeastern Qinghai–Tibet Plateau. Three stations—Qingshizui (QSZ), Tiantang (TT), and Xiangtang (XT)—represent the upstream, midstream, and downstream reaches. Study Focus Hydrologic alteration was assessed using 32 Indicators of Hydrologic Alteration and the Range of Variability Approach (RVA). Station-specific operational division points were used for phase comparison. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal-window dependence, alternative period definitions, and uncertainty in the short QSZ post-impact record. Principal component analysis (PCA), with leave-one-year-out stability assessment, was used to derive representative indicators. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Under station-specific periods, overall RVA alteration was 74.22% at QSZ, 33.20% at TT, and 26.95% at XT. Under the fully harmonized comparison (reference period: 1977–1990; post-impact period: 2015–2022), values were 78.91%, 70.31%, and 75.00%, indicating high alteration across all three monitored reaches and no monotonic upstream-to-downstream decline. Group-level responses were non-uniform: monthly-flow magnitude alteration was greatest at QSZ, whereas timing, extreme-flow and baseflow, pulse, and rate-of-change groups were highest at XT. These results indicate reach-specific differences in the dominant alteration dimensions. PCA retained 6–7 indicators per station. The 90-day maximum flow showed high sampling stability across all stations, whereas Baseflow index stability was station dependent. Reduced sets showed close internal consistency with the full assessment but do not constitute independent validation.

title: Advancing streamflow prediction in ungauged basins: From standalone regionalization techniques to ensemble averaging
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ruolin Chen, Chao Deng, Xin Yin, Chengjing Xu
abstract: Study region 154 unregulated catchments across Australia, representing diverse hydroclimatic conditions. Study focus This study develops and evaluates a multi-method ensemble (MME) regionalization framework for continuous streamflow prediction in ungauged catchments. Using the SIMHYD hydrological model, 11 regionalization methods were evaluated, including spatial proximity, physical similarity, principal component regression, partial least squares regression, random forests, extreme gradient boosting, and ensemble averaging strategies. The 154 catchments were classified into three relatively homogeneous clusters using principal component analysis-based clustering, and regionalization performance was assessed through leave-one-out cross-validation. New hydrological insights for the region The SIMHYD model achieved satisfactory calibration performance, with a median Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.723 during the calibration period. However, regionalization performance varied across catchments, with no single method consistently outperforming the others. Physical similarity with output averaging achieved the highest overall median square root-transformed Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE sqrt ) of 0.695, while the MME achieved a comparable value of 0.687. Notably, Cluster 2 exhibited the poorest overall prediction performance among the three clusters, yet MME achieved the highest median NSE sqrt (0.624) within this cluster. These findings suggest that ensemble averaging provides an effective approach to continuous streamflow prediction in ungauged catchments.

title: Cross-spring heterogeneity in hydrogeochemical patterns during regional-earthquake windows: δD-δ 18 O and major-ion observations along the East Kunlun Fault Zone, Northeastern Tibetan Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Chang Lu
abstract: Study region Fault-controlled springs along the East Kunlun Fault Zone drain groundwater systems with contrasting water types, circulation depths, and structural settings. Whether a common regional-earthquake window is expressed by comparable stable-isotope and major-ion patterns across these systems remains unresolved. Study focus We monitored δD and δ18O at Maqu, Maixi, and Wenquan from January 2023 to February 2026 and used a major-ion archive extending from 2021. The dataset contains 1040 isotope records, 1391 ion analyses, and 1010 matched spring-date records. Spring-specific cumulative baselines and identical event windows were applied to the Jishishan M6.2, Hongyuan M4.9, and Longxi M5.6 earthquakes. Piper analysis, principal component analysis, meteorological screening, and long-term GPS strain rates characterized background differences. New hydrological insights for the region The nine spring-event pairs did not share a reproducible signature. Within ±30 d, deuterium-excess (d) or meteoric-water-line-parallel (d’) departures occurred in seven of the nine spring-event pairs, whereas same-date ion support was identified in only three pairs. Maixi showed repeated pre-Jishishan Ca2+ and HCO3 - decreases accompanying its isotope sequence; Maqu was isotope-only, whereas Wenquan showed a post-event, multi-ion-supported departure. Only four of the 74 event-assigned spring-date records with isotope departures coincided with heavy daily precipitation, and none coincided with a 7-d temperature extreme. Isotope departures therefore support evaluating same-date solute observations and cross-spring replication before regional generalization.

title: Differentiable process-based modeling for identifying soil water transport under rainfall pulses in Mu Us Sandy Land
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jiaxin Shi, Yongnan Zhu, Nan Li, Hao Wang, Jianhua Wang
abstract: Study Region This study was conducted in the Mu Us Sandy Land, Inner Mongolia, China, a representative semiarid sandy ecosystem where global climate change is profoundly altering rainfall pulse regimes and local ecohydrological processes. Study Focus To address the lack of systematic quantitative interpretation regarding soil moisture dynamic responses and internal water flux partitioning under evolving rainfall patterns, this study developed a process-based differentiable soil water framework using high-frequency in situ observations (0–160 cm profile). The framework leveraged automatic differentiation for efficient, gradient-based global inversion of soil hydraulic parameters. Furthermore, multi-scenario numerical simulations within a frequency-based rainfall framework were performed to systematically evaluate the synergistic control of rainfall magnitude, peak intensity, temporal rainfall structure, and antecedent soil moisture on soil water dynamics. New Hydrological Insights for the Region The results reveal pronounced non-linear threshold responses and vertical stratification of soil water in the sandy land. Minor-to-moderate rainfall pulses (5–15 mm) primarily trigger responses within the shallow active layer (0–60 cm), with approximately 63.88% of infiltrated water lost via soil evaporation. In contrast, detectable deep profile recharge (>100 cm) occurs only when cumulative precipitation overcomes shallow soil storage deficits during heavy or sustained rainfall events. While rainfall magnitude serves as the primary driver of soil moisture redistribution, antecedent soil moisture and temporal rainfall structure exert strong modulating effects on wetting-front velocity and storage efficiency. Elevated antecedent soil moisture reduces soil water storage conversion capacity but significantly accelerates wetting-front propagation. Under large rainfall magnitudes (>30 mm), uniform rainfall patterns yield optimal water storage conversion efficiency (33.60%–66.80%), promoting soil water accumulation throughout the profile. Conversely, early-peak concentrated rainfall triggers high wetting-front propagation velocities (up to 4.20 cm/h under intense rainfall), facilitating rapid migration into deeper soil layers. This study provides a physics-constrained differentiable modeling paradigm and essential quantitative benchmarks for water resource management and ecohydrological restoration in semiarid sandy ecosystems facing climate variability.

title: Long-term groundwater quality evolution under changing monitoring networks: Hydrochemical characteristics, health risks, and land-use associations in the Yinchuan Plain, Northwest China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zihan Dong, Fengbo Sun, Dongwang Zhang, Lei Zhang
abstract: Study region The Yinchuan Plain is an arid irrigated region in northwestern China. Rapid urbanization and land-use change have raised concern for groundwater quality, but the monitoring network has also changed, so a regional trend may reflect the wells sampled. Study focus The present study evaluated groundwater quality during 1991–2011 by integrating hydrochemical characteristics, entropy weighted water quality index (EWQI), principal component analysis (PCA), probabilistic human health risk assessment (HHRA), and Bayesian structural equation modeling (BSEM). New hydrological insights for the region Groundwater remained weakly alkaline and predominantly Ca·Mg-HCO3 type, and salinity defined the main hydrochemical axis.
