Mean TDS across the full monitoring network declined from 943.2 to 856.5 mg/L; however, median TDS in the matched wells increased from 854 to 913 mg/L and the proportion of samples exceeding the Class III limit rose from 35.1% to 38.6%. The apparent freshening is therefore partly attributable to changes in the monitoring network. HHRA showed that non-carcinogenic risk was primarily associated with additive contributions from As and F⁻, highlighting trace-element risks that may not be captured by salinity indicators or EWQI alone. Year-specific BSEM further showed temporally inconsistent associations among agricultural land use, the Na+-Cl--SO4 2- salinity construct, and EWQI, with no persistent land-use pathway supported across the study period. These findings demonstrate the importance of combining regional network summaries with repeated-well observations and trace-element risk assessment when evaluating long-term groundwater quality evolution in this and similar arid irrigated plains.

title: Joint flood diversion impacts of semi-restoration polder areas and flood storage and detention areas on the complex river-lake system of Poyang Lake, China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Tianfu Wen, Chao Deng, Fei Xu, Linus Zhang, Mou Leong Tan, Jing Li, Yang Xia
abstract: Study region Poyang Lake, the largest freshwater lake in China, is a complex river-lake system hydraulically connected to the Yangtze River. Semi-restoration polder areas (SRPAs) and flood storage and detention areas (FSDAs) constitute the two principal flood diversion systems for mitigating extreme floods in the region. However, the joint effects of these two types of flood diversion areas under different flood hydrographs remain insufficiently understood. Study focus This study employed a physically based large-scale two-dimensional hydrodynamic model that explicitly incorporated both SRPAs and FSDAs to investigate their joint flood diversion effects in the Poyang Lake system. Three representative extreme flood events (1954, 1998, and 2020), representing distinct flood hydrograph characteristics, were selected to evaluate flood diversion performance through comparative hydrodynamic simulations. Multiple indicators, including water-level reduction, time lags, and flood losses, together with a fuzzy optimum selection model, were adopted to identify optimal flood diversion schemes and reveal coupled hydrodynamic mechanisms unique to Poyang Lake. New hydrological insights for the region The effectiveness of joint flood diversion is fundamentally governed by flood hydrograph characteristics. Temporal hydrodynamic responses, including water-level reduction, time lags, and inundation dynamics, varied substantially among the three representative flood events, highlighting the importance of flood evolution and diversion timing in coordinated flood management. Spatially, water-level reductions were generally greater in the broad main lake than in the narrow outlet channel, where backwater effects from the Yangtze River may constrain the effectiveness of flood diversion. Coordinated operation of SRPAs and FSDAs can effectively reduce critical water levels and alter the timing of critical-water-level exceedance, with pronounced combined peak attenuation observed under the steep single-peak flood. Most importantly, the comparison across the three flood events reveals that hydrodynamic coupling between SRPAs and FSDAs varies with flood hydrograph characteristics, ranging from strong synergy to relatively independent regulation. This finding helps explain the variations in diversion benefits among historical floods in Poyang Lake and highlights the need to account for flood evolution and the temporal relationship between diversion processes when evaluating joint flood diversion schemes. These insights provide a scientific basis for adaptive flood diversion operation, integrated floodplain management, and flood risk mitigation in Poyang Lake and other river-connected lakes worldwide.

title: A lag-aware and interpretable two-stage framework for identifying dominant precipitation-related predictors in the data-scarce Mekong River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Xi Weng, Tianshan Zeng, Yiqun Sun, Dongdong Gao, Qiongfang Li, Xiaogang Tian, Nengmin Zhu, Hongle Shi
abstract: Study area The Mekong River Basin is a data-scarce transboundary basin where sparse, unevenly distributed, and temporally discontinuous gauge observations hinder reliable precipitation estimation, particularly under strong subregional hydroclimatic heterogeneity. Research focus This study developed a lag-aware and interpretable two-stage framework to identify dominant precipitation-related predictors across the basin. In the first stage, transfer entropy (TE) was used to preliminarily screen candidate predictors by assessing directional lagged dependence from each candidate variable to precipitation over 1–7-day lags. In the second stage, tree-based machine learning and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to quantify predictor contributions within the fitted models and diagnose predictor structures across subregions and rainfall regimes. New hydrological insights The framework reduced a high-dimensional candidate predictor space to compact sets of 10–15 inputs. Under a common sample-based split, the compact models achieved a mean Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.232, compared with 0.275 for models using the complete preliminarily screened sets, and performed better overall than conventional feature-selection alternatives. Across subregions, cloud microphysical variables aloft and lower-atmospheric moisture variables were recurring contributors to modelled precipitation. Convective available potential energy (CAPE) and directional transport-related predictors also played important roles. In the heavy-precipitation subset (≥90 mm day−1), transport-, flux-, and energy-related predictors became more prominent in the fitted-model SHAP rankings. This rainfall-regime contrast provides a useful diagnostic of regional precipitation processes, although the heavy-precipitation results remain exploratory because of the limited number of gauge-day samples.

title: Identifying phreatic aquifer recharge sources and evaluating groundwater quality: Application of an end-member mixing analysis with statistically guided tracer selection in the Zishui River estuary
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Pengyu Fu, Xue Ping, Xing Liang, Menggui Jin, Zhikai Chang, Liqun Sun, Xin Zhang, Zhixin Zhang
abstract: Study region The Zishui River estuary, located in Hunan Province, China, is a transition zone from hilly-hillock areas to alluvial plain, where phreatic aquifer recharge processes are complex and their impacts on groundwater quality remain insufficiently understood. Study focus Identifying groundwater recharge processes is critical for resource management and groundwater quality regulation. Traditional End-Member Mixing Analysis (EMMA) involves subjective tracer selection, and previous studies have often separated recharge-source identification from groundwater-quality assessment. To reduce subjectivity in tracer pre-selection, we applied an EMMA workflow supported by Student’s t-test-based tracer screening. We quantified contributions of four recharge components: precipitation, confined groundwater, surface water, and anthropogenically modified recharge, and evaluated recharge-quality links using hydrogeochemical and isotopic data. New hydrological insights for the region Hill-hillock areas dominated by rainfall (contributing >50% of recharge) exhibit low pollution due to rapid water renewal, whereas most plain zones (with ~40% confined groundwater input) face high geogenic contamination risks (like As and Mo). Transition zones recharged by anthropogenic sources (up to 60% of total recharge) face severe threats from nitrogen and heavy metals (Co, Se, Ag, and Cd). The proposed workflow provides a transparent statistical basis for tracer pre-selection and supports the assessment of recharge-related groundwater-quality patterns in the Zishui River estuary, offering useful implications for groundwater protection in similar basins.

title: Groundwater-dependent vegetation reveals potential groundwater discharge zones in data-scarce alpine headwaters of the Yellow River
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Fen Gou, Gaihong Jia, Yingying Yao, Shuitao Guo, Yiqing Wang, Zhenjiang Wu, Fang Ji, Michele Lancia, Chunmiao Zheng
abstract: Study region The headwaters of the Yellow River in the Tibetan Plateau. Study focus Groundwater discharge sustains alpine headwater ecosystems by maintaining baseflow and buffering the effects of climate variability and drought. However, its regional distribution remains difficult to constrain because of complex terrain, permafrost conditions, and sparse groundwater observations. This study used groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) as an ecological indicator of persistent subsurface water supply to identify potential groundwater discharge zones. We integrated GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage anomalies, Sentinel-2 optical indices, Sentinel-1 radar indicators, and hydro-topographic variables to constrain GDV mapping during low-water-storage periods and infer potential spring discharge zones. New hydrological insights for the region Terrestrial water storage anomalies showed strong spatial heterogeneity during 2002–2023, with trends ranging from −2 to 12 mm yr⁻¹ and low-water-storage months accounting for 21%–73% of the study period. High-confidence GDV was concentrated along the Yellow River mainstream, river-valley wetlands, lake margins, and fault-related zones. We identified seven high-confidence springs, 55 potential springs, and broader groundwater discharge zones. These inferred discharge features showed contrasting spatial organization across the basin: the central and western regions were characterized by sparse, point-like potential springs, whereas the southeastern region was dominated by continuous belt-like diffuse discharge along river valleys, wetlands, and shallow groundwater systems. This framework provides a basis for targeted spring surveys and for assessing groundwater-dependent ecosystems under ongoing permafrost degradation.

title: Seasonal variations in nitrate sources and transformation indicators in the upper Xiangjiang River Basin, China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yuxin Qin, Ziqiang Yang, Bing Li, Junxing Chen, Ruotong Xiong, Xia Jiang, Jia Wang, Liang Wang, Mingke Luo
abstract: Study region The upper Xiangjiang River Basin in China; the Xiangjiang River is a tributary of the middle Yangtze River. Study focus By integrating hydrochemistry, dual nitrate stable isotopes (δ15N–NO3 - and δ18O–NO3 -), and the Bayesian mixing model MixSIAR, this study characterized seasonal and spatial variations in nitrate, indicators of nitrogen transformation, and source contributions across the study area. We compared nitrate source characteristics with studies from the upper, middle, and lower Yangtze River Basin. New hydrological insights for the region Nitrogen pollution in the upper Xiangjiang study area showed pronounced seasonal and spatial variability. Mean TN and NO3 -–N concentrations during the rainfall season were 2.22 and 1.73 mg N L−1, respectively, substantially higher than 0.42 and 0.13 mg N L−1 during the regular season. Hydrochemical and dual-isotope patterns were consistent with nitrification contributing to nitrate formation, while no spatially coherent isotope signal of net denitrification was evident in surface waters. MixSIAR identified soil organic nitrogen (SON) as the largest nitrate source in both seasons, contributing 45.2% in the rainfall season and 52.6% in the regular season, followed by manure and sewage (M&S) at 33.5% and 37.0%, respectively. These results indicate that nitrate in the upper Xiangjiang River Basin is jointly influenced by soil nitrogen pools and manure/sewage-related inputs, with nitrate concentrations, spatial patterns, and source contributions varying substantially between seasonal hydrological settings.

title: The regulation mechanism of North Atlantic Oscillation on precipitation in the Tibetan Plateau: An isotopic perspective
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Baijun Shang, Feng Wang, Hui Gao, Tonggang Fu
abstract: Study region: The Tibetan Plateau (TP), known as the "Asian Water Tower," plays a critical role in shaping Asian hydrological cycles and maintaining regional ecological security. Study focus: The North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) is closely associated with precipitation patterns over the TP and, by modulating the westerly circulation, leads to distinct precipitation processes over the northern and southern TP. In this study, we use observed precipitation stable isotopes in conjunction with the IsoGSM model to elucidate the mechanisms by which the NAO regulates the inverse precipitation patterns between the northern and southern TP. New hydrological insights for the region: During NAO events, circulation anomaly signals propagate eastward, resulting in lower precipitable water content (ΔPWC) over the southern TP and higher ΔPWC over the northern TP, generating an inverse precipitation pattern between the southern and northern TP. The northern local meteoric water line (LMWL) has a slope of 7.63 and an intercept of 5.53, while the southern LMWL has a slope of 7.57 and an intercept of 7.06. The slopes of the southern and northern LMWLs are both lower than the Global Meteoric Water Line (GMWL) slope, which may suggest relatively high temperatures in the moisture source areas. In contrast, the differing intercepts reflect distinct atmospheric processes, with subsidence associated with anticyclonic systems dominating the southern TP and ascending motion associated with cyclonic systems dominating the northern TP. Based on precipitation stable isotopes, this study improves the understanding of NAO impacts on precipitation processes and provides a reference for simulating atmospheric circulation effects on precipitation patterns over the TP.

title: Anthropogenic disturbance reconfigures carbon cycling pathways in mountain-lake continua: Insights from hydrochemistry, isotopes, and microbial communities
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zuobing Liang, Yi Jin, Tao Hu, Zhengliang Yu, Yumei Yan, Zaizhi Yang, Yifan Xu, Xin Xiong
abstract: Study Region Two adjacent mesoscale stream catchments (Streams W and L) draining the Lushan Mountain massif (29°26′-29°41′N, 115°52′-116°08′E) in Jiangxi Province, subtropical China, into the Bali Lake and Poyang Lake basins. Spanning a continuous elevation gradient from alpine headwaters (>1000 m) to lowland lake margins (<20 m), the two catchments share a humid subtropical climate and broad geological setting but differ in land-use intensity, local lithology, and anthropogenic pressure, together forming a natural mountain–lake continuum. Study Focus Anthropogenic activities profoundly affect biogeochemical cycles in freshwater ecosystems, yet their specific effects on carbon dynamics in subtropical mountain–lake continua remain incompletely characterized. This exploratory spatial study compares carbon cycling between the two catchments to help separate anthropogenic disturbance from natural variation. Twenty-four stream water samples (12 per catchment), collected in January 2025, were analyzed using an integrated framework combining hydrochemical analysis, stable carbon isotopes (δ¹³CDIC), Bayesian DIC source apportionment (MixSIAR), EEM-PARAFAC optical characterization of dissolved organic matter (DOM), and 16S rRNA microbial community sequencing. The objectives were to characterize hydrochemical differences and dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) sources, resolve spatial variation in DOM composition and bioavailability, and explore associations between bacterial community structure and DOM components along the continuum. New Hydrological Insights for the Region Stream W displayed elevated NO₃⁻, Cl⁻, and SO₄²⁻, consistent with domestic sewage and agricultural runoff, whereas Stream L was more strongly influenced by natural carbonate weathering, although lithological contrasts between the catchments also contribute to the observed patterns. DIC varied with elevation in both streams; Bayesian apportionment estimated sewage as the primary DIC contributor in Stream W (median 70.4%, 95% CI: 58–81%) and soil-CO₂-driven carbonate weathering as dominant in Stream L (median 54.8%, 95% CI: 43–67%). PARAFAC resolved four DOM components: Stream W showed a higher proportion of labile components and a more systematic downstream evolution, while Stream L exhibited greater spatial heterogeneity consistent with discrete point-source inputs. Exploratory microbial analyses revealed genus-level community differences and system-specific DOM-taxa associations warranting experimental follow-up. These results provide a spatial baseline indicating that diffuse-source and point-source disturbance may call for different management approaches in subtropical mountain–lake continua, pending validation by longitudinal monitoring.

title: How reliable are satellite precipitation products in extreme events? Insights from the “23•7” rainstorm in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Zitong Zhou, Qian Ma, Yan Guo, Guocan Wu, Ying Li, Ge Gao, Lingjun Liang
abstract: Study region The Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region experienced the July 2023 “23·7” extreme rainstorm, characterized by complex rainfall evolution. Study focus A process-oriented framework was developed to evaluate eight satellite precipitation products against observations from 174 rain gauges. The evaluation examined intensity-dependent detection and estimation, rainfall-peak representation, temporal phase matching using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW), and spatial structure using the Structure–Amplitude–Location (SAL) method. New hydrological insights for the region During the “23·7” extreme rainfall event, satellite errors varied systematically with rainfall intensity. Overestimation dominated at 0.1–0.8 mm h⁻¹ , while systematic underestimation emerged above 4.0 mm h⁻¹ . Peak detection rates ranged from 53.3% to 77.3%, with most timing errors occurring within ±1 h. Peak-to-peak alignment reduced the negative bias relative to same-time evaluation, indicating that temporal phase mismatch contributed to the apparent underestimation, although residual biases remained after alignment. Spatially, median SAL location errors were below 0.05 for all products, while discrepancies were more evident in structure and amplitude. Overall, the results from this event reveal that intensity-dependent errors manifest differently across temporal and spatial dimensions.

title: Contrasting spatiotemporal patterns of assimilatory nitrate, phosphate and N 2 O emission in hilly and plain rivers
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Renhua Yan, Yuxin Zou, Ao Wang, Jiacong Huang, Qing Zhu, JiaLong Yan, Junfeng Gao
abstract: Study region Zhonghe Watershed, a northwestern upper sub-watershed of the Taihu Basin, Southeast China, and a key drinking water source for the Yangtze River Delta. Study focus This study quantifies the diel and seasonal variations in assimilatory nitrate, phosphate, and N2O emission fluxes in hilly and plain rivers during wet and normal periods. The research aims to understand the underlying mechanisms driving these processes and identify the key environmental factors influencing nutrient transformation and water-air N2O emission. New hydrological insights for the region Hilly river exhibit higher nitrate assimilation rates and lower N2O emissions compared to plain river, primarily due to its steeper gradients, stronger hydrodynamics, and higher dissolved oxygen concentrations. The diel and seasonal variations in assimilation of nitrate and phosphate and N2O emission are influenced by factors such as light, temperature, and hydrological conditions. For example, nitrate assimilation is higher during the day due to light-driven photosynthesis, while N2O emissions are higher during the wet season due to increased nutrient loads and reduced dissolved oxygen concentrations. The study identifies key environmental factors influencing nutrient transformation and N2O emission, including nitrate and phosphate concentrations, dissolved oxygen, pH, and hydrodynamics. These findings provide valuable information for developing effective management strategies to mitigate eutrophication and N2O emissions in the region.

title: Synergistic effects of multiple factors on surface runoff initiation time at mountainous hillslopes: A case study in the upper reach of the Danjiangkou Reservoir, China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Xiaoxia Tong, Li Li, Wenfeng Ding, Dongguo Shao, Jianming Li, Longzhang Fang, Fuyuan Liu, Jinquan Huang, Guanhua Zhang, Qianjin Dong
abstract: Study region The Guanshan River watershed, China. Study focus Predicting surface runoff initiation time (T sur ) is critical for flash flood early warning in mountainous watersheds. We quantified how rainfall intensity (RI), slope gradient (S), soil thickness distribution pattern (STDP), and initial soil moisture (θ ini ) jointly regulate T sur through 72 laboratory simulations and 26 field plots. Three-way ANOVA decomposed the main and interaction effects, and two threshold models derived from the fitted T sur model (CR and CR+ASM) were validated on independent field plots. New hydrological insights for the region T sur decreased with RI and θ ini , each following a power function. The accelerating effect of S depended on RI: raising S from 5° to 15° and 25° shortened T sur by 60.5% and 75.1% at 30 mm/h but only 33.0%–66.0% at 120 mm/h, reflecting a shift from lateral-drainage to infiltration excess. RI×S and the STDP-involving interactions explained 19.19%–20.07% and 30.96%–34.87% of T sur variance, showing STDP acts as a pathway regulator, not a direct control. The fitted T sur model yielded cumulative rainfall (CR) thresholds CR 1–CR 4 that partition runoff generation into three stages; which differed between thick and thin soil layers (CR 4 = 38.64 vs. 32.67 mm) because CR alone ignores the initial storage deficit. Reformulating this criterion as CR + ASM ≥ W crit nearly eliminated this difference (≤2.32 mm) and reproduced runoff initiation under extremely dry conditions where rainfall-only indicators failed.

title: A scenario-neutral framework for regional drought risk management to assess climate change impacts in a large river basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jiyoung Kim, Ji Eun Kim, Seung Beom Seo, Tae-Woong Kim
abstract: Study region The Seomjin River basin, one of South Korea’s large river basins, exhibits significant spatial variability in hydrological drought conditions across its sub-basins. Study focus This study proposed a regional drought risk assessment framework that integrates the joint drought management index (JDMI), which enables comprehensive assessment of drought risk, with a scenario-neutral approach that enables sensitivity analysis across a wide range of plausible climate futures. A total of 209 climate stress time series were generated by combining 19 precipitation and 11 temperature scenarios and were applied to 15 sub-basins of the Seomjin River in South Korea. A response surface was generated using the maximum JDMI estimated from runoff time series derived from the climate stress time series. Subsequently, response surfaces were used to assess climate change impacts for shared socioeconomic pathways (i.e., SSP2–4.5 and SSP5–8.5). New hydrological insights into the region under study Hydrological drought severity in the Seomjin River basin was found to be governed primarily by precipitation change, whereas temperature exerted a secondary, amplifying influence under precipitation-deficit conditions. The proposed JDMI-based framework identified 1992–1996 as the most severe drought episode among the 47 five-year moving windows (1974–2024) in the Seomjin River Dam basin (#4001), with a maximum JDMI of 2.168 corresponding to a severe drought stage and an estimated annual water deficit of 13.6 × 106 m3. Two independently documented historical droughts in the 1994–1998 and 2015–2019 windows were classified as severe and moderate drought stages, with JDMI-based water deficits of 13.1 × 106 and 11.0 × 106 m3 per year, respectively. Mean reservoir storage in these windows was 18.02 × 106 and 13.29 × 106 m3 below the long-term mean, providing independent evidence of drought impacts. A comparison of observed and simulated low-flow deficits showed substantial underestimation of deficit volumes, indicating uncertainty in absolute deficit estimates. When 18 CMIP6 GCMs were mapped onto the response surfaces, an average tendency toward drought mitigation appeared from the near future (2025–2060) to the far future (2061–2100). However, under SSP5–8.5 in the far future, the projections spanned all drought stages (D0–D4). These results indicate that greater inter-model spread, rather than a change in mean drought severity, is the dominant challenge for drought risk management in the basin.

title: Evaluating the influence of reservoir storage dynamics on runoff processes using multi-source remote sensing automation: Jiaoyi Basin case study
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Xingyu Wu, Ke Zhang, Xiaoji Shen, Xuejun Yi, Haijun Wang, Wei Gao, Cuiying Chen, Wei Liu, Shen Wang
abstract: Study region The Jiaoyi Basin (3345.12 km²) in Shandong Province, China, contains five small and medium-sized reservoirs, three of which lack continuous storage observations. The study covers 2018–2022. Study focus We developed an automated waterbody-extraction method combining iterative Otsu thresholding with Random Forest object recognition and a Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 storage-fusion method. In total, 1016 satellite scenes (690 Sentinel-1 and 326 Sentinel-2) were used across the five reservoirs. The methods were developed and evaluated at the two data-rich reservoirs using 392 scenes (278 Sentinel-1 and 114 Sentinel-2) and then applied to the three data-scarce reservoirs. Reconstructed daily storage was analyzed using lagged Spearman correlation, the Reservoir Influence Index (RI), and reservoir-aware Grid-Xinanjiang (GXAJ) simulations. New hydrological insights for the region Waterbody extraction achieved a coefficient of determination (R²) up to 0.9103 and Kappa up to 0.9848, while storage fusion reduced normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) by 0.0609 and 0.0429 in the validation period at Tangcun and Xujiaya, respectively. The five-reservoir RI was 0.09, and peak storage-change–streamflow correlations were 0.29–0.53, indicating detectable but modest daily regulation. Incorporating reservoir dynamics increased Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (NSE) by 0.01 and reduced peak-flow and absolute runoff-volume errors by 1.6 and 1.1 %age points, respectively, mainly improving peak and recession simulations.

title: Assessing dynamic variations in snow accumulation and ablation for hydrological processes in northwest arid China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Chuan Wang, Zhi Li, Yupeng Li, Gonghuan Fang, Fan Sun
abstract: Study region The arid region of Northwest China has experienced pronounced warming and wetting under climate change. snowpack exhibits significant spatiotemporal heterogeneity, and changes in snow accumulation and ablation strongly influence regional solid water resources and snowmelt runoff. Study focus Using ERA5-Land daily snow water equivalent (SWE) reanalysis data, this study quantifies the rates, durations, and long-term evolution of snow accumulation and ablation during 1951–2022 and investigates their primary climatic drivers. New hydrological insights for the region The multi-year average snow accumulation rate (1.07 mm/d) is lower than the ablation rate (1.63 mm/d), with both peaking in the Altay, Ili-Tianshan, and Kunlun Mountains, indicating strong topographic control. Over the past 72 years, accumulation rates increased slightly, whereas ablation rates decreased, both exhibiting elevation dependence. Low-rate events dominate both phases, with a shorter accumulation period and a longer ablation period. Atypical processes, including ablation during the accumulation phase and accumulation during the ablation phase, are widespread, particularly in alpine regions. Snow accumulation and ablation are jointly controlled by maximum snow water equivalent (SWEmax), peak SWE timing, and snow phenology. Total snow accumulation increased slightly, whereas total ablation shows spatial heterogeneity. Reduced ablation during the accumulation phase and enhanced accumulation during the ablation phase increase regional solid water storage. These findings improve understanding of asymmetric snow dynamics and support snowmelt runoff simulation and water resources management.

title: Mekong River sediment decline, downstream reassembly, and weakening sediment exchange with Tonle Sap Lake
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Bo Liu, Khosro Morovati, Zilong Zhao, Hongling Zhao, Guangheng Ni, Fuqiang Tian
abstract: Study region Mekong River Basin. Study focus Dam expansion has disrupted Mekong sediment transport, yet mainstream sediment decline, downstream reassembly, and sediment exchange with Tonle Sap Lake are often studied separately. We combine long-term suspended-sediment concentration (SSC) observations, period- and hydrograph-limb-specific rating curves, and daily discharge reconstructed by a coupled hydrological–hydrodynamic model at Chroy Chang Var (CCV; delta apex) and Prek Kdam (PK; Tonle Sap gateway). Rating-curve and reconstructed-discharge uncertainties are jointly propagated to quantify changes from pre-dam (1962–1992) to post-dam (2010–2024). New hydrological insights for the region Mean annual suspended sediment load (SSL) at Chiang Saen declined by 85.7%, from 68.00 [95% uncertainty interval: 64.78, 71.46] to 9.75 [9.06, 10.41] Mt yr⁻¹ . Yet post-dam SSL at CCV was 54.55 [50.81, 58.90] Mt yr–1, of which Chiang Saen represented only 17.9% and cumulative net interstation changes 82.1% [80.6, 86.3%]. These are net reach-scale changes, not identified sediment sources or historical recovery. At PK, mean lakeward SSL was 2.41 [2.26, 2.56] Mt yr–1 and the mean inflow-minus-outflow balance was −0.59 [−0.87, −0.33] Mt yr–1. Lakeward SSL and reverse-flow volume declined significantly and covaried, although shared discharge dependence partly explains this correlation. Reconstructed flow-weighted SSC showed no significant trend, whereas observation-based evidence for declining SSC was model-dependent. The modern Mekong shows upstream depletion, downstream reassembly, and weakening sediment connectivity with Tonle Sap Lake.

title: Revealing the spatio-temporal evolution and driving mechanisms of watershed vegetation ecosystem stability using a novel integrated framework
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jiping Yao, Shengzhi Wang, Haoyu Xue, Xu Luo, Guoqiang Wang, Shen Qu, Xiaoman Jiang, Zhendong Yang, Wenxing Zhang, Xiaojing Zhang, Ruihong Yu
abstract: Study region The Hunhe Basin lies in the Inner Mongolia section of the Yellow River Basin, China, a typical arid and semi-arid watershed where large-scale ecological restoration has greatly increased vegetation cover while intensifying pressure on limited water resources. Study focus Reconciling restoration and water sustainability requires disentangling how vegetation ecosystem stability (VES) responds to external climatic drought and internal water deficit. We developed an ecological resilience (ERes) model analogized to Hooke’s Law that integrates climatic dryness degree (CDD) and vegetation water deficit pressure (VWDP). CDD, VWDP and ERes are quantified from water imbalance and residual vegetation growth capacity, with slope trend and sensitivity analysis isolating key ERes controls. Applied across Hunhe Basin over 1982–2020, we disentangle VES dynamics and underlying drivers. New hydrological insights for the region CDD dominated ERes variations in spring and summer, whereas VWDP, the imbalance between vegetation available water (surface runoff and soil water) and ecological water demand, controlled ERes in autumn, winter, and annually, making water deficit the core driver of VES decline. Restoration improved VES in northern and eastern restoration zones (ERes II→III/IV), but excessive afforestation under water-limited conditions caused marked decline (−0.51 < SlopeERes < −0.45) in western and northeastern areas. Positive CDD–VWDP feedbacks propagated stability loss across most of the basin (−0.52 < SlopeERes < −0.30), indicating that restoration intensity must match regional water availability.

title: Natural matrix effects on the transport of chlorinated phenols through Danube alluvial sediments
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Tamara Apostolović, Marijana Kragulj Isakovski, Irina Jevrosimov, Jelena Beljin, Peng Zhang, Srđan Rončević, Snežana Maletić
abstract: Study region Six layers of Danube alluvial sediment were collected at the Petrovaradinska ada groundwater source near Novi Sad, Serbia. This permeable alluvial system is relevant to riverbank filtration and drinking-water protection because surface water–groundwater exchange may transport organic micropollutants. Study focus Sorption and transport of 4-chlorophenol (4-CP), 2,4-dichlorophenol (2,4-DCP), 2,4,6-trichlorophenol (2,4,6-TCP), and pentachlorophenol (PCP) were examined using natural Danube water. Batch sorption and column transport experiments were combined with isotherm modelling and analysis of sediment-property relationships. Results were compared with previous experiments using a synthetic aqueous matrix. New hydrological insights for the region Sediments were predominantly sandy, containing 70–93% medium sand, 0.85–2.4% clay, 0.06–0.23% total organic carbon, and specific surface areas of 0.76–2.14 m² g⁻¹ . Sorption equilibrium was generally reached within 12–24 h. Retardation was compound- and layer-dependent: 1.45–2.80 for 4-CP, 1.35–2.45 for 2,4-DCP, 1.00–1.50 for 2,4,6-TCP, and 2.40–4.60 for PCP. Maximum sorption capacities were generally lower in Danube water than in the synthetic matrix, indicating that natural-water constituents influence contaminant partitioning. Overall, the sediments provide limited and variable protection, highlighting the need to account for sediment heterogeneity and water composition when assessing contaminant transport and groundwater vulnerability.

title: Elevation-dependent threshold effects of social-ecological-landscape factors on water supply service flow in a plateau mountain city
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Qingpu Li, Xiaoqing Zhao, Yuju Ran, Zixiang Sun, Zexian Gu, Yuenan Wang
abstract: Study region Kunming, a typical plateau mountain city in southwestern China facing severe water scarcity. Study focus Water supply service flow (WSF) is the potential water supply service transferable downstream after local demand is satisfied. This study simulated the direction and quantity of WSF in 2010 and 2023 across four elevation gradients. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model with Shapley Additive Explanations (XGBoost-SHAP) and a piecewise structural equation model identified the dominant drivers of WSF and their threshold effects, that is, the driver values at which a factor's influence on WSF reverses between positive and negative. New hydrological insights for the region Between 2010 and 2023, the water supply–demand deficit area expanded from 5.85% to 11.33% and total WSF quantity declined by 36.79%. The dominant drivers of WSF were elevation gradient-specific: ecological and landscape-pattern factors controlled Gradient I, ecological factors controlled Gradient IV, and socioeconomic and ecological factors jointly controlled Gradient II and Gradient III. Each key driver showed a gradient-specific threshold; in Gradient IV, for example, the precipitation threshold sustaining WSF fell from about 978 mm in 2010–894 mm in 2023. Overall, these elevation-dependent thresholds and driving mechanisms provide a scientific basis for spatially differentiated water-resource management.

title: Impact of soil moisture intrinsic signal structure on agricultural drought forecastability in the Yangtze River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Lue Zhou, Gengxi Zhang, Thian Yew Gan, Huimin Wang, Jinbai Huang, Shuai Zhou, Jin Zhao
abstract: Study region Yangtze River Basin (YRB). Study focus This study examines how two intrinsic temporal properties of soil-moisture drought signals are associated with realized forecast skill: persistence-related singularity structure, characterized by the maximum singularity strength (α max), and multifractal complexity, quantified by the singularity-spectrum width (Δα). A Joint Standardized Soil Moisture Index (JSSI) was constructed across five accumulation scales, and multifractal detrended fluctuation analysis (MF-DFA) was used to characterize multiscale temporal structure. Support Vector Regression (SVR), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) models were selected to forecast JSSI at 1-, 3-, and 6-month leads. New hydrological insights for the region the maximum singularity strengths (α max) and width of the singularity spectrum (Δα) show the most consistent associations with forecast skill and significant spatial organization across the basin. At the 1-month lead, α max provided the clearest common direction of skill variation, while responses to Δα were more model dependent. Cross-model agreement was strongest at the 3-month lead, with correlations among fitted forecastability surfaces of 0.993–0.999. At the 6-month lead, α max remained a common organizing axis, while the association with Δα became increasingly architecture dependent. Geopotential, long-term mean LAI, and soil type jointly explained 36.62% and 43.35% of the spatial variation in α max and Δα, respectively. Overall, soil-moisture temporal structure provides an important context for drought forecastability.

title: Depth-dependent seasonal associations of runoff and evapotranspiration with soil ice in the source region of the Yellow River
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Lei Song, Yanping Li
abstract: Study region The Source Region of the Yellow River (SRYR) is an alpine permafrost basin on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau and provides a setting for examining depth-dependent seasonal associations between soil ice, runoff, and evapotranspiration (ET). Study focus Using monthly WEB-DHM-PF soil ice simulations (1964–2024), observed basin outlet runoff, and reanalysis ET, this study examined annual phase associations and seasonal segmented relationships within the upper 0–2 m profile. Lagged correlation, segmented model comparison, and Bootstrap assessed when runoff and ET correspond to soil ice, where supported relationships occur across regions and depths, and how low ice slope direction and statistical support vary. New hydrological insights for the region Soil ice associations with runoff and ET mainly reflected the annual freeze and thaw cycle, with phase correspondence varying systematically with soil depth. Runoff associations extended through most of the soil profile in the degraded region but were concentrated in the shallow and middle zones of the stable region, whereas ET showed a relatively continuous vertical phase structure in both regions. Supported segmented relationships were more frequent for ET than for runoff. Breakpoints showed no consistent depth trend. Under the selected positive phase alignments, statistically supported positive low ice relationships occurred mainly in spring and autumn. Interpretation should consider uncertainty in simulated soil ice and the different spatial supports of basin outlet runoff and regional mean ET.

title: Vegetation productivity responses and environmental controls under flash drought stress in the Yellow River Basin
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jincheng Wu, Kunxia Yu, Peng Li, Zhanbin Li, Shengde Yu, Lu Jia, Xue Li, Zihui Yue, Zhi Yang, Yan Xu
abstract: Study region The Yellow River Basin, China Study focus Flash droughts, characterized by rapid soil moisture depletion within short timescales, increasingly threaten ecosystem stability and vegetation productivity. This study, focusing on the Yellow River Basin, analyzed two decades (2000–2020) of soil moisture (SM), vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and gross primary productivity (GPP) data. By examining the coupled dynamics of SM and VPD, the spatiotemporal evolution of flash droughts, and their impact on vegetation productivity, we employed partial correlation analysis, flash drought detection, SM–VPD decoupling, and Random Forest–SHAP modeling. New hydrological insights for the region Flash droughts exhibited prominent spatial heterogeneity across the basin, with the highest frequency occurring in the middle and lower reaches. Rapid soil moisture depletion induced persistent vegetation water stress in these regions, where SM dominated GPP limitation, with a maximum of 24 flash drought events and 256 cumulative pentads recorded at localized hotspot pixels. In contrast, upstream plateau regions experienced fewer flash droughts, where VPD served as the primary limiting factor for ecosystem productivity. SM–VPD decoupling revealed distinct nonlinear threshold responses, whereby GPP peaked under moderate water conditions (50th-60th SM and VPD percentiles) but declined sharply under intense soil or atmospheric drought. Across hydroclimatic gradients and functional types, cropland GPP depended strongly on SM supply, whereas forests exhibited greater VPD sensitivity and climatic resilience.

title: Phase-dependent responses of surface water dynamics to precipitation in the South China Karst based on remote sensing
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Qianying Mei, Rui Li, Zhongfa Zhou, Kaicun Wang, Qiaoyan Zhang, Chaoyang Xue, Shitian Tang, Jie An, Wanquan Zhang, Zhenhong Yi
abstract: Study region The Southern China Karst (SCK) region represents one of the most extensive karst landscapes worldwide and plays a critical role in regional water resources, ecological security, and sustainable development. Surface water systems in this region are highly sensitive to climatic variability and increasing human disturbances under global climate change. Study focus This study examines the phase-dependent responses of surface water dynamics to precipitation variability in the SCK region during 1990–2020. Multi-source remote sensing data were processed using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform to extract surface water extent based on a hybrid water index. Stepwise regression and interaction effect analyses were employed to quantify the relative contributions of climatic and anthropogenic drivers and to explore their combined influences on surface water changes. New hydrological insights from the region Surface water dynamics in the SCK exhibited a pronounced phase-dependent pattern, with expansion during 1990–2007 followed by contraction during 2008–2020. More importantly, the precipitation–surface water relationship shifted from a significant positive correlation to a significant negative correlation, revealing a precipitation-surface water response paradox at the regional scale. This finding suggests that increasing precipitation does not necessarily result in greater surface water availability in karst environments. Interaction analyses indicated that rising temperatures, intensified irrigation demand, and increasing precipitation variability progressively weakened the hydrological benefits of precipitation. The representative Nanpan-Beipan River Basin reproduced the same phase-dependent transition, further supporting the robustness of this pattern. These findings demonstrate that surface water responses in large karst regions are non-stationary and jointly regulated by climate variability, human activities, and karst hydrogeological processes.

title: Satellite-based monitoring of groundwater depletion and land subsidence in a fossil aquifer: Integrating InSAR and GRACE in the moghra development area, Egypt
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Ahmed Shalby, Romysaa Elasbah, Shymaa A.K. Fayad
abstract: Study region The Moghra development area is a rapidly expanding groundwater-dependent agricultural reclamation region in Egypt’s Western Desert, underlain by the non-renewable Moghra Aquifer. Study focus This study investigates the coupled evolution of groundwater depletion and land deformation using GRACE/GRACE-FO gravimetry (2002–2025), GLDAS soil-moisture estimates, and dual-geometry Sentinel-1 InSAR processed with LiCSBAS (2018–2023). Groundwater-storage and deformation time series were evaluated using robust trend analysis, change-point detection, and lag-correlation analysis. New hydrological insights for the region Soil moisture showed a weak but significant upward trend (+0.148 ± 0.009 cm yr⁻¹), suggesting that a persistent decline in soil moisture did not explain the overall decrease in terrestrial water storage. The full-period GRACE analysis indicated an overall groundwater-storage decline (−0.28 cm yr⁻¹). Phase-specific estimates became more negative after 2012 (−0.08 cm yr⁻¹) and 2020 (−0.16 cm yr⁻¹), although they were not statistically significant after accounting for temporal dependence. Across the wells field, the mean estimated InSAR vertical velocity was −0.46 mm yr⁻¹ (spatial SD = 0.43 mm yr⁻¹). The phase-specific slopes were more negative after 2021, changing from −0.09 to −0.53 mm yr⁻¹ , but neither phase showed a statistically significant monotonic trend. The strongest lagged association occurred when groundwater-storage variations preceded vertical displacement by approximately seven months, consistent with a possible delayed association between regional storage change and localized deformation. These findings support continued joint monitoring of groundwater storage and surface deformation in the Moghra development area.

title: Balancing freshwater security and saltwater intrusion risks: A self-correcting dual-chlorinity framework for dry-season ecological flow inference in tidal estuaries
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jiahui Li, Danrong Zhang, Guangwen Shao, Yiqing Guan, Wenming Zhang, Yufei Ma, Deyu Miao, Guoqing Wang, Peng Liu
abstract: Study region The Minjiang River Estuary, a tide-affected river system in Southeast China, where dry-season saltwater intrusion (SWI) threatens freshwater intake security. Study focus This study develops a self-correcting dual-chlorinity framework to infer dry-season ecological flow requirements for SWI mitigation under data-limited conditions. The framework integrates two complementary chlorinity representations that characterize delayed chlorinity responses under low-flow conditions and phase-dependent semi-lunar tidal modulation. Through adaptive dual-model reconciliation, consensus chlorinity estimates are obtained under varying discharge and tidal conditions and used to infer a management-oriented ecological-flow interval, which is independently evaluated using a hydrodynamic-diffusion model. New hydrological insights for the region Dry-season chlorinity is jointly controlled by persistent freshwater deficits and phase-dependent tidal modulation. Results show that the minimum discharge required to substantially reduce chlorinity exceedance varies from approximately 600–700 m³ /s across representative dry-season tidal conditions. Lower discharge is sufficient under weaker tidal forcing, whereas stronger spring tides require higher discharge. Hydrodynamic-diffusion simulations further confirm that ecological-flow regulation substantially reduces the duration and spatial extent of SWI, although short-duration exceedances may persist during extreme spring tides. The proposed framework provides a practical basis for ecological-flow regulation in tide-affected estuaries under limited data conditions.

title: Improving hydrological partitioning simulations by incorporating subsurface critical zone structure in an alpine catchment on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Congshuai Gao, Xiaoyan Li, Guangrong Hu, Yuanhong Deng
abstract: Study region The Qianhuli catchment is located in the upstream region of Shaliu River watershed on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, China. It comprises south-facing and north-facing hillslopes and a valley. Study focus Hydrological partitioning describes the allocation of precipitation among evapotranspiration, surface runoff, subsurface runoff, snow sublimation, deep percolation, and subsurface storage. Accurately quantifying hydrological partitioning is essential for assessing water resources, but simplified subsurface critical zone (CZ) representations obscure spatial storage and drainage differences. We incorporated soil and underlying weathered bedrock thicknesses measured by ground-penetrating radar into the Cold Regions Hydrological Modelling platform. Three schemes representing shallow soil, uniform CZ profiles based on observed means, and observed CZ heterogeneity were evaluated. New hydrological insights for the region The heterogeneous scheme achieved a validation Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.77, compared with 0.48 and 0.52 for the shallow and uniform schemes, respectively. Simulated surface runoff dominated the south-facing hillslope (60.6% of total runoff), whereas subsurface runoff dominated the north-facing hillslope (78.5%), where subsurface storage was more than twice as large. Evapotranspiration was also higher on the north-facing hillslope. These contrasts suggest that layer thickness and hydraulic characteristics jointly regulate water storage and lateral drainage, while soil moisture differences may influence evapotranspiration. This work demonstrates that representing subsurface CZ heterogeneity is important for improving land surface models and reducing uncertainty in alpine water resource predictions.

title: Spatially heterogeneous groundwater–soil moisture drought coupling across China: Lagged responses, climatic controls, and nonlinear risk transitions
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jing Wang, Guotao Dong, Chenguang Xiang, Xinghan Li
abstract: Study region This study examines groundwater–soil moisture drought relationships across China, spanning arid northwestern to humid southeastern regions. Monthly 1-km groundwater and soil-moisture data for 2005–2022 were analyzed across four observation-derived aridity classes. Study focus We assessed spatial heterogeneity, 0–12-month lag structure, nonlinear responses, and climatic dependence using 210 paired months. Temporal autocorrelation, spatial multiple testing, and lag-selection bias were addressed through effective-sample-size adjustment, BH-FDR control, effect-size sensitivity, reverse-direction analysis, and simultaneous Fisher-z screening. Climate-adjusted associations accounted for precipitation and vapor-pressure-deficit anomalies with clustered and bootstrap uncertainty. New hydrological insights for the region Groundwater-deficit frequency was spatially heterogeneous, whereas soil-moisture drought was more uniform and compound events were localized. Robust associations covered 6.32%, 5.24%, and 2.18% of valid area at correlation thresholds of 0.20, 0.30, and 0.40, respectively. Bidirectional and lag-stability analyses showed that optimal lags describe temporal ordering rather than causality. Nonlinear drought-risk amplification was strongest in semi-arid and semi-humid regions. The national transition near GDI = 2.125 had a broad bootstrap range (0.369–2.375), precluding interpretation as a universal physical threshold. After climatic adjustment, a robust GDI–SMDI association remained only in the semi-humid region (β = 0.054; 95% CI: 0.012–0.096). Groundwater deficit is therefore a conditional regional drought indicator rather than a universal causal control.

title: Projecting watershed health and ecological security in Iran
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Seyed Hamidreza Sadeghi, Ali Nasiri Khiavi, Reza Chamani, Negin Behnia, Vahid Moosavi, Hamid Nouri, Padidehsadat Sadeghi, Mohammad Hossein Shoushtari, Abdulvahed Khaledi Darvishan, Mehdi Vafakhah, Hamidreza Moradi Rekabdarkolaei
abstract: Study region The study was conducted in Iran and at 640 third-order watersheds. Study focus The research synthesizes dynamic hydro-climatic and land-use factors in a Pressure-State-Response (PSR) framework to project the Watershed Health (WH) and Ecological Security (ES) in Iran from 2033 to 2053. Machine learning (RF/SVM/KNN), SARIMA, and Markov chain models using TerrSet algorithms were applied to predict relevant indicators across 640 third-order watersheds to assess current and anticipate future WH and ES trajectories. New hydrologic insights Our results present an alarming prospect for environmental trends in 2053, indicating an 11.9% decrease in annual rainfall and a 2.87°C increase in temperature, resulting in a 77.7% decrease in the Palmer Drought Severity Index. Of specific concern are land-cover changes, of which the increase in barren land by 81.4%, at the expense of rangelands (-34.4%) and forests (-15.9%), reflects the increasing rates of desertification. Spatial analysis reveals stark regional differences, where northern watersheds, particularly the relatively forested Caspian Region, remain moderately healthy. Conversely, southeastern watersheds, particularly Sistan, face a critical condition, with 70% of the territory expected to become unhealthy by 2053 due to severe water stress and soil erosion. The results further indicate that the country as a whole has experienced the most severe ecological degradation, with vulnerable areas increasing from 25% in 2033–35% in 2053, especially in the south.

title: Exploring suspended sediment concentration determinants in mountain rivers using machine learning and structural equation modeling
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yuning Tan, Ying Chen, Chongming Yu, Wenjie Li
abstract: Study region The lower Jinsha River Basin, China, a mountainous basin with high sediment yield. Study focus Flood sediment transport in mountain rivers reflects interactions among hydrological and physiographic factors. This study combines flood-event identification, sediment rating curves, and hysteresis analysis to characterize temporal shifts in sediment transport, and then integrates data-driven models and pathway analysis to identify and quantify the main controls on daily suspended sediment concentration. New hydrological insights for the region Using 60,254 daily records from ten rivers (10²–10⁴ km²), we found lower sediment concentrations at comparable discharges in 2007–2020 than in 1970–1987, while clockwise discharge–sediment hysteresis persisted across the studied rivers. Among five data-driven models, the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) performed best overall, achieving NSE values of 0.743 and 0.714 in the two periods. SHAP analysis revealed interactions between current hydrological forcing and antecedent sediment conditions. PLS-SEM estimated positive direct effects of current discharge and antecedent sediment concentration on sediment concentration (β = 0.794–1.030 and 0.680–0.695, respectively). Antecedent discharge showed a positive indirect effect through current discharge (β = 0.719–0.952) and a negative direct effect (β = −1.031 to −0.831). These findings indicate that daily sediment dynamics in the lower Jinsha River reflect both current discharge and antecedent sediment conditions, supporting their joint consideration in regional sediment monitoring and flood-related sediment assessment.

title: Spatiotemporal variations of runoff and sediment flux in the Source Region of the Yellow River: Driving factor shifts and sub-regional attribution
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Jinjin Liu, Zhiwei Li, Xiongdong Zhou, Gaolei Zhao, Shimin Tian
abstract: Study region The Source Region of the Yellow River (SRYR), China. Study focus This study examines spatiotemporal variations and driver shifts in runoff and sediment flux at four stations: Huangheyan, Jimai, Maqu, and Tangnaihai. Trend analyses used available 1955–2021 records, whereas attribution across four station-defined sub-regions used consistent precipitation, evaporation, and land-use data for 1970–2020. Mann–Kendall tests, double mass curves, and climate elasticity analysis were applied, with stages defined separately for each sub-region. New hydrological insights for the region Annual runoff showed no significant monotonic long-term trend, but mean runoff was lower after 1991. Sediment flux generally decreased and was more seasonally concentrated than runoff. Jimai–Maqu contributed the largest runoff share (50.65%), whereas Maqu–Tangnaihai dominated sediment yield (63.25%), indicating a spatial mismatch. Precipitation and evaporation both increased significantly (p < 0.01) and were positively correlated, reflecting coupled water-supply and evaporative-loss effects. During T1→T2, evaporation exerted the strongest estimated negative influence on runoff and sediment flux in all reaches, whereas residual non-climatic effects on sediment differed among reaches. During T2→T3, precipitation was the leading positive influence on runoff recovery in Reaches II–IV, but negative residual effects offset precipitation-related sediment increases in Reaches III and IV. Land-cover changes provide complementary evidence of reach-specific water retention and sediment regulation. Thus, runoff recovered across reaches while sediment responses diverged, underscoring sediment availability and connectivity for reach-specific management.

title: Hydrological controls on deep learning streamflow transferability across contrasting basins
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Chaowei Xu, Yasong Chen, Yunpeng Zhao, Hou Jiang, Yating Zhu, Boyang Jia, Yukun Hou, Tengfei Huang, Guangrong Cao, Dianchang Wang, Yangxiaoyue Liu
abstract: Study region The Yuan River basin, a major tributary of the middle Yangtze River in China, is used as the source basin for model development, and the model's transferability is further evaluated across global hydrological zones. Study focus Accurate streamflow hindcasting using deep learning (DL) is essential for water resources management, yet transferring DL models from local to global scales remains a critical challenge. This study developed a multi-strategy ensemble DL framework that integrates feature selection, time-varying filtering-based empirical mode decomposition, Newton-Raphson-based optimization, and the CNN–BiLSTM–attention network to hindcast daily streamflow and diagnose cross-basin transferability under contrasting hydroclimatic conditions. New hydrological insights for the region In the source basin, the proposed framework achieved robust and statistically consistent improvements over the ML/DL benchmarks. Transfer experiments across 3486 basins showed that the modeling workflow performed most effectively in hydrologically compatible regions, including saturation-excess basins, snowmelt- or permafrost-influenced regimes, and catchments with coherent seasonal runoff patterns. Poor transferability to arid infiltration-excess basins and dryland systems with transmission losses highlights the heterogeneous runoff mechanisms that disrupt rainfall-runoff relationships between source and target basins. These results indicate that cross-basin DL transfer is associated with runoff generation similarity, rainfall spatial organization, regime regularity, and anthropogenic influences, rather than neural architecture alone, thereby informing water resources management across diverse global basins.

title: Potential and constraints of ERA5-driven dynamical downscaling to estimate landslide-triggering rainfall conditions, evaluated for the Marche region in Italy
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Flavia Ferriero, Stefano Luigi Gariano, Maria Teresa Brunetti, Massimo Melillo, Silvia Peruccacci, Elisabetta Napolitano, Guido Rianna
abstract: Study region Marche region, central Italy: a mountainous and hilly area between the Apennines and the Adriatic Sea, highly prone to rainfall-induced shallow landslides. Study focus This study investigates whether three convection-permitting dynamical downscaling products available for Italy of the ERA5 global reanalysis, namely MERIDA-HRES (grid spacing ~4 km), MOLOCH-MORE (~1.7 km), and VHR-REA (~2.2 km), can be used to reconstruct landslide-triggering rainfall conditions and derive rainfall thresholds. A catalogue of 360 rainfall-triggered shallow landslides recorded in the region between 2002 and 2024 is analysed, and triggering conditions are reconstructed from both a regional rain gauge network (145 stations) and the three products. New hydrological insights for the region Compared with rain gauges, all products underestimate cumulated rainfall and overestimate rainfall duration, leading to biased triggering conditions and lower thresholds, especially for short durations. The evaluation of two recent severe events reveals a marked contrast in performance: the intense, localized, September 2022 event is severely underestimated by all products, whereas the severe, widespread, May 2023 event is better reproduced. A further analysis confirms that this limitation is inherited from the driving ERA5 reanalysis. Overall, downscaled reanalyses show potential for regional landslide early warning, but they should be used as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, ground-based observations. Moreover, the rainfall thresholds cannot be transferred from gauge-based to model-based rainfall without careful recalibration.

title: A Standardized Socio-Hydrological Drought Index integrating non-stationary streamflow and evolving water demand: A case study of a humid catchment in southern China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yewei Liu, Wen Wang, Yongwei Liu, Zhansheng Ji
abstract: Study region: The Linshui River basin is a humid, monsoon-influenced catchment in southern China with pronounced seasonal streamflow variability and intensive irrigation. Study focus: This study develops the Standardized Socio-Hydrological Drought Index (SSHDI), coupling non-stationary streamflow with evolving water demand. It combines change detection and CDF mapping, historical downstream demand reconstruction with efficiency adjustments, and priority-based monthly demand thresholds. A raw deficit ratio derived from five-day averaged streamflow and demand thresholds retains the physical supply–demand interpretation, while Generalized Logistic fitting and a standard normal transformation yield SSHDI values expressing relative socio-hydrological stress. New hydrological insights for the region: In the Linshui River basin, significant abrupt streamflow shifts occurred in January, August, November, and December. SRI-defined droughts frequently reflected spring runoff anomalies despite sufficient supply, whereas SSHDI-defined stress clustered in July–November as post-flood flows receded and irrigation demand remained high. Across 1980–2022, the SSHDI identified 84 stress events versus 81 SRI–defined hydrological drought events, with 21 SSHDI stress events (25.0%) containing no days of estimated supply–demand deficit (SHDI > 0). In 2019 and 2022, elevated standardized stress occurred while streamflow exceeded the fixed 20 m3/s warning threshold. These findings suggest that, in similarly humid, irrigation-intensive catchments of southern China, the critical season of demand-related water stress may follow flood recession rather than coincide with anomalous spring runoff.

title: Precipitation sources and evaporation sinks of China’s drylands from 2001 to 2024
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Haitao Zhang, Junshuo Li, Conrad Zorn, Peng Tian, Eerdun Hasi, Yingjun Xu
abstract: Study region China’s drylands, spanning arid and semi-arid regions of northern China and the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where water availability is strongly constrained by precipitation and atmospheric moisture transport. Study focus We used ERA5 reanalysis and the WAM2layers moisture-tracking model to quantify precipitation sources, evaporation sinks, recycling ratios, and moisture surplus from 2001 to 2024 within a bidirectional atmospheric water-vapor budget framework. The tracking results were further linked with ERA5-Land evaporation components to examine how land-surface evaporation processes contribute to terrestrial moisture transport. New hydrological insights for the region China’s drylands exhibit a persistent west-to-east moisture transport structure. On average, approximately 69% of precipitation originates from terrestrial sources, including Central and South Asia and adjacent continental regions, while about 67% of evapotranspired moisture precipitates over land, mainly in eastern China and Northeast Asia. Both precipitation and evaporation recycling ratios exhibited declining trends, indicating reduced local moisture recycling efficiency and an increasing relative contribution from long-range transport. Vegetation transpiration dominates terrestrial moisture transport, accounting for more than 40% of both terrestrial precipitation sources and total evaporation within China’s drylands, with its contribution increasing over time, whereas the contributions of soil and snow evaporation decreased or remained stable. Overall, China’s drylands function as a spatially heterogeneous but regionally connected atmospheric moisture system, simultaneously receiving upwind moisture, recycling local evaporation, and redistributing moisture to downwind regions

title: HBV-guided residual learning for daily runoff estimation under observed hydroclimatic forcing and flood-event diagnosis in an upper Huai River catchment
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yiming Qiang, Ruling Hong, Haoli Wang, Duanqiang Zhai
abstract: Study Region: The Beimiaoji catchment, a flood-prone tributary catchment of the upper Huai River Basin, China, was examined using daily runoff and gauge precipitation (2015–2024), ERA5-Land temperature and potential evapotranspiration, and catchment-context rasters. Study Focus: This study evaluated an HBV-guided encoder–decoder LSTM (HG-ED-LSTM) for daily runoff estimation under observed hydroclimatic forcing. The framework integrates antecedent hydroclimatic information, separately encoded HBV runoff sequences, and catchment-context features through gated fusion to correct the target-day HBV estimate. Performance was assessed using hv-blocked five-fold validation, benchmark comparisons, ablation experiments, and high-flow diagnostics covering nine representative and all 35 eligible peak-centered windows. New Hydrological Insights for the Region: In the Beimiaoji catchment, HBV provided a process-based runoff baseline but exhibited a negative aggregate bias (PBIAS = −23.79%). Incorporating HBV-guided residual correction improved NSE from 0.721 to 0.811, reduced RMSE by 17.9%, and brought PBIAS to −0.22%. Across 35 high-flow windows, pooled RMSE decreased by 33.6%, while mean peak-magnitude error declined by 50.8%. The pooled signed event-volume bias also improved from −28.98% to −3.43%, indicating a closer agreement with observed high-flow runoff volumes. Peak-timing performance varied between the representative and expanded event sets, highlighting the complementary value of magnitude- and timing-based evaluations. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of HBV-guided residual learning to improve daily runoff estimation and high-flow representation in the upper Huai River Basin under observed forcing.

title: Study on multi-objective water resources optimal allocation in water network areas based on water-energy-carbon synergistic governance
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Yuzhang Wang, Zengchuan Dong, Jitao Zhang, Ziqin Zheng, Wenzhuo Wang, Li Ren
abstract: Study area Northern Jiangsu Study focus Water resources optimal allocation is essential for coordinating regional water-use conflicts and promoting sustainable development. However, existing models face challenges in representing complex hydrodynamic processes in plain river networks with strong human interventions, and the integration of carbon considerations into water allocation remains limited. This study develops a Water-Economic-Carbon-Spatial Multi-objective Optimization Model (WEC-SMOM). The framework integrates generalized river network hydrodynamic modeling with NSGA-III-based multi-objective optimization and a projection pursuit-based compromise solution selection method to coordinate water-supply reliability, economic benefits, and carbon emissions under complex flow conditions. New hydrological insights for the region Applied to Northern Jiangsu, the proposed framework quantifies trade-offs among economic benefits, water-supply reliability, and carbon emissions. Results reveal two independent pathways for reducing water shortages. Under unchanged infrastructure conditions, the regional water shortage rate decreased from 2022 to 2035 by 4.4, 0.3, and 0.2 %age points under the 95%, 75%, and 50% water-supply guarantee scenarios, respectively. Under identical demand-year and hydrological conditions, HRSC-II reduces water shortages by an additional 2.7–5.4 %age points during extremely dry years compared with the pre-project scenario, with reductions exceeding 6 %age points in some terminal cities. These findings distinguish the contributions of demand management and infrastructure development and provide insights for sustainable allocation in complex river network systems.

title: Assessing future eco-hydrological behaviour of a typical Sahelian agro-ecosystem under climate change for the 21st century
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Lena Collet, Jordi Etchanchu, Nanée Chahinian, Aaron Boone, Geremy Panthou, Françoise Vimeux, Nesrine Farhani, Ibrahim Maïnassara, Chloé Ollivier, Marc Oliver-Soulayrol, Brune Raynaud--Schell, Taeken Wijmer, Jérôme Demarty
abstract: Study Region The Sahel is dominated by a monsoon climate, where most of the population relies on subsistence agriculture. This study focuses on a typical agro-pastoral area in southwestern Niger. Study Focus Significant gaps remain in climate change impact projections in the Sahel. Indeed, capturing the impact of rapid hydrological processes necessitates high temporal resolution scenarios and adapted ecohydrological models, which has rarely been done in Sahel. This study addresses this gap by building climate scenarios at a 30-minute time step, by combining an observational dataset with CMIP6 projections for five models, two emission pathways (SSP245 and SSP585), and two horizons (2050 and 2100). These scenarios are used in a land surface model, SiSPAT, to assess future changes in water and energy cycles. Vegetation response to climate evolution is also considered. New Hydrological Insights for the Region All scenarios project a temperature increase for 2100 (+3.8°C for SSP245, +6.3°C for SSP585), with up to 10 days over 45°C during the growing season. Projected rainfall intensification is more uncertain (+27 to +56% by 2100). It leads to an increase in runoff (+168 mm/yr) and drainage (+132 mm/yr) for SSP585–2100, raising concern over flooding and soil erosion. Considering vegetation response to climate evolution strongly affects evapotranspiration seasonality (+/- 1 mm/day during some months). This study highlights the impact of climate scenarios on water and energy cycles with current agricultural practices.

title: Diagnosing catchment hydrological memory in the Po, Arno, Ticino and Adda basins (north-central Italy) through a multi-scale standardized drought index
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Arianna Di Paola, Massimiliano Pasqui, Edmondo Di Giuseppe, Sara Quaresima, Leandro Rocchi, Elena Rapisardi, Emanuele Romano, Ramona Magno
abstract: Study region North-central Italy: the Po, Arno, Ticino and Adda basins, spanning Mediterranean pluvial, snow-dominated Alpine and lake-regulated regimes. Study focus Drought propagation depends on how catchments integrate precipitation anomalies across accumulation timescales. Existing approaches summarize this memory with a single accumulation scale, or with transfer functions that are hard to compare across basins and seasons. We extend the D(SPI) index to test whether alternative attenuation patterns of precipitation memory can be distinguished against standardized streamflow anomalies (SQI1), characterizing the extent, seasonality and uncertainty of catchment memory. Classical transfer-function models serve as benchmarks. New hydrological insights for the region The Po and Adda show stable precipitation-streamflow relationships through the year, whereas the Arno and Ticino show stronger seasonality and periods of weak coupling. Alternative attenuation patterns, each at its own accumulation window K, often explain streamflow equally well, so neither the pattern nor K is identifiable alone. The data do constrain the effective memory (mean age of the precipitation months driving the index), from 0.4 to 1.5 months in the Arno to 1.9–4.5 months in the Adda. Benchmarks and D(SPI) reach comparable explanatory power and weight the same recent months. At monthly resolution, memory is better characterized by its effective extent than by a unique attenuation pattern. Results are in-sample; the Ticino record is short (1964–1994), and the Ticino and Adda are Po tributaries.

title: Supply–demand assessment of ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction capacity: Focusing on drought and flood risks
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Wentong Yang, Wei D. Xu, Junfei Chen, Peng Zhang, Chuanyi Wang
abstract: Study region Henan Province, China. Study focus The potential of ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction to simultaneously mitigate drought and flood risks remains insufficiently understood. This study developed a framework to jointly assess the supply–demand matching of ecosystem-based drought disaster risk reduction capacity (Eco-DDRR) and ecosystem-based flood disaster risk reduction capacity (Eco-FDRR). Supply was represented by risk-reduction ecosystem services and demand by the hazard–exposure–vulnerability framework. The Eco-DDRR and Eco-FDRR supply–demand matching indices, denoted as D-SDI and F-SDI, respectively, were further used to examine their associations, dependence structures, and co-occurring state probabilities. The results were then used to assess potential synergies, trade-offs, and differentiated management needs across cities. New hydrological insights for the region Several cities showed positive associations between D-SDI and F-SDI, with some exhibiting upper-tail dependence. This indicates a stronger tendency for high matching levels to co-occur and suggests potential for coordinated improvement of D-SDI and F-SDI. D-SDI declined across most of the study area, whereas F-SDI generally increased, suggesting a priority for improving Eco-DDRR supply–demand matching. In addition, slight mismatch in both D-SDI and F-SDI was the dominant co-occurring state in most cities, while other high-probability state combinations varied considerably across cities, supporting classification into five management types. Overall, the framework highlights the potential of ecosystem-based disaster risk reduction for integrated drought–flood risk management and offers a hydro-ecological perspective for developing disaster-resilient cities.

title: Machine learning modeling of spatially distributed soil moisture time series for a hillside at Sulmachun watershed, South Korea
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology: Regional Studies, Volume 68 Author(s): Dahong Kim, Dongwon Ko, Jeongseop Lee, Sanghyun Kim
abstract: Study region The study focuses on a steep, 4000 m² headwater hillslope within South Korea's Sulmachun Catchment. This monsoon-influenced region receives 1636 mm of annual rainfall (70% during summer) and features sandy loam soils under a mixed forest canopy. Study focus The research evaluates the predictability of spatially distributed soil moisture time series using MLP, 1D-CNN, and LSTM machine learning models. By analyzing soil moisture measurements across vertical and transactional profiles, the study aims to determine the optimal temporal lag (memory effect) for accurate predictions and to map underlying hydrological processes based on model performance. New hydrological insights for the region The LSTM model outperformed others by effectively capturing complex temporal dependencies. The modeling revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in hydrological memory across the hillslope. A short term 6 h antecedent lag was optimal for midslope regions, reflecting rapid vertical infiltration and post rainfall storage release.
